title: Overly Wild
author: Niao Song Mi
synopsis:
Niao Song Mi's Cosmic Universe Series: Overly Wild

[Male lead steals love from his brother / Second male chases his wife to the crematorium, double purity][Fake obedient, truly rebellious little princess vs. scheming, cold, and seductive prince]

At the age of eight, Song Shuangxu was abandoned in an empty house to fend for herself. It was Shen Yu who took her in when no one else wanted her.

The boy in a school uniform and white shirt bent down to her: "Come with me, okay?"

From that day on, Shen Yu became her entire world.

Shen Yu doted on her, pampered her, and raised her like a princess. Unfortunately, she could only ever be his little sister.

Shuangxu watched as women came and went in his life, his playboy nature breaking her heart. Her secret feelings for him withered in the barren corners of her heart, growing into a field of wild grass.

In Shuangxu’s eyes, He Tingzhou was her brother’s friend, a terrible bastard, someone to avoid at all costs.

She never thought she would one day have an illicit relationship with He Tingzhou.

At a gathering, as the wine flowed and the atmosphere grew lively, in a darkened suite on the second floor, she was pinned against the door by a man, his kiss nearly suffocating her.
He Tingzhou bit her ear, lazily threatening, "If you don’t want your brother to hear, be good."

chapters.title: A Prominent Figure
chapters.content:
Song Shuangxu’s return to the country this time was sudden; she hadn’t told anyone.

As the plane landed and she heard the airport broadcast in standard Mandarin, surrounded by the faces of her compatriots, she finally felt the reality of being back on her homeland.

Shuangxu wore a light beige trench coat over a simple linen white shirt and jeans, yet an air of nobility radiated from her silky, soft hair.

The driver, with a thick Beijing accent, asked, "Miss, where to?"

"The Third Hospital."

April in Yan City was bursting with the vitality of spring’s renewal. Shuangxu hadn’t been back in five years. This hasty return was because her senior, Shu Yang, was ill.

When she entered the hospital room, the emaciated Shu Yang was sitting cross-legged on the bed, murmuring, "Form is emptiness, emptiness is form... men are only for casual play, never for serious feelings..."

Shuangxu’s worries along the way dissipated. "How did getting sick lead you to see through the world?"

Shu Yang, who had been reciting scriptures, opened her eyes, her joy overflowing. "Hey, why are you back?"

"Of course I’d come back if you’re in trouble." Shuangxu sat down by the bed. "What did the doctor say?"

Recently, Shu Yang had been diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome—a malignancy originating from hematopoietic stem cells, also known as pre-leukemia.

Her long-term boyfriend had not only stolen all the cash from the company’s accounts and half the core team but also taken off with the technical data Shu Yang had worked on for two years.

"A bad news and a good news," Shu Yang said. "The doctor says I’m already at intermediate-2 risk, with a high chance of progressing to leukemia. I need chemotherapy."

"And the good news?" Shuangxu hoped for something positive.

"The good news is, chemotherapy can only control it, not cure it. It’ll also severely damage ovarian function. I might never be able to have children."

At first, Shuangxu thought she’d mixed them up, but after considering, neither piece of news was good.

"This is good news?" She touched Shu Yang’s forehead. "Did this illness affect your brain too?"

"Realizing a man is scum isn’t good news?" Shu Yang was naturally carefree. "Besides, I never wanted kids. I suspect this disease is hereditary—my dad died of leukemia."

She and Chen Peiran had been together for four years, returning to the country to start a business together. Who could have predicted that the moment she fell ill, Chen Peiran would flee with the money without hesitation.

Shuangxu frowned. "I don’t expect him to help in hard times, but could he at least not kick you while you’re down?"

"Men are all like this. The most unreliable thing in the world is love. Women who believe in love will always suffer for it."

Shuangxu couldn’t argue with that.

"Even though I’ve never been in love, I’ve suffered because of it." Shuangxu said. "I still have some savings. I’ve transferred it to your card. It’s not much, but it should help you get by for a while."

Shu Yang checked her phone banking balance and let out a rooster-like shriek. "This is not much?!"

Shuangxu’s "not much" and her "not much" were clearly not the same concept.

Shuangxu covered her mouth to quiet her. "Shh... Just know I’d do anything for you. Don’t get excited."

Shen Yu had always doted on her, giving her pocket money since she was little. After she was sent abroad, worried she might struggle alone in a foreign land, he increased her allowance several times. Over five years, it added up to a considerable sum.

"Don’t talk about doing anything—you could take my liver and kidneys, and I’d still be fine!" Shu Yang said. "You really lent me this much? In my current state, I might not be able to pay you back..."

Shuangxu said, "Consider it my investment."

Feixue was already on the brink of bankruptcy. Everyone else was avoiding it, so only a 24K pure gold fool would invest now.

Shu Yang hadn’t cried when she broke up with her ex or when she signed the chemotherapy consent form alone in the hospital. But now, tears welled in her eyes.

"In the end, you’re the one I can rely on!"

She was strong, but having someone to back her up in times like this made all the difference.

Shuangxu smiled and hugged her, patting her back. "A man who can’t share hardship isn’t worth keeping. It’s fine. I’m here with you."

Shu Yang suddenly sat up. "Oh, right! You came back so suddenly—what about your family? Did they let you come back?"

Regarding her family, regarding what happened before she went abroad, Shuangxu rarely brought it up.

Shu Yang only knew that her relationship with her family wasn’t close, that she had a brother who was the most important person to her.

And that five years ago, Shuangxu had been forcibly sent abroad.

—She called it exile.

Shuangxu’s reaction was calmer than expected. "The worst that could happen is being sent away again. I was mentally prepared before coming back."

At this moment, Shuangxu didn’t know that news of her return had already been spread by an unnoticed bystander.

If asked which heiress had the most famous reputation in Yan City’s elite circles, Song Shuangxu would definitely be in the top three.

Apart from her complicated background, it was also because of the renowned Shen Yu behind her.

After passing through several hands, the news finally reached Yue Zifeng. He immediately posted the photo in a small group chat, tagging Shen Yu multiple times without a response.

Shen Yu had just left a meeting when he received the call. "What are you busy with that you’re not replying? Shuangxu is back—why didn’t you tell us?"

Shen Yu moved the phone away from his ear, opened WeChat, and saw the photo of Shuangxu.

The background was a hospital, bustling with people. As if sensing someone was taking her picture, she turned around, her hair brushing her cheek, her clear eyes slightly confused.

He exited the photo and opened his chat with Shuangxu, confirming there were no new messages.

After Shuangxu went abroad, their contact had lessened. The child who used to follow him like a shadow no longer shared everything with him.

The last time she had initiated a message was over two months ago: "Happy New Year."

But returning to the country without telling him—wasn’t that a bit too rebellious?

The secretary handed him a large financial document. Shen Yu took the pen and signed, his expression unchanged. "Why should I tell you?"

"Come on, Shuangxu is like my sister too." Yue Zifeng was enthusiastic. "Let’s take her out for dinner tonight. I haven’t seen her in ages—I miss her."

"Take your own sister out."

"My sister is only seven. Should I take her to a kids’ meal? That wouldn’t even fill the gap in my teeth."

"Then you should see a dentist." Shen Yu hung up the phone, flicking his fingers lightly outward. The secretary closed the door and left.

He dialed Shuangxu’s number.

When Shuangxu answered the phone, she was just leaving the hospital.

She naturally understood why Shen Yu was calling. As she picked up, she pondered how to explain her sudden return.

Shen Yu spoke first, his tone casually natural. "You’re back?"

"Mhm. Just arrived this afternoon."

"What were you doing at the hospital? Not feeling well?"

Shen Yu’s calm and measured voice steadied her heart, which had been floating anxiously since she boarded the plane.

"I’m fine. I just came to see my senior."

Shen Yu didn’t say much, only, "Come home for dinner tonight. Send me your address, and I’ll have someone pick you up."

Shuangxu obediently replied, "Okay."

As dusk fell, the late spring in Yan City still carried a chill. Shuangxu tightened the collar of her trench coat and stood by the roadside. She didn’t wait long before the car arrived.

The driver came around to the back, respectfully opening the door for her. "Miss Shuangxu."

Shuangxu handed him her suitcase and bent down to get in the car. Only then did she notice the man sitting inside.

---

chapters.title: No One Here Expected Her Return
chapters.content:
Shen Yu had come straight from the company, wearing a crisp, expensive light gray suit.

Time had left no traces on his refined face. The look he gave Shuangxu was the same as she remembered.

Gentle. Reassuring.

Yet, despite Shen Yu visiting her every year, she suddenly felt a sense of unfamiliarity.

Seeing her hesitation to get in, Shen Yu called out, "Xiao Jiu."

At the sound of his deep, calm voice, a wordless bitterness surged in Shuangxu’s nose.

She quickly lowered her eyes, bent down to enter the car, and said, "Brother."

The car drove smoothly through the evening rush hour traffic, the cabin silent.

Shen Yu crossed his legs and asked her, "What time was your flight?"

"A little after two."

"Why didn’t you ask me to pick you up?"

"I didn’t want to disturb your work." Shuangxu said. "Taxis at the airport are convenient."

Shen Yu’s gaze shifted from the other side, observing her downcast expression.

She used to be so lively, the child he had spoiled, who loved and depended on him the most, and was fearless around him.

Now she was very well-behaved.

But being too well-behaved made her seem distant. Even her posture radiated estrangement.

Ever since she was forced to go abroad, she hadn’t even come back for Spring Festival—maybe out of defiance, or simply because she didn’t want to see these people in the country.

The last time Shen Yu saw her was last year, on her birthday. She had a high fever and was curled up alone in her foreign apartment. He had flown over to see her.

She had changed a lot compared to when she used to follow him around.

The green immaturity of her youth had disappeared over the years of separation, replaced by the refined beauty of a mature woman.

Shen Yu looked at her for a while before saying, "Xiao Jiu has become distant with me."

"It’s not that, I just..."

I didn’t want to trouble you—that was still being distant.

Shuangxu simply forced a reason. "I wanted to surprise you."

Adult surprises had a 50% chance of turning into shocks.

When Shuangxu and Shen Yu returned to the Shen family home, Shen Changyuan and his wife were already waiting.

As soon as she entered, Fu Yun joyfully pulled her over, examining her from all angles, first saying she had grown taller, then that she hadn’t changed much and looked the same as before.

"You video call her every month—of course you wouldn’t notice the difference." Shen Changyuan seemed in high spirits. He asked Shuangxu, "Why didn’t you tell us in advance that you were coming back? We didn’t have time to prepare anything at home."

"It was a last-minute decision." Shuangxu explained. "I left in a hurry and didn’t get a chance to tell you."

"You must be starving, arriving so late." Fu Yun said. "Tonight’s dishes are all your favorites. When Aunt Wang heard you were coming back, she was overjoyed."

The table was filled with Shuangxu’s favorite dishes from childhood. A steamed garoupa was placed in front of her, and the black chicken soup was fragrant and delicious.

Fu Yun kept serving her food, while Shen Changyuan asked a few questions about her life abroad. The conversation inevitably turned to her return trip.

"How long did you take off for this vacation?"

Shuangxu knew the minefield was approaching, but she didn’t want to lie.

She put down her chopsticks, lifted her head, and seriously said, "I quit my job."

After she said this, the living room fell into silence.

"You quit your job?" Fu Yun’s chopsticks paused in her hand, looking at her in surprise, then at Shen Yu. "I never heard you mention it. How could it be so sudden?"

Quitting her job abroad meant she might not be leaving Yan City this time.

The earlier warmth and harmony seemed like a layer of exquisitely crafted glass—beautiful, but fragile.

"Are you quitting your airline job to return to China for development?" Shen Changyuan asked.

Shuangxu didn’t answer. Instead, she asked, "Can I come back?"

Fu Yun hesitated. "You were doing so well abroad. Why did you suddenly want to come back?"

Why did she suddenly want to come back?

On one hand, it was because of Shu Yang’s illness. On the other hand, and more importantly, she wanted to come home.

But Shuangxu knew that wasn’t the answer they wanted.

Life abroad was good, but it couldn’t compare to her emotional attachment to Yan City.

This was where she had grown up—with scorching summers and long, cold winters.

Unfortunately, no one here expected her to return.

At this moment, Shen Yu, who had been silent, placed a plate of deboned fish in front of Shuangxu.

The fish meat was tender and translucent, placed on a white porcelain plate. It made a soft clink as it touched the table, breaking the uncomfortable silence.

"How is your senior doing?"

Shuangxu briefly explained Shu Yang’s condition.

Shen Yu asked, "Do you need my help?"

She shook her head. "The chemotherapy plan is already set. The best medications are being used. We’ll have to see the results after treatment."

The topic was thus shifted.

After dinner, Fu Yun insisted Shuangxu stay at home, not giving her a chance to refuse, and directly pulled her upstairs.

"Your room was just cleaned today. All your old things are still here, just as they were. Look—" Fu Yun proudly pointed at the brand-new pink floral bedsheet. "I bought this specially for you. Do you like it?"

Shuangxu said again, "Thank you, Auntie."

"Always saying thank you. No need to be polite with me."

Fu Yun paused for a moment, holding her hand. "It’s good that you’re back. You were all alone in such a distant place, unfamiliar with everything. If something happened, there’d be no one to help you. I couldn’t rest easy. Last time your brother went to see you, he said you were feverish and delirious, lying alone at home without even water to drink. It broke my heart—I tossed and turned all night."

As she said this, her eyes reddened. Shuangxu hurried to comfort her. "I’m fine. I’m all grown up now—I can take care of myself."

"You’re still just a little girl, no matter how old you are." Fu Yun caressed her cheek. "You’ve never been able to sleep on planes. You must be exhausted. Go take a hot shower and get some rest."

After Fu Yun went downstairs, Shuangxu slowly walked around her room, her fingertips brushing the desk and the bookshelf against the wall.

This was the room she had lived in for ten years. Even the dust in the air carried a familiar scent.

After showering, Shuangxu wanted to go downstairs to tell Aunt Wang, to make some soup for Shu Yang. She stopped at the staircase landing.

Through the railing’s gap, she could see the living room. Shen Yu was sitting with his back to her, facing Shen Changyuan and Fu Yun.

"Ah Yu, tell me honestly—did you really not know about Shuangxu’s return in advance?" Fu Yun asked. "Did you agree to it?"

Shen Yu crossed his legs, his voice indifferent. "If she wanted to come back, she would. She doesn’t need anyone’s permission."

"Then tell me, now that she’s back, what are you thinking?"

Shen Yu said, "You and the Song family sent her away together. You didn’t ask for my opinion back then."

"It was for your own good." Fu Yun said. "Back then, those rumors were about to drown our family. If it weren’t for her..."

Shuangxu leaned against the wall, feeling the cold seep into her back.

Shen Yu interrupted her, his tone calm. "Children gossip and spread rumors. Others took them seriously, and so did you."

Fu Yun fell silent.

Shen Changyuan patted her hand. "Let’s not bring up the past. She hasn’t wanted to come back these past few years because she thought we didn’t want her to, and it hurt her. Since the child wants to come back, let’s not send her away again."

"No matter what, this will always be her home." Fu Yun’s affection for her was genuine.

"But Ah Yu, Shuangxu isn’t a child anymore. Even real siblings need to avoid suspicion—let alone you two."

Shuangxu didn’t listen any further. She turned and went back to her room.

chapters.title: He Tingzhou
chapters.content:
Perhaps it was jet lag, but Shuangxu lay on her familiar and comfortable bed, wide awake.

Since she couldn't sleep, she decided to dig out her old game console and cartridges. After a few rounds, her hands remembered the old game all too well.

Afraid of disturbing Shen Yu, she didn't turn on the sound.

It wasn't until she heard the sound of a car downstairs and saw the light seeping through the gap in the curtains that she realized dawn had broken.

She walked to the window and pulled the curtain aside, watching Shen Yu's car drive out of the courtyard.

After turning off the game and preparing to go back to sleep, she had just closed her eyes when her phone chimed with a WeChat message.

Brother: [Come downstairs for some breakfast before going back to sleep]

When Shuangxu went downstairs, Fu Yun and Shen Changyuan were talking in the living room. They stopped as soon as they saw her.

"Why don't you sleep a little longer?" Fu Yun said. "You woke up just in time. Look how much your adoptive father dotes on you. Early in the morning, he sent someone to queue up at Xu Ji to buy breakfast—shrimp dumplings, custard buns, and hand-shredded chicken, all your favorites."

Shuangxu glanced at Shen Changyuan, who was drinking tea across from her.

He wouldn't do such a thing. Shen Yu would.

But Shuangxu pretended not to know and smiled. "Thank you, adoptive father."

After finishing breakfast, she didn't return to her room to sleep. Instead, she used the excuse of visiting Shu Yang at the hospital and left.

When she arrived at the hospital, Shu Yang was on the phone.

No one knew what the person on the other end said, but her face was livid. After hanging up, she raised her hand as if to throw her phone away.

Shuangxu reminded her, "That's 10,000 yuan."

Shu Yang gritted her teeth and took it back.

"What happened to make you so angry?"

Shu Yang was usually carefree, so whatever had angered her this much must be serious.

Shuangxu set up the small dining table. She had brought a nutritious meal and a vegetable and fruit juice rich in vitamins.

It contained Shu Yang's most hated carrots, but she was too furious to notice the taste and chugged down most of the glass.

"Chen Peiran, that damn bastard, took our technical data and ran to Chénxīng, which has been suppressing Feixue all along. Now he's even connected with Yun Dun Group."

"Yun Dun has been paying close attention to our liquid hydrogen drone research since before the New Year. The cooperation was almost certain, but he pulled this stunt. No wonder I couldn't get in touch with Yun Dun these past few days."

Shuangxu had met Chen Peiran before. He was a handsome and refined man, which was probably why he had won Shu Yang over.

She hadn't expected him to be such a disloyal, opportunistic scoundrel.

She frowned and tried to soothe Shu Yang. "Don't panic. The cooperation isn't something he can just snatch away. Contact Yun Dun again and talk it over."

Shu Yang threw off her blanket. "No, I have to go to Yun Dun myself."

Shuangxu quickly pushed her back down.

"You're in this condition. Where do you think you're going? You have chemotherapy tomorrow. Don't run around."

"But you don't understand, if Yun Dun's contract is taken by Chénxīng, Feixue will really have a hard time recovering!"

Shu Yang didn't regret losing her fertility, but having her research results stolen was like having her own child taken away!

The liquid hydrogen drone was Feixue's core project, which they had poured almost all their resources into over the past two years. It was like their lifeline.

"Several of the company's veterans have been taken away by Chen Peiran. Now there's no one to take their place. Our top technical expert, the town's treasure, is socially anxious. Only I can handle this."

And she was seriously ill.

No wonder Chen Peiran was despicable. He was taking advantage of others' misfortunes.

Shuangxu sighed. "Stay in the hospital and rest. I'll go in your place."

Shu Yang temporarily arranged an assistant for Shuangxu, a young girl named Liao. She carried a stack of project documents to the office desk.

"The documents aren't complete. Some were taken by Director Chen. Let me know if anything is missing, and I'll find it for you."

Shuangxu had the same professional background as Shu Yang, so she didn't take long to get up to speed. After quickly familiarizing herself with Shu Yang's project progress, she took Liao with her to Yun Dun.

On the way, she crammed last-minute information, searching for Yun Dun Group on her phone.

The available information was limited. Apart from the cold and solemn official website of the group, there were only a few scattered mentions in some finance or military channels.

Liao chattered beside her:

"Yun Dun has many confidential military projects. I heard that if you sneak in at night and climb over the wall, you'll be arrested and sentenced if caught."

"They also have a huge aircraft production base in the western suburbs. A whole tarmac is filled with fighter jets. It's super impressive!"

"There's nothing online about their President He. It seems like he has a military background. In any case, he's very mysterious."

Military background? Surname He?

Before she could finish, the car had already arrived.

Yun Dun Group's headquarters was towering and solemn. The guards were stricter than those at the surrounding buildings. The entrance was heavily guarded, with sentries every five or ten steps.

Shuangxu took Liao to the front desk. "Hello, we're from Feixue Innovation Technology. We're here to see President He."

"Do you have an appointment?"

Shuangxu politely replied, "Could you please ask Mr. He if he has time? Fifteen minutes would be enough."

"Sorry, Mr. He's schedule is full today."

"Then tomorrow or the day after?"

"Sorry, you can call the secretary's office to make an appointment."

The female employee in the blue suit spoke softly, her evasive tactics smooth and practiced.

"See? President He won't see us at all. Director Shu tried to make an appointment with him several times but couldn't. They must have already signed with Chénxīng. You know how shameless Chénxīng is. To win the Yun Dun Group contract, they'd probably pay to take it." Liao's shoulders slumped dejectedly. "Maybe we should just go back..."

Just as she finished speaking, the elevator door opened, and someone walked out.

Speak of the devil—it was Chen Peiran.

"How come you're here?" Chen Peiran was quite surprised to see Shuangxu. Then he noticed Liao and gave a knowing look.

"Did your senior sister call you back from abroad? I must say, you're quite foolish to come all the way back from abroad to join her. She's in trouble herself right now."

Liao looked as if she had stepped on dog excrement, her face filled with frustration. Hearing him mention Shu Yang, she flew into a rage.

"Director Chen, Director Shu is still in the hospital. After all these years, don't you have any conscience left?"

Chen Peiran smirked, placing himself on the moral high ground with ease. "Haven't I been conscience enough to her? I wasted years of my time on her. It's already merciful that I didn't ask her to compensate me for my youth. Without me, with her science student brain, would Feixue be where it is today?"

Men always easily placed themselves on the moral high ground. "Who knows? Maybe her illness is from being cooped up in the lab all day, exposed to those things. If she had listened to me earlier and settled down to have a child, she wouldn't be worried about infertility now."

Liao's face turned red with anger. "That's going too far!"

To be honest, Shuangxu really wanted to smash her computer bag into Chen Peiran's self-righteous face.

But she remembered the purpose of her visit. Arguing with him was a waste of time.

She grabbed Liao's wrist and pulled her back. "There's no point in talking about conscience with someone who has none."

Chen Peiran had returned to China with Shu Yang to start a business. In just three years, they had established themselves. He considered himself a young talent and social elite, and didn't take these two young girls seriously at all.

"You're not here to discuss the liquid hydrogen drone business, are you?" Chen Peiran's tone was contemptuous, and he proudly waved the A4 document in his hand. "I'll tell you the truth. I've already secured the contract with Yun Dun. Don't waste your effort."

Shuangxu reached out. "Let me see."

"How can I show you something so important?" Chen Peiran stuffed the document into his briefcase.

Shuangxu had a rough idea of what was going on.

She turned to the receptionist. "Could you please tell Mr. He that Song Shuangxu is here to see him."

Liao was a bit confused and whispered, "Do you know President He?"

Good news: Yes.

Bad news: Not well.

But in front of Chen Peiran, Shuangxu didn't show any weakness.

No matter how little she knew him, it was better than being a complete stranger, right?

With that thought, she mysteriously said, "I've known him for many years."

Chen Peiran's smirk was full of contempt. "Who in Yancheng doesn't know He Tingzhou? But one-sided recognition doesn't count as 'knowing.' Have you been abroad for so long that you've forgotten the rules of Yancheng? Do you know who He Tingzhou is?"

"Do you know who his father is?"

Even in Yancheng, where the elite gathered, the He family was at the very top of the pyramid, untouchable.

Shuangxu wasn't intimidated at all. She retorted, "Do you know who I am?"

Chen Peiran scoffed, thinking this little girl, who hadn't even grown up, was trying to act tough.

"You could be anyone, but President He isn't someone just anyone can meet. Your senior sister couldn't even get an appointment with him. What makes you think you can?"

As soon as he finished speaking, the female employee who had been seeking instructions upstairs handed the receiver to Shuangxu with both hands, her tone respectful.

"Mr. He asks you to take the call."

Chen Peiran's expression changed, his features threatening to split apart in all directions.

Shuangxu smiled slightly and took the phone in front of him, calling out, "Brother Tingzhou."

---

chapters.title: Dear Little Sister
chapters.content:
The people at the front desk all fell silent at the same time. Chen Peiran stood to the side, staring at her intently.

The landline clearly transmitted the man's voice. The faint electric current made it sound magnetic, with a hint of flirtation that Shuangxu wasn't sure she was imagining.

"Which dear little sister is this?"

...

What the hell? If it weren't for the fact that this was Yun Dun's company line, Shuangxu would have suspected it was a wrong number.

She discreetly covered the receiver and turned her back.

Liao immediately "understood" and dragged Chen Peiran away, loudly saying, "Director Chen, eavesdropping on others' conversations is so rude!"

People around them looked over. Chen Peiran's expression was a bit awkward. He pushed her away. "Why are you shouting?"

Shuangxu spoke into the receiver. "I'm Song Shuangxu."

The voice on the other end: "Song what?"

Shuangxu's hope that "maybe he would help as a favor to an acquaintance" vanished.

She hadn't expected He Tingzhou to not even remember her name. She had no choice but to bring up Shen Yu.

"Shuangxu." She enunciated clearly. "Shen Yu's sister."

"Looking for your brother?" The man's tone was still casual, with no hint of warmth. "He's not here."

Shuangxu: "I'm looking for... you."

There was a three-second silence on the other end of the phone.

He Tingzhou's tone was light and lazy. "Wait."

Five minutes later, He Tingzhou's chief assistant personally came down to greet them. With great politeness, he ushered Shuangxu into the elevator. "Miss Song, this way, please."

Chen Peiran's expression was too ugly to describe.

Liao hadn't expected her to actually succeed. Hope burned brightly within her despair. "You really know President He? Then we've won this time for sure!"

"Not so fast." Shuangxu covered her mouth and whispered, "He and I... aren't that familiar."

President He only wanted to see Shuangxu alone. Liao had to stay in the lobby, watching enviously as the elevator doors closed.

The shiny metal door frame reflected Chen Peiran's tense and twisted expression, a far cry from his earlier confident arrogance.

She felt an immediate sense of satisfaction.

"Director Chen, your face looks terrible. Anger is anger, but don't get sick from it, hahahaha."

Chen Peiran glared at her, too flustered to retort. He hastily took out his phone, lowered his voice, and made a call. "Find out who Song Shuangxu really is."

He hadn't expected He Tingzhou to actually agree to see her.

Chénxīng had gone to great lengths to connect with Yun Dun Group through a mid-level executive. He had visited Yun Dun so many times, and the person he had been in contact with was a minor head of the technology development department. He hadn't even caught a glimpse of He Tingzhou.

If she really knew He Tingzhou, then the cooperation between Chénxīng and Yun Dun would be doomed, wouldn't it?!

Shuangxu herself wasn't so confident.

He Tingzhou was Shen Yu's friend. Logically speaking, with Shen Yu's connection, this small liquid hydrogen drone contract should be easily secured.

But among Shen Yu's group of friends, Shuangxu had the least contact with—and was most afraid of—He Tingzhou.

Her limited impressions of He Tingzhou could be summed up in one word: bad.

Upon reaching the president's office on the top floor, the chief assistant knocked on the door. A cold, indifferent voice came from inside. "Enter."

Very different from the voice on the phone earlier.

The chief assistant pushed open the door and politely gestured for her to enter.

Shuangxu let out a long breath, the loose strands of hair on her forehead lifting and then falling back down. She steeled herself and stepped inside.

He Tingzhou's office was in a cold, dark gray color scheme. The hard lines and metallic feel announced the owner's aloofness.

She hadn't expected there to be other people inside.

Several men in suits were seated in the reception area. It was no wonder Shuangxu's eyes were first drawn to He Tingzhou—he was far too striking among them.

Unlike Shen Yu's refined handsomeness, He Tingzhou's facial features were sharply defined, with thick eyebrows, deep-set eyes, and a high nose bridge. He was devastatingly handsome in an aggressive way.

He was seated on a black leather sofa with its back to the floor-to-ceiling windows. His shoulders were broad and straight, with hard lines tapering at the waist, leading down to long legs encased in dark trousers.

When the door opened, he lifted his gaze.

His eyes were cold, sharp, and narrow, and with just one glance, Shuangxu felt an overwhelming pressure.

He Tingzhou's gaze slid over her indifferently, as if he hadn't even seen her clearly.

Shuangxu didn't understand why he had let her in if he was in the middle of a meeting.

She discreetly sat down a little distance away and closed her ears to avoid eavesdropping.

After nearly twenty minutes, the conversation on the other side ended. Once those people had left, Shuangxu stood up and walked toward the reception area.

He Tingzhou remained seated, his head lowered as he looked at documents, as if he had forgotten about her presence.

Shuangxu knew that this bit of time was only obtained thanks to Shen Yu's influence. While he was reviewing documents, she began to explain the purpose of her visit.

He Tingzhou didn't even lift his head. The steel pen scraped across the paper with a sandpaper-like sound.

His fingers were long and strong, and the pen strokes were forceful, the sound varying between light and heavy, like a dragon soaring through the clouds.

Shuangxu briefly outlined Feixue's latest progress on the liquid hydrogen drone project. Halfway through, she noticed that He Tingzhou's attention had shifted from the documents to her at some point.

The open blue file folder lay on his lap as he supported his forehead with his fingers, staring at her without blinking.

His eyes were sharply defined, and his pupils were a deep, dark ink.

Shuangxu couldn't tell if he was listening intently or just spacing out.

"The liquid hydrogen drone project is the result of two years of research and development by Feixue. Chénxīng obtained the research results through dishonest means, due to a disagreement between the two founders..."

"Lovers' quarrels are none of my business." He Tingzhou finally spoke.

"I want the technology, not their love child. It doesn't matter if the child takes the father's or mother's surname."

"It does matter."

Shuangxu methodically explained, "Shu Yang is a graduate student in aircraft design and engineering. Chen Peiran studied finance. The technical core of Feixue's R&D department has always been Shu Yang. More important than the technology itself is the talent that controls it."

She paused. "Since President He has been following this project for so long, you should trust Shu Yang's capabilities."

He Tingzhou's eyebrow twitched slightly. "Not calling me Brother Tingzhou anymore?"

Shuangxu thought to herself, You don't even remember me.

"...Brother Tingzhou." She corrected herself.

He Tingzhou stared at her thoughtfully for a few seconds. "Regarding Feixue's matters, why are you the one coming to pull strings?"

Shuangxu wanted to say she wasn't specifically here to pull strings. She had been thrust into this role at the last minute and hadn't even considered this angle.

But if the connections could be used to help Shu Yang, then it would be a good outcome.

"Shu Yang is my senior sister. She's currently in the hospital and can't come herself. I'm here on her behalf."

"You're the first person to use backdoor connections to reach me." He Tingzhou seemed amused. "I could make an exception for you."

"Chénxīng can have the same terms. If they want to sign, they can make an appointment with the secretary themselves."

Shuangxu frowned. "Chénxīng's offer is almost like giving it away for free to connect with Yun Dun Group. Anyway, this project belongs to Feixue. They can take it without spending a penny, with no cost. But it's different for Feixue. Feixue has invested a lot of money and effort into this project."

If they gave it to Yun Dun for free, wouldn't the past two years have been for nothing?

Shuangxu tried to negotiate with him. "Can we discuss the terms again..."

Before she could finish, He Tingzhou's lips curled into a meaningful smile.

His black dress shirt was unbuttoned at the top two buttons. With that smile, he looked less like a group president and more like a dissolute, mischievous young master.

The steel pen spun a few times between He Tingzhou's fingers. His way of speaking was light and lazy, like flirting:

"Little princess, you don't have that much face with me."

chapters.title: The Heartless Girl
chapters.content:
When Shuangxu returned to the main hall, Chen Peiran was still there.

She had been upstairs for nearly forty minutes, and Chen Peiran had waited for forty minutes.

As soon as the elevator arrived, Chen Peiran swiftly turned his head.

Chen Peiran was not a native of Yancheng. He had studied abroad on a government scholarship, and coming from a third-tier city, he had no understanding of the top social circle in Yancheng.

In the few years since he had returned to China, Shuangxu had been away, so he had no idea that his junior, Shu Yang, actually had quite a background.

Not only was she the daughter of Minister Song from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but she was also the adopted sister of the young master of the Shen family.

Xiao Liao rushed forward: "How did it go? How did it go?"

Shuangxu gently shook her head, and Xiao Liao's face fell instantly.

Chen Peiran's anxious heart finally settled. He had thought she was capable, but she was just average.

Adjusting his tie, he walked up to Shuangxu with a swagger, blocking their path.

"I told you there was no chance, but you insisted on humiliating yourself. Do you think He Tingzhou is someone you can just approach? No matter how powerful your father is, he still has to lower his head before the He family."

Shuangxu really disliked men who talked too much.

"Men who talk too much might have kidney problems. Kidney deficiency and insufficient yang energy affect heart and lung function, leading to excessive talking to aid breathing. Have you been to the hospital for a check-up?"

She spoke at her usual unhurried pace, making it sound convincing. Chen Peiran unconsciously touched his kidney area before realizing what she meant, his face turning pale.

"I won't stoop to your level. When you go back, advise your senior to get proper treatment for her illness. Why is she picking a fight with me? Does she think she can win?"

Shuangxu had originally planned to tell Shu Yang the result later, to see if there was another solution.

But she hadn't accounted for Xiao Liao, the loudspeaker.

Xiao Liao imitated Chen Peiran so perfectly that Shu Yang was furious, snapping a pair of chopsticks in half.

"When I get out of the hospital, I'll skin him alive and slice him into sashimi!"

Shu Yang usually believed in parting amicably in breakups, each going their own way. Why must it be so messy and undignified?

Chen Peiran was the first exception.

Xiao Liao was indignant: "Skin him! We must!"

Shu Yang's will to survive was ignited: "Ask the doctor for me, can chemotherapy be done faster? Once a day? I'm in a hurry to get out."

Xiao Liao stood up abruptly: "I'll go right now!"

Shuangxu was speechless: "Sit down. Chemotherapy isn't a spa. Doing it every day would make even Yama bow to you."

Xiao Liao: "Oh." She sat back down.

Shu Yang calmed down, was silent for a few seconds, then suddenly pointed at Xiao Liao and said to Shuangxu: "Do you know why Chen Peiran didn't take her away?"

Shuangxu couldn't hold back her laughter.

Xiao Liao: "Because I'm loyal to you."

Shu Yang said: "You should be loyal to Chen Peiran. Go pester him."

Xiao Liao grumbled, and the two started bickering. Shuangxu checked the time, stood up, and said: "I have to go. It's my brother's birthday today."

"Is it that Shen Yu brother of yours?" Xiao Liao looked envious. "I found his photos. He's so handsome it hurts!"

"Yeah." Shuangxu's eyes curved into a smile. Before leaving, she instructed Xiao Liao: "Take good care of your boss Shu. Just don't let her die."

The birthday party was at Shen Yu's private villa. In the evening, as Shuangxu carried the cake into the car, the Shen family driver smiled and asked: "Is the cake for the young master?"

"Mm."

When she was a child, her interests changed often, but Shen Yu always took her hobbies seriously. Swimming, equestrianism, archery—he had personally taught her all of them.

But baking was something he had never touched. He had specially hired a teacher for her. Shuangxu had only learned the basics before her three-minute passion shifted to swimming.

However, the tradition of making a cake by hand for Shen Yu's birthday—especially for Shen Yu—had always remained.

Shuangxu hadn't returned to Yancheng in five years. Without public appearances, the buried rumors had resurfaced with her return.

In previous years, she had been abroad and hadn't come back for Shen Yu's birthday. But this year, there was no reason to avoid it.

Since returning, she had ignored all the outside chatter. Today, she had made up her mind: no matter what strange looks she received, she would act blind.

The three-story white French-style building was brilliantly lit, illuminating the night sky. The crystal chandeliers radiated splendor, and the sweet aroma of champagne flowed with the moving figures.

At the entrance, a pair of twins were talking, wearing red and blue dresses respectively. When they saw Shuangxu, they looked her up and down.

Shuangxu took off her coat and handed it to the servant. There were many people, but she didn't see Shen Yu.

Near the bar, a few men were holding drinks and chatting. Yue Zifeng was wearing a flashy pink shirt, his elbow resting on the bar. Noticing that everyone's attention was drawn to the entrance, he casually glanced over while sipping his cocktail and froze.

The girls here were all dressed in fine clothes and heavy makeup, each vying for beauty. Shuangxu's makeup was extremely light, yet her beauty was effortless.

She had a standard oval face with delicate features. Though her appearance was naturally striking, her clear and innocent eyes somehow made that beauty seem pure.

Yue Zifeng had always said she had eyes that made people want to protect her.

The crystal chandeliers in the banquet hall seemed to favor her, wrapping her in a silky glow. Her black off-shoulder dress hugged her figure, the hem ending just above her slender ankles. The straps of her high heels were tied around her delicate bones.

Yue Zifeng's eyes lit up: "Yo! Isn't this little Shuangxu?"

He put down his glass and walked over, giving Shuangxu a big hug: "Haven't seen you in years. The little girl has grown so beautiful."

He was Shen Yu's childhood friend and had watched Shuangxu grow up.

Shuangxu felt a sense of warmth seeing him. She carefully held the cake with one hand and let him hug her with a smile: "Brother Zifeng."

"How long has it been since we last saw you? You ran off abroad and stayed for years, didn't even come back after graduating. Don't you miss your brothers at all?"

Shuangxu shook her head without giving face: "No."

"Heartless girl." Yue Zifeng said, "If you don't miss us, you must miss your brother, right?"

Shuangxu just smiled without answering.

A man holding a wine glass came over: "Come on, little sister, let me hug you too."

Yue Zifeng immediately slapped him away: "Scram. What are you? Do you think you're worthy of hugging her? Shen Yu will beat you to death when he comes."

Everyone knew how much Shen Yu doted on this sister. The man didn't get angry: "Just wait. If he's going to beat someone, he'll beat you first."

Shuangxu placed the cake on the table and saw that there were already seven or eight cakes, each more exquisite than the last.

Her blueberry mousse cake seemed too plain in comparison, like a security booth in a high-end villa community.

After placing the cake, she was about to leave when she overheard a hushed conversation.

"Is that her? I can't tell at all..."

"How could you tell? Who would write 'shameless' on their face?"

"She looks quite innocent..."

"You're the innocent one! She's cunning. Knowing that her status as an illegitimate daughter isn't accepted in the Song family, she's been clinging to the Shen family, waiting for an opportunity to latch onto Shen Yu."

Shuangxu pretended not to hear and turned to leave. But the woman in red continued.

"Brother and sister having an affair, how disgusting."

"Ah~ Shen Yu doesn't seem like that kind of person..."

"Do you know what kind of person he is? Otherwise, why would he keep a little girl with no family or connections by his side? Maybe he's into that..."

Shuangxu had spent years learning not to care about others' opinions, but she couldn't tolerate them speaking about Shen Yu with such contempt and vulgarity.

She turned back and walked up to the twins, looking at them quietly: "Into what?"

---

chapters.title: A Slap to Start the Appetite
chapters.content:
The woman in red, who had just been whispering, showed a hint of guilt. What could be more embarrassing than being caught gossiping and questioned on the spot?

Quickly, she changed her expression, putting on a warm, sisterly smile: "Shuangxu, long time no see. We've missed you so much while you were away."

Shuangxu's eyes were gentle and clean, but her gaze toward them was cold: "If you missed me so much, why didn't you message me? Don't you have my number?"

The other woman covered up her embarrassment: "I thought you had changed your number."

"If you had tried, you would know I haven't." Shuangxu's cold eyes fixed on her, not intending to let them off. "You didn't finish your sentence earlier. Why did you stop?"

The woman in red looked flustered: "I was just repeating nonsense I heard from others..."

Before she could finish, Shuangxu stepped forward and slapped her across the face.

Slap—the sound was crisp and loud.

The woman hadn't expected her to hit her. She let out a cry and covered her face, immediately panicking and apologizing: "I'm sorry, I shouldn't have talked. I won't listen to others' nonsense again! Miss Song, please don't be angry..."

Shuangxu turned to the woman in blue, whose face had paled. She stammered nervously: "I didn't say anything. It was all her."

Shuangxu coldly replied: "Even in a comic dialogue, the straight man has to play along. You were eagerly supporting her jokes just now. Now you remember to disassociate?"

She raised her hand again, and both women flinched in unison.

Shuangxu picked up a double-layer cream cake from a nearby table and placed it in front of them.

"Today is my brother's birthday. I don't want to ruin his mood, or it wouldn't just be one slap. If you can't control your mouths, then stuff them."

Her tone was neither light nor heavy, but her manner was cold and overbearing: "You can leave when you finish this cake."

Shuangxu said this and then walked straight past them.

The two women stared at the huge cake in front of them, not daring to breathe.

Shuangxu had only taken a few steps when she suddenly met a gaze.

She looked up and saw someone leaning against the wooden railing of the staircase.

He Tingzhou looked as if he had just woken up. The buttons of his gray silk shirt were loosely fastened, and his well-defined face exuded a sleepy, lazy charm, making his ambiguous, neither good nor evil aura even more pronounced.

His eyes were full of amusement. It seemed he had watched the entire commotion.

Shuangxu paused.

"Truly terrifying." He Tingzhou, ever the troublemaker, remarked, "I won't have my mouth sealed, will I?"

Shuangxu didn't feel she was wrong for hitting them. In fact, she had gone easy on them.

But being seen by others was not good. It made her seem overbearing, as if Shen Yu hadn't raised her properly.

"I was just inviting them to have some cake."

He Tingzhou put his hands in his pants pockets and walked down the stairs with a lazy gait.

"Do you have to start with a slap before eating cake? Is that your family's rule?"

He was really tall. As he passed by her, his shadow fell heavily over her.

Shuangxu thought for a moment and turned to call out to him.

"Brother Tingzhou."

He Tingzhou turned slightly, raising an eyebrow to signal her to speak.

Currently, Feixue was in a dilemma due to pressure from Chenxing.

Collaborating with Yundun meant handing over their hard work for free, leaving nothing behind.

But not collaborating meant handing the opportunity to Chenxing, and their hard work would still go to waste.

Feixue was built from scratch by Shu Yang. Naturally, it couldn't compare to a well-funded, established company like Chenxing Technology. Shu Yang had poured almost all her resources into the development of the liquid hydrogen drone.

Either way, it was a loss. No matter who they gave it to, they faced bankruptcy.

Since she had run into He Tingzhou, she had to try her best.

Shuangxu said: "I know Chenxing's offer is very low, but a low price doesn't mean it's a good deal. Feixue can promise to share future technological development results with Yundun first. In the long run, Yundun's cooperation with Feixue will be more valuable."

"My senior is in a really difficult position right now. This cooperation is very important to her. Can you give her a chance?"

He Tingzhou lowered his head slightly, putting on the gentlemanly demeanor of a tall person towards a shorter one. He asked leisurely: "What if I refuse?"

His eyes were dark, and though he had looked half-asleep moments ago, now he stared straight into Shuangxu's eyes, giving her the feeling of being preyed upon by a hawk.

Shuangxu said: "I..."

He Tingzhou: "What, are you going to invite me to have some cake?"

...

Shuangxu knew she didn't carry much weight with him. Helpless, she had to bring up Shen Yu again.

"You and my brother are friends. Can you help as a favor to him?"

He Tingzhou straightened up, resuming his nonchalant demeanor: "If you want to use your brother's influence, have him come talk to me."

Shuangxu pressed her lips together.

Originally, she had planned to ask Shen Yu for help today, but now she didn't want to bother him over this.

The twins' words still echoed in her ears. She didn't want people to speak about Shen Yu in that despicable manner again.

Of course, she knew that if she asked, Shen Yu would definitely help her.

She also knew that if Shen Yu stepped in, with just a word, the problem that was troubling her and Shu Yang would be solved effortlessly.

When she was a child, she could naturally enjoy his protection. Now that she was grown up, if she couldn't do anything for him, she should at least learn not to rely on him.

In the few seconds of her silence, He Tingzhou had already turned to leave.

He Tingzhou walked straight to the table. Someone came over to greet him, but he ignored them, pulled out a chair, and casually selected a cake from the dazzling array, dragging it in front of himself and picking up a fork.

Shuangxu opened her mouth, but before she could make a sound,

The polished silver fork had already dug into her blueberry mousse cake, lifting a piece into He Tingzhou's leisurely, well-fed mouth.

Shuangxu's mouth could only close again.

She hadn't shown her face in years, and many people took the opportunity to network with her.

Talking behind her back and flattering her to her face was a skill the people in this circle had mastered.

It didn't matter what her relationship with Shen Yu was. As long as there was a relationship, it was enough. At worst, she still had her father.

Shen Yu was at the mahjong table. Catching sight of her, he beckoned, and someone added a chair beside him.

Shuangxu was about to sit down when Yue Zifeng next to her stretched out his hand, pulling the chair towards him: "Shuangxu, come sit with me! Every time you sit with your brother, his luck gets incredibly good. Today, come give me a buff."

Shen Yu said: "He's just bad at the game. Even the God of Wealth couldn't save him."

Shuangxu looked around. Yue Zifeng's twenty-something years of mahjong might as well have been played with his feet. Forget her—even the God of Wealth couldn't save him.

No wonder he always lost money. All that could be said was that he lost it in style.

Shen Yu's phone on the table lit up, a message popping up. Shuangxu glanced at it but didn't look closely before turning away.

Shen Yu ignored it. After a while, a call came in.

Only then did he pick up the phone, and as he stood, his palm rested on Shuangxu's head: "Come take my place."

Shuangxu went over to replace him. She drew a great hand, and just as she was about to flip over the winning tile, she heard the man across from her ask: "Lord Zhou, care to join us?"

Looking up, she saw the well-fed He Tingzhou walking over and sitting in the seat vacated by the other side.

He glanced at the tiles and disdainfully tsked: "What terrible luck."

Shuangxu's upstream player, Zuo Zhong, laughed: "With Shuangxu here, how can anyone else have good luck?"

After saying that, he played a one-bamboo tile. Shuangxu was just about to reach for a tile.

He Tingzhou drew two tiles from his own wall and threw them out: "Pong."

Shuangxu withdrew her hand.

She didn't know if He Tingzhou was doing it on purpose, but it was either his own pong or feeding tiles to Yue Zifeng. Shuangxu didn't get to draw a single tile for three rounds.

By the fourth round, she finally had a chance to draw.

Her luck had arrived, and it was exactly the three-bamboo she needed to win. She was about to take it back.

"Put it down." He Tingzhou's voice was like a basin of cold water poured over her. "Pong."

Shuangxu: "..."

"Are you lacking in virtue?" Yue Zifeng had seen enough. "Wasn't Shuangxu about to win?"

Shuangxu silently chanted "the client is father" in her mind. Shu Yang's father was now her father.

She forced herself to put the tile back: "Not winning."

He Tingzhou's chair was tilted back, the back legs on the ground. He pressed against the chair back, slowly rocking, not even sparing her a glance.

---

chapters.title: I’ll Stop If You Cry
chapters.content:
Shuangxu quite liked playing mahjong. Usually, she played with Shen Yu and the others. The brothers all treated her like a pet, coaxing and indulging her, which naturally made her happy.

But He Tingzhou was not in the "good brother" category.

Not only did he not let her draw tiles, but he also kept setting her up to lose.

The chips on Shen Yu's table were quickly lost by her. Shuangxu's eyebrows knitted together.

She felt that He Tingzhou was deliberately targeting her.

This man was used to bullying the weak, and she was no exception.

Yue Zifeng couldn't bear to watch and begged him, "Can you just let me play? If you make Shuangxu cry, Shen Yu will come back and hold you accountable."

He Tingzhou glanced over from across the table, examining Shuangxu's eyes with interest. "Is she crying? If she cries, I'll stop."

Yue Zifeng said, "You're such a jerk."

Shuangxu had reason to believe that even if she really cried, He Tingzhou wouldn't stop.

The first time she met He Tingzhou, she was only seventeen.

At that time, all she knew about him came from various rumors outside: arrogant and domineering, outrageous in his actions, bullying others with his power, almost killing someone... and so on.

In short, he was not a good person.

Shuangxu remembered her first impression of He Tingzhou: cold, with a hint of danger.

Whenever He Tingzhou came to the Shen family, she would greet him and then stay as far away as possible.

On the rare occasions when Shen Yu had to leave for something, she had to stay and entertain the guest, forced to be alone with He Tingzhou.

At that time, she had just started learning chess and took it out to play with He Tingzhou.

Shen Yu had taught her chess personally, and she thought she had learned it well. Shen Yu always let her win and allowed her to take back moves, but He Tingzhou was different.

He showed no mercy and crushed her completely.

Shuangxu wasn't afraid of losing, but she didn't like being humiliated.

She didn't want to play anymore and tried to put the chessboard away, but He Tingzhou's sharp, narrow eyes lazily glanced over, mocking her: "Running away after losing, aren't you ashamed?"

For a while, she even developed a shadow over chess.

When Shen Yu returned from his call, he took one look at the obvious situation on the table and raised an eyebrow. "How are you bullying my little Jiu?"

Shuangxu immediately gave up her seat to him. She was annoyed by He Tingzhou's targeting, but since she needed his help, she had to endure it and even tried to smooth things over for him.

"I'm not very good at this."

Shen Yu laughed, patting the back of her head twice, just like before, and handed his phone to Shuangxu before returning to the table.

"Watch carefully."

Shen Yu and He Tingzhou were evenly matched, going back and forth, at least regaining some of the ground Shuangxu had lost.

Shuangxu watched from the side.

She used to not study these techniques; her card games relied on luck, as if blessed by the God of Wealth.

Only now did she realize there were many intricacies involved—counting cards, planning ten steps ahead, knowing not only your own hand but also your opponents' like the back of your hand.

When the game was intense, she moved to the opposite side unnoticed by anyone.

She glanced at He Tingzhou's cards but couldn't understand them.

Because this man didn't arrange his cards at all; however they were dealt, that's how they stayed. A Four of Circles and a Nine of Bamboo with a Red Dragon in between, a One of Characters and a Two of Characters separated by an entire Milky Way.

The disarray had a built-in anti-peeping effect.

Shuangxu was trying to figure out in her mind what he was waiting for when He Tingzhou suddenly turned his head. "Figured it out, little spy?"

Everyone at the table, who had been focused on the game, suddenly looked at Shuangxu.

She felt like a thief caught red-handed and publicly executed.

"I didn't..." She wanted to explain that she wasn't peeping, just curious about his playing style.

He Tingzhou rocked his chair, speaking to her in a tone used to dismiss a child: "Waiting for Eight of Characters. Go back and report to your brother."

When gods fight, it's always the mortals who suffer. Yue Zifeng had lost almost all his money and suddenly realized, slapping his thigh: "I was wondering how Shen Yu always wins. Turns out he brings a little cheat!"

Shuangxu had no way to defend herself.

Shen Yu just smiled, tapping his half-smoked cigarette against the crystal ashtray. He didn't refute the accusation of sending a spy and took the blame.

"All's fair in love and war."

With that, he played an Eight of Characters.

He Tingzhou was indeed waiting for an Eight of Characters and, without hesitation, laid down his cards, rocking his chair: "Hu."

Shuangxu really wanted to kick the leg of his chair.

She obediently sat back and didn't go near He Tingzhou again.

At midnight, the cake with candles was placed in front of Shen Yu. Everyone formed a circle, singing "Happy Birthday" as he was surrounded in the center.

Shuangxu was squeezed to the back by someone.

This would never have happened before she turned eighteen. Everyone around Shen Yu knew how much he doted on her.

But sooner or later, she would have to get used to it. She couldn't stand by his side forever, and this was something Shuangxu was slowly learning to accept.

She was following the rhythm, clapping along, when Shen Yu's gaze passed over the others and fell on her.

The orange candlelight cast shifting shadows on his features. He reached out to her: "Jiu, come here."

Everyone in the circle turned to look at her. Those in front quickly made way.

Shuangxu walked over. Shen Yu placed his hand on her left shoulder, bringing her in front of him, directly facing the flickering candles on the cake.

"Make a wish."

She used to do this often. She always had so many wishes she couldn't finish making them. Even on her own birthday wasn't enough; she always made wishes on Shen Yu's birthday too.

And every wish she made, Shen Yu would help her fulfill.

Shuangxu could feel the various gazes on her, each with different meanings.

But the girl who loved making wishes had grown up and knew not all wishes could come true.

"I don't have any wishes right now." Shuangxu said, "Brother, it's your birthday. You should make the wish."

Shen Yu's eyes, deepened by the flickering candlelight, held the same tenderness as always when she looked closely. He touched her hair. "Then save it. Make the wish when you have one."

In the second half of the birthday party, the air was thick with the scent of alcohol.

Shuangxu hadn't rested properly since she came back these past few days. She couldn't hold on and fell asleep on the sofa for a while. When she woke up, she was covered with a blanket.

A servant was standing nearby. Seeing her awake, he said: "Young Master said if you're sleepy, go upstairs to the room and sleep."

Shuangxu followed the sound of laughter and saw that Shen Yu and Yue Zifeng were still drinking with those people.

These young masters were in high spirits, with beautiful and delicate women nestled in their arms.

As the birthday boy, Shen Yu inevitably had to be forced to drink by those people.

He had his long legs crossed, leaning back relaxed on the sofa. Two buttons of his white shirt were undone. His right hand, holding a cigarette, rested on the arm of the sofa. The cigarette burned on its own. She didn't know if he was drunk or just distracted.

The woman sitting next to Shen Yu was particularly striking in her beauty. Shuangxu felt she had seen her before, perhaps some actress, but she couldn't recall who.

Still half-asleep, Shuangxu stared blankly in Shen Yu's direction.

She heard Yue Zifeng, already tipsy, teasing: "She took a late-night flight to come celebrate your birthday. How come you haven't shown any appreciation?"

Shen Yu: "Are you jealous?"

Yue Zifeng: "Am I the kind of person to let you have her if I were jealous?"

"That won't do." The actress smiled sweetly, naturally resting her chin on Shen Yu's shoulder.

This used to be her privilege.

She had been clingy to Shen Yu since she was little. Whenever Shen Yu went out with Yue Zifeng and the others, she insisted on going along, and Shen Yu always took her.

Because she was there, they all behaved themselves. Back then, there were no women around Shen Yu. When she was sleepy, she would lean on him and fall asleep.

Shuangxu's blank stare retracted, lowering her gaze to the ground. Her fingers, resting on the edge of the sofa, were long and pale.

After a moment, she lifted her head again, showing no sign of abnormality, and asked the servant: "Where is Brother Tingzhou?"

"I haven't seen Mr. He. He probably left."

Shuangxu immediately stood up and hurried towards the parking lot.

The servant, holding the blanket, asked behind her: "Are you leaving? Aren't you going to say goodbye to Young Master?"

Shuangxu shook her head: "I won't disturb him."

---

chapters.title: Love Unrequited, Hate Born from Love
chapters.content:
The late spring night wind seeped cold into her skin. Shuangxu shivered, only then realizing she had forgotten her coat when she came out.

The liveliness and warmth of the crowd were left behind in the brightly lit house. The parking lot was desolate under the sparse starlight.

She didn't want to go back in. After searching around, she saw He Tingzhou's all-black Koenigsegg was still there, but he wasn't in the car.

She stood under a tree waiting. The night sky in the late hours seemed even more empty, the dark ink-like color isolating the laughter from the front yard of the villa behind a transparent barrier.

Shuangxu heard footsteps and saw from afar a tall and straight figure, long legs striding through the night, walking leisurely towards her.

He Tingzhou approached his car and pressed the key fob. A figure emerged from under the shadow of the tree.

"Brother Tingzhou."

He Tingzhou took half a step back with a start.

He supported himself against the car, steadying his nerves, which had been startled in the pitch-black night.

A pair of inscrutable sharp eyes stared at the person opposite in the darkness. Small in stature but startling.

"What are you doing, hiding here to rob me?"

I'm 1.66 meters tall, and you're 1.88 meters. Am I crazy to rob you?

Shuangxu had gotten a bit cold waiting. Without beating around the bush, she got straight to the point: "The blueberry mousse you ate earlier was made by me for my brother."

To prevent He Tingzhou from denying it, she had even taken a photo as evidence at the time.

He Tingzhou lowered his eyes to glance at her phone screen. His well-proportioned face showed not a hint of embarrassment.

"So, you poisoned the cake for your brother, and I accidentally ate it?"

Shuangxu took her phone back, speechless. "Why would I poison my brother?"

He Tingzhou leaned casually against the car door. "Love unrequited, hate born from love?"

Shuangxu's fingertips unconsciously tightened around the fabric of her skirt.

The cold wind rushed through her spine, freezing all the blood in her body. She opened her mouth, but the first sound didn't come out.

Who could be as vile as He Tingzhou? Others might gossip behind his back, but he stabbed her in the front.

The wind blew across her face, arms, and calves, cold to the bone. Shuangxu resisted the urge to run away from him immediately, maintaining a calm expression.

"I didn't mean anything else. You ate the cake, but I just hope you can reconsider the collaboration with Feixue."

She didn't dare to ask for too much. It wasn't that she didn't want to, but it was just a cake, not worth that much.

But it was the birthday cake she made for Shen Yu. He Tingzhou had eaten it, so giving a little favor wasn't too much to ask, was it?

He Tingzhou stood still, motionless.

If not for the tree shadow behind him still swaying, it would have been like a movie scene frozen due to poor internet speed.

Shuangxu didn't understand what was wrong with him. Seeing him frozen for three seconds without moving, she was about to speak.

He Tingzhou moved, serious: "I've considered it. No."

...

If silence had a shape, it would be the white-eye Shuangxu barely managed to suppress at this moment.

The blood that had just frozen was now boiling with anger.

"Can you consider it seriously?"

He Tingzhou clearly didn't have the conscience of someone who had eaten her food: "Three seconds aren't serious enough, little princess. You're really troublesome."

He simply didn't want to give her any chance, not even a little.

Shuangxu felt a bit depressed. He had eaten the cake she made for Shen Yu, and she couldn't exactly make him spit it out.

She was afraid He Tingzhou would actually spit it out in front of her. How disgusting.

"Forget it." She shouldn't have had any illusions about him.

"Forget it just like that?" He Tingzhou said.

Shuangxu didn't understand what he meant.

He put his hands in his pockets, lazily leaning against the car door: "My stomach is a bit delicate. I don't feel well after eating your cake. I need to go for a check-up tomorrow. If my stomach is damaged, remember to take responsibility."

"...What?" Shuangxu's mind couldn't keep up with his unconventional train of thought.

She quickly recalled the ingredients she used for the cake. They were all newly bought today and shouldn't have any problems...

"For your brother's sake, I won't hold you accountable." He Tingzhou was magnanimous. "Remember to tell your brother he owes me a favor."

Not far away, a couple laughed and quarreled as they came out of the villa and got into a car. Soon, the car drove out of the parking lot.

A gust of wind passed, lifting the hem of Shuangxu's skirt.

She hadn't succeeded in her request.

She had been taken advantage of instead.

Originally, she didn't want Shen Yu to owe him a favor, but after all this, not only had she failed to achieve her goal, but she had also lost the cake and ended up owing him a favor.

Shuangxu knew she had been played. She felt wronged and had nowhere to appeal, so she had to swallow it.

She was in a really bad mood today. Her heart felt like a sponge soaked in some liquid, blocking it, along with some accumulated emotions, all rushing towards her tear ducts at the same time.

Shu Yang's weakening body, Chen Peiran's swaggering, the unwelcoming home, and the actress in Shen Yu's arms...

Shuangxu only felt a warmth in her eyes as her vision was quickly blurred by the rising moisture.

She lowered her eyes. "If you don't want to help, forget it. Sorry for wasting your time."

After saying that, she turned and walked away quickly.

At the moment she turned, He Tingzhou saw a glint of moisture flash in her eyes.

She was quite thin but not bony, the kind of tender and delicate thinness. The black dress fitted her curves perfectly, and from behind, she looked slender.

The night wind was strong, and she walked hurriedly, as if she might be blown away.

He Tingzhou leaned against the car, reflecting on himself for a few seconds, wondering if he had bullied her too much.

"Mr. He is actually this kind of person?" Shu Yang was very shocked.

She had met He Tingzhou once at a drone industry expo.

That day's exchange conference gathered experts, scholars, industry elites, and outstanding entrepreneurs from around the world. Shu Yang had managed to get a spot and was discussing the development of liquid hydrogen drones with a potential investor when He Tingzhou happened to overhear. That was how Feixue had caught the attention of Yundun Group.

However, the person who had given her the business card that day and contacted her afterward was a mid-level manager from Yundun responsible for the drone sector.

She only remembered that from afar that day, He Tingzhou was surrounded by conference chairs and academicians—industry heavyweights.

He wore a high-end custom suit, tall and straight, standing out like a crane among chickens. Facing a circle of people flattering him, his face showed not a hint of expression.

How high and mighty he was.

Although Shuangxu had told Shen Yu not to help, he still arranged for the hospital to give Shu Yang a VIP ward.

The side effects of Shu Yang's chemotherapy were severe. The doctor had given her anti-nausea medication to relieve it somewhat. Her face was pale, and she was extremely exhausted.

Shu Yang's impression of him was that he was devastatingly handsome and untouchable. She never expected his personality in private to be so... despicable.

"Not helping is fine, but he's at least your brother's friend. How can he bully you like this?"

"I shouldn't have had any illusions in the first place. Just because he's my brother's friend doesn't mean he has to give me face."

Shuangxu now saw the reality and her own naivety clearly, her brows furrowed with worry. "Maybe I still have to ask my brother."

"Don't. Don't trouble your brother." Shu Yang said, "He Tingzhou is too difficult to deal with. If he wanted to give your brother face, he would have done it long ago without you having to beg him. In the adult world, since he hasn't agreed, his meaning is already clear. Why must we force this issue?"

chapters.title: If I Don’t Get It, I’ll Cry
chapters.content:
Shuangxu was surprised: "So you're just going to hand over his project to Chenxing?"

"If they want it so badly, let them have it."

"I thought you wouldn't be able to swallow this."

"Of course I feel bad—it's my own child. But others can waste my hard work; I can't waste it myself. Chenxing wants a price war, and we definitely can't win against them. It makes sense for Yundun to choose them. Given the same product, I'd pick the cheaper one too."

Over the past few days, Shu Yang had come to terms with it and convinced herself: "It's fine. If others play dirty and I lose, it just means I misjudged them. But the shame isn't on me—I have a clear conscience."

"That money you gave me already solved Feixue's financial problems. Everyone's overdue salaries and bonuses have been paid. Worst case, we start over. Once I recover from my illness, I will get my revenge!"

Suddenly, Shuangxu said, "Do you still remember when we first met?"

Of course Shu Yang did: "Back then, you were so cold. You had acute gastroenteritis, and I kindly took you to the hospital, running around for you. In the end, you just handed me a roll of dollars and dismissed me."

"Not dismissed—thanked," Shuangxu corrected. "I had just been betrayed by my best friend back then. I didn’t want to make new friends."

"No wonder you never contacted me again after leaving the hospital," Shu Yang said. "Speaking of which, I should thank my mixed-race ex-boyfriend."

At the time, that ex of hers lived in the same building as Shuangxu. One night, he sent her a harassing text message.

Whether or not to tell the person involved was a dilemma.

After thinking it over, Shuangxu took the risk of possibly offending both parties and forwarded the message directly to Shu Yang.

"That day, when you stormed into my place, I thought you were going to hit me," Shuangxu said. "I didn’t expect you to drag me to his place and slap him twice—once for yourself, once for me—then dump him with such flair."

"At that moment, I thought, This woman is so carefree. I really like her personality," Shuangxu turned to look at Shu Yang, her smiling eyes serious. "I’m glad that after all these years, you’re still the same Shu Yang who can let go so easily."

Shu Yang spread her arms and hugged her: "Then take a lesson from your senior here. The most important thing in life is to let things go. Men? They’re everywhere."

Shuangxu froze, her expression in that instant like a secret she had tried hard to hide had been exposed. "How did you know..."

"Just a guess." Shu Yang smiled weakly but slyly. "Shuangxu, your eyes are so beautiful. It’s a shame they only see your brother."

That night, when Shuangxu returned to the Shen family home, it was nearly 10 PM.

As she got out of the car, her phone buzzed in her pocket. It was a call from the Song family.

Her return to China couldn’t be hidden from the Song family. After her public appearance at Shen Yu’s birthday party a few days ago, the rumors about her return to Yancheng had become undeniable fact.

She had come back without permission, and Cui Ning would inevitably seek her out. Shuangxu wasn’t surprised at all.

Although Shuangxu bore the surname Song, her position as the Song family’s eldest daughter had always been unstable. She was Song Mianzhi’s daughter, but Cui Ning, Song’s wife, was not her mother.

She had grown up in the Shen family and had never been close to the Song family—her relationship with them could even be described as distant.

Five years ago, when they had forcibly sent her abroad, the already thin familial affection had grown even thinner.

Shuangxu stood under a tree outside the door, listening to the refined and noble voice on the other end of the phone: "When did you come back?"

"Last Tuesday."

"If it weren’t for someone mentioning it today, I wouldn’t even have known you were back in the country," Cui Ning said. "You’ve been back for so many days and haven’t even thought to visit home."

Her words carried reproach for her disrespect, but Shuangxu knew better than anyone that if she really went back, she would only be met with disdain.

What Cui Ning was truly upset about was that she had returned to the country without their permission.

"I’ve been busy lately. I’ll go when things settle down," Shuangxu said.

"Come back this weekend."

Cui Ning gave the order directly, leaving no room for refusal, then hung up coldly.

Shuangxu pulled the phone away from her ear. Since Cui Ning could no longer hear her, she muttered, "Whoever wants to go can go."

Just as she was about to step inside, a sudden honk startled her. Only then did she notice the Koenigsegg—shaped like a giant cockroach—parked not far away on the side of the road.

The window rolled down, revealing He Tingzhou sitting inside, watching her.

Shuangxu didn’t want to acknowledge him, but she couldn’t be impolite.

So, in the first second she saw him, she swiftly averted her gaze, pretending she hadn’t seen him and continued walking forward.

As if she were a blind woman with her eyes wide open.

Just as she took a step, the man’s deep, indifferent voice reached her: "Don’t pretend."

Shuangxu took a deep breath with her back to him, then turned around politely: "Brother Tingzhou, what a coincidence."

He Tingzhou: "Not a coincidence. I was looking for you. Come here."

Shuangxu took two small, reluctant steps toward him, stopping two meters away from the car. "Do you need something?"

You again.

He Tingzhou looked at her with mild disdain, as if getting any closer to him would suffocate her.

"I don’t like looking up at people. Get in the car."

So difficult to please.

Shuangxu no longer needed his cooperation and was avoiding him as much as possible. "I just came back from the hospital. I might be carrying all sorts of germs. I wouldn’t want to infect you."

He Tingzhou’s thin lips curled slightly in mockery. "Get in and try. See if you can take me down."

...

Shuangxu bit the inside of her lip, but in the end, she took a step forward and walked around to the passenger side, getting into the car.

The matte black high-end leather and carbon fiber interior was as cold and ruthless as He Tingzhou himself.

The moment Shuangxu sat down, she was enveloped by a cool, deep scent.

A chilly, pine-like fragrance with a hint of vitality—and a touch of... sweetness.

He Tingzhou had a piece of candy in his mouth, biting down on it as he glanced at her indifferently.

"Which university did you attend?"

"Stanford." Shuangxu didn’t know why he was asking.

He Tingzhou: "Is Stanford’s motto ‘Serve your senior sister with your life’?"

Shuangxu choked. "Can’t I do it for myself? I now own half of Feixue."

"Half the shares to buy the Shen family’s little sister? Director Shu is quite the businesswoman."

Shuangxu disliked his tone. "My senior sister has been very good to me. Whether or not she’s taken advantage of me, I know myself."

A light scoff escaped He Tingzhou’s throat, thick with sarcasm. "Little princess, there are plenty of people who’ve been good to you."

Were there really that many? Shuangxu didn’t think so.

"I had a deep psychological shadow from being abandoned by my birth mother as a child. So when I was sent abroad, I was in a really bad state. My senior sister was the only one who cared about me."

"The food abroad really isn’t good. It’s hard to find authentic Chinese restaurants. I’d never even touched a stove before—I couldn’t even tell how cooked noodles were."

"Senior sister often came to keep me company and cooked Chinese food for me. For Chinese New Year, she ran half the city just to gather ingredients to make dumplings for me."

Shuangxu said, "If we’re being technical, she never saved my life, and we haven’t known each other for that long. But she was the one who stayed with me through the hardest times. Now that she’s in trouble, shouldn’t I help her?"

He Tingzhou clearly didn’t understand this kind of bond or emotion.

"Do you think your brother knows that a plate of dumplings can swindle you out of twenty million?"

Shuangxu knew he wouldn’t get it.

How could someone like him—born into eminence, towering above the masses—understand the feeling of being abandoned?

"In my heart, there are things more valuable than twenty million. I don’t feel like I’ve lost anything." Shuangxu didn’t want to say more. "Are you done mocking me? Can I leave now?"

He Tingzhou dropped a document onto her lap.
