It was a contract for the liquid hydrogen drone, with the same terms as the one initially offered to Shu Yang.

The frown between Shuangxu’s brows turned into suspicion.

"Aren’t you refusing? Chenxing is practically begging to give it to you for free. Why choose us?"

Crunch. He Tingzhou bit down on the candy, chewing slowly. "If I don’t give it to you, you’ll cry. The little princess has such a temper—if you go tattle to your brother, I’m afraid your whole family will come after me with a cake."

"I didn’t cry..." Shuangxu wanted to deny it, but then she thought—if admitting it would help Feixue secure the deal, why not?

She understood why He Tingzhou had changed his mind.

Offending her was one thing, but he and Shen Yu were close brothers. Shen Yu doted on her, and for such a trivial matter, it wasn’t worth straining their relationship over. To a conglomerate like Yundun, this small project was like a single hair on a lion’s body. Better to give her face.

Realizing this, Shuangxu took the contract and got out of the car. Before closing the door, she leaned down and said to him, "Thank you, Brother Tingzhou."

---

chapters.title: She Slapped Her Face Until It Swelled
chapters.content:
In the morning, as she went downstairs, Shen Yu was sitting in the dining room, drinking coffee and checking work emails.

Shuangxu didn’t know he had come back last night. She sat across from him and quietly ate breakfast.

This kind of silence was rare between them. Normally, she was a chatterbox around Shen Yu, sharing every little thing with him.

This time, Shen Yu was the first to speak: "Mom said you’ve been going to the hospital every day to take care of your senior sister."

"Mhm. Her mother hasn’t been well these past few years, and she’s afraid of worrying her family, so she hasn’t told them about her illness yet."

"Taking care of a patient is a nurse’s job. Don’t exhaust yourself."

Although Shen Yu didn’t interfere with her friendships, he wasn’t exactly pleased that the little sister he had doted on was running around taking care of someone else.

"I know." Shuangxu responded.

"The treatment plan was consulted on by the top hematology experts in the country. There won’t be any problems. Don’t worry."

He was concerned about Shu Yang’s illness for her sake. Shuangxu stirred the congee in her bowl and hummed in response.

Sensing her low mood, Shen Yu glanced at her. "Upset?"

"No." Shuangxu changed the subject. "Brother, do you know any lawyer friends?"

"Already in trouble so soon after coming back?" Shen Yu pinched his coffee cup with his long fingers, his voice tinged with amusement. "Come on, what kind of trouble have you gotten me into?"

The faint morning light shimmered in his eyes. Shuangxu averted her gaze. "Not me. My senior sister has some financial disputes with her business partner. The lawyer I found isn’t very competent."

"It’s nothing major." Shen Yu said, "I’ll arrange someone for you."

"Thank you, Brother."

The lawyer Shen Yu arranged contacted Shuangxu that same afternoon. He was an experienced senior lawyer specializing in economic cases—using a sledgehammer to crack a nut for such a minor dispute.

That weekend, Shuangxu was busy meeting with the lawyer, so naturally, she didn’t return to the Song family. Cui Ning’s order was treated as nothing more than background noise.

When she returned to the Shen household that evening, Fu Yun hadn’t gone to bed yet. She was sitting in the living room waiting for her.

Upon seeing Shuangxu, Fu Yun had the housekeeper, Wang Sao, bring over a cup of warm milk. "What have you been busy with these past few days? You’ve been coming back so late every night."

"Helping my senior sister with her company’s matters." Shuangxu didn’t actually like milk, but she still took it obediently.

"You haven’t been back home since you returned, have you?" Fu Yun said. "Find some time to go visit. You should still go back when you can."

Probably Cui Ning had already contacted her.

The Shen and Song families were close, and many times, Fu Yun had to consider Cui Ning’s face to maintain harmony.

"I’ve been too busy." Shuangxu downed the milk in one go, let out a yawn, and said, "I’m so tired, Auntie. I’m going to bed."

With that, she quickly went upstairs to her room. Fu Yun watched her retreating figure, utterly exasperated. "She runs away every time this comes up."

"Miss Shuangxu isn’t close to them at all. The Song family never even raised her for a single day. Back then, when Director Song’s slap was so forceful it left her face swollen, and then Mrs. Song sent her away without a word for all these years—now that she’s just returned to the country, she’s already in a hurry. Does she expect Miss Shuangxu to never come back at all?"

Wang Sao was completely on the side of the young lady she had raised. "If it were me, I wouldn’t want to go back and get scolded either."

"Don’t add fuel to the fire," Fu Yun said. "After all, they are her family. In the future, Shuangxu’s marriage will still have to be arranged by the Song family. If we upset Cui Ning, what good will come of it for her?"

Wang Sao sighed. "With Mrs. Song the way she is, what kind of good marriage can she arrange for Miss Shuangxu?"

Fu Yun gave Cui Ning a call about this.

"They didn’t mean to avoid coming back—she’s probably just been too busy and forgot. Her senior sister is seriously ill, and the company is apparently having some trouble. That senior sister took very good care of her when she was abroad. They have a very deep bond. These days, she’s been running around for her senior sister’s sake. I haven’t even been able to see her."

These noble-sounding reasons didn’t convince Cui Ning. She coldly replied, "You haven’t been able to see her, but I hear your Shen Yu has."

Fu Yun’s tone turned unpleasant. "What do you mean by that? Yu has always treated Shuangxu like a sister. It’s perfectly normal for them to see each other occasionally."

Cui Ning didn’t say much more. She simply sent Fu Yun a video.

It was from Shen Yu’s birthday party. The atmosphere was lively, and Shuangxu was standing at the table with Shen Yu, who was cutting the cake. From the angle, it looked as if he had her half-encircled in his arms.

The video was only a little over ten seconds long. By the time the noisy sounds ended, Fu Yun’s expression had already changed.

Cui Ning’s tone remained composed. "Have you forgotten why we sent her away in the first place? If the Shen family thinks the scandal from five years ago wasn’t embarrassing enough, then I’m not afraid to sacrifice the Song family’s reputation to make sure you all lose face together."

Shuangxu wasn’t actually tired at all. Back in her room, she flopped onto the bed, feeling utterly dejected.

She disliked the Song family—not just because she had no affection for them, but also because of what had happened five years ago.

Shuangxu’s background wasn’t a secret in their circles. Everyone knew that the Song family’s eldest daughter was not Cui Ning’s biological child.

Her biological mother had been a direct subordinate of Song Mianzhi. At the time, Song Mianzhi had just started working in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It was no surprise that her young, elegant superior had captured her mother’s heart.

The two had slowly developed feelings while working together. Back then, Song Mianzhi had still been single. Unfortunately, their social statuses were too unequal. Shuangxu’s maternal grandfather had been a vice-ministerial level official, while Song Mianzhi’s career had only just begun. A lowly translator’s background clearly wasn’t a match for his ambitions.

Grandfather Song had forcefully broken them up, but Shuangxu believed that wasn’t the only reason.

Song Mianzhi loved his career and himself the most.

Her mother had been stubborn, with a strong sense of pride. Forced to resign, and later discovering she was pregnant, she never told Song Mianzhi. She had raised the child alone. For the first eight years of her life, Shuangxu had lived with her birth mother.

Then, her mother abandoned her.

She had deep psychological trauma from being abandoned, so when the Song family had tried to send her abroad five years ago, she had begged them not to. She had wanted to call Shen Yu, but her phone had been taken away. They had locked her in a room for several days before putting her on a plane.

Every time she recalled how she had felt back then, she felt suffocated.

The next morning, Shuangxu went downstairs and found Fu Yun busy cooking something in the kitchen.

It was ginger soup made with charred red dates and snow pears, sweetened with rock sugar.

She hated the taste of ginger and despised drinking ginger soup, so whenever she caught a cold as a child, Fu Yun would make this sweet ginger soup for her.

She hadn’t had it in years, but smelling the familiar scent now made her feel a pang of nostalgia.

The pears had been cooked until they were semi-transparent. Shuangxu leaned in and used a fork to sneak a piece.

"Is someone in the family sick?"

The Shen household had three cooks alone, and Fu Yun rarely cooked herself. The only people she would personally make ginger soup for were few and far between.

She was perfectly healthy, and Shen Changyuan had been away on a business trip these past few days. That left only...

"Your brother has a fever."

Fu Yun ladled the hot soup into a thermos. "The temperature’s been fluctuating these past few days, and he never takes care of himself. When you go out later, take this to him on your way."

Shuangxu didn’t dare delay. She swallowed the piece of pear in her mouth—tinged with ginger—and grabbed the thermos before rushing to Shen Yu’s place.

chapters.title: Deliberately Letting Her See
chapters.content:
After Shuangxu turned seventeen, Shen Yu moved out of the Shen family home to live alone.

After he moved out, his visits home became fewer and fewer, and the frequency at which Shuangxu saw him went from daily to once a week.

Fu Yun said he was busy with work, but she was still unhappy, resting her chin on her desk during class with a listless expression.

Her best friend swore up and down, "Your brother is already twenty-five! He must have a girlfriend. Living at home is inconvenient, so he moved out to bring women back overnight."

Shuangxu said she was talking nonsense: "My brother doesn't have a girlfriend."

After all, every time she went to Shen Yu’s place, she never saw any woman there.

At the time, she didn’t believe it—until later, on Shen Yu’s birthday, she hid in his apartment to surprise him and personally witnessed him kissing a woman.

At that moment, it was no exaggeration to say her world collapsed.

She knew Shen Yu’s door lock password—he always used the same one. In the past, she had gone there every weekend, but after that, she never went again.

The car drove to the apartment building, and Shuangxu carried the thermos upstairs.

She didn’t know if Shen Yu had seen a doctor, nor did she know if he had medicine at home. She had just passed a pharmacy and bought some on a whim.

After ringing the doorbell and waiting a while, the door opened. First, she saw a head of chestnut curls, followed by the woman’s exquisite, beautiful face.

Shuangxu was completely caught off guard and froze.

It was the female celebrity from that night. Even without makeup, she was stunningly beautiful, unforgettable at a glance. She wore only a man’s dress shirt, the oversized hem covering her hips, her legs bare, not even wearing slippers.

The celebrity held the door with one hand, her slightly hostile gaze sweeping up and down Shuangxu, as if sizing her up as some kind of rival.

"You looking for Shen Yu? He’s still asleep."

Shuangxu, after a moment of stiffness, found her voice: "I brought my brother some ginger soup."

"You’re his sister?"

Everyone around Shen Yu knew he had a beloved little sister.

The celebrity’s attitude immediately did a 180-degree turn. A flicker of shame crossed her face. She smoothed her deliberately tousled hair, pulled up the open collar of the shirt, and spoke softly, even with a hint of ingratiation: "Wait a moment, I’ll go get him."

Shuangxu stood at the door without moving: "No need. You can take it in."

She handed over the thermos and medicine, shoved her hands into her coat pockets, turned, and left.

"Hey..." The celebrity watched her retreating back, realizing she had made a huge mistake this time. She had offended Shen Yu’s family on their first meeting.

Just as she was feeling regretful, Shen Yu came out of the bedroom, his voice still hoarse from the fever: "Who’s here?"

"Your sister came to bring you ginger soup, but she didn’t come in and left."

Shen Yu’s gaze slid over the thermos and medicine bag in her hands, pausing slightly. Whether it was her imagination or not, the weariness in his brows and eyes seemed to slowly cool.

She was at a loss, and before she could react, Shen Yu had already passed her, grabbed his coat, opened the door, and went out.

The elevator was a bit slow—or maybe it wasn’t, but every second felt unbearably long to Shuangxu.

When the doors finally opened, she stepped in and turned around, only to see Shen Yu’s figure walking out.

She lowered her gaze, looking at his feet as he approached the elevator: "Brother."

Shen Yu’s voice was a bit hoarse, likely from the cold: "Why didn’t you call me when you came?"

"Didn’t want to disturb you." Shuangxu said, "I still have to go to the hospital to see Senior Sister."

"I’ll take you."

"No need, you’re sick. Rest more."

"It’s just a cold." Shen Yu stepped into the elevator and pressed the basement button.

There was some silence in the elevator. Shen Yu turned his head to look at her. She stood in the corner, her shoulder pressed against the wall, keeping the farthest distance from him.

Shen Yu had driven himself today. On the way to the hospital, Shuangxu stared blankly out the window.

Shen Yu spoke to her, but she didn’t hear him until he called again: "Xiao Jiu."

"Hmm?" Shuangxu came back to her senses and realized they had already arrived at the hospital. She opened the car door and got out, then bent down to say to him: "Brother, I’m leaving. Take care of yourself."

Shen Yu didn’t speak, his gaze at her inscrutable. Shuangxu was distracted and didn’t notice anything.

After a pause, Shen Yu said: "Go in."

She responded and hurriedly walked into the bustling crowd of the hospital.

Shuangxu felt like she was the one with a high fever. Walking under the warm April sun, yet a chill seeped from her bones.

She knew Shen Yu had women around him.

But knowing in her mind was different from seeing with her own eyes.

The former was a dull, persistent ache; the latter was a sharp, stabbing pain that jolted the numb into wakefulness, tearing open a bloody wound.

She was fully aware—Fu Yun had deliberately sent her there today, deliberately let her see.

How had she become so guarded against her?

When she reached the hospital building, Shuangxu suddenly came to her senses and remembered that today was the day she was supposed to sign the contract with Yun Dun.

Yun Dun’s joining would determine whether Feixue could make a comeback. As the side effects of chemotherapy gradually subsided, Shu Yang’s health had improved a bit these past two days. To show Feixue’s seriousness about this collaboration, she had personally taken Xiao Liao to Yun Dun Group to sign the contract today and wasn’t at the hospital at all.

So Shuangxu didn’t go upstairs. Instead, she sat on a bench downstairs, basking in the sun.

With her eyes closed, the sunlight warmed her face, and her limbs slowly regained warmth.

Hadn’t she decided before returning to the country to adjust her position and be a well-behaved sister? Why was she upset?

Shuangxu, Shuangxu, she warned herself in her mind.

You have no right to be upset.

---

Shu Yang and Yun Dun received surprisingly good treatment this time at Yun Dun. Upon entering, they were greeted by a dedicated staff member who escorted them all the way to the elevator.

Since He Tingzhou’s meeting hadn’t ended yet, the secretary led them into a lounge and served them exquisite coffee and pastries.

There were also two slices of blueberry mousse cake.

Shu Yang couldn’t eat much of it, so after a small taste, the rest went into Xiao Liao’s stomach.

Xiao Liao, while eating, grumbled: "This He Zong is really difficult. He’s so scheming—if he lived in ancient times, he’d be the kind of treacherous and ruthless tyrant. Now he gives you a piece of cake, but who knows, maybe before I finish eating, he’ll slit my throat and dig the cake out."

Shu Yang: "Stop it, I’m going to throw up."

Before long, the door to the adjacent meeting room opened, and a group of men in suits walked out.

Among them, He Tingzhou stood out like a finely edited layer from a comic book world, towering above the otherwise unremarkable executives.

Xiao Liao: "Wow, so handsome! He looks just like my future husband!"

Shu Yang: "If you’re not afraid of getting your throat slit, I have no objections."

Outside the glass door, He Tingzhou had been casually listening to someone speak when the secretary approached and said something to him. He glanced into the lounge.

His gaze swept across both of their faces, paused for a microsecond, then indifferently withdrew.

Five minutes later, they were sitting face-to-face with He Tingzhou in the meeting room.

He Tingzhou sat in a chair with his back to the window, legs crossed, revealing a section of black dress socks beneath his trousers.

The signing process went exceptionally smoothly. He didn’t even say a word before readily signing his name.

After receiving the freshly printed contract, Shu Yang said a few polite words of thanks and appreciation for the cooperation.

He Tingzhou capped his pen and casually asked: "Why isn’t Song Shuangxu here?"

Xiao Liao’s mood, like a small blade of grass reviving from the ashes, was filled with hope. Without a second thought, she revealed Shuangxu’s whereabouts:

"Our little boss went to bring her brother ginger soup."

---

chapters.title: Which Woman Isn’t Infatuated with Him?
chapters.content:
Hearing Xiao Liao excitedly say that the signing process went smoothly, Shuangxu’s heavy, rain-laden mood lightened somewhat.

Shu Yang touched her face: "Why are you so pale? Are you running a fever too?"

"No." Shuangxu said, "Maybe I’m just naturally pale."

"Cut it out!" Shu Yang, who was far from naturally pale, put her hands on her hips. "Showing off your good genes, huh?"

"Yeah." Shuangxu bickered with her for a few words, and when she laughed, her complexion finally looked a little better.

After sending Shu Yang back to the hospital, she began handling recruitment matters.

The technical department staff had originally been brought in by Shu Yang. When the two partners split, most of them chose to side with her.

Chen Peiran had taken away Feixue’s management and administrative personnel. For a tech company, administration was the flesh and blood. Although losing them had dealt a heavy blow, the core framework remained, so a comeback was still possible.

However, to return to normal operations, filling the vacant positions was necessary.

After a busy day, as everyone was leaving, Xiao Liao and another girl discussed sharing a ride home. Seeing Shuangxu still in the office, Xiao Liao tilted her head and asked: "Little boss, aren’t you leaving yet?"

"In a bit."

"It looks like it’s going to rain soon. You should head back early."

Shuangxu turned to look outside and only then realized the sky had darkened.

But at the thought of the Shen family home, at the thought of Fu Yun, her mood sank to the bottom of the valley, as if drowned by a reverse tide, unable to resurface.

Not wanting to go home, she decided to go to a bar for a drink instead.

Inside Blue Night Club, music thundered, and scantily clad men and women danced wildly in the center. She ordered a cocktail and sat at the bar.

The bartender’s skills were lackluster, and the drink was terrible, but she still ordered a second one.

As she drank, two men approached, sitting on either side of her, their gazes openly lecherous. "Beauty, why are you drinking alone?"

A strong, vulgar cologne wafted into her nose. Shuangxu ignored them, finished her drink, pulled out a bill from her bag, placed it under the glass, and pushed it back, stepping down from the stool to leave.

"Hey, don’t rush off." One man reached out to stop her, deliberately or not flashing the Rolex on his wrist. "It’s fate that we met. Let me buy you a drink. Let’s get to know each other."

Shuangxu was already in a bad mood, and with her path completely blocked, she was extremely impatient: "I don’t see fate, only shit."

The man’s face fell, but he quickly forced a laugh with his companion: "You’ve got quite the personality."

"I like feisty girls like you. How about we have some fun?"

As he spoke, his hand moved toward her shoulder.

She turned her head, her beautiful, striking brows and eyes cold: "You’d better not touch me."

"What if I do?" The man didn’t take her threat seriously at all.

The bartender, unable to bear it, said: "Bro, bullying a girl isn’t cool."

"What’s it to you!"

His combative spirit flared, and he reached out to grab Shuangxu, but halfway, his hand was intercepted by another that came slashing in from the side.

Someone placed their hand on his shoulder in a brotherly manner, smiling: "If you want to play, play with me. Why bother my sister?"

The two men, who had been so arrogant moments ago, immediately groveled like dogs before their master upon seeing Yue Zifeng, their tone syrupy: "Young Master Yue, what a coincidence. Is this your sister?"

If Yue Zifeng was here, was Shen Yu also around?

Shuangxu subconsciously looked behind him. Zuo Zhong and a few others were there, but she didn’t see Shen Yu.

At the edge of the crowd, He Tingzhou leaned lazily against the railing, hands in his pockets, chewing gum as he watched from afar.

The flickering, shifting lights turned the dancers in the club into a group of demons and monsters. His sharp nose divided the light and shadow, his expression one of complete indifference.

Seeing his face, Shuangxu knew that if Yue Zifeng and the others hadn’t been there today, He Tingzhou wouldn’t have bothered with the situation.

Yue Zifeng smiled, narrowing his eyes: "Of course she’s not my sister. My sister is only seven."

The two men visibly relaxed.

In Yancheng, offending the Yue family meant you wouldn’t be able to walk away unscathed.

Before they could fully exhale, Yue Zifeng’s smile vanished. The earlier amiable, Buddha-like warmth turned icy as Yama in an instant. He slapped the man’s face a few times: "This is Young Master Shen’s precious little sister. Next time, open your eyes wider. If you so much as touch a finger of hers, I’ll chop off all ten of yours without hesitation."

The two men, terrified, apologized repeatedly, bowing deeply to Shuangxu: "Miss Shen, we were blind not to recognize you. We just saw you drinking alone and thought you might be lonely..."

It wasn’t clear who this apology was directed at. In any case, Shuangxu wasn’t a Shen.

"Lonely your ass!" Yue Zifeng directly waved over security: "Drag these two to the men’s room and beat them up! Look at their shifty eyes—they piss me off. With two holes in their heads and no eyeballs, these stupid bastards!"

The two men were still pleading: "Young Master Yue, please! We’ve even drunk together before..."

Yue Zifeng said viciously: "Beat them half to death! As long as they don’t die, it’s fine. If they do die, blame Shen Yu!"

After dealing with them, Yue Zifeng returned to his carefree demeanor: "Sis, why are you here alone? Drinking by yourself isn’t fun. Come, let’s go upstairs and have some real fun."

Shuangxu immediately shook her head, intending to refuse: "No, I was just about to leave—"

Before she could finish, Yue Zifeng, without another word, pulled her toward the upstairs.

"Young Master Shen isn’t here today, so I can’t just let you drink alone in a place like this. It’s full of bad people. If I take my eyes off you for a second and some blind fool bullies you, your brother will be mad at me."

Zuo Zhong added: "This is your Brother Zifeng’s turf. If you get bullied here, your brother would skin him alive."

Hearing that Shen Yu wasn’t there, Shuangxu gave up resisting and followed him upstairs.

The group chatted as they ascended. The stairs were carpeted, and the lighting was so dim it was hard to see anything. Whether it was a wrinkle in the carpet or a cigarette burn, Shuangxu’s high heel got caught.

Her foot stumbled, and as she stepped up, her descending foot stepped on someone’s.

She heard a soft "tsk" from behind. She immediately apologized: "Sorry—"

A hand supported her waist, giving a light but firm lift, helping her up.

His fingertips left a swift yet strong touch on her waist. As she stood on the step and turned her head, she met He Tingzhou’s dark, intense gaze.

Perhaps it was too sudden. The distance between their eyes exceeded the safe limit, and Shuangxu’s heart jolted as if struck by lightning.

She: "...Sorry."

He Tingzhou withdrew his hand, putting it back in his pocket. His indifferent expression made the act of helping her seem more like he was pushing her away because she had stepped on him.

"What for? You can’t even climb stairs without tripping. Should I ask your brother to get you a baby carrier to haul you up?"

His tone was extremely casual, but the words were far from pleasant. The people ahead—Yue Zifeng and the others—all turned back.

Shuangxu stepped aside to let him pass: "You go first."

He Tingzhou moved past her and went upstairs.

Yue Zifeng said: "What’s with you? Why are you always picking on my sister? Don’t you have any brotherly magnanimity?"

He Tingzhou didn’t: "She didn’t call me brother."

There weren’t many people tonight—just the familiar group of brothers. Yue Zifeng led her into a private room and had a server bring over a bottle of fruit beer. He opened it and handed it to her.

Shuangxu thought to herself, Kid’s stuff. Who are you looking down on?

Yue Zifeng beckoned her to sit beside him. To her right was He Tingzhou’s single sofa.

He had an extreme air of lazy nonchalance wherever he went. As soon as he sank into the sofa, someone thoughtfully handed him a cigarette and poured him a drink.

Their conversation mostly revolved around financial futures, venture capital, private equity—topics Shuangxu wasn’t interested in and only half understood.

After a while, the topic somehow turned to Shen Yu’s cold.

"Rumor has it that the famous actress skipped out on the film set to take care of him. She’s really devoted."

"Devotion is useless. Which woman isn’t infatuated with him?" Yue Zifeng said. "That actress was just sent away today. She was even ambushed by fans at the airport. Didn’t you see the news?"

Shuangxu lowered her head and sipped her fruit beer. Whether she was sent away or not had nothing to do with her.

"Isn’t it about time for our little sister to start dating?" someone asked her. "Did you have a boyfriend abroad?"

Shuangxu hadn’t expected the topic to suddenly shift to her. She paused, then answered: "Yes."

chapters.title: Secret Crush on Me
chapters.content:
Actually, they hadn’t dated, but she felt that saying they had would save a lot of trouble.

Then she thought, if she had a boyfriend, maybe Fu Yun would feel more at ease and stop treating her like a thief who still harbored feelings for Shen Yu.

Yue Zifeng let out a surprised "Aiyo": "Which foreign stinky brat? What does he look like? Foreigner or Chinese? Why didn’t you bring him back for us to see?"

"Broke up." Lying was easy.

"How did you break up?"

Shuangxu found him nosy, took a sip of her drink, and said, "Just playing around."

The moment she said that, the air went silent for a few seconds.

Shuangxu felt a very noticeable gaze fall on her.

She followed it and met He Tingzhou’s eyes.

What are you looking at?

Shuangxu didn’t understand why her words were so shocking.

Among the young masters present, every single one of them had played with more women than she had known men.

She was usually too well-behaved, and Shen Yu protected her like a princess in a castle. Hearing such words from her mouth left all the brothers stunned.

He Tingzhou’s deep eyes fixed on her with great interest: "How many have you played with?"

That’s none of your business.

Shuangxu tossed the hot potato back: "Brother Tingzhou, how about you? How many have you played with?"

Years of experience weren’t for nothing. He Tingzhou wasn’t so easily stumped by her question. His thin lips curled slightly: "I don’t play with men."

...Fair enough.

"Aiyo, little sister has really grown up," Yue Zifeng sighed emotionally, his feelings no less intense than when his own little sister, at the age of three, had slapped him for the first time.

"You were so small back then, and in the blink of an eye, you’ve learned how to toy with men’s feelings."

Shuangxu said: "Didn’t you play with women when you were twenty-two?"

"Damn. You’re right." Yue Zifeng laughed, "Little sister, what kind of man do you like? Tell your brother, and I’ll find a good one for you."

Shuangxu’s ideal type already had a living, perfect template.

Refined, gentle, and always infinitely patient with her.

But she couldn’t say that, so she lied.

"I like wild, domineering, and unreasonable men."

"Yo." Yue Zifeng suddenly grinned mischievously, "Aren’t you just describing your Brother Tingzhou’s ID number?"

Shuangxu herself was stunned.

She had just said the opposite of Shen Yu, not intending to allude to He Tingzhou.

The others laughed, and someone teased He Tingzhou: "Hey, Lord Zhou, little sister Shuangxu has a crush on you. What do you say?"

Shuangxu turned her neck along with them.

The private room wasn’t lit with fancy lights. The warm orange glow was hazy, casting a soft light over everyone.

He Tingzhou leaned against the sofa, his light gray dress shirt unbuttoned halfway, a cigarette between his thin, sharp lips. In the interplay of light and shadow from the mood lighting, he squinted at her.

Just as Shuangxu was about to speak, he took the cigarette from his mouth with two fingers and said in a low, slightly hoarse voice: "Secret crush on me."

Shuangxu: "..."

This was a huge misunderstanding.

He tapped the cigarette against the rim of the glass on the table, the ash falling into the light brown whiskey. Drawing out his words, he said: "Forget it. I don’t play with friends’ little sisters."

Who said I wanted you to play with me?

She couldn’t possibly have a secret crush on He Tingzhou.

She had intended to explain, but thinking of Fu Yun, maybe letting everyone misunderstand that she had a crush on He Tingzhou would make things simpler.

Moreover, she knew that He Tingzhou knew her little secret.

He said that on purpose to tease her.

So she simply didn’t explain and replied: "Oh, then I’m heartbroken."

Yue Zifeng laughed like a maniac. He didn’t take it seriously at all. With He Tingzhou’s shameless, always-bullying-little-sister demeanor, one would have to be possessed to have a crush on him.

"Cut the crap. Since when do you have principles?"

He Tingzhou wasn’t annoyed: "How do you know I don’t?"

"You have none." Yue Zifeng was one hundred and twenty percent certain, "If you had any, you’d be my dad from now on!"

People with sisters at home had a strong sense of brotherly duty. Before midnight, Yue Zifeng started urging everyone to leave.

They had all been drinking, and Yue Zifeng was looking for someone to take Shuangxu home when he spotted He Tingzhou. He directly pushed Shuangxu toward him: "Perfect, you didn’t drink. You take little sister home."

Remembering the last time she was tricked, Shuangxu didn’t dare owe him any favors.

"I don’t need—"

Before she could finish her refusal, He Tingzhou’s eyelids drooped as he glanced at her: "What, you’re still thinking of taking advantage of me under the cover of night?"

Shuangxu: ?

She was baffled: "I never—"

"Why else wouldn’t you ride in my car." He Tingzhou wore a "Don’t explain, you just want my beauty" expression.

He hooked his fingers around the high-end coat casually draped over the back of the sofa, tossed it over his shoulder, bit his cigarette, and walked out with loose, relaxed steps.

Shuangxu had no choice but to follow.

Even after sitting in the passenger seat, she still couldn’t figure out the logic.

Not riding in his car meant she wanted to take advantage of him?

Then if someone wanted to stay away from him, wouldn’t that mean they loved him to death?

Unable to figure it out, she gave up. He Tingzhou was always inscrutable.

For example, he didn’t drink, yet he came to a bar, the noisiest place in the world, to sleep.

His thinking probably just liked to take the road less traveled.

He Tingzhou put out his cigarette before getting into the car. He tossed his suit jacket over to the passenger seat, probably forgetting there was someone there today, a habitual gesture.

Shuangxu was hit in the face by the cold, sharp chill from his clothes. She turned to glance at him.

"Take it." He Tingzhou started the car, steering with one hand, smoothly gliding from the parking spot onto the main road.

The sports car had no back seat, and she couldn’t just throw his coat away. She had no choice but to fold it up and place it on her lap, arranging it neatly.

Accepting someone’s kindness without a word was impolite, but Shuangxu really couldn’t think of any topic to discuss with him.

Talk about life? She and He Tingzhou’s lives were poles apart; there was nothing to say.

Talk about the liquid hydrogen drone project? Please, it was after work hours.

She couldn’t possibly talk about the rumors surrounding him, like almost getting someone killed...

Not every young master in Yancheng was as outstanding as Shen Yu. Many were extravagant and dissolute second-generation rich kids who could rely on their families to smooth over any trouble they caused. Like the notorious playboy from the Zheng family.

Shuangxu knew very little about He Tingzhou, only hearing bits and pieces from others.

Years ago, Commander He had assisted in breaking up an international drug trafficking ring at the China-Myanmar border. Those people were extremely vicious and had kidnapped the then five or six-year-old He Tingzhou and his mother. His mother had died during that time.

This was likely a taboo subject; no one dared mention it in front of He Tingzhou. Shuangxu had only overheard a few drunken men at a banquet carelessly revealing a detail or two.

When she curiously asked Shen Yu about it later, Shen Yu had knocked on her head: "So nosy, should we change your name to Song Daling?"

So in Yancheng, He Tingzhou could do whatever he pleased, however he pleased.

The He surname was a mountain built on power and influence, a family of high-ranking officials and military heroes for three generations. He had the capital to poke a hole in the sky if he was displeased.

Lost in thought, He Tingzhou’s hand suddenly reached toward her without warning.

Shuangxu jolted, reflexively dodging, her back pressing against the car door.

Noticing her startled reaction, He Tingzhou slightly lifted his eyelids: "What are you dodging for?"

He reached out to open the glove compartment in front of the passenger seat.

The dim light from outside illuminated his hand—long fingers, prominent veins on the back, exuding a wild strength. Blue veins coiled upward, disappearing into the expensive cuffs of his shirt.

Shuangxu watched as he pulled out a box of candy, peeled one, and popped it into his mouth. He smirked: "Between the two of us, I should be the one afraid of being taken advantage of."

"..." Shuangxu sat still, "I was just afraid I’d take advantage of you."

He Tingzhou’s dark eyes glanced over, letting out a low hum: "Try it and see."

Did she have the guts to try?

The key point was, she wasn’t stupid.

He parked in front of the Shen family’s gate. Shuangxu didn’t waste a second, placing the folded coat on the seat and waving her hand: "Goodbye, Brother Tingzhou."

Then she quickly ran into the house.

---

chapters.title: Future Sister-in-Law
chapters.content:
At this hour, Fu Yun and the servants had already gone to bed. The lights in the Shen family’s villa were dimmed, with only the hallway light left on for her.

Aunt Wang draped an outer coat over her shoulders and came out of her room to greet her: "Why so late? Madam was waiting for you all this time. When you didn’t come back by midnight, she was so worried. I had to coax her to bed. Are you hungry? The kitchen left some fish soup. Should I cook you a bowl of noodles?"

"It’s fine, I’m not hungry." Shuangxu said softly, "Go back to rest. I’m going to bed too."

Aunt Wang watched her go upstairs before returning to her own room.

Shuangxu didn’t turn on any more lights. She tiptoed upstairs to her bedroom without disturbing anyone.

The next morning, when Fu Yun saw her, she asked: "Where did you go last night? Aunt Wang said you didn’t come back until early morning."

"Went drinking with Brother Zifeng and the others." Shuangxu acted normally, as if nothing had happened yesterday.

Seeing her calm expression, Fu Yun’s uneasy heart finally settled.

Aunt Wang brought over the coffee. Shuangxu ate her fried egg, listening to Fu Yun across from her say: "Your brother turned thirty-one after his birthday. It’s time to settle his marriage. I discussed it with your stepfather yesterday. We plan to choose a suitable girl from a well-matched family in Yancheng. Your brother doesn’t have any objections. When you have time these days, help me take a look?"

"Sure." Shuangxu looked up and smiled, "The person you choose will definitely be great."

Fu Yun probably only said this to test the waters. In reality, she only asked Shuangxu to look at photos once.

In a family like the Shens, marriage was a binding of interests between two families. It wasn’t something the younger generation could interfere with. Moreover, she wasn’t even part of the Shen family.

Born into this class, she might not even be able to control her own marriage, let alone Shen Yu’s.

When she received Yue Zifeng’s call, she had just finished showering.

Yue Zifeng asked her to come out and play. Shuangxu said: "You guys have fun. I’m getting ready for bed."

"So early to sleep? Is the bed at home more comfortable than the one in America?" Yue Zifeng said, "You used to be so eager. Even if your brother didn’t take you, you insisted on tagging along. Now no matter how much we call, you won’t come. Really not coming? Your future sister-in-law is here. Aren’t you coming to see her?"

Shuangxu felt a slight ringing in her ears, wondering if water had gotten in during her shower.

She hadn’t expected things to progress so quickly.

Already... decided?

Who was she? Which family’s daughter? She didn’t know anything.

Shuangxu didn’t want to go. She pulled the blanket over her face, but then worried that not going would seem strange and raise suspicion.

What should a sister’s attitude be toward her future sister-in-law?

Curious, excited, eager to find out...

So she pretended to be excited and replied: "Of course I want to see her. Send me the address."

By the time Shuangxu arrived at the club, forty minutes had passed.

Yuehai Tang was a special place. Its charm wasn’t in its luxury. On the contrary, compared to the opulent facades of other clubs, this Siheyuan courtyard within the Second Ring Road was already "precious" enough.

Of course, it wasn’t lacking in luxury. The white jade steps were carved with scroll patterns, and a single podocarpus tree transplanted into the courtyard was worth millions.

Those who came here to relax were all young masters and ladies from wealthy or powerful families. Any one of them, picked at random, had an illustrious background.

Young girls flocked to this place. Though the name "Yuehai Tang" sounded romantic, in reality, money, power, and desire were its true colors.

This place wasn’t membership-based, but ordinary people couldn’t get in.

Vehicles weren’t allowed inside, so Shuangxu got out at the entrance.

As she walked in with her handbag, she saw a pure black Koenigsegg boldly parked in the courtyard.

Well, who let him have the surname He.

When Shuangxu entered the private room, the group was in high spirits.

It was very lively inside, with many people, men and women, some familiar, some not.

"Little sister, over here."

Yue Zifeng beckoned her over, pulled her close, and pointed with his drink at the woman sitting next to Shen Yu. Smiling, he said: "Do you know who this is? Your future sister-in-law."

Unlike the elegant and dignified young ladies from noble families that Shuangxu had imagined, this woman was very young, only in her early twenties, with bright, lively eyes.

It was unclear whether it was the dim lighting in the private room or Shen Yu’s expression that was naturally so indifferent.

He didn’t deny it, just glanced at Yue Zifeng with a faint look, using his usual tone for teasing him: "Your leaky mouth needs to see a dentist."

Yue Zifeng didn’t mind: "Shuangxu is your sister, not an outsider. What’s the big deal?"

"It’s not a done deal yet." The woman was a bit embarrassed, a very genuine and unpretentious shyness. With her innocent and carefree demeanor, it was clear she had been pampered by her family.

She looked at Shuangxu with curiosity: "You’re Xiao Jiu?"

Only Shen Yu called her Xiao Jiu.

Shen Yu had discussed her with this marriage candidate but had never mentioned a word to her.

The other party even knew her nickname, yet she knew nothing about her.

This gave Shuangxu a subtle, isolated feeling.

In truth, this day would come sooner or later. Eventually, Shen Yu would have his own family, his own wife, and children. The privileges she had once enjoyed would inevitably be lost.

"Hello, I’ve wanted to meet you for a long time. I’m Lu Manni." Lu Manni smiled friendly.

Shuangxu returned with a polite smile: "Miss Lu, hello."

"Why so formal? Just call me Manni. We’re the same age." Lu Manni said, "Don’t listen to Zifeng’s nonsense. I’m not your sister-in-law yet. It’s just that our families have this idea, and they want us to get to know each other first."

No difference.

In arranged marriages, it was about the union of two families. As long as the two parties didn’t find each other repulsive at first sight or had some fatal flaw, the marriage could easily be settled.

Shuangxu just went along: "Then I’ll address you as such when the time comes."

Lu Manni took out her phone: "Come, let’s add each other on WeChat."

In front of Shen Yu, Shuangxu naturally couldn’t refuse.

As soon as their friend request was accepted, Lu Manni familiarized herself by linking arms with Shuangxu and even leaned in for a sniff: "You smell so good. What perfume are you wearing?"

"..." Shuangxu’s social anxiety was about to be sniffed out.

But this was her "future sister-in-law," so she endured it and didn’t pull her arm away: "I didn’t wear any perfume today."

Lu Manni laughed and said to Shen Yu: "Your sister is so cute."

Although they were in the same circle, Shuangxu and Lu Manni didn’t know each other at all.

Lu Manni was He Tingzhou’s cousin; Commander He was her maternal uncle. Her father held an important position in the Military Commission. In his early years, due to his job, he was often stationed in Lincheng, so she had grown up in Lincheng with her parents.

Shuangxu and Lu Manni’s life trajectories had just missed each other. When Shuangxu was in Yancheng, Lu Manni was away, and when Lu Manni returned five years ago, Shuangxu had been sent abroad.

Lu Manni was good friends with Song Leyan, Shuangxu’s half-sister from a different mother.

Unfortunately, the two sisters of the Song family had a relationship like enemies.

The group’s conversation mostly revolved around Shen Yu and Lu Manni, with light-hearted jokes among friends, keeping the atmosphere relaxed and cheerful.

Lu Manni was only twenty-two after all. Teased by everyone, her face turned red. Leaning toward Shuangxu, she asked: "Xiao Jiu, tell me secretly, does he have any flaws that no one else knows about?"

Shuangxu said: "My brother has no flaws."

"You’re asking the wrong person. If you ask my sister, she’d give Shen Yu a perfect ten. You should come ask me." Yue Zifeng extended his hand, "Give me a hundred yuan, and I’ll tell you all of Shen Yu’s little secrets."

Lu Manni laughed and slapped his palm: "I don’t believe you. I only believe Xiao Jiu."

Shuangxu heard this and turned to look at her, a hint of inquiry in her eyes.

Had Lu Manni truly forgotten their last encounter, or was she pretending in front of Shen Yu?

chapters.title: Do You Have Feelings for Your Brother?
chapters.content:
The most noble and wealthy young heirs of Yan City had gathered here today. The owner of Moonlit Begonia personally delivered several bottles of rare Rémy Martin Louis XIII.

The plump old man, who looked kind and approachable, smiled, "With all the young masters present today, my humble establishment is honored. These few bottles of wine are a small token to add to the joy. Please don't reject my modest gift, Young Master Shen."

"Wow, Director Qin is really generous."

Shuangxu thought to herself, even the club owner knew about it. Maybe she was the only one in the world who didn't.

A soft, gentle female voice came from inside the private room, warm and tender: "Has Lord Zhou woken up?"

Shuangxu followed the sound and looked over.

This private room was reserved exclusively for them and was usually not open to the public. The interior was extremely spacious. In the dimly lit area, two low-color-temperature spotlights were on, casting a muted glow. She hadn't paid any attention to that corner at all.

It was only now that she noticed, in the shadowy darkness, a man was lying on a long sofa.

The sofa was too short for his long legs, so they were crossed and propped up on the armrest, with his hand resting over his eyes.

On the carpet beside him, a woman in a qipao knelt, holding a fan and gently fanning him.

The temperature in April was not hot at all, but the fan was being waved purely for the intoxicating tenderness of the scene.

Even when sleeping, he had a beauty attending to him by his pillow—when it came to luxury, who could compare to He Tingzhou?

Shuangxu thought to herself, why did this man like to sleep everywhere?

She didn’t know what kind of exciting and exhausting nightlife he had to be this tired, able to sleep through all the noise in the private room.

He Tingzhou lazily sat up, stood, and pushed aside the half-drawn sheer curtain as he came out.

A man sitting on a single sofa tactfully made room for him. He Tingzhou sat down and asked someone for a cigarette.

The fan-wielding beauty followed him out and sat on the armrest beside him.

The tight qipao outlined her perfect figure. She crossed her fair, slender legs in a side split, her soft, delicate body leaning toward He Tingzhou. Her hand, with its wine-red nail polish, was as tender as if boneless as she held the lighter to light his cigarette.

She was a stunning beauty, not like an ordinary hostess.

Bloodline suppression made Lu Mannan clearly a bit afraid of him. She seriously called out, "Cousin."

Yue Zifeng was asking He Tingzhou, "I heard the leader came back a couple of days ago?"

He Tingzhou’s lazy gaze swept over, his long lashes visible from this angle. "Why are you asking about his whereabouts? Planning to assassinate him?"

"I didn’t—"

He Tingzhou said, "If you want his life, you don’t need to go to that much trouble. I’ll take you to him later. If he finds out you have such thoughts, he might even praise your courage."

Yue Zifeng almost dropped to his knees in fear. He raised three fingers to the sky and swore, "Heaven above, earth below, I truly have no such treasonous thoughts!"

He Tingzhou gave a light, mocking laugh and flicked his cigarette ash. "What’s there to be afraid of? It’s just a matter of taking a bullet. The old man has excellent aim. I guarantee it’ll be painless."

His old man was someone who required top-level security for his movements. Even if Yue Zifeng had a body full of guts, he wouldn’t dare utter those two words.

He Tingzhou could joke about it, but Yue Zifeng would have to sleep with one eye open tonight after going home.

Yue Zifeng slapped his own mouth. "Damn it, I shouldn’t have shot my mouth off!"

Lu Mannan was paying a bit too much attention to Shuangxu, always subtly steering the conversation toward her.

"Little Nine is so pretty. Does she have a lot of suitors?"

"No," Shuangxu said. "I don’t have any suitors."

Lu Mannan said, "But I heard that Zheng Zuye once pursued you. Later, Shen Yu even made him apologize to you. What happened?"

Before Shuangxu could answer, Yue Zifeng scoffed, "You don’t know what kind of person Zheng Zuye is. That wasn’t pursuit; that was harassment."

It had been years since that old, rotten business. Zheng Zuye was a notorious playboy in their circles, abusing the Zheng family’s power to do whatever he pleased. Rumor had it he’d been playing with women since middle school.

His kind of bad was different from He Tingzhou’s. He Tingzhou’s bad was dangerous, but Zheng Zuye was rotten to the core.

Back then, Shuangxu was only fifteen, a young girl. After encountering him a few times at certain events, Zheng Zuye started harassing her.

When Shen Yu found out, he went directly to the Zheng residence to settle the score. Old Master Zheng, unable to bear the shame, personally forced his grandson to apologize to her. Only then was the matter resolved.

After that, Zheng Zuye never bothered her again.

"Young Master Shen really protects you a lot," Lu Mannan said.

Shen Yu had indeed been very protective of Shuangxu. Before she came of age, there hadn’t been a single proper suitor.

Right after graduating high school, before she even turned eighteen, she was sent abroad. During those years overseas, apart from Shu Yang, she refused all social activities. Anyone who mentioned her would call her aloof. Where would suitors come from?

Speaking of this, Yue Zifeng remembered something and turned to Shen Yu. "Did you know your sister found a boyfriend abroad? Your family’s fresh and tender cabbage has been secretly nibbled on, and you don’t even know."

Shen Yu, sitting across from them, looked over at Shuangxu. "In a relationship?"

Shuangxu hadn’t expected Yue Zifeng to bring it up in front of Shen Yu. She didn’t look at Shen Yu’s expression. "Mmm."

Shen Yu, holding his cigarette, rubbed his temple with his fingers and didn’t say anything.

Yue Zifeng sighed deeply. "She used to be so well-behaved, following you around like a little tail, calling ‘Brother~’ ‘Brother~’ every day with such a sing-song voice."

The scattered blue smoke half-concealed Shen Yu’s expression as he picked up his drink. His long fingers tapped the rim of the glass. "She just looked well-behaved. She’s stubborn through and through."

"Is there anyone more stubborn than my sister? Back then, if I hadn’t seen you parading around with your sister every day, making me jealous, I wouldn’t have begged my mom for a sister. And what did I get? A little troublemaker."

"Really?" Lu Mannan asked. "Was Little Nine that cute when she was little?"

At this, Yue Zifeng got animated. "You should’ve seen her back then. Chubby little face, big eyes, one cry and she could melt anyone’s heart. No wonder Shen Yu had a soft spot for her and took her home. If it were you, Left Zhong, he’d have cried so hard that Shen Yu’s car wheels would’ve stopped just to avoid running over him. It was already good enough that he didn’t roll over him."

"Hey," Left Zhong said, "don’t drag me into this."

Yue Zifeng said, "If my sister grows up to play with men, I’ll definitely skin that man alive, cut him into pieces, dip him in soy sauce, and feed him to the dogs."

"Mr. Yue, that’s a double standard," the qipao beauty next to He Tingzhou spoke up with a soft, pleasant laugh. "You men can play with women, but women can’t play with men?"

"Of course you can play, Beauty Mu. My sister is different," Yue Zifeng said, feeling that only Shen Yu and he shared this sentiment. "Why don’t you ask Shen Yu if he wants to strangle that guy."

Shen Yu tapped his cigarette ash, his expression indifferent. "You might as well go ask the commander for a bullet."

Lu Mannan glanced at him, then at Shuangxu, looking thoughtful.

Yue Zifeng groaned, "Damn, everyone’s ganging up on me." Then he turned to Shuangxu. "Sis, come chat with me."

Shuangxu stood up. "I need to use the restroom."

The restroom was extremely quiet. Shuangxu absentmindedly rubbed her fingers under the running water. She heard footsteps and looked up, seeing Lu Mannan enter through the mirror.

Lu Mannan tilted her head. "Do you dislike me a lot?"

Shuangxu countered, "What makes you think that?"

"Just a feeling."

"Don’t overthink it." Shuangxu turned off the gilded faucet and slowly dried her hands. "You’re beautiful, cheerful, and likable. Who would dislike you?"

As she turned to leave the restroom, Lu Mannan suddenly looked at her and said, "Hey, do you have feelings for your brother?"

---

chapters.title: Time Bomb
chapters.content:
For a moment, Shuangxu froze in place, unable to move.

She pinched her fingertip, and after a few seconds, she found her voice. "No. Don’t misunderstand. What Song Leyan said back then, don’t take it seriously. She and I don’t get along; she was just spreading rumors."

Whether Lu Mannan believed her or not, Shuangxu didn’t know.

After all, they weren’t blood-related siblings. Putting herself in Lu Mannan’s shoes, she thought she’d probably feel uncomfortable too.

After a moment of silence, she spoke again. "You don’t have to believe me. Just believe in my brother’s character. I hope my existence doesn’t affect your opinion of him."

When Shuangxu returned to the private room, the conversation had already moved on to other topics.

The sofa where He Tingzhou had been sitting was now empty. He and the beauty had disappeared.

As for where they went, Shuangxu didn’t care.

She directly picked up her bag. Yue Zifeng looked puzzled. "You’ve only been here for a little while. Leaving already? Not waiting for your brother?"

"I’m a bit tired. You all enjoy yourselves." Shuangxu said, "Brother, I’m heading back first."

Leaving the warm, fragrant private room, she stepped into the courtyard of the siheyuan. A cool breeze rustled the branches of the luohan pine.

Noticing the ostentatious black supercar, Shuangxu realized there was someone under the tree.

The qipao beauty was leaning toward the car window, speaking softly. "Lord Zhou, not playing anymore?"

"Not in the mood." He Tingzhou sounded bored.

The beauty said, "Then should I take you somewhere fun?"

He Tingzhou, resting his hand on the car window, flicked his cigarette ash and laughed lazily, his words drawn out. "What’s fun? Let me hear it."

Shuangxu didn’t want to disturb their flirtatious "elegance," but his car was parked so arrogantly, right in the middle of the only path in and out.

She had no idea when the two of them would finish, and she didn’t want to stand there watching a live broadcast. After some thought, she decided to walk past them openly.

It was hard for a living person to go unnoticed.

The woman straightened up and spoke to Shuangxu in a tender voice, though without the coquettishness she used with He Tingzhou. "Miss Song, leaving already?"

"Mmm."

He Tingzhou’s sharp, dark eyes glanced at her indifferently.

"Need a ride?"

Shuangxu wasn’t so blind as to not see they were flirting.

With such a glamorous beauty by his side, who had time to take her home?

Moreover, He Tingzhou had never been kind to her. He was probably just being polite. After all, once the Shen and Lu families became in-laws, he would be Shen Yu’s cousin by marriage—doubly related.

She understood the false politeness. "No need to trouble you, Brother Tingzhou. You do your thing."

He Tingzhou said, "Which eye of yours saw me busy?"

Both eyes did.

Others were drinking while he took a nap—wasn’t that conserving energy for a night of passion with a beauty?

Shuangxu didn’t dare say that. She explained, "My driver brought me..."

Before she could finish, He Tingzhou took his eyes off her, stepped on the gas, and the arrogant roar of the engine grated on her nerves as he drove off.

Shuangxu was stunned.

She hadn’t expected him to so ruthlessly abandon the beauty.

The beauty herself seemed used to it, adjusting her earring that had been swayed by the wind. The charm in the corner of her eyes was so alluring that even Shuangxu, a woman, could feel it. "He really doesn’t know how to cherish beauty."

Back home, Shuangxu took a shower and buried herself under the covers. She felt exhausted, yet her mind was wide awake, buzzing with elusive thoughts.

She didn’t know why, but even though she hadn’t stayed at the club for long, it had drained her mentally.

Her phone buzzed with a WeChat message. She reached for it.

Lu Mannan: [Are you home yet?]

There had always been many women who liked Shen Yu, sprouting up like bamboo shoots after a spring rain.

Some tried to take a roundabout route through Shuangxu, while others resented her for occupying too much of Shen Yu’s attention.

But without exception, they all had to win her over.

When Shuangxu was younger, she had innocently delivered love letters for them. Shen Yu never read those letters, but she, full of curiosity, would open and study them carefully.

She had seen this kind of ingratiation many times, but Miss Lu of the Lu family had no need to fawn over her.

Shuangxu replied politely: [Yes, thank you for your concern.]

Lu Mannan: [Are you free tomorrow? Let’s go shopping together.]

Shuangxu declined: [Sorry, I have plans tomorrow.]

After that, Lu Mannan would message her every few days, inviting her to meals, shopping, or trendy spots.

Shuangxu didn’t understand what she was trying to do or what she was still probing for. She declined each time with politeness, but because she was too polite, her distance was also very clear.

In the adult world, she believed the other party would understand her meaning.

After all, Lu Mannan seemed naive and carefree but was actually very clever.

Lu Mannan sent several messages, and seeing Shuangxu’s consistently cold attitude, she stopped trying to force the issue.

A few days later, Fu Yun called, saying there were guests at home and asking Shuangxu to come back early.

When she returned to the Shen residence from the company, she saw Lu Mannan sitting in the living room.

Lu Mannan waved at her. "Little Nine, we meet again."

Fu Yun was all smiles. "Mannan has been waiting for you for half the day."

Shuangxu immediately felt uncomfortable but couldn’t say anything in front of Fu Yun. "Miss Lu, what brings you here?"

Lu Mannan, seemingly not picking up on the distance in her tone, said, "My mom’s birthday is coming up. I really don’t know what gift to give her and was hoping you could help me brainstorm."

"I’m not good at picking gifts either." Shuangxu passed the buck. "You should ask someone else for help."

Lu Mannan pitifully blinked her eyes. "But I don’t have any other friends. I grew up in Lin City with my dad when I was little. I don’t know many people in Yan City."

What kind of pitiful act was this? Weren’t you and Song Leyan good sisters?

But Shuangxu couldn’t say that. Lu Mannan’s pitiful act wasn’t meant for her.

Sure enough, Fu Yun came to persuade her. "Every time you buy me a gift, it’s always perfect. Just help Mannan pick one. It won’t take much time. How about I make you some red bean soup with dried tangerine peel tonight, dear?"

Even though Shuangxu was reluctant, she had to agree.

Fu Yun arranged for a driver to take them. On the way, Shuangxu turned her face to the window the entire time, ignoring Lu Mannan.

"Don’t be mad." Lu Mannan poked her arm. "I didn’t mean anything by it. I couldn’t get a hold of you, so I had to use a little trick."

"I’m not mad." Shuangxu said. "You know using my adoptive mother to pressure me means you’re smart. What’s the point of me being mad?"

"So you shouldn’t have refused me in the first place."

Shuangxu turned her head and saw the confident smile on Lu Mannan’s face—a smile of someone sure of victory.

"What do you really want?"

"I want to be friends with you."

Shuangxu was too lazy to beat around the bush with her. "My brother and my adoptive mother aren’t here. You don’t need to put on an act. How about being more direct?"

Lu Mannan glanced at the driver’s seat. The driver was from the Shen family.

Shuangxu got out of the car and walked into a café. She ordered a private room with good privacy, and as soon as the door closed, the two of them sat face to face.

Shuangxu got straight to the point. "You’re different from other women. You’re my brother’s potential marriage partner, with two families backing you. You don’t need to fawn over me. I don’t dislike you, and even if I did, for my brother’s sake, I’d still be polite to you. So you don’t need to test me repeatedly."

"I’m just really curious about you."

Lu Mannan used tongs to pick up a sugar cube and drop it into her coffee, stirring slowly. "I won’t hide it from you. I really like Shen Yu. Actually, when I first returned to Yan City and saw him at a banquet, I fell for him. Do you know that heart-thumping feeling?"

"That night, I only exchanged a few words with him. I asked him where the restroom was, and he had someone take me there. I said thank you, and he just gave a light, almost perfunctory smile. But I blushed all night. Of course, I was too young back then. You understand, you’re the same age as me."

Shuangxu didn’t want to hear this. "You should tell him these things, not me."

Lu Mannan acted as if she hadn’t heard and continued, "I know he’s had other women before. I don’t mind. At his age, with his charm, it would be abnormal if he hadn’t been with any women. Those women don’t matter to me. The most threatening one is you."

"A fiancé with a non-blood-related adoptive sister, who’s also very beautiful, and whom he dotes on..."

She glanced at Shuangxu as she said this. "Don’t you think you’re a time bomb?"

chapters.title: Go with Big Brother?
chapters.content:
That suffocating feeling, like being blocked by a sponge, came again.

Shuangxu was sick of being treated like a thief, but she had a guilty conscience—she couldn’t blame anyone.

If there was anyone to blame, it was herself.

The whole world was telling her she was wrong, that her love for Shen Yu was an unforgivable sin, that she was a shameless, delusional white-eyed wolf.

Shuangxu also hated having to say, "Don’t worry, I’m just his sister. I won’t affect you in any way."

Lu Mànmàn shrugged. "I don’t think so. You like him. I know."

"Then what do you want?" Shuangxu met her gaze. "Do you want me to cut ties with my brother so you can sleep soundly? I can answer that right now—impossible."

"I don’t want my presence to change how you see my brother. I’ve never thought about ruining your perfect match. But my brother will always be my brother. No one can change that. If you can accept it, then accept it. If you can’t, make your own choice. Don’t pressure me—I’m not responsible for your ‘unhappiness.’"

"You’re so obedient in front of your brother. Why are you so harsh with me?"

"Are you my brother?" Of course people had different levels of closeness. Could family and outsiders be treated the same?

Shuangxu said bluntly, "If you don’t want to listen to reason, then I’ll be direct—are you going to marry him or not?"

Honestly, before today, Lu Mànmàn had always thought Shuangxu was a soft, obedient, and easy-to-control person.

But now she had a feeling that this rebellious side was the real Song Shuangxu.

"I’m not that domineering. After all, you’ve lived together for so many years. Even raising a dog creates a bond, let alone siblings. But as your future sister-in-law, don’t I have the right to know the truth about my little sister-in-law?"

"If you really think you have that right, why not just ask my brother directly?"

Lu Mànmàn smiled again. "Are you sure you want me to ask him, ‘Does your little sister like you?’"

Shuangxu hated how Lu Mànmàn used Shen Yu to threaten her, but she couldn’t deny that this tactic was indeed the most effective.

"My background—Song Leyan must have told you. I was abandoned by my mother. When I was eight, she didn’t want me anymore and sent me back to the Song family. My dad was working abroad at the time, and Aunt Cui and Song Leyan had moved to Europe with him. I was left alone in China with no one to take care of me, so I was entrusted to the Shen family."

"What about your grandfather?"

"My grandfather is the person in the world who dislikes me the most."

Shuangxu’s fingertips pinched the handle of her coffee cup, her grip tight. She traced the smooth porcelain surface, her voice as calm as if she were telling someone else’s story: "He was very displeased that my mother had me in secret and then sent me back. He also thought I was timid, cried a lot, and had a petty, small-minded nature. He left me with the nanny and ignored me."

Lu Mànmàn had been cherished by her entire family since childhood, growing up in a fairy-tale-like world. She couldn’t understand how some children in this world could be unwanted by both father and mother, with living relatives, yet still feel like orphans.

"Then why did Yue Zifeng say Shen Yu was the one who brought you home?"

Shuangxu looked at her for a moment before answering cautiously, "The Shen and Song families were neighbors. My brother passed by, saw how pitiful I was, and took me home."

Lu Mànmàn gave her a sympathetic look.

Shuangxu couldn’t be bothered to judge whether her sympathy was genuine or not. She didn’t need it. She put down her coffee and picked up the bag on the chair.

"I’ve told you everything you wanted to know. What you think is your business. Don’t bother me again."

Night silently spread beyond the glass windows. At this hour, the café had few customers. She pushed open the partition door and left without looking back.

The Shen family’s driver was waiting outside the café. Shuangxu had him take Lu Mànmàn home, then walked alone along the quiet street outside the mall before climbing onto a large bridge.

After nightfall, Yan City was a dazzling spectacle, a different kind of prosperity.

The damp, cool wind brushed her face. Below the bridge, the river rushed by. The lights along the embankment stretched in a line, extending from this moment all the way back to when she was eight years old.

The story she had told Lu Mànmàn was the abridged version.

For a child, being abandoned by their mother was earth-shattering. Especially when her mother had clearly loved her, yet decided she didn’t want her anymore.

At eight years old, she understood many things. She knew her mother was sending her away. She didn’t want to go, so she clung to the doorframe, refusing to let go. But her mother forcibly pulled her away.

That day, while waiting at the restaurant for Song Mianzhi to pick her up, she kept throwing a tantrum. Her mother, perhaps reluctant, tried to coax her by saying she’d buy her favorite ice cream from the shop next door. But Shuangxu, in her bad mood, refused to go. So her mother went alone, asking the shopkeeper to keep an eye on her.

Left alone in the restaurant, Shuangxu watched as people came in one by one. Each time a man of a certain age entered, her resistance grew stronger. The final straw was when a sleazy-looking man kept staring at her.

She was terrified. Impulsively, she ran out of the restaurant, wanting to go home. But she was in an unfamiliar place, got lost, and couldn’t find her way back—she couldn’t even find the restaurant again.

All the grievances welled up inside her. She stood at the intersection and sobbed uncontrollably until a pair of clean sneakers appeared in her tear-blurred vision.

A handsome boy, as if stepped out of a comic book, crouched down in front of her, his eyes curved as he asked, "What’s wrong, little one?"

She was crying so hard she could barely breathe, but he was patient. He listened to her blubber for a long time and even bought her a beautiful little cake.

He noticed her guard was up, so he took her to the police station and stayed with her until her mother came to pick her up.

Shuangxu remembered that day vividly—the way he smelled, the warmth of his palm when he ruffled her hair, the way he said "Goodbye" before leaving.

She also remembered that after she got home, her mother, who had spent the entire afternoon searching for her because she had run off, beat her severely.

She cried all night, until her tears ran dry. The next day, her mother took her directly to the Song family. Shuangxu was quiet the whole way, no longer throwing a tantrum.

As she watched her mother’s retreating figure, she hoped in her heart that her mother would turn around and look at her one last time. But she never did.

Song Mianzhi had already left the country the night before due to a work transfer. Her mother’s decision to send her back was sudden—his original arrangements had never included this unexpected daughter. He had only set aside time for one lunch with them. When no one showed up at the restaurant, he left.

So the Song family’s house was empty.

Only two caretakers were there, neither of whom knew her, and they whispered about her background.

The pain of being abandoned by her mother and the helplessness of being isolated overwhelmed her. A few days later, Grandfather Song finally made time to visit the villa to see her.

His presence was already stern, and the way he looked at her was full of disdain. The little girl’s uneasy demeanor annoyed him, and he left after only a few minutes.

The caretakers only ensured she had three meals a day. Beyond that, they barely spoke to her.

Shuangxu was left alone in that empty villa, like someone forgotten by the entire world.

Every day, she crouched by the fence in the courtyard, staring outside like a wild mushroom growing there, still naively hoping her mother would come back for her.

She never did.

But she did wait for that handsome big brother.

Big Brother wore the uniform of his high school, a bag slung over his shoulder. Every evening, he would pass by the fence outside.

Each time, Shuangxu’s little mushroom head would turn like a sunflower, following him.

Finally, one day, he stepped across the lush green lawn toward her. He stood outside the wrought-iron fence of the garden, bent down, and stared at the unwanted little girl for a while before asking:

"Want to go with big brother?"

That year, Shen Yu was sixteen.

Outsiders only knew that she had been entrusted to the Shen family for care. But they all got one thing wrong.

The one who raised her wasn’t Mr. and Mrs. Shen Changyuan—it was Shen Yu.

---

chapters.title: If I Can’t Have You, I’ll Jump in the River
chapters.content:
At sixteen or seventeen, boys were at an age of reckless abandon—some raced cars, some chased girls, some smoked, got tattoos, or pierced their lips. Shen Yu, on the other hand, had taken in a little girl.

Everyone knew he treated this little sister like a treasure, spoiling her endlessly, giving her whatever she wanted, and taking her everywhere.

The little trash the Song family didn’t want had been raised like a princess by him.

When Shuangxu spoke to Lu Mànmàn about those abandoned years, she didn’t feel the slightest bit sad. The wounds inflicted by her birth family had all been healed by Shen Yu.

What pained her was that she felt she was being forced down a path where she would lose Shen Yu, pushed forward with no way to stop.

Sometimes she wondered if she had read too many love letters written to Shen Yu by girls, infected by some hidden virus in the words. Otherwise, how could she have fallen for her own brother?

When the whole world had abandoned her, it was Shen Yu who had picked her up and taken her home.

But what if one day, even Shen Yu abandoned her? What then?

She sat on a bench by the bridge, letting the wind blow over her for a while. The wind grew stronger, tousling her hair.

If only she could wake up and return to her childhood.

If only she never had to grow up.

A black sports car sped past her, then slowly reversed back a moment later.

The honking pulled Shuangxu out of her long daze. She turned her head in confusion and saw the black supercar parked by the roadside.

He Tingzhou rolled down the window. His gaze lingered on her red-rimmed eyes for half a second before sweeping behind her, raising an eyebrow.

"If I can’t have you, you’ll jump in the river? That’s some deep love."

A wave of absurdity crashed over her, shattering both her wind-blurred mind and the suffocating heaviness in her heart.

She turned her head away, but a few seconds later, she couldn’t hold back a laugh.

She laughed once, then immediately pursed her lips, pretending she hadn’t.

What kind of person was this? So random.

"Get in." He Tingzhou said.

Sitting in his car always made her uneasy. Shuangxu didn’t move.

"So, the river today—must jump, huh?" He Tingzhou crossed his arms and leaned back. "Go ahead. I’ll watch."

"I’m not going to jump. I’m just sitting here for a while." Shuangxu explained. "You don’t need to worry about me. I’ll go home by myself."

He Tingzhou seemed convinced that if she didn’t go with him, she’d find a chance to jump.

"Should I call your brother to talk you out of it?"

…

At the mention of Shen Yu, she relented. She sighed and obediently opened the passenger door to get in.

He Tingzhou didn’t start the car right away. Instead, he glanced at her from the driver’s seat for a while.

Shuangxu probably had no idea what she looked like at the moment—her hair messed up by the wind, her eyes red-rimmed. Together, it made her look like a child who had been bullied, not knowing who to turn to, sitting alone by the river.

She noticed his gaze and turned her head, confused. "What?"

"Waiting for you to cry."

He Tingzhou’s wrist hung lazily on the steering wheel, the tendons and veins prominent. His tone was mocking. "When are you going to start? Should I call ‘action’ for you?"

…Thanks a lot.

"I’m not going to cry." Shuangxu didn’t understand when she had given him the impression that she was a crybaby. She had never cried in front of him.

He Tingzhou’s lips twitched ambiguously. "You’ll go home and cry in your brother’s arms, right? How old are you? Still clinging to people."

Shuangxu opened her mouth, then closed it again. She had nothing to say.

It was true—when she was little, she had cried a lot. The moment she was unhappy, tears would fall without warning. No need to call "action."

She really didn’t feel like talking tonight. Rather than forcing small talk with He Tingzhou, it was better to just stay quiet.

The luxury sports car sped along the wide, straight road. The city lights blurred past the windows. The city’s millennia-old history, one person’s joy and sorrow—all just a grain of sand in the torrent.

At a traffic light, a pink G-Wagon pulled up beside them.

The passenger window rolled down, and a clear female voice called out: "Handsome."

Shuangxu looked over. A stylishly dressed woman leaned out the window, her figure stunning in a tight tank top. She was flirting with He Tingzhou.

"All alone?"

Probably because of the height difference and the darkness, she hadn’t noticed Shuangxu in the car.

"No." He Tingzhou propped his elbow on the window, his tone lazily improper. "A ghost."

…What the hell.

"Do you have a girlfriend?" the woman asked.

"Do you want me to?" He Tingzhou flirted with effortless ease.

The woman was skilled too, throwing him a sultry glance. "If you want one, you’ll have one."

In the half-light, He Tingzhou’s face carried a contradictory mix of coldness and warmth.

He chewed on a piece of candy lazily. "Forget it. Someone might get jealous. Then she’ll jump in the river."

Shuangxu: …

What does that have to do with me?

Handsome men were everywhere, but a stunningly beautiful, rich, and charming man driving a luxury sports car? That was rare.

The light turned green, but the woman wasn’t ready to give up so easily. She leaned halfway out the window and tossed over a card.

"I’m free all night. Call me~"

The card, smelling of perfume, fluttered onto He Tingzhou’s lap. He picked it up with two fingers. A phone number was written on it in black ink.

Shuangxu glanced at him. His expression was nonchalant—she couldn’t read anything from it.

But he didn’t throw the card away. He just held it between his fingers as he drove, occasionally tapping it lightly against the steering wheel when stopped at a red light.

Shuangxu turned her face toward the window.

Looks like she was delaying his romantic encounter.

A moment later, the car stopped in a dim, unfamiliar alley. Only the faint light from the buildings on either side illuminated the area. It was secluded and dark.

Where was this?

Why were they here?

The car door slammed shut. Shuangxu’s mind, lost in thought, jolted awake. In the quiet, late-night alley, a flurry of sensational headlines flashed through her mind.

Young Girl Found Dead in Alley at Night, the Killer Turns Out to Be…

Thump, thump—He Tingzhou knocked on the window.

Shuangxu rolled the window down a crack and peered out at him.

He Tingzhou was looking down at her, his tall figure silhouetted against the light. When their eyes met, it felt like jumping into an unknown abyss.

His brow bones were high, his eyes a mix of almond and phoenix shapes—sharp and narrow like a sword’s edge, yet the slight upturn at the corners gave them a hint of tenderness.

They stared at each other for a few seconds.

He Tingzhou finally spoke, slow and deliberate: "What are you doing, sneaking a peek at me through a crack? You don’t think I can see you, do you?"

Shuangxu: "…I was waiting for you to say something."

"Do I need to invite you to get out? You’ve got quite the princess attitude." He Tingzhou rested his right hand on the car roof, leaning in lazily. "Please, Your Highness."

… Shuangxu unbuckled her seatbelt and got out. "Where are we going?"

"To get a bowl of noodles."

Only then did she notice a noodle shop nearby. The old wooden sign had no LED lights, making it easy to miss at night. Only a small patch of warm light spilled from the entrance.

"I’m not hungry."

"I didn’t ask you." He Tingzhou said. "If you’re not hungry, just watch me eat."

Fine.

The shop tucked away in the alley had been around for years but was kept clean. Even before they got close, the aroma wafted over.

Shuangxu hadn’t realized she was hungry until the smell hit her. Her stomach reminded her that she hadn’t eaten dinner yet.

chapters.title: Missing
chapters.content:
He Tingzhou seemed to be a regular customer. The owner was an ordinary middle-aged man who brought up two bowls of beef noodles and chatted casually with him, "Haven't seen you in a while, been busy?"

He Tingzhou picked out the green onions from his bowl one by one. "Yeah, busy minding other people's business."

The owner laughed, not at all offended, and looked at Shuangxu with a kind gaze. "First time I've seen you bring someone. Such a pretty young lady, your girlfriend?"
