He Tingzhou didn’t deny it, sounding like a man afraid of a clingy woman. "She’s been making a fuss over me, what can I do?"

Shuangxu forced a smile under the owner’s slightly surprised expression, too lazy to explain.

Though the shop was tucked away and unassuming, the food was surprisingly good. The broth was rich and fragrant, and the noodles were hand-pulled, thin yet chewy.

A bowl of hot noodles warmed her up, chasing away the bone-chilling wind from the riverside.

Shuangxu ate until she was a little flushed, her nose slightly red. When she lifted her head, she found He Tingzhou watching her.

He hadn’t eaten much of his noodles. Leaning back in his chair, he idly played with the coarse ceramic teacup from the noodle shop, his long legs stretched under the square table, looking as if he were doing her a great favor.

"Good?" he asked.

Shuangxu nodded twice, curious. "How do you know about such a hidden place?"

"Haven’t you heard whose territory Yan City is?" His arrogance was as natural as breathing. "There’s nowhere in this city I don’t know."

Shuangxu blurted out, "Even the women’s bathroom?"

Only after saying it did she realize how bold she was being, daring to talk back to him.

He Tingzhou raised his right eyebrow slightly. "So chatty. Done eating?"

"Done." Shuangxu took a napkin and carefully wiped her lips clean. The lipstick she had applied earlier had long since faded, revealing their natural rosy hue.

He Tingzhou glanced over. "Then go pay."

"Me?" Her almond-shaped eyes widened slightly. It wasn’t that she was unwilling, but she hadn’t expected it.

Whether she was with Shen Yu or Yue Zifeng and the others, no one had ever made her, as the younger sister, pay the bill.

"Or should I pay?" He Tingzhou said with the self-righteousness of a big shot. "I picked you up from the riverside, took you home, and even treated you to noodles. Are you crushing on me, or am I crushing on you?"

...

"Didn’t bring money? If you can’t afford it, call your brother."

...

Shuangxu gave up and obediently took out her phone to pay.

Only when she opened her phone did she notice over twenty missed calls—from the driver, Uncle Wang, Fu Yun, and Shen Yu.

And there were pinned WeChat messages.

Brother: [Where are you?]Brother: [Xiao Jiu, answer the phone.]

She didn’t know what had happened. Just as she was about to call Shen Yu back, Fu Yun called again.

As soon as she answered, Fu Yun asked anxiously, "Shuangxu, where did you run off to?"

"I went shopping with Miss Lu, didn’t you know?" She was a bit confused.

"Old Wang said after dropping off Manman, he went back to pick you up but couldn’t find you. Your phone was off too. I was worried sick." Fu Yun’s tone was reproachful. "Child, why didn’t you answer your phone?"

She had been lost in thought by the river and hadn’t noticed the time. Only now did she realize that three hours had passed since she left the mall.

"I was in a meeting and had my phone on silent. I forgot to turn it back on." Shuangxu rubbed her forehead in frustration.

"Your brother drove out to look for you. Call him back quickly."

Shen Yu’s phone was picked up almost as soon as she dialed. Shuangxu called out, "Brother," then suddenly choked up, not knowing how to explain her "disappearance" that night.

There was a moment of silence on the phone before Shen Yu spoke, his voice still gentle. "Where did you go?"

"To eat noodles." Shuangxu said.

"Give me the address."

Shuangxu gave him the address of the noodle shop. Shen Yu said, "Don’t wander around. Wait for me."

Shuangxu responded with an "mm" and hung up, standing silently in place for a moment.

At this hour, there were no other customers in the shop. It was eerily quiet.

Remembering she hadn’t paid, she took out her phone again and asked the owner, who was preparing to close, "How much?"

The owner smiled kindly. "Mr. He has already paid."

Already paid?

Shuangxu turned her head. The seat where they had been was empty. He Tingzhou had left at some point without her noticing.

She walked out of the shop and found He Tingzhou leaning against his car, smoking.

Broad-shouldered and long-legged, his body was like a clothes hanger. The wind slightly lifted his shirt, and under the glow of the car lights, he exuded a carefree charm.

"My brother is coming to pick me up. I’ll wait for him here." Shuangxu thought for a moment before saying to him, "Brother Zhou, thank you for today."

Even though she hadn’t intended to jump into the river, her mood had indeed been terrible at the time. Having someone pull her back from the cold wind by the river and treat her to a steaming bowl of noodles—her gratitude was sincere.

Through the swirling smoke, He Tingzhou glanced at her, his response very much in character: "You’re welcome."

He stubbed out his cigarette, straightened up, got into the car, and the Koenigsegg roared away arrogantly, probably eager to rush off to some romantic rendezvous.

By the time Shen Yu arrived, it was twenty minutes later.

The owner, being kind-hearted or perhaps out of respect for He Tingzhou, waited until Shen Yu came to pick her up before closing.

The old alley was too quiet at night; it wasn’t safe for a young girl to be alone.

Shuangxu thanked the owner and got into the car. Shen Yu glanced at the simple and secluded noodle shop. "Why did you come all the way here to eat noodles?"

For some inexplicable reason, she instinctively hid He Tingzhou’s name. "A friend recommended it. The noodles here are really good."

"Did you come with a friend?" Shen Yu asked.

"Mm. He left first."

The car drove out of the alley and onto the asphalt road. After a moment of silence in the car, Shen Yu casually asked, "What did you talk about with Manman?"

"Not much." Shuangxu replied. "I went with her to buy a birthday present for her mother."

"What did you buy?" Shen Yu asked.

She hesitated. She hadn’t actually entered any shops that afternoon and couldn’t come up with a lie on the spot. "Coffee... shop."

She was lying, and she’d have to let Lu Mannan cover for her later.

When they returned to the Shen residence, the living room was brightly lit. Shen Changyuan, who had been on a business trip, had already returned. Fu Yun was still awake, waiting for them in the living room.

Seeing them return, Fu Yun finally let out a breath of relief. She couldn’t help but scold, "You ran off to eat noodles without even telling Old Wang. We couldn’t find you, and your phone was off. We were worried sick looking for you. You’re already grown up, but you still act like a child, doing whatever comes to mind without considering the consequences."

Shuangxu lowered her head in apology. "I’m sorry, Aunt Fu. I made you all worry."

Shen Changyuan patted Fu Yun’s shoulder to calm her. "It’s fine that she’s found. Shuangxu didn’t do it on purpose."

Then he said to Shuangxu, "Your aunt is just worried. When we couldn’t reach you, she was so anxious she paced around the house and even called your brother back."

Shuangxu nodded. "I know."

Fu Yun was still upset. "I’m not blaming you, but you need to be more responsible. It was just supposed to be a trip to buy a gift with Manman. Even if you were unhappy, you shouldn’t have..."

Shen Yu cut her off, reaching out to gently tap Shuangxu’s head. "Go upstairs and rest."

Shuangxu glanced at Fu Yun. Because of Shen Yu’s protection, Fu Yun’s expression darkened even more.

Shen Yu’s tone was calm. "Listen."

---

chapters.title: She Should Move Out
chapters.content:
That night, Shuangxu didn’t sleep well. Her dreams were fragmented, many of them scenes from her childhood.

When she woke up, the sky was bright. Sunlight streamed in through the curtains, casting a shimmering glow on the textured wallpaper, serene and quiet.

Shuangxu lay in her bed, looking around her room.

She had lived in the Shen household for ten years. Every lamp’s warmth, every tile’s pattern, was as familiar to her as her own blood. She could walk up the spiral staircase on the second floor with her eyes closed.

This place was a 15-minute drive from her high school. She had learned to swim in the pool here. The turtle she had impulsively decided to raise at twelve years old was still living leisurely in the pond in the courtyard.

The word "home" in her mind was personified by this house. But after turning eighteen, many things changed.

Those five years she was sent away were like a long desensitization process. And from the moment she returned to the country, the countdown to leaving this home officially began.

She should move out.

When Shu Yang learned of her plan, she didn’t comment, only silently offering support. "You can stay at my place first. You have my house key anyway. I have two rooms there. If you like it, you can live with me permanently."

Shuangxu understood her meaning. "Don’t worry, I have a place to go. I own an apartment at 9 Songming Road."

Shu Yang, who was taking medicine, almost choked on her water. She coughed twice. "9 Songming Road?"

"What’s wrong? Is there a problem with that place?" Shuangxu was a bit confused by her intense reaction. Had something happened at Songming Road in the past few years while she was away?

"The only problem is that the prices there are so absurdly high that us ordinary people can’t even dream of it." Shu Yang patted her chest to comfort herself.

"You still lack the extravagant habits of a rich young lady. I often forget that you’re actually loaded!"

"Do you have the nerve to say that?" Shuangxu huffed. "I spent my 20 million on a dog."

Shu Yang: "Woof."

"You’re ridiculous." Shuangxu laughed.

Shu Yang laughed too, then asked, "Have you talked to your brother about this?"

Shuangxu paused, fiddling with the empty plastic pill blister pack, tearing off all the foil. "I haven’t figured out how to tell him yet."

"It’s easy to come up with an excuse." Shu Yang saw through her. "The main thing is whether you can get past this hurdle in your heart."

It was normal for a grown child to move out and live independently, but Shuangxu’s situation was different. The Shen family wasn’t her real family. Moreover, there was the incident five years ago, which had always been an unspoken barrier between them.

Before Shuangxu could contact Shen Yu, he called first. "Keep your evening free. I’m taking you to meet someone."

In the evening, Shuangxu changed into a semi-formal but not overly dressy light blue gingham dress that fell just above her knees. The color was very spring-like, both elegant and lively. She wore a cream-colored trench coat over it when she went out.

At 7:05, Shen Yu’s car pulled into the courtyard. Shuangxu was already waiting at the door.

Shen Yu was on a work call, his gaze slowly falling on her through the car window.

Shuangxu jogged a few steps forward. The driver got out to open the door, and she bent down to get in, saying, "Brother, you’re late."

Shen Yu curved his lips. "Mm, what do you want this time?"

The subordinate on the other end of the call, who was reporting on work, asked in confusion, "...Mr. Shen?"

Shen Yu’s smile was still there, but the tenderness in his voice had disappeared. He was all business. "Send me a report later."

When Shuangxu was in school, she had a dedicated driver, but she always hoped Shen Yu would pick her up. If he was late, she would be unhappy, and he would buy her gifts to appease her. Over time, it became a habit.

Only after he hung up did Shuangxu speak.

"Brother, I want to move out."

Shen Yu was silent for a long time, the smile in his eyes slowly fading.

Shuangxu saw a hint of sadness in his gaze.

She opened her mouth to explain, but Shen Yu’s phone rang again.

He answered it, and the call lasted until they arrived at the restaurant.

The person Shen Yu took Shuangxu to meet was the director of the Yan City Aviation Research Institute.

During the meal with Director Xu, Shuangxu behaved impeccably.

Yan City, the capital of power, where every brick and stone was laid with authority. At the top of the pyramid were the aristocratic families like the He, Shen, Zheng, and Yue clans.

The old master of the Song family was also a prominent figure, but compared to the Shen family, he still lacked the deep-rooted heritage passed down from his ancestors.

Coincidentally, Director Xu and Song Mianzhi were high school classmates and had some personal connection. He remembered the daughter he often brought along, who was lively, clever, and a bit spoiled.

But he had never seen this one before.

The Song family’s affairs were unknown to outsiders, but among classmates, some inside stories had been heard. This eldest daughter was not the biological child of the current Mrs. Song.

But with Shen Yu there to back her up, no one dared to be neglectful.

Director Xu praised Shuangxu highly. "Women are rare in the aviation field. The hardships of this industry are invisible to outsiders. I didn’t expect Miss Song, such a quiet and gentle young lady, to have such passion and aspirations."

Shuangxu said, "I’m not quiet, and I don’t think I’m delicate. My brother has always supported me since I was little. I can try anything I like."

Director Xu laughed. "Then we really have to thank Director Shen for his encouragement, so we don’t lose a talent like you."

"In recent years, the drone market has developed rapidly. From agriculture to logistics and even the military, drones have unique advantages. The domestic prospects in this field are also very broad. Our institute has its own drone research and development team, undertaking many national-level projects. High-end technical talents like Miss Song, who have returned from abroad, are exactly what we need. If you have time in the next few days, you can come and visit our institute."

Shuangxu said, "Maybe."

The intention of tonight’s dinner was clear to both parties. Shen Yu wanted to arrange for his sister to work at their research institute. Being able to speak directly to Shen Yu, Director Xu naturally made everything clear.

But Miss Song’s response seemed to indicate a lack of interest in their institute? He subconsciously looked at Shen Yu beside him.

The latter’s expression didn’t change, but he slowly glanced at Shuangxu and subtly changed the subject. "I heard Director Xu’s son started his own business?"

"Yes, he’s loved cars since he was a child. He quit his stable job at the tobacco bureau and insisted on developing new energy vehicles with his friends. They’ve invested a lot of money, but there’s no sign of the car yet."

As soon as he mentioned his troublesome child, Director Xu sighed. Their family wasn’t like those wealthy families with deep pockets to squander.

"Recently, he’s been busy running around for loans. I haven’t seen him in days."

"Young people having this kind of ambition is a good thing." Shen Yu smiled slightly. "Later, I’ll say hello to President Zhou of Hengtai Bank. Have him submit his materials, and whether it works out depends on their company’s qualifications."

Director Xu was overjoyed and immediately raised his glass with both hands. "Then I really must thank Director Shen. I’ll toast to you on his behalf."

After the meal, the car ride back was quiet.

Shuangxu wanted to explain, but seeing Shen Yu’s closed eyes as he rested, she remained silent.

As they neared the Shen residence, Shen Yu opened his eyes and had the driver stop the car by the roadside.

He got out of the car and lit a cigarette, smoking slowly.

Shuangxu watched from the car for a moment before getting out and walking over. "Brother, are you mad?"

Shen Yu flicked his cigarette ash and looked at her in the night. "First you want to move out, then you refuse the job I arranged for you. Your wings have hardened, and you want independence, huh?"

"I just don’t like that job." Shuangxu said. "If I go there, I won’t have any real development. They’ll just treat me like a mascot, but what they’re really worshipping is ‘privilege.’ Maybe they’ll even mock me behind my back for being connected."

"Is privilege a bad thing? No one will bully you."

"Privilege is great when you can enjoy it." Shuangxu lowered her head and kicked a small pebble on the ground, falling silent for a while.

"What if one day, I no longer have you backing me up?"

chapters.title: I Am the Song Family’s Disgrace
chapters.content:
By then, she would be nothing.

The smoke in front of Shen Yu dissipated with the wind, and the night, fluid like water, spread into a deep ink color before his eyes.

"Cursing me? Does my life look that short to you?"

"I didn’t mean that." Shuangxu wanted to explain but didn’t know what to say.

Shen Yu’s voice seemed to carry the wind: "Xiao Jiu has grown up. Not like when she was little, always coming to her brother for everything."

Shuangxu’s nose suddenly stung, and the suppressed emotions surged like a broken dam, bursting through her eyes.

She wanted to say it wasn’t true, but she knew it was a lie.

From the moment she was sent away five years ago, she was no longer the same Xiao Jiu as before.

She hung her head, and large tears fell to the ground, silently disappearing.

Shen Yu stubbed out his cigarette, and his palm rested on her head, gently rubbing.

Shuangxu had beautiful long hair, like silk soaked in water, black and soft.

She didn’t like others touching it casually. Even Yue Zifeng, who used to idly ruffle her hair like Shen Yu, wasn’t allowed.

"If you don’t want to go to the institute, what do you want to do?" Shen Yu asked.

Shuangxu suppressed the sob in her throat and said steadily, "I plan to start a business with my senior."

Shen Yu neither agreed nor disagreed: "Want to start a business? Should I open a company for you to play with?"

Shuangxu shook her head: "My senior’s liquid hydrogen drone project really interests me. Feixue’s research strength is strong, and there’s still a lot of room for development in the future. I have high hopes for it."

Shen Yu didn’t dampen her enthusiasm and smiled: "Then I’ll wait for the day you ring the bell at your IPO."

Shuangxu hummed in agreement.

She remembered the conversation in the car that was interrupted by a phone call and hesitantly brought it up again: "Brother…"

"I’ll let you move out if you want to." Shen Yu knew what she was going to say. "The house on Songming Road was prepared for you."

Shuangxu felt relieved: "I haven’t told Aunt Fu yet."

Shen Yu soothed her by patting her head: "I’ll handle Mom."

She didn’t know exactly what he said to Fu Yun, but somehow, the matter of her moving out of the Shen family home passed Fu Yun’s approval without a hitch.

The house on Songming Road had never been lived in. The furniture was complete, but there were no daily necessities. She ordered the missing items online and had them all delivered.

She didn’t take much from the Shen house. The things she packed were sent over by the family driver.

Many old books would never be opened again. The wardrobe full of clothes, shoes, and bags belonged to her teenage years— not only were the styles outdated, but the sizes no longer fit.

Just like this room, it only belonged to the Xiao Jiu before she turned eighteen.

Shuangxu had originally wanted to take her pet turtle with her. She had already ordered a fish tank for the new home, but after searching the pond in the garden for a long time, there was no sign of the turtle.

She went to ask the servant who usually fed it: "Where is Gui Gui?"

The servant was also puzzled: "It was still here yesterday. It must be hiding in some corner again, being lazy."

This turtle often escaped, finding some nook or cranny to hide in.

Shuangxu said, "Then call me when you find it."

When Shu Yang heard she was moving, he said he wanted to help. He even snuck out of the hospital behind the doctor’s back.

Shuangxu’s reaction was cold: "If you can’t stay put and want to come out to have fun, just say so. Do you think I’d make you work? You’re more fragile than glass right now— one touch and you’ll bleed nonstop."

Shu Yang’s illness was like that— anemia, low platelet count, and once he started bleeding, it was hard to stop. He was also prone to repeated infections.

"Fine, I won’t pretend anymore." Shu Yang immediately collapsed weakly onto the new sofa. "I’m delicate right now. I can’t do any work. You two finish up quickly and order me some takeout."

Xiao Liao was hopping around the house like a rabbit, exclaiming as he went: "Oh my god, I’ve only seen a kitchen this shiny in TV dramas!" "Oh my god, this walk-in closet is bigger than the three-bedroom apartment at my house!" "Oh my god, this bathtub is big enough for four muscular men to bathe together!"

Shuangxu was unpacking the boxes she had brought from the Shen house when Xiao Liao suddenly pounced over: "Boss, rest a bit, let me do it!"

"I can do it myself. Haven’t you been running around for three rounds already? Aren’t you tired?"

Before she could finish, Xiao Liao snatched the box from her hands: "I’m young and strong."

"Who are you implying is old and weak?" Shu Yang lounged leisurely on the sofa. "Just give her a chance to show off. I think she wants to quit her job right now and come work for you as a nanny."

Xiao Liao looked embarrassed: "Hehe."

After all, what young person wouldn’t want to have their own room in a luxury duplex in the Third Ring Road?

Even if it was just a nanny’s room.

"I don’t need a nanny." Shuangxu thought for a moment. "But my turtle is missing. There’s an empty spot in the fish tank. Do you need it?"

Shu Yang laughed bitterly.

Shuangxu went to get them water. Buried in the boxes, Xiao Liao looked up and asked: "Boss, did you really win the city youth swimming championship?"

Shuangxu looked at the trophy she was holding, carefully wrapped in shock-absorbing foam: "Yes. I love swimming."

This was the longest-lasting hobby she had ever had. Shen Yu had even hired a professional swimming coach for her.

She had won many trophies growing up, but this was the only one she brought from the Shen house, which showed how much it meant to her.

"I won it when I was sixteen. It was my first swimming competition trophy, and my only one."

"Ah," Xiao Liao said, "so your talent was just a flash in the pan?"

Shuangxu laughed softly and raised an eyebrow: "I’m actually very strong. But after this competition, my dad explicitly forbade me from participating again."

"Why?"

"Because his work required the family to maintain a low profile, especially me." Shuangxu smiled indifferently. "I am the Song family’s disgrace. It’s best if I don’t appear in public."

After the competition, a photo of her holding the trophy with a radiant smile was published on the front page by the organizers. But the excitement of winning vanished when she received a transoceanic call from Song Mianzhi.

After all, Song Mianzhi didn’t even call her once a year. The only time he did was to forbid her from competing again.

Xiao Liao couldn’t understand: "Where’s the disgrace? You’re clearly so beautiful."

Shuangxu was taken aback for a moment, then laughed and collapsed onto the sofa: "Thank you for your novel perspective. I feel comforted."

Shu Yang also laughed uncontrollably: "How did someone with your IQ even get into a key university?"

"Great wisdom appears foolish," Shuangxu said.

"See!" Xiao Liao jumped up. "Only Boss understands how to appreciate me!"

The three of them laughed and joked as they unpacked. There wasn’t much, but they didn’t finish until evening.

This was probably the most relaxed moment Shuangxu had had since returning to China.

Xiao Liao volunteered to escort Shu Yang back to the hospital. Shuangxu saw them off at the entrance and watched the car drive away.

As she turned to go back, she noticed a stretched limousine parked by the roadside.

A driver in white gloves stood in front of the car, bowing to her from a distance before opening the car door.

Shuangxu’s good mood for the day plummeted.

She walked over and got into the car. The driver closed the door.

The Minister’s wife was an elegant woman, always dressed in tasteful Chanel suits, her hair immaculately styled, not a speck of dust on her shoes. The words "noble" and "graceful" were etched into every cell of her being.

She sat across from Shuangxu with poised demeanor, first glancing out the window at the luxury high-rise.

"This house is nice. Shen Yu is quite generous with you."

Shuangxu knew her visit wasn’t about the house: "If you like it, buy one."

Cui Ning finally spared her a glance: "Your arrogance as Miss Song is growing. It’s hard to even get a meeting with you. The Shen and Song houses are next to each other. You come and go from the Shen house every day, but you can’t spare a moment to visit your own home?"

Shuangxu: "I’m learning from Yu the Great."

Three passes by his home without entering.

Her indifferent attitude displeased Cui Ning, who asked directly: "When do you plan to return to the United States?"

---

chapters.title: Better Not Harbor Any Ill Intentions
chapters.content:
"I’m not ‘returning’ to the United States." Shuangxu said, "I don’t like it there. I’ve already quit my job abroad. I came back this time and I’m not leaving."

"Who told you to quit? Shen Yu or Fu Yun? Did you discuss such a big decision with me and your father?"

Shuangxu remained calm in the face of her displeasure: "I decided on my own."

"Without their permission, you dare make decisions on your own?"

Cui Ning seemed to assume someone from the Shen family was backing her up. She was most annoyed by Shuangxu’s closeness with the Shen family. How many times had she been stabbed in the back because of this, as if she couldn’t tolerate others and had pawned her child off on someone else.

"Don’t think I don’t know. Shen Yu wants to arrange for you to join the institute. Old Xu and your father are old classmates. He went over your father’s head to ask Old Xu to arrange a job for you. Does he not respect us at all?"

Shuangxu said, "If you’re unhappy that he went over your heads to help me find work, you can personally contact Director Xu to arrange something for me."

Of course, that wasn’t what Cui Ning meant.

Shuangxu knew, so she mockingly curled her lips. "Rest assured, I refused the job at the institute. But don’t get too happy—the reason I refused is because I plan to start a company with someone."

"You don’t need to take your anger out on my brother and Aunt Fu. I came back to China because I wanted to, and I’m staying because I want to. I’m an adult now. I’m free to do as I please."

Cui Ning’s expression turned colder: "Shuangxu, although I’m not your biological mother, I am your legal mother. No matter how good the Shen family is to you, if I want to send you away, there’s nothing they can do to help you."

Shuangxu knew that. Five years ago, that was exactly how she had been sent abroad.

"I’m not going anywhere." She was neither servile nor arrogant. "I’m not the helpless underage girl I was five years ago. If you want to put me on a plane, you’ll have to tie me up first."

Cui Ning’s eyebrows furrowed deeply. She truly hadn’t expected that a few years abroad would give Shuangxu such a rebellious streak.

She glared at Shuangxu displeasedly for a while, then regained her composed elegance. Her voice was haughty and cold: "You’ve really grown bold. Fine, if you want to come back, come back. I wouldn’t want anyone saying I can’t tolerate you. As long as you don’t cause trouble for me, I don’t care where you are."

"Understood."

Shuangxu got out of the car to leave. Cui Ning, still seated inside, said: "The marriage between the Shen and Lu families is about to be finalized. During this time, you behave yourself. Better not harbor any ill intentions."

What ill intentions could she possibly have?

Shuangxu didn’t respond. It was unclear if she had heard. She closed the car door and turned to walk back.

It was already nine o’clock. The bustling East Third Ring Road was a river of lights, but No. 9 Songming Road stood in serene isolation amidst the noise.

This luxury duplex was in an excellent location. It was Shen Yu’s eighteenth birthday gift to her.

Shuangxu had always known that the ones who forced her to go abroad five years ago were not only Song Mianzhi and Cui Ning, but also Shen Changyuan and Fu Yun.

That was why she had refused to return to China—for there was no home left to return to.

On her eighteenth birthday, spent in California, Shen Yu had flown over to see her. He transferred the house to her name, meaning to give her a place to return to.

She understood it all in her heart.

On the weekend, Shu Yang reserved a private room at a hotel for a company dinner. It was both a formal welcome for Shuangxu taking over as CEO of Feixue and a reward for the old employees who had stood by her through the storm.

Shuangxu went to pick up the custom-made cake, so she arrived at the hotel a little later than everyone else.

When she reached the hotel, Xiao Liao sent her a WeChat message: "Are you here yet? Are you here yet? Are you here yet? This lobster has been tempting me for ten minutes!"

Shuangxu laughed and replied with a voice message: "You start eating first."

As she spoke, she noticed an unfriendly gaze. She looked up and saw the man at the elevator turn around.

It was Chen Peiran again.

They met on a narrow path. The last time they saw each other, the smug and self-satisfied Director Chen now looked disheveled and dejected. His hair seemed unkempt for days, his beard was scruffy, and dark circles hung under his eyes.

"Shuangxu Song, I really underestimated you." Chen Peiran glared at her. "How did you convince He Tingzhou? Using your father?"

Shuangxu said, "It’s none of your business what I used."

Chen Peiran had spent a lot of money and time courting the director in charge of the drone division at Yun Dun. Just as the collaboration was about to succeed, at the last moment, that bald man suddenly stopped taking his calls.

This was a project he had submitted to Chengxing to prove his loyalty. Without it, he couldn’t establish himself at Chengxing. He had been so anxious that he developed blisters on his lips. It wasn’t until Chengxing’s people sarcastically told him to stop wasting his time that he learned Yun Dun had already signed a contract with Feixue.

Yesterday, a court summons had just been delivered to him. Feixue had hired a well-known lawyer in the industry to sue him.

Losing both the deal and face, that bald man was coming here today specifically to confront him. He hadn’t expected to run into Shuangxu.

"You never know what someone might use!" Chen Peiran vented all his anger on Shuangxu. "I’ve heard that the Song family doesn’t even acknowledge you as their daughter. They gave you away to be raised by others. Would your father really help you?"

"Shu Yang went through so much trouble and couldn’t secure the contract, but you came back a few days ago and already got He Tingzhou on board. I think you must have slept with him!"

Passersby around them looked over curiously. Shuangxu remained unmoved: "What does that have to do with you?"

Chen Peiran was furious, his bitter and sarcastic nature fully exposed: "Being pretty sure has its perks. Spread your legs, and all problems are solved."

Shuangxu frowned slightly, her voice cold: "Control your mouth. If you slander me again, I’ll add a defamation charge to the lawsuit."

"Do you think I’m afraid of you? What slander? If you didn’t sleep with him, why did He Tingzhou suddenly change his mind? He turned down a major company like Chengxing to work with a nearly bankrupt small company. He refused free offers and insisted on paying a high price. Is he crazy, stupid, or brain-damaged?"

Chen Peiran’s voice grew louder with each word. Just as his furious rant reached its peak—ding—the elevator across from them opened with a chime.

He Tingzhou appeared before him without warning.

A detached, leisurely voice asked, "Surprised?"

Chen Peiran, like a chicken whose neck hadn’t been properly wrung, suddenly fell silent.

Shuangxu followed his terrified gaze and looked back in surprise.

Inside the elevator stood several men in suits, each with increasingly peculiar expressions.

The man in the center had his hands in his pockets, his suit jacket pushed back to reveal a crisp white dress shirt and a taut waistline tucked into his trousers. He was the picture of debonair charm.

"Director He..." Chen Peiran’s face rapidly turned ashen. His lips trembled as he tried to salvage the situation. "I... I didn’t... Let me explain..."

He Tingzhou: "Straighten your tongue before you speak. It’s hard to listen."

"Director He, what a coincidence. Did you come here to eat in person?" Chen Peiran’s expression shifted to one of servility, the change so abrupt it was almost comical.

He Tingzhou said coolly, "If I don’t eat in person, should you eat for me?"

Chen Peiran’s face flushed red: "Director He, Yun Dun clearly agreed to collaborate with Chengxing. A verbal agreement is still an agreement. How come you turned around and signed a contract with Shuangxu Song? Aren’t you playing me?"

"Playing you? What are you worth playing with?"

The young master of the He family, raised under overwhelming power and privilege, didn’t hide his arrogance or domineering nature: "Even if I did play you, so what? What are you, anyway?"

Chen Peiran, after all, was a prominent young talent. His face, humiliated in public, was almost turning the color of a pig’s liver: "What’s so great about the He family?!"

He Tingzhou scoffed: "It is great. What, do you want to be a He too? Call me ‘Dad,’ and I’ll acknowledge you as my godson. My grandfather at home is waiting to hold his grandson."

"Pfft..."

A young man behind him couldn’t help but laugh. Chen Peiran, furious and embarrassed, glared at him. The man quickly composed his expression: "Sorry."

An untimely image popped into Shuangxu’s mind—Chen Peiran, pacifier in mouth, being held and soothed by Commander He...

She pressed her lips together, maintaining her calm expression.

chapters.title: Inappropriate Thoughts
chapters.content:
Chen Peiran's chest heaved violently. Seeing the man puff up like a pufferfish, he suddenly spotted a man with a Mediterranean hairstyle and pointed at him, shouting:

"President He, your company's Director Fan personally promised me a collaboration with Chenxing. He took so many benefits from me, but now he's going back on his word. No matter how powerful the He family is, you can't bully people like this!"

In broad daylight, Chen Peiran dumped a huge accusation on the He family. Cold sweat instantly broke out on Director Fan's forehead. He rushed over, pushing Chen Peiran, and scolded, "Think before you speak!"

He Tingzhou paid no mind to the crowd's gaze. With a condescending air, he took his right hand out of his pocket and pointed at Chen Peiran. His sharp, knife-like eyes swept over Director Fan's bald head.

"Handle him, or I handle you."

"I assure you, I will resolve this matter thoroughly!" Director Fan repeatedly guaranteed, dragging Chen Peiran away. "Let's settle this between us, don't cause a scene in front of President He!"

Shuangxu’s phone rang—probably Xiao Liao, who must be waiting anxiously.

Shuangxu said, "Brother Tingzhou, I’ll go now."

After saying that, she answered the phone while preparing to step past him to go upstairs.

He Tingzhou lowered his gaze, watching her figure pass by him. With a meaningful tone, he said, "So eager to sleep with me?"

In the phone, Xiao Liao’s "I'm alre—" was cut off abruptly, followed by a chorus of "Ooooh~ Ooooh~" as if a company retreat at Mount Emei was taking place.

Xiao Liao had put it on speaker!

He Tingzhou probably heard it too. "Are you calling a monkey?"

Shuangxu froze for a moment before quickly hanging up the phone she had answered less than ten seconds ago. She subconsciously glanced at the few men behind He Tingzhou.

The men immediately averted their eyes in all directions, looking at the ceiling, the floor, the air—wishing they could hang a sign on their heads that read, "I'm deaf, I didn't hear anything."

"I didn't..." She rarely felt so flustered. "I don't have inappropriate thoughts about you."

"Then how do you explain not clarifying when someone spreads rumors about you to your face?"

"It doesn't matter what he thinks if you say it's a rumor. There's no need to explain to him." Shuangxu forced herself to stay calm. "If others suspect something and I have to prove myself, isn't that letting them lead me by the nose?"

"Is that so?" He Tingzhou questioned. "Or is it because you, the toad, want to eat swan meat and deliberately create misunderstandings to spread rumors with me?"

"...You're the toad."

Shuangxu blurted it out and immediately regretted it.

In the past, she had only dared to complain in her mind. But ever since the last time they had noodles together, for some unknown reason, she had started to speak more freely with He Tingzhou, her mouth moving faster than her brain could control.

"Fine, you're the swan. You want to eat this toad. Happy now?" He Tingzhou didn't even bother arguing over such meaningless titles.

Shuangxu: "..."

He Tingzhou slowly said, "You should also manage your desire for me. It's so intense every day, I'm quite scared."

...Scared of what?!

The row of subordinates behind him all had expressions that said, "Ha, did I just hear something I shouldn't have?"

Shuangxu felt that even if she had ten mouths, she couldn't explain herself now.

Even when Chen Peiran had slandered her to her face, she hadn't been this speechless.

After saying that, He Tingzhou, with his hands in his pockets, walked past her with a leisurely stride.

Each subordinate followed behind him. As they passed Shuangxu, each one gave her a subtle smile that combined respect, caution, and tacit understanding.

She took a deep breath and walked into the elevator with a whatever, do-as-you-please attitude, pressing the close door button three times in a row.

As soon as she entered the private room, pairs of eyes shot toward her like searchlights. Her colleagues' gazes were one more ambiguous than the next.

"Oh my, who was that on the phone just now?~"

"It was a couple talking, and I just happened to pass by."

Shuangxu's calm and composed demeanor was quite convincing, but Xiao Liao didn't buy it. She had clearly heard another line...

Before Xiao Liao could question her, Shuangxu struck first: "I just ran into Chen Peiran downstairs."

Everyone's attention was instantly diverted: "What was he doing there? Such bad luck."

"That man has such short-sighted vision. If he had gone out and started his own business, others would have respected him. But instead, he went to lick Chenxing's stinky shoes. I look down on him!"

"In my opinion, it's good that a scumbag like Chen Peiran left. If he hadn't, our little boss wouldn't have come here."

While everyone was badmouthing Chen Peiran in unison, Shuangxu secretly let out a sigh of relief.

She really should have clarified immediately. If this rumor spread any further, the whole world would know about her secret crush on He Tingzhou.

Who knew that one moment of hesitation would lead to such a... steep turn of events.

Shu Yang squinted and leaned over to whisper in her ear: "That voice just now sounded a bit familiar. I couldn't place it at first. Who was it?"

"Don't ask." Shuangxu picked up her juice and took a sip. "Unless you're giving me 20 million right now, I won't say a word."

Shu Yang immediately took back her pulse: "Forget it, he's not worth 20 million."

The Shen and Lu families were of matching status. Shen Yu was outstanding among the younger generation, flawless in every aspect. Lu Mannan had also fallen in love with him at first sight. This match of equal social standing was readily agreed upon by both families, and the marriage discussions proceeded smoothly.

The first formal meeting between the two families was set for the end of the month.

Shuangxu had been raised in the Shen family since she was a child. Even if she didn't share their surname, she was still considered half a Shen. On such an occasion, she had to be present.

"Actually, I don't think it's a big deal if you don't go." Shu Yang said. "The Shen family raised you out of kindness, but you're just a dry sister. Not going wouldn't be considered impolite."

"But he's my brother." Shuangxu said. "How could I not go?"

Shu Yang was about to undergo her second round of chemotherapy. She had just had blood drawn and was lying in the hospital bed. She looked at Shuangxu with concern: "I'm afraid you'll have a hard time then."

"I'll have to get used to it eventually." Shuangxu was trying to learn to accept it.

If her liking Shen Yu was a small flower that sprouted during her girlhood, that flower had grown in barren soil and had long since withered. She was trying to uproot it.

Even if it wasn't Lu Mannan, it would be Zhang Mannan, Wang Mannan, or Li Mannan. She had to accept that Shen Yu would marry another woman.

That day, Shuangxu arrived at the restaurant ten minutes early. She wore a modified sleeveless qipao in a new Chinese style—black, formal, neither eye-catching nor inappropriate.

Fu Yun patted her hand and instructed: "Today is our first formal dinner with the Lu family. When you meet Uncle and Aunt Lu later, be polite, understand?"

She still didn't trust Shuangxu.

Shuangxu pretended not to notice and lowered her eyes obediently: "I understand."

It was at this moment that the Lu family arrived. Hearing the voices outside, Shuangxu turned her head and looked out the window.

At that glance, she froze.

Lu Mannan was also wearing a black qipao today. Although the style was slightly different, at first glance, both the dress and the hairstyle were too similar.

chapters.title: Must Not Embarrass Lu Mannan
chapters.content:
Fu Yun was clearly stunned. Her gaze shifted from Lu Mannan back to Shuangxu, her expression becoming difficult.

"What a coincidence."

Wearing the same outfit was embarrassing anywhere, let alone on an occasion like this.

When the two of them met face to face later, the scene would be even more awkward.

Shen Yu hadn't expected this either. He paused and comforted them: "It's fine, Mannan isn't petty."

"Even the most open-minded woman would mind wearing the same outfit, especially today." Fu Yun frowned, worried. "It would be embarrassing for her on our first meeting, and in front of her parents, they might feel uncomfortable too."

Shen Yu unbuttoned his shirt and took off his suit jacket, handing it to Shuangxu: "Wear this for now."

Fu Yun's frown deepened: "It's obvious this is your clothing."

Before Shen Yu could say more, Shuangxu stood up.

Today's main character wasn't her. She was very clear about that. It was the first time meeting the parents, and she couldn't embarrass Lu Mannan.

So it was she who needed to avoid the situation.

"I'll go find a change of clothes."

Fortunately, the private room in this Chinese-style restaurant had two doors. Before the Lu family entered, she quickly exited through the other side door.

She asked the manager if there were any emergency clothes available, but this request was too difficult for a restaurant. So she inquired about the location of the nearest women's clothing store and hurried out of the restaurant, intending to buy a new outfit on the spot.

As she lifted her skirt and stepped over the threshold, she almost collided with someone around the corner.

He Tingzhou supported her arm, steadying her so she didn’t bump into him.

Shuangxu took half a step back to steady herself. He let go of her hand and looked down at her with his casually dark eyes: "Throwing yourself at me?"

But Shuangxu had no time to argue with him today: "Brother Tingzhou, sorry, I'm in a hurry..."

As she spoke, she noticed the car behind He Tingzhou. The situation was urgent, and she couldn't afford to be polite: "I need to buy a change of clothes. Can you take me there?"

The driver had dropped them off at the restaurant. Today's meal would take at least two hours. Usually, they would use this time to eat elsewhere nearby, and calling him back would take time.

She didn’t have a domestic driver's license, and taking a taxi wouldn’t be as fast as having a ready car.

She rarely looked at him with such a pleading gaze. Even when she had discussed cooperation with him, she had always been methodical, discussing terms point by point.

He Tingzhou glanced at her.

The qipao itself wasn't particularly eye-catching. The dark embroidered orchids were faintly visible, clearly chosen for subtlety.

But the size fit her perfectly, the black fabric making her skin look as white as pearls. Her neck was slender, and she truly resembled a swan—her waist thin, her hips forming a graceful, undulating curve.

"Are you not satisfied with being this beautiful? Do you plan to dress yourself up as a celestial being to outshine someone?"

Shuangxu had no time to explain. Seeing he didn’t seem to have good intentions to help, she stepped past him and ran off to hail a taxi.

He Tingzhou leaned against the car door, crossing his arms: "The nearest mall is a fifteen-minute drive away. Round trip is half an hour. Are you sure you want to make the two families wait that long?"

"There's a clothing store to the east..."

Before she could finish, He Tingzhou said: "Mm, I passed by it on the way here. It sells sportswear."

...

This kind of occasion naturally wouldn't allow for sportswear.

Shuangxu stood frozen on the side of the road, wondering if she could just run away today. Would Shen Yu be disappointed in her?

He Tingzhou wasn't driving his sports car today, but a four-door sedan. He reached behind him and opened the car door, taking out a spare dress shirt from the car and throwing it to her.

Shuangxu quickly raised her hands to catch it. Looking at the men's dress shirt in her hands, it seemed there was no better option now.

"Brother Tingzhou, thank you."

By the time Shen Yu called, she had already returned to the restaurant with the clothes.

"I found a change of clothes, Brother. I'll be back as soon as I'm done. Don't worry."

There was a moment of silence on the other end of the phone before Shen Yu's voice came through, his emotions unreadable: "That's good."

Shuangxu asked a service staff for a changing room and scissors. She cut the qipao at the waist, turning it into a half skirt.

He Tingzhou's dress shirt was far too big for her. Fortunately, the silk fabric was light and had good drape, so it wouldn't look too exaggerated.

She rolled up the overly long sleeves several times and tied the hem into a knot. The white silk shirt paired with the embroidered half skirt actually looked decent.

Although it was a bit casual for today's occasion, it was the best she could do.

When she returned to the private room, the atmosphere inside was just right.

Mr. Lu wore a proper Zhongshan suit, his face kind and smiling. Mrs. Lu was much younger than Shuangxu had imagined, her hands well-maintained and delicate—clearly a woman who had been pampered and sheltered from a young age.

Her smile and the shape of her eyes were strikingly similar to Lu Mannan's. She praised Shuangxu warmly: "You're really quite striking. In my opinion, you're much prettier than those celebrities on TV."

Lu Mannan probably hadn't told her about her feelings for Shen Yu.

Shuangxu obediently smiled and said, "Thank you, Auntie."

She sat at the end of the table, with He Tingzhou sitting next to her.

He was Lu Mannan's cousin and today represented the He family.

Shen Changyuan asked Commander He: "It's been a long time since we last met. How is the Commander's health lately?"

"Fine. At sixty, he has the body of a twenty-year-old. He's even sturdier than me." He Tingzhou crossed his legs, maintaining his usual improper demeanor.

"How old is Tingzhou this year? I remember you're two years younger than Ah Yu."

"Twenty-eight."

Fu Yun said: "Then it's about time you settled down. You and Ah Yu are around the same age and good brothers. Getting married early would also allow the Commander to have a grandson soon."

Ever since He Tingzhou's mother passed away, Commander He had never remarried. While other wealthy families had numerous children and even illegitimate ones, the He family, despite their power, only had the cold and lonely father and son.

Already have one. Shuangxu thought to herself.

He Tingzhou leaned back in his chair, a smile playing at the corner of his mouth. That smile was extremely casual, floating on the surface without reaching his heart: "I don't have Shen Yu's good fortune."

This statement was a roundabout compliment to both parties, and it made everyone at the table smile happily.

Shen Yu smiled faintly: "Your good fortune is still shallow. Others wouldn't even be alive."

Shuangxu heard everyone laughing and joined in with a smile.

He Tingzhou turned his head to glance at her.

She was like a robot programmed with a certain routine—neither interjecting nor making grand gestures to reach for food. She just lowered her head, staring at the plate of spicy bullfrog in front of her.

Quiet, with minimal presence.

Only certain specific conditions—like the sound of everyone's laughter—could activate her program, causing her to react briefly before continuing to immerse herself in her own world, eating.

The shirt she wore looked like a regular oversized style, but the collar was clearly too big, revealing her delicate and exquisite collarbone. It was hard to tell whether her fair skin or the silk was softer and smoother.

He Tingzhou's gaze passed over that porcelain-like neck. Her long hair, which she had tied up, had now been let down, spreading across her back like another layer of satin.

"Can you help me remove the fish bones?"

Shuangxu looked up at the sound, seeing Lu Mannan tilting her head toward Shen Yu: "I love eating fish, but I always get the bones stuck."

Her tone carried a hint of coquettishness, just the right amount to not be annoying.

Shen Yu, of course, wouldn't refuse.

He was someone who made everything he did look pleasant, including removing fish bones. Shuangxu had seen it many times before.

The plate of white, tender fish meat was placed in front of Lu Mannan. She bent her eyes and said, "Thank you~"

Shuangxu lowered her head and continued eating the bullfrog.

The bullfrog was flavorful, with fresh and chewy meat, though a bit spicy.

As she ate, she heard the person next to her say: "Does one's own relative taste better?"

At first, Shuangxu didn't understand. She turned her head in confusion, meeting He Tingzhou's narrow, meaningful eyes. Slowly, she realized what he meant.

She looked at the bullfrog on her chopsticks...

Wasn't the bullfrog a relative of the toad?

She couldn't eat it anymore.

chapters.title: Where Do You Live?
chapters.content:
At the end of the banquet that day, Fu Yun gave Lu Mannan a very expensive set of jewelry as a gift.

The teardrop-shaped emerald was set in a diamond necklace, dazzling and radiant, along with matching rings and earrings, each piece worth tens of millions on its own.

Shuangxu had seen this set of jewelry in the wedding photos of her and Shen Changyuan; it was what she had worn on her wedding day.

"This was a gift from Grandma A Yu when I married Changyuan. Now I can finally pass it on to you."

To give such a family heirloom to Lu Mannan before the formal engagement showed how much Fu Yun approved of and valued her future daughter-in-law.

The Lu family was indeed delighted. Lu Mannan, feeling overwhelmed by the favor, stood up and threw her arms around Fu Yun's neck, coquettishly saying, "Wah, Auntie, you're too good to me! Should I change my address and call you Mom now? Would that seem too uninhibited?"

Fu Yun was so amused she almost bloomed like a flower.

Mrs. Lu laughed and scolded, "You, you have no shame."

"I have nothing to be ashamed of; I'm too happy for that." Lu Mannan immediately took off the necklace around her own neck. "This necklace is so beautiful, A Yu, help me put it on."

Shen Yu took the necklace and helped her put it on.

Lu Mannan's joy was overflowing, her eyes shining like stars. The elders all looked on with satisfaction.

Shuangxu, sitting across the table, felt like she was in the audience of a theater, watching a happy play under the spotlight that had nothing to do with her.

Fu Yun and Mrs. Lu repeatedly praised how good it looked on her. Lu Mannan specifically asked Shuangxu again, "Xiao Jiu, does it look good?"

Shuangxu said, "It looks good."

Lu Mannan smiled, her eyes brimming with joy. "If you say it looks good, then it must really look good."

Perhaps happiness witnessed by a rival would be even more wonderful.

Shuangxu thought to herself, I should have said it looked bad to annoy her.

Mrs. Lu, seeing this, thought they were close: "You two really get along well."

"We're the same age," Lu Mannan said, "so we have a lot in common."

Shuangxu didn't feel they had much in common at all.

Her life trajectory with Lu Mannan's did not overlap at all. They lived in different eras of Yancheng. The parental love Lu Mannan had was something she never had. The fear of abandonment she felt was something Lu Mannan had never experienced or understood.

The only common ground between them might be their similar taste.

After the banquet, as they left the Wangchun Building, Shen Yu and Lu Mannan walked ahead.

Lu Mannan, clinging to Fu Yun's arm, coquettishly called her "Auntie" repeatedly, making Fu Yun beam with joy.

Shuangxu walked at the back, with He Tingzhou in front of her.

He Tingzhou had his hands in his pockets, walking lazily, slowly creating some distance from the group ahead.

On the covered walkway, while the people ahead couldn't hear, Shuangxu thanked him: "Brother Tingzhou, thank you for your help today."

She had worn his shirt, so He Tingzhou probably wouldn't want it back.

"How much was your shirt?" she asked sincerely. "Or should I buy you a new one?"

He Tingzhou turned his gaze to her: "And then let you justify keeping this one?"

"...Why would I keep your shirt?"

"That's a question for you," He Tingzhou said lightly. "What do you want to do with my shirt."

"I'm not that perverted." Shuangxu felt she had become numb. Soon, she might even accept that she was a toad.

"Then I'll wash it and return it to you."

In the car on the way home, Fu Yun looked at the completely transformed outfit Shuangxu was wearing, which no longer resembled a qipao at all.

"Where did you get that in such a short time?"

"I borrowed it." She answered vaguely.

"If it were just a normal dinner, it wouldn't matter if you bumped into someone. But today is special; I'm sorry for the inconvenience." Shen Changyuan's tone was somewhat apologetic.

"It's fine." Shuangxu's expression was calm. "As long as it didn't affect everyone's mood."

"You and Mannan have similar tastes. It's quite a coincidence that you wore the same thing."

Shuangxu just smiled and didn't say anything.

After returning home, she took He Tingzhou's shirt to the dry cleaner. She originally wanted to ask Shen Yu for his WeChat but decided to ask Yue Zifeng instead.

Yue Zifeng asked, "What do you want with Brother Tingzhou's WeChat?"

Shuangxu came up with a half-true excuse: "Last time at Wangyue Building, he left his shirt behind, and I need to return it to him."

Yue Zifeng knew about the dinner at Wangyue Building with the Shen and Lu families. He didn't think much of it: "Just throw it away. Brother Tingzhou's clothes are disposable; he never wears the same thing twice."

She could throw it away, but she didn't want to do that cow a favor.

Shuangxu said, "I can't just throw it away; I'll let him throw it away himself."

Yue Zifeng forwarded He Tingzhou's business card: "I've already told him, so you can add him directly."

He Tingzhou's profile picture was of water—clear, rippling water. Like the sea in the Maldives, a very pure light blue.

It was completely different from his usual demeanor.

Shuangxu sent a friend request, which was quickly accepted.

[Brother Tingzhou, I've washed your shirt. How should I return it to you?]

He Tingzhou replied concisely: [Bring it over.]

Shuangxu: [Then I'll bring it to your company tomorrow morning.]

He Tingzhou: [So you're looking for any excuse to spread rumors with me? Should I hold a press conference for you and buy some paid articles to announce it to the world?]

Just how many women had pursued him for him to be this sensitive?

Shuangxu had no choice but to say: [Then I'll bring it to your house. Where do you live?]

He Tingzhou sent her a location: [Bring me a cake.]

From the sound of it, he wanted her to bring it over now.

Since she had borrowed his shirt and he had helped her out greatly last time, Shuangxu had no complaints.

She didn't know his taste, but he seemed to like blueberry mousse, so she randomly bought one from a store on the way.

The address He Tingzhou gave her was a villa in Yanxi. When Shuangxu arrived, the entire villa was brightly lit but completely silent, without a single sound.

The door opened automatically. She walked in with the cake and the shirt. The living room had a high ceiling of 6 meters, spacious and open, with floor-to-ceiling windows facing a neatly trimmed lawn. Outside, there was a large swimming pool filled with water, reflecting the courtyard lights.

There wasn't even a housekeeper at home. Shuangxu didn't dare to move around freely. She sat in the living room and waited for a while, planning to send He Tingzhou a message saying she had delivered the items and would leave.

Before she could finish typing, she heard slow, dragging footsteps from the second floor.

He Tingzhou looked as if he had just taken a shower. He was wearing a black round-neck sweater and casual pants. His short hair was damp, and the relaxed home atmosphere softened his sharp aura.

"Brother Tingzhou." Shuangxu stood up and greeted him. Then she saw a Doberman with erect ears following behind him.

She wasn't afraid of dogs, but such a robust, adult carnivorous animal was inevitably intimidating.

Dobermans were inherently fierce, and He Tingzhou's looked particularly strong. Its weight might even match hers.

He Tingzhou walked over, and the Doberman followed.

He Tingzhou sat down on the sofa to her left, opened the cake, and started eating with a fork. "Sit."

Shuangxu was just about to sit down when He Tingzhou said, "I was talking to the dog."

"...Oh." Her butt was suspended in mid-air, unsure whether to sit or stand.

Just as she was thinking of leaving directly, the Doberman walked around the coffee table and sat down to her right.

The dog had a stern and majestic expression, staring at her motionlessly.

Shuangxu's body stiffened slightly. She reassured herself that pet dogs were usually well-trained and wouldn't bite people randomly.

But who knew? He Tingzhou himself had no manners... No, what she meant was, if He Tingzhou wasn't a good person, how could his dog be any good?

She stared at the Doberman, and the dog stared back at her. After a moment of standoff between the human and the dog, she was the first to look away.

Just as she was about to concede and look away, the dog came over and sniffed her, then licked her hand with its tongue.

"Ah!" Shuangxu almost jumped up, instinctively moving a big step toward He Tingzhou.

---

chapters.title: I’m Not Blushing, Why Are You?
chapters.content:
He Tingzhou leisurely enjoyed his cake, ignoring the situation.

Shuangxu looked at him, trying to get him to control his dog: "It's licking me."

He Tingzhou didn't even lift an eyelid: "It's hungry."

...?

If it's hungry, it should eat dog food.

Shuangxu was exasperated. She moved a little more, placing her hand on the side far from the dog, secretly grateful she was wearing long pants today.

"Don't you have... dog food at home?"

He was only feeding himself, not the dog, leaving it so hungry it had to lick people.

"No."

"Then what does it usually eat?"

He Tingzhou finished half the cake, put down the fork, and lazily leaned back, lifting his gaze to glance at her. "Meat."

She knew he was a jerk who liked to tease her, but Shuangxu was genuinely a little scared.

She decided to leave immediately, standing up from the sofa: "I'll go now."

He Tingzhou neither agreed nor disagreed. Leaning on the leather sofa, he supported his temple with his index finger and looked at her indifferently.

Shuangxu looked left and right, caught in a dilemma.

To her left sat He Tingzhou, and to her right sat the dog. To leave, she would have to pass by either the man or the dog.

After hesitating between He Tingzhou and the dog for a moment... Should she climb over the back of the sofa? Or jump over the coffee table...

Forget it, that would be too undignified.

"Brother Tingzhou, can you make it move away for a bit?" she said. "I can't get out."

He Tingzhou, indifferent, had no intention of helping: "Talk to it yourself."

...

Shuangxu looked at the fierce adult Doberman and politely attempted to communicate: "Can you move aside?"

The dog didn't indicate whether it understood.

The dog lay down on the spot.

Shuangxu let out a long sigh and walked toward He Tingzhou.

At the very least, He Tingzhou wouldn't bite her.

The distance between the sofa and the coffee table was enough for one person to pass through, but He Tingzhou had stretched his legs out, almost blocking the entire path.

He sat comfortably like a gentleman, with no intention of moving his precious feet.

Shuangxu didn't want to ask him again to move his noble legs. She lifted her leg and carefully sidestepped over his legs.

Her front foot landed steadily, but her back foot unexpectedly caught on him, causing her to suddenly lose balance and fall forward.

He Tingzhou watched coldly from the side, making no move to help.

The instinct to break a fall didn't have time to consult the brain. In her panic, Shuangxu instinctively braced herself with her hand.

Only when she came to her senses did she realize her hand was pressing against He Tingzhou's thigh.

He Tingzhou glanced down, then lifted his gaze.

Shuangxu unexpectedly plunged into the dark, whirlpool-like depths of his eyes.

"You fell quite naturally." He Tingzhou raised an eyebrow. "Does it feel good to touch?"

Controlled by the will to survive, her hand regained its sense of touch as he spoke. The muscles under her palm were firm and hard, almost allowing her to imagine their fierce explosiveness.

Shuangxu immediately pulled her hand back as if scorched, her cheeks burning as she apologized: "I'm sorry."

He Tingzhou stared at her deeply, but his expression was extremely casual: "I didn't blush when you touched me. Why are you blushing?"

"I didn't mean to touch you." Shuangxu secretly moved her hand behind her back, a futile attempt to cover up.

"You're the one who wouldn't let me pass."

He Tingzhou's lips curled up slightly: "Pass where?"

Two very ordinary words with no hidden meaning, yet for some reason, Shuangxu's face burned even more. Maybe it was because of those eyes.

He Tingzhou had high brow bones and deep-set eyes, making his eyes particularly cold and sharp. Most of the time, they gave off a distant, aloof feeling.

But as soon as they held a hint of a smile, they became full of affection, incredibly charming.

"The shirt is returned, and the cake is my treat. We're even. Goodbye." She turned and left as soon as she finished speaking.

He Tingzhou watched her retreating figure, which concealed a hint of panic beneath its composure. The dog also watched her back.

After Shuangxu's figure disappeared, He Tingzhou withdrew his gaze, and the dog lay down on the floor out of boredom.

Shuangxu had never been in a relationship in her life. Her feelings for Shen Yu had just begun to sprout but never had the chance to be expressed before being nipped in the bud.

No matter how calm and steady she appeared on the surface, at her core, she was still an untouched blank slate.

As she left the house, she pressed her palm against her cheek, manually cooling herself down.

He Tingzhou knew she liked Shen Yu. That phrase "love unrequited" had been painfully sharp.

Shuangxu also knew he had been mocking her all along, but why did the situation feel like it was going off the rails?

Wait... Could He Tingzhou really think she had shifted her affection and was secretly in love with him?

Back at her home on Songming Road, as she was about to sleep, she scrolled through her Moments and saw Lu Mannan's new post.

Lu Mannan had been hanging out frequently with Yue Zifeng and his friends lately. As Shen Yu's fiancée and He Tingzhou's cousin, she naturally received a lot of special treatment.

Coupled with her outgoing and enthusiastic personality, it was easy for Miss Lu to win others' affection.

She was quickly integrating into Shen Yu's circle.

That had originally been Shuangxu's circle as well.

It would be hypocritical to say she welcomed it, but it wasn't exactly rejection either. It was more like a damp, indescribable mist spreading in her chest. It didn't cause pain, but it silently dampened her clothes.

Shuangxu liked the post and swiped past it.

She really wanted to talk to Shu Yang, but it was too late. Shu Yang was probably already asleep. Chemotherapy took a huge toll on the body; each session could take half a life.

She truly had few friends. If it weren't for Shu Yang's unexpected entry into her life, she would have resisted making friends.

So now, even if she wanted to find someone to talk to, there was no one.

She used to have a close girlfriend with whom she shared everything, but in the end, the secrets she shared became knives plunged into her back.

Shuangxu put her phone aside and forced herself to close her eyes and sleep.

She saw Lu Mannan again at the hair salon. Shuangxu was getting a trim and was about to leave when a group of chattering women entered.

Lu Mannan and Song Leyan were surrounded by a group of socialites, including the pair of twins she had seen at Shen Yu's birthday party.

"Leyan, isn't that your sister?" someone noticed her first.

Song Leyan was two years younger than Shuangxu. Her appearance was half like Cui Ning and half like Song Mianzhi, while Shuangxu had completely inherited her mother's features.

However, Song Leyan was spoiled and willful, with none of Cui Ning's grace. At just twenty years old, her pretty but arrogant face rolled her eyes as she hugged her arms and said disdainfully, "Don't talk nonsense. I'm an only child; where would I get a sister?"

Her friends, who always flattered her, chimed in, "That's true. Neither your grandfather nor your father acknowledges her."

"Director Song was even transferred abroad without taking her. Her own mother didn't want her. You tell me, she must be pretty annoying if even her own parents don't want her."

Shuangxu couldn't be bothered to respond, not even sparing them a glance.

Lu Mannan spoke up for her: "You're being a bit harsh. Xiao Jiu is my friend."

The twins immediately warned her solemnly, "Mannan, don't be fooled by her innocent appearance. You consider her a friend, but you don't know what she thinks about Shen...".

Shuangxu, who had already reached the door, stopped in her tracks and turned to look at them.

chapters.title: Unrepentant
chapters.content:
"Don't you have a memory? Do I need to repeat what I said last time?"

Shuangxu's tone was indifferent. The twins, still haunted by the slap from last time, immediately shut their mouths in fear.

"You don't have to be afraid of her," Song Leyan sneered. "I'll get that slap back for you sooner or later."

Shuangxu looked at her with cold eyes. "No need to wait. You can take it now. Do you want me to slap you that badly?"

Song Leyan scoffed. "Song Shuangxu, do you dare hit me?"

She had been spoiled and domineering since childhood. She was the one who hit others, never the other way around.

Shuangxu said, "Why wouldn't I dare? Do you have thorns on your face?"

"After being exiled abroad for a few years, your mouth has gotten sharper," Song Leyan's eyes were filled with malice. "Last time, you couldn't even speak, just stood there pale and trembling."

The group of bejeweled young ladies behind her all revealed smug, expectant expressions.

Lu Mannan didn't show disdain, but she stood among them.

This scene coincidentally overlapped with one from five years ago.

Shuangxu stood opposite them, and for a moment, it felt like she was back at the welcome party that had thrown her into hell.

When she was sent to the Song family, Song Leyan had already followed Song Mianzhi to settle in Europe. The two of them had barely even seen each other since they were young.

She had never received any affection from the Song family, nor any of their wealth. She didn’t care for either, and had never intended to compete with this sister.

Theoretically, if they could mind their own business, they could coexist peacefully.

But Song Leyan refused to let that happen. If it weren't for her provocation, Shuangxu wouldn't have been sent away five years ago.

That year, Song Mianzhi was transferred back to Yan City, and Song Leyan returned with him. To welcome her, someone hosted a party. Shuangxu received an invitation. She didn’t want to go, but Fu Yun said Song Leyan had just returned, and she should give her face, that the sisters should get along.

So she went.

Many people attended that day—daughters of prominent families in Yan City were all gathered. When Shuangxu arrived, she noticed everyone looking at her strangely. She was confused until she saw her best friend standing behind Song Leyan, avoiding her gaze guiltily.

In front of everyone, Song Leyan laughed and said, "You like Shen Yu, huh? He treats you like a sister. You want to have an affair with your own brother? How shameless."

That day, just like today, Song Leyan looked down on her with disdain, backed by a group of supporters, mocking and ridiculing her for having indecent thoughts about her own brother.

They said Shen Yu was perverted, maybe even a pedophile.

At that moment, Shuangxu felt like she had been stripped naked and thrown into the sun, exposed for all to see.

She had cautiously liked Shen Yu, and before she even had the chance to tell him, she was humiliated in this way.

From that day on, rumors began to spread.

To suppress the rumors, Cui Ning publicly acknowledged her as his goddaughter. Due to the face of the Shen and Song families, the rumors were suppressed and didn’t spread widely.

But Song Mianzhi was furious. He sent someone to take her from the Shen family, locked her up, and as soon as the paperwork was done, sent his disgraceful daughter abroad.

Shuangxu pinched her stiff fingertips. "You dare bring that up."

Song Leyan defiantly huffed, "If you dared do it, why can’t I bring it up?"

"Exactly," her lackey chimed in. "You have no shame, so why would you be afraid of us talking about it?"

"How do you have the face to come back?"

"It was all rumors." Lu Mannan's lips curled up slightly, though her smile was faint. "A Yu and Xiao Jiu are very close siblings. Let's not spread rumors anymore, okay?"

The group of lackeys looked at her and shut their mouths awkwardly.

If Lu Mannan hadn’t been here today, Shuangxu would have definitely slapped her.

Lu Mannan could see that too. She said to Shuangxu, "Xiao Jiu, do it for my sake, okay?"

Shuangxu looked at her for a moment, then raised her hand and delivered a solid slap to Song Leyan's face.

Song Leyan let out a cry and covered her face. The twins behind her instinctively flinched to the side. The others looked at each other in shock and fear—no one expected Song Shuangxu to have the guts to hit Song Leyan.

"Song Shuangxu, are you crazy? You dare hit Leyan. Aren’t you afraid Song Director will kill you?"

"Then I’ll kill her first."

Shuangxu shook her sore right hand and said to Lu Mannan, "I can give you face, but this slap was owed from five years ago. I can’t let it go today."

"Next time, then." She said.

Lu Mannan was stunned.

This side of her was completely different from the gentle and quiet Xiao Jiu she knew in front of Shen Yu.

Song Leyan, still covering her face, stared in disbelief. Shuangxu put her hand into her coat pocket, turned around, and walked away with a flourish.

The group of women angrily said, "How did she become so arrogant?"

"She’s only arrogant because Shen Yu backs her up."

"Manman, you better watch out for her. She definitely still has designs on Shen Yu!"

Lu Mannan watched Shuangxu’s retreating figure and said nothing.

The slap felt good, but it didn’t improve Shuangxu’s mood much.

Even if she gave Song Leyan ten slaps, it wouldn’t turn back time.

The predicament she was in now was all thanks to Song Leyan.

This half-sister was like poison—any contact with her made Shuangxu feel annoyed.

Returning to the house on Songming Road, the entire place was silent. She stood in the entryway for a while, feeling as if everything was unfamiliar.

The lamp, the sofa, the solid wood dining table, and the empty fish tank.

She called the Shen family and asked if her turtle had been found. Wang Ayi answered, "I’ve checked all the places it usually stays, but there’s no sign of it. It’s really strange."

Great, even the turtle had abandoned her.

Unwanted trash.

Wang Ayi then asked if she was getting used to living there, her tone worried: "It would be better to come back home. You’re all alone there, and there’s not even a hot meal when you return. The madam said she could hire an auntie for you, but you refused."

Shuangxu didn’t like living alone with a nanny—childhood trauma.

She smiled indifferently, "I lived alone abroad for five years. I’m used to it. It’s fine."

Wang Ayi fell silent.

After hanging up, Shuangxu buried her face in the down pillow. Just as she was about to suffocate, the phone rang.

"Little sister, asleep yet?" Yue Zifeng’s voice always sounded cheerful.

"Not yet."

"Then go to bed early. Tomorrow, we’re taking the yacht out to sea."

Without a doubt, Shen Yu and Lu Mannan would be there.

Shuangxu casually made up an excuse: "I get seasick."

"What seasick? You never got seasick with me. Did you practice swimming in the waves for nothing?" Yue Zifeng said, "You haven’t been out with us lately, and you won’t even come out for meals. Did you have a fight with your brother?"

"It’s not that—" Before Shuangxu could finish, the phone was taken by someone else.

Then, Shen Yu’s clear voice came through: "What’s wrong?"

Shuangxu sighed in resignation. "Nothing. Tomorrow, I have to visit my senior first. I’ll meet up with you all later."

---

chapters.title: Uninvited Guest
chapters.content:
The sky over the sea was low and blue, clear and pure, lifting everyone’s spirits.

The sea breeze hit their faces, bringing a refreshing, moist air.

The harbor was filled with rows of sailboats and yachts. Among them stood a super yacht over a hundred meters long, pure white, majestic like a magnificent giant building.

A crew member in white gloves carried her luggage. Shuangxu boarded the ship via the gangway, where Yue Zifeng was waiting for her on the deck.

"Ah, our little Song has finally arrived." Yue Zifeng led her into the cabin, teasing, "Don’t forget about me when you become successful someday."

Shuangxu removed her earphones from her ears. "What did you say?"

"Forget it, I talked for nothing." Yue Zifeng shouted again in the wind, "I said your brother has someone to take care of him now, but I don’t. In the future, remember to support me in my old age. My later years are entrusted to you."

Shuangxu wasn’t about to take on that responsibility. "Why not have your own sister support you?"

"My sister isn’t as reliable as you." Yue Zifeng scoffed, "She puts sand in my food every day. When I’m old, she’ll probably feed me shit."

Shuangxu remembered his sister as a two-year-old when she left the country—she had even held her. She didn’t expect the little girl to grow up to be so capable.

She couldn’t help but laugh. "Having food to eat is already good. Why be picky?"

"See, you look so much prettier when you smile." Yue Zifeng said as they walked inside, "You used to smile so much as a kid. America must be a man-eating place to have eaten away all of little Shuangxu’s smiles."

Only then did Shuangxu realize Yue Zifeng was deliberately trying to cheer her up.

She had thought he had noticed her recent unhappiness, but after entering the cabin, she realized there was another reason.

The luxury of this super yacht was beyond imagination. The deck had a helipad and accommodated small yachts and mini submarines. The interior included a cinema, a gym, and other entertainment facilities. At the stern, there was a huge swimming pool—like a luxurious castle on the sea.

The first-floor living room was spacious, with a gorgeous crystal chandelier hanging from the ceiling. At the moment, everyone was gathered here, drinking and chatting.

In addition to the people Shuangxu expected, there was also Song Leyan.

Song Leyan was sitting with Lu Mannan. Upon seeing Shuangxu, she gave her a "just you wait" look and silently humphed at her.

Yue Zifeng knew the sisters didn’t get along. Normally, they didn’t have much interaction with Song Leyan either—there was a generational gap, and they weren’t close. Moreover, they knew about the time Song Leyan had led the bullying against Shuangxu.

They had never taken Song Leyan’s nonsense seriously. That girl was like a little gangster, always forming cliques. Shuangxu, on the other hand, was someone they had watched grow up—there was a clear distinction between familiarity and estrangement.

"Give her some face for Manman’s sake." Yue Zifeng lowered his head and gently coaxed, "You don’t have to pay attention to her. We’re all here. She can’t bully you."

"It’s fine." Shuangxu was annoyed by her, not afraid.

As for Lu Mannan bringing Song Leyan, she didn’t mind.

She had never expected Lu Mannan to understand her. People could only truly empathize with experiences they shared. Lu Mannan and she were not the same kind of people.

Lu Mannan and Song Leyan were the same kind—darlings of their fathers, precious treasures taken along on business trips, the apple of their family’s eye. That was why they could be friends.

Shuangxu greeted Shen Yu and the other brothers. Her gaze lingered for a moment when it passed over He Tingzhou.

He Tingzhou had an effortless arrogance no matter where he was. He occupied an entire sofa by himself, a magazine covering his face as he slept.

The cover girl was seductive, obscuring his three-dimensional, noble face.

Disgusting.

But what made Shuangxu’s body tense involuntarily was that today, he was wearing a very familiar white silk shirt.

It was almost identical to the one she had borrowed before.

She was afraid Shen Yu or Lu Mannan would recognize it.

But men’s shirts were all more or less the same style. He Tingzhou seemed to favor this kind of comfortable, skin-friendly fabric. She couldn’t be sure it was the same one.

Yue Zifeng had said he never wore the same clothes twice, right? Maybe it was just a similar style.

Shen Yu and Lu Mannan didn’t react, so it was probably just her overthinking.

This matter was like a hair dropped on her nerves—too small to grasp, but she knew it was there, occasionally causing slight disturbances.

Shuangxu’s gaze kept flickering toward He Tingzhou.

Everyone was drinking, chatting, and laughing without restraint. The noise was so loud that no one could possibly sleep, right?
