She curiously asked in a low voice, "Won’t this disturb him?"

Yue Zifeng said it was fine: "He likes to sleep with people talking around him."

She had seen many light sleepers who needed silence, but this was the first time she had encountered someone who used human voices to help them sleep.

It was nearly evening, and the clouds were dyed a gradient warm orange by the setting sun.

Yue Zifeng checked the time. "Alright, everyone’s here. Let’s set sail."

He had just informed the captain when a series of footsteps came from the deck.

"Going out to sea today, and you didn’t even call me? More people make it livelier."

A carefree voice entered the cabin. Shuangxu felt a familiar sense of annoyance and turned around.

The man wore a pair of triangular sunglasses and a flashy printed shirt with beach trousers. He pushed the sunglasses up to his forehead, revealing a face that made Shuangxu frown.

After many years, Zheng Zuye’s roguish thug demeanor hadn’t changed one bit.

Someone politely called out, "Young Master Zheng." Old Master Zheng was formidable, and even if this grandson was a troublemaker, he wasn’t someone to be trifled with.

"I was wondering whose yacht was so flashy parked here. Turns out it’s acquaintances. Were you waiting for me?"

Yue Zifeng clicked his tongue. "What wind blew you here?"

"Of course, the fragrant breeze from your big yacht." Zheng Zuye invited himself in and sat down on the sofa, spreading his arms wide behind him and propping his left leg over his right.

Yue Zifeng looked at Shen Yu in exasperation, then at He Tingzhou.

Shen Yu’s expression was extremely calm, showing no emotion.

He Tingzhou was sleeping soundly on the sofa, completely unaware of the uninvited guest.

In Yan City, the major families of He, Shen, Zheng, and Yue jointly occupied the same land, connected by shared interests, but privately, they had different circles.

For example, Yue Zifeng, Zuo Zhong, and Shen Yu were childhood friends with the closest relationship. They had become familiar with He Tingzhou later, but their group had never mixed with Zheng Zuye.

Not for any other reason—just that they looked down on him, couldn’t get along, and weren’t the same kind of people.

This guy was a bastard, but now that he was here, they couldn’t exactly throw him off the ship.

Zheng Zuye seemed determined to stay. Yue Zifeng wanted to kick him out, but since they were all prominent figures, they had to consider the Zheng family’s face.

If there was one person on this ship who would dare throw Zheng Zuye off, it would be the unrestrained He Tingzhou.

Unfortunately, that guy was fast asleep.

Just then, the gangway outside began to retract—the ship was about to depart.

Well, even if they wanted to leave, they couldn’t now.

chapters.title: Demanding a Kiss
chapters.content:
He Tingzhou slept until mealtime before waking up.

A crew member came to announce that dinner was ready. Yue Zifeng was about to call him when he lifted the face of the sexy woman on top of him and slowly sat up.

"Damn," Yue Zifeng said, "you sure know how to wake up."

"Hungry."

He Tingzhou, still sluggish, picked up a cigarette case from the table, took out a cigarette, held it between his teeth, and lifted his eyelids slightly toward Shuangxu. "Lighter."

Shuangxu had been staring at the shirt he was wearing, and upon hearing his voice, she looked up. After a two-second stare, she realized he was talking to her.

What a spoiled young master, used to being waited on hand and foot. Would it kill him to reach out himself?

Shuangxu handed him the lighter from the table not far from her. He Tingzhou lit his cigarette and tossed the lighter back to her. She hastily caught it with both hands to keep it from falling.

It wasn't her lighter anyway. What was the big deal if it just stayed on the table?

She got up and followed the others to the dining room. Zheng Zuye caught up from behind her. "Long time no see, little beauty."

"Don’t provoke me." The disgust in Shuangxu’s brows was unmistakable.

When she was fifteen and still underage, this man had already been leering at her. Shen Yu had protected her, and old Mr. Zheng had personally scolded him before he finally backed off.

Zheng Zuye grinned. "Just saying hello. Why so tense?"

Shuangxu ignored him and quickened her pace.

Zheng Zuye’s eyes roamed over her.

Shuangxu’s beauty wasn’t just in her features. Every part of her—her hair, eyebrows, teeth, shoulders, even the proportions of her legs and the curve of her ankles—was flawless.

There were plenty of women more glamorous and sexy than her. Zheng Zuye had played with many so-called innocent ones, but none had her unique allure.

She wore a gray-green blouse and a black skirt, the shirt tucked into the waistband. It was nothing special—office workers dressed like this all the time—but her waist-to-hip ratio was undeniably captivating.

With his experienced eye for women, Zheng Zuye estimated her measurements: 88-56-88.

He licked his teeth and muttered to himself, "That waist would feel amazing to grab."

"Your neck would feel amazing to grab too."

A flat voice came from behind. Zheng Zuye turned to see He Tingzhou walking past him with an air of indifference.

Dinner on the yacht was five-star quality. Afterward, there was a party. Shuangxu returned to her room to rest for a while, changed clothes, and when she came out, she ran into Song Leyan in the hallway.

The moment Song Leyan saw her, she remembered the slap from last time. Her face had hurt for days, and being hit in front of so many people had been humiliating.

"Last time, you slapped me and I haven’t paid you back yet."

"You’ve come to the wrong place for that." Shuangxu looked at her. "You can’t pay me back here."

Song Leyan gritted her teeth. On this ship, everyone was Shen Yu’s friend, and they all treated Song Shuangxu like a treasure. She was the weak one.

"If I hadn’t gone to Europe with my dad for ten years, you’d be nothing. Do you really think you’re some little princess of Yan City? Don’t you see how people look at you? You’re the shameless one, forcing yourself on Shen Yu."

Shuangxu’s eyes turned cold. "If you can’t learn how to speak properly, I’ll teach you again."

Song Leyan scoffed. "You should manage yourself first. You like Shen Yu so much—do you think Lu Mannan would ever accept you? She has the Lu family backing her up. What do you have? You can’t seriously think Shen Yu would offend the Lu family for you, can you? If he had to choose between you two, who do you think he’d pick?"

"You worry about who he picks," Shuangxu said coldly. "It’s not you, so why do you care?"

Song Leyan, who had been smugly certain she’d hit a nerve, was left speechless.

Shuangxu turned to leave, and as she passed her, she dropped a line: "Lay off the salt."

It wasn’t until Shuangxu was long gone that Song Leyan realized she’d been mocked. Furious, she jabbed her elbow into the wall, only to wince in pain and clutch her arm.

The yacht had already reached international waters. The dark blue sea and sky blended into one, and the sound of waves carried laughter.

Everyone gathered at the stern club. The champagne tower exuded fragrance, and the symphony orchestra played a magnificent waltz.

Some drank, some danced—everyone was in high spirits.

He Tingzhou lounged in the sofa area. No matter where he was, he carried an air of effortless dominance, as if the whole world belonged to him. He propped his feet on the coffee table, lowered his gaze, and typed on his phone with one hand, not sure who he was messaging.

Shuangxu took a glass of champagne and found a seat across from him. Just as her eyes flicked toward He Tingzhou’s shirt again, she was caught in the act.

He Tingzhou tossed his phone onto the sofa. "Like looking so much? Come over and take a closer look."

Shuangxu couldn’t very well explain that she suspected he was wearing a shirt she’d worn before—that would sound too self-important. She took a sip of her drink to change the subject.

"Brother Tingzhou, aren’t you going to dance?"

He Tingzhou’s brow twitched meaningfully. "Are you inviting me to dance?"

...Had her Chinese deteriorated from living abroad? Which part of that sentence sounded like an invitation?

No, her Chinese was fine. It was He Tingzhou looking at her like a 360-degree panoramic toad.

Shuangxu was a little distressed. He couldn’t actually have misunderstood, could he?

That would be troublesome.

Just as she was agonizing over how to clarify the growing misunderstanding, Yue Zifeng came over and called her. "Sis, come dance!"

Shuangxu shook her head. "I’m not dancing."

Her refusal was ignored. Yue Zifeng simply dragged her away. "Sitting here is no fun. Come on, let me show you your brother’s charming dance moves!"

Yue Zifeng had no shame. His exaggerated, goofy movements made Shuangxu laugh brightly.

When everyone was tipsy and tired from dancing, they returned to the sofa area to rest.

Shen Yu beckoned her over and handed her his phone, which was in a video call with Fu Yun. Shuangxu held the phone and chatted with Fu Yun for a while before hanging up.

Someone suggested playing Avalon to pass the time. Yue Zifeng took out a deck of cards. "Avalon’s too much brainwork. I’m tired. Let’s play King’s Game."

One joker and ten numbered cards. The one who drew the joker (the King) could order the holder of any number to do something.

The first two rounds were played with some restraint. In the third round, He Tingzhou drew the joker.

Shuangxu’s sharp eyes caught a glimpse of He Tingzhou’s card. She quickly flipped her own card face down to prevent him from seeing it and using it as an excuse to mess with her.

A soft snort came from beside her. He Tingzhou had seen her little move.

She interpreted that snort as "delusional."

He Tingzhou had no interest in her at all. He glanced at Yue Zifeng and issued his order: "Take a swim around the ship."

Everyone else called out card numbers, but he arrogantly called out a person.

"Still the toughest." Yue Zifeng stood with his hands on his hips, waving his own card. "You want me to go parade around? If you’re so capable, guess what card I have."

He Tingzhou smirked. "The mirror behind you is reflecting it."

Yue Zifeng immediately turned to look. Sure enough, there was a decorative mirror on the shelf behind him.

He Tingzhou lazily lifted his chin. "Go on, then. Ten of Hearts."

Yue Zifeng: "Damn it!"

The crowd cheered as they gathered on the deck. Yue Zifeng downed a glass of wine to warm up, took off his shoes, and cursed as he jumped in.

When he finished his swim and came back, dripping, the game truly entered its uninhibited phase.

Party games were all about the thrill. Shuangxu used to love watching them shamelessly mess with each other, happily enjoying the show from the sidelines.

But she never expected to see Shen Yu in such a game.

Lu Mannan drew the joker. She had to choose a man from those present to kiss.

Yue Zifeng squinted teasingly. "Ooh, who do you want to pick? I bet it’s Shen Yu."

Lu Mannan’s cheeks were flushed, whether from the alcohol or shyness. But even her shyness was bold and unashamed. Amid the good-natured jeers, she tilted her face up to Shen Yu, asking for a kiss.

---

chapters.title: All Comers Welcome
chapters.content:
Shuangxu was sitting right next to Shen Yu. She could clearly see the expectant, radiant look on Lu Mannan’s face.

But she couldn’t see Shen Yu’s expression, nor the way he looked down at Lu Mannan.

It was probably gentle.

"Shen Yu, you’re not going to kiss her?" Yue Zifeng itched to push their heads together.

"Come on, man."

"Playing innocent, huh?"

Amid the teasing from his friends, Shen Yu gave a faint smile and leaned down toward Lu Mannan.

At the same moment, Shuangxu lowered her eyes, refusing to watch.

She stared at the floor, suddenly feeling the gentle sway of the ship on the waves. But that shouldn’t be—this yacht was so large, so steady.

He Tingzhou glanced at her. She was lost in her own world, completely unaware, and thus missed the flicker of boredom in his expression.

"Who’s the Ace of Spades? Step forward, don’t think you can hide."

Yue Zifeng’s shout snapped her out of it. She looked up to find the game had moved to the next round, and everyone was searching for the next unlucky victim.

Shuangxu caught a gaze from across the table. Song Leyan, holding the joker, gave her a meaningful look. "I’m the King, you know." She spoke while staring at Shuangxu. "Ace of Spades, step forward yourself."

Shuangxu noticed something and reached for her own card. On the back, she felt a slight crease—someone had marked it.

Yue Zifeng searched around and finally looked at the last person. "Little Shuangxu, it’s not you, is it?"

Shuangxu flipped her card over. It was the Ace of Spades.

The triumph in Song Leyan’s eyes was obvious. She repeated the task: "Pick someone to your left or right. Use your mouth to pass the card."

The lively scene suddenly fell silent. All eyes were on Shuangxu.

To her left was Shen Yu. To her right was He Tingzhou.

Song Leyan had deliberately put her in a difficult position.

Passing a card with your mouth meant the two people’s lips would be pressed tightly together with only a thin card between them. It was almost as intimate as a direct kiss.

She knew Shuangxu liked Shen Yu. But would she dare choose him?

If she chose He Tingzhou—who didn’t know about this young master of the He family’s temper? He didn’t give face to anyone, not even the Emperor. If he publicly rejected her, she’d be humiliated beyond recovery.

Lu Mannan’s gaze also fell on Shuangxu, seemingly curious about her choice.

Shuangxu unconsciously tightened her fingers.

Clink—the light sound of a glass being placed on the table broke the tension. Shen Yu’s expression was extremely indifferent, his voice devoid of emotion. "It’s getting late. Let’s call it a night."

Yue Zifeng played along. "Right, I need to go take a hot shower before I catch a cold."

Song Leyan refused to back down. "Everyone else played. Why can’t she? Passing a card isn’t that big a deal. You were just feeding grapes mouth-to-mouth to some beauty earlier. What’s the problem now?"

Yue Zifeng was silenced.

"It’s fine." Shuangxu said.

Zheng Zuye swirled his glass, smirking. "Or you could pick me. I’d be happy to help."

She’d rather pick a pig than Zheng Zuye, that scoundrel.

Shuangxu picked up a playing card, bit it between her teeth, and turned to the right.

So much for my toad reputation, she thought. It was about to be confirmed.

Song Leyan was about to correct her—this wasn’t how you passed a card—when Shen Yu’s gaze swept over.

That look was quite cold. She shut up.

He Tingzhou was sprawled lazily on the sofa, motionless, his face bored.

Shuangxu leaned toward him. He watched her approach with cold eyes, showing no intention of cooperating.

Those sharp black eyes held only indifferent apathy.

As if he were watching a play that had nothing to do with him—her predicament, caught between a rock and a hard place, and the forced calm that still betrayed her unease through her eyes.

She was the clown on stage. He was one of the spectators below.

Shuangxu had expected him not to give her an easy way out, but she hadn’t expected such coldness and humiliation.

She had never done anything like this before. With all those eyes on her, she knew Song Leyan was gloating, knew Shen Yu was watching.

Her face flushed, not from shyness, but from embarrassment.

Forget it. Let it be. Everyone saw. It was He Tingzhou who refused to cooperate, not her being unable to play, not her clinging to Shen Yu hopelessly.

She was about to pull back when He Tingzhou hooked an arm around her waist and pulled her close.

Shuangxu, caught off guard, tumbled into his arms. Before she could react, He Tingzhou held her and, under her startled gaze, lowered his head. His teeth closed around the other end of the card.

In that moment, Shuangxu almost felt his breath intertwining with hers. His nose brushed against hers, so light it might have been her imagination.

The heat in her cheeks skyrocketed. Shuangxu realized she had forgotten how to breathe.

She saw He Tingzhou’s lashes. They were surprisingly long.

That thin, cold eyelid suddenly lifted. She crashed, unprepared, into He Tingzhou’s dark, profound pupils. Her heart jolted violently.

She could almost feel his body heat. That arm around her waist, the faint pine scent that usually clung to him—now, like a thin mist, enveloped her entirely.

The entire ship seemed to fall into a deathly silence, leaving only the sound of waves crashing against the hull.

Someone’s glass slipped from their hand, shattering on the floor. The noise startled Shuangxu, and she quickly pulled away from He Tingzhou’s embrace.

He Tingzhou turned his head, spat out the card, and leaned back against the sofa.

Lu Mannan was also surprised. This cousin, whom she had never dared to approach all her life, had actually cooperated with Shuangxu in the game.

But then again, men were probably all the same. When ambiguity came knocking, they never refused.

She shifted her gaze back to Shen Yu. His expression was unchanged, as usual.

But as her eyes swept past, she noticed his hand on the armrest. His knuckles were white with tension.

chapters.title: Is Your Affection Such a Precious Thing?
chapters.content:
"Wow~~~"

"Zhou Ye, you're something else!"

Yue Zi squinted so hard her eyes nearly popped out: "Just catch the card, why are you holding Shuangxu's waist?"

He Tingzhou looked lazy and indifferent: "How else am I supposed to catch it? Or should you do it instead?"

Shuangxu could hear them teasing He Tingzhou, but their voices, though entering her ears, couldn't be processed by her brain. She didn't catch a single word they said.

Her fingers pressed against the edge of the sofa as she stared blankly at the patterns on the floor, waiting for the heat on her face to slowly fade.

The game ended, and the people at the stern dispersed. As Shuangxu stood up, she met Shen Yu's gaze.

"This kind of game doesn't have to be played." Shen Yu spoke, his voice still gentle. "Don't force yourself next time."

Shuangxu nodded: "Mm."

Only then did she realize that He Tingzhou had left at some point.

She turned to leave the stern, while Shen Yu sat back on the sofa and lit another cigarette.

Yue Zi patted his shoulder a couple of times. As an older brother, he understood an older brother's feelings best. Even as an adult, who wouldn't want to flip the table seeing their sister playing such games with someone?

"It was just a game, and your sister didn't go overboard."

Song Leyan had hoped for a good show. Though the outcome wasn't as exciting as she'd imagined, seeing Shuangxu's expression, she must have felt terrible doing that in front of Shen Yu, hahaha.

Yue Zi glanced at her: "I'm telling you, stop bullying your sister. She didn't do anything to you."

"Playing a game counts as bullying?" Song Leyan scoffed. "You're the one who called her to play. So you're the one bullying her."

Yue Zi clicked his tongue: "You little brat, no one likes you."

This remark made Song Leyan's face fall: "Who cares if you like me? What do you think of yourself?"

Shen Yu, with a cigarette between his fingers, rested his arm on the armrest. His demeanor was calm and composed, but his voice carried an unusual chill in the sea breeze.

Without even looking at Song Leyan, he lowered his eyes to flick off the ash and said to Yue Zi: "Send her off the ship tomorrow morning."

Shuangxu walked along the ship's side passage for a while. She walked slowly, and the chatter and laughter of the people ahead gradually faded. Some were still not satisfied and made plans to go to the spa or find a place for another drink.

Others, who had just hooked up today, reluctantly went into their rooms together.

When she returned to the third floor, she saw He Tingzhou on the deck.

This deck was empty, and the light was dim. As she approached, she saw a tall figure standing by the railing.

He Tingzhou was smoking. The strong sea wind pressed his silk shirt tightly against his body, and the smoke dispersed between his fingers in the shape of the wind.

Shuangxu had initially intended to go straight back to her room but, after a moment's thought, walked over to him.

"Tingzhou Ge."

The wind at sea was strong, and her voice was soft. He Tingzhou turned his gaze.

Her long hair was blown into a messy dance, the deep and dark hues of the sea contrasting with her fair skin. Her delicate and clear features looked like a meticulously painted fine brushwork painting.

He Tingzhou: "What's up?"

Shuangxu could sense his unusual coldness today, though she didn't understand the reason.

Of course, He Tingzhou had never been warm to her.

"Thank you for giving me a way out during the game just now."

She chose her words carefully: "Actually, I... I don't have a crush on you, nor do I have any improper thoughts about you. I was afraid of causing any misunderstandings for you, so I wanted to explain. I didn't explain before because I thought you already knew..."

She didn't finish.

"What misunderstanding?" He Tingzhou asked.

"That I like you."

He Tingzhou slowly took a drag of his cigarette, tapping it with his fingertips. The falling ash disappeared into the sea. His tone was light and slow: "Is your affection such a precious thing?"

Shuangxu was taken aback.

He Tingzhou said: "Aren't you using me to cover your tracks? Why expose it? Aren't you afraid your little secret will be discovered?"

It seemed she had overthought it.

He had been teasing her all along, and she had actually worried he might misunderstand.

She brought this humiliation upon herself. How stupid could she be?

"You didn't misunderstand, so that's good."

After saying this, she turned and walked away. He Tingzhou watched her back, his expression unreadable.

Shuangxu reached the stairs and then turned back. Biting her lip and furrowing her brows, she returned to stand in front of him: "Have I offended you? Why do you always mock me?"

She didn't want to offend him, but those words really hurt.

So casually said, yet far more hurtful than anything Song Leyan had said.

Song Leyan targeted her because she disliked her, but why did He Tingzhou do it? She didn't understand.

Shuangxu had been grateful to him. For the way out today, and for his help on several previous occasions.

That bowl of hot noodles had made her think the distance between her and He Tingzhou had closed a little. Occasionally, she dared to be bold in front of him, voicing her inner complaints. Only now did she realize how much she had overestimated herself.

He Tingzhou countered: "When did I mock you?"

"How is my affection not precious?" Shuangxu questioned. "What gives you the right to say that about me?"

He Tingzhou leaned against the railing, one long leg propped up: "Whether it's precious or not, ask your brother. Why ask me? You like him, not me."

"What does whether I like my brother or not have to do with you? He is the best person to me in this world. What's wrong with me liking him? What did I do wrong?"

Perhaps her emotions had risen and fallen too many times, suppressed to a critical point, or perhaps He Tingzhou's sharp words had truly hurt her. She suddenly couldn't hold back.

"So righteous. Why don't you go tell him yourself?" He Tingzhou's eyes were dark and cold, his voice devoid of warmth as he glanced toward the ship's cabin behind her.

"He's probably still awake. Let me call him out for you. How about you confess to him in person?"

"This is my own business, none of your concern!" Shuangxu tightened her pale fingers. "I haven't hurt any of you."

He Tingzhou crushed his cigarette and threw it into the trash bin.

"Then don't act like everyone has hurt you."

"What kind of expression have I been making?" Shuangxu's voice trembled slightly in the sea breeze. "Everyone is on guard against me, everyone can use this to control me. If I want to return home, I have to consider many people's feelings. Who am I putting on a show for? Who cares if I'm wronged?"

The dim light from the ship's lanterns fell into her moist eyes. He Tingzhou saw the redness at the corners of her eyes, her gaze at him like an injured yet stubborn rabbit, or a wild lily drenched by rain.

After the anger, Shuangxu suddenly remembered from his cold attitude that he was Lu Mannan's cousin.

He and Lu Mannan rarely interacted and weren't close, so much so that she had forgotten he was her cousin. But without a doubt, he would stand on Lu Mannan's side.

Thus, the surging anger in her chest slowly subsided, replaced by a belated clarity as she calmed down.

What was she, arguing with He Tingzhou here?

She admitted she was prone to crying, but she knew tears were only cherished by those who cared about you.

So she suppressed all her emotions.

"I'm sorry, I forgot. You're Miss Lu's cousin. You defend her, find me redundant, and that's understandable."

He Tingzhou didn't speak. His pupils were dark, and the look he gave her was like the distant, dark sea surface, with no visible waves.

"In your eyes, I'm just an unrelated, threatening dry sister. Even if I've done nothing. It's fine, I understand. If I were in your position, I'd dislike me too, as a stumbling block."

"You don't have to worry. I won't ruin my brother's life. I hope for his happiness more than any of you."

After saying these words, she turned and walked away against the wind.

---

chapters.title: Can't Even Ask for Help?
chapters.content:
The soundproof materials ensured absolute silence in the cabin. The suite was even more luxurious than a hotel.

Shuangxu sat on the edge of the bed for a while, wide awake, and decided to go out for some air.

Even in early May, the sea could still be cold, but the pool water was surprisingly warm.

Her slender body moved like a nimble fish, swimming freely in the water.

After swimming back and forth several times, until she was tired, she floated on her back on the water's surface, looking at the thick, dark blue night sky.

She slowly let herself sink, submerging into the water.

All the world's sounds were blocked out. The buoyancy felt gentle and peaceful, enveloping her, supporting her, protecting her.

Shen Yu's significance to her was like this body of water.

She tried to imagine, if years ago, when she was crying on the street, Shen Yu hadn't stopped, what would have happened?

Would she have been kidnapped by a bad person, or met another kind soul?

If Shen Yu hadn't taken her away from the Song family, would she have been left to fend for herself there, developing a twisted and sick personality, or one day dying alone in that empty house with no one knowing?

Tonight was moonless. If she disappeared, probably everyone would feel relieved and happy.

At the limit of her breath, Shuangxu surfaced, wiping the water from her face. The previously empty poolside now had a man standing there.

Zheng Zuye's bright eyes stared straight at her: "Swimming so late at night, too lonely to sleep?"

Shuangxu instantly lost interest. She swam to the other side and grabbed the ladder to get out.

She had come swimming purely because she was in a bad mood after arguing with He Tingzhou and acted on impulse. She hadn't changed into a swimsuit.

Her black dress was soaked and clung to her body. As she bent down to pick up a towel, Zheng Zuye's blood boiled with excitement.

She wasn't a voluptuous beauty, her figure was slender, with a very thin waist, but it didn't detract from the parts that should be curved or perky. Her ankles were delicate, and her skin was tender all over.

Shuangxu draped the towel over herself and was about to enter the cabin when Zheng Zuye walked around the pool and grabbed her wrist.

"Where are you going in such a hurry? Let's chat."

"I have nothing to say to you."

Shuangxu tried to pull her wrist free but couldn't. Zheng Zuye's bold eyes raked over her body.

"Haven't seen you in years, how did you get even more seductive? Hmm? Developed? Damn, Shen Yu's luck is really something!"

"Don't tarnish my brother with your vulgar and dirty thoughts." Shuangxu couldn't break free, and her wrist hurt from his grip. She coldly shouted: "Let go!"

During the struggle, the towel around her fell off. Soaked and glistening, her angry stare made Zheng Zuye's heart race.

"Stop pretending to be pure. Shen Yu keeps you by his side every day, hasn't he touched you?"

Shuangxu raised her other hand to strike, but Zheng Zuye caught that too, then leaned in to sniff her neck: "You smell so good."

The alcohol he had drunk all night rushed to his lower abdomen, fueling his desire. He couldn't wait to take her right there.

Shuangxu never expected him to be so bold, daring to touch her under Shen Yu's nose.

"My brother is still upstairs. How dare you touch me!"

"Your brother is busy in bed with Lu Mannan. He doesn't have time for you. By the time he comes down, I'll already be done with you."

"Do you think if you succeed tonight, he'll let you off tomorrow?"

"Tonight, I'll take care of you first. Tomorrow's problems can wait until tomorrow."

Zheng Zuye had done far worse things outside. As long as his grandfather was alive, no one could do anything to him.

Shen Yu was refined and too polite, unlike He Tingzhou, who acted purely on whim. Zheng Zuye knew his ground. Even if this was Shen Yu's territory, if Shen Yu wanted to kill him tomorrow, his grandfather would still protect him.

At worst, he'd get another beating. So what? He'd enjoy himself first.

Shuangxu kicked and hit him with her hands and feet, but she had just come out of the pool, without shoes. Her tender feet kicking his legs didn't hurt him much.

She struggled with all her might but was still easily controlled by Zheng Zuye. The disparity in strength between a man and a woman made her feel utterly desperate at that moment.

Instinctively, she turned her head toward the cabin, hoping someone would notice her, but on the vast yacht, no one could hear the commotion here.

Suddenly, she saw the figure by the railing upstairs.

Like seeing a savior, she instinctively called out: "Tingzhou Ge!"

Zheng Zuye paused, then looked up.

The salty sea breeze blew as He Tingzhou's tall figure stood by the railing on the third floor, hands in his pockets, his downward gaze indifferent.

Shuangxu even clearly saw the disgust in his eyes.

He had been there all along. He had seen, but he clearly had no intention of intervening.

Zheng Zuye, seeing that He Tingzhou had no intention of ruining his fun, relaxed: "You called the wrong person. Even if I kill you tonight, he won't save you."

A chill froze Shuangxu's heart. The words for help stuck in her throat. She opened her mouth but couldn't make a sound.

It was understandable.

He had no obligation to save her.

She was pushed against the railing by Zheng Zuye. In her struggle, her foot hit a protruding metal point, and the sharp pain instantly forced out physiological tears.

Just then, two crew members ran out of the cabin, shouting: "Miss Song!"

Zheng Zuye cursed under his breath and let go of her: "I saw her almost fall, just helping her."

The crew members draped the towel back over Shuangxu. She was pale, her whole body shaking. They escorted her all the way to the third floor.

He Tingzhou stood in the same spot, turning his head. His indifferent gaze swept over her disheveled appearance as before.

"Can't even ask for help?"

I called you.

You ignored me.

"Weren't you fierce enough when you were yelling at me just now?" He Tingzhou said. "Why are you dumb now?"

Shuangxu still didn't speak, standing in front of him wrapped in a towel, quietly. But then again, she had always been an excessively quiet girl.

The crew members left after delivering her, leaving only the sound of the waves on the deck.

He Tingzhou looked down at her for a while.

"Speak."

She finally spoke, saying: "Thank you." Then she turned to walk into the cabin.

She always remembered He Tingzhou's cold, detached, and onlooker's gaze, which made her, who wanted to ask for help, feel a chill all over.

She couldn't associate him with the crew members who had saved her. She knew she should be grateful, but she also wanted to keep her distance from him forever and never speak to him again.

He Tingzhou's gaze slid over her bare feet. Blood trickled down her fair instep, leaving a bloody footprint with each step.

He clicked his tongue, strode forward, bent down, and swept her up in his arms.

Shuangxu immediately pushed against him to get down. He Tingzhou glanced at her: "Infirmary or your brother's room, choose."

Shuangxu complied.

He Tingzhou carried her into the ship's infirmary and placed her on the medical bed. Shuangxu's legs dangled in the air.

He Tingzhou found a disinfectant wipe and lifted her ankle.

Shuangxu tried to pull away. He Tingzhou glanced at her: "Call your brother?"

She fell silent and stopped moving.

It hurt a bit when he wiped the wound. She flinched reflexively, and He Tingzhou threw the used wipe aside.

"Spoiled."

With these two words, Shuangxu's suppressed emotions suddenly broke through the critical point. Tears uncontrollably surged out.

They wetted her lashes, falling one after another in a string.

She didn't make a sound, just sat on the edge of the bed, quietly shedding tears.

"One word and you cry?" He Tingzhou said. "Little princess."

Shuangxu still didn't make a sound, turning her face away, her lips pressed tightly together.

Her black hair, wet and dripping, hung behind her, making her face look even cleaner and more transparent, except for her almond-shaped eyes, which were red and continuously shedding tears.

He Tingzhou took a piece of candy from his pocket, unwrapped it, and pinched her chin to force her mouth open.

Shuangxu's mouth was forced open, and a piece of candy was immediately popped in.

Her eyes were still red, utterly bewildered: "...What are you doing?"

He Tingzhou crumpled the candy wrapper in his hand and precisely tossed it into the trash bin. His expression was lazily indifferent: "You were about to cry, so I'm coaxing you."

...

Shuangxu, with the candy in her mouth and tears still hanging on her lower lashes, felt her grievances like a turned-on faucet. She wanted to cry but couldn't.

chapters.title: Then Offend Me
chapters.content:
The door was knocked twice, and the doctor, who had already rested, was hastily called up to quickly treat Shuangxu’s wound, which had been cut by metal, and applied medicine.

The wound was a bit deep, so the doctor gave her a tetanus shot and admonished, "Be careful not to infect the wound. Try not to get it wet before it heals."

Shuangxu nodded in agreement.

After the treatment, the doctor looked at He Tingzhou, then at her, and subtly probed, "Should we tell Young Master Shen about this?"

He assumed it was He Tingzhou who had done it.

Shuangxu was soaked, wrapped in a bath towel, clearly having just been in the water, and her foot was injured like this—it was obvious he hadn’t done anything good.

What a bastard.

He didn’t dare offend either side. If he told, he was afraid He Tingzhou would hold a grudge; if he didn’t, and Shen Yu found out tomorrow, he might come after him later.

He Tingzhou said indifferently, "It’s up to her."

In the past, if someone bullied her, Shuangxu would have immediately gone to Shen Yu in a wronged manner.

But now, even she herself had begun to doubt whether she was a trouble to Shen Yu.

Taking his fiancée out to sea for fun, yet she was the one ruining the mood.

Shen Yu would definitely not let this go. If he stood up for her again when they returned, he would likely end up on bad terms with the Zheng family.

If it weren’t for her, things would be much simpler.

Shuangxu unconsciously picked at her nails. "I’ll tell him tomorrow."

She didn’t know if Lu Mannan was really in Shen Yu’s room. She couldn’t just go knock on the door and disturb them now.

The suite was on the same floor. On the way back to her room from the infirmary, Shuangxu and He Tingzhou walked one after the other through the carpeted hallway.

When they reached the door, she stopped and turned to He Tingzhou. "Brother Tingzhou, don’t take to heart what I said earlier. I have no right to be angry at you. I might have unknowingly offended you during this time. I’m sorry, it won’t happen again."

After saying this, without waiting for He Tingzhou’s reaction, she went inside and closed the door.

She was very polite, even respectful, nothing like the unrestrained way she had been when she called him a "toad" before.

She was very at ease with close people, smiling often, and would act coy, like when she used to be with Shen Yu.

She was never this distant with him, as if she wanted to use the Queen Mother’s hairpin to carve out a Silver River between them.

As soon as Shuangxu entered the room, she heard two loud knocks on the door.

She turned back and opened the door slightly.

"You have quite the princess temper." He Tingzhou crossed his arms and leaned against the door frame, cutting to the chase. "Which part of what I said made you angry?"

Shuangxu was confused. "What do you mean?"

"Was it when I said your affection isn’t precious, or when I said you have a pitiful face?" He Tingzhou asked.

She remained silent.

In his entire life, Young Master He had never reflected on his own words or actions. He raised his eyebrows, looking back, and after setting aside the unpleasant mood at the time, even he felt he had been unreasonable.

"Or was it when I told you to confess to your brother?"

Shuangxu didn’t understand what game he was playing now. She held the doorknob and said, "What do you want?"

"I take back everything I said tonight." He Tingzhou lowered his gaze to her. "Is that okay?"

His expression was actually serious, which surprised and confused Shuangxu.

She looked at He Tingzhou for a few seconds, then averted her eyes. "No need. What you said was just your true feelings."

"Who said that?" He Tingzhou said righteously. "Can you read my mind? How do you know I wasn’t just saying that?"

Shuangxu really thought he was strange. He had already said those hurtful things, and now he wanted to take them back.

"Suit yourself." She didn’t want to delve into it or pay attention to it.

She could feel He Tingzhou’s gaze on her. "If there’s nothing else, I’m closing the door."

He Tingzhou raised his hand to prop open the door she was trying to close. "Say it clearly. What are you sulking about? How can I coax you if you don’t tell me?"

How could he possibly be so kind as to coax her? Probably because he saw her cry and was afraid she would tell Shen Yu tomorrow.

"You don’t need to coax me, and I’m not sulking."

She just needed to recognize her place and stay in line in the future, not to think of herself as anything special.

Standing close, He Tingzhou was a head taller than her. He looked down at her lightly. "I insist on coaxing you."

"Stop teasing me." Shuangxu said, "I’m really not angry with you."

He Tingzhou examined her, as if judging.

After a few seconds: "Then offend me."

...

What a bizarre request.

Shuangxu just wanted to draw a clear line in the future and not get entangled with him. Since He Tingzhou was blocking the door, she had no choice but to endure and say:

"I won’t offend you again. Let’s just pretend tonight never happened."

"I don’t like going to bed with unresolved issues. If you’re going to sulk, do it tonight." He Tingzhou domineeringly gave her a choice: "You offend me, or I coax you until you’re no longer angry."

Shuangxu was really exhausted, and he was making her speechless. What kind of person was he?

Her temper flared, and she pushed against his chest with both hands. "I don’t want to talk to you right now. I need to rest. Bye!"

He Tingzhou looked down at her hands and, following the force of her push, took a step back.

The door closed in front of him. From inside, a soft mutter came: "You’re crazy."

After all the commotion tonight, even if she wasn’t sleepy, Shuangxu was mentally exhausted. She lay down on the bed and quickly fell asleep.

Probably because she had caught a chill and been exposed to the sea wind, she developed a high fever in the middle of the night, her whole body burning up.

She slept fitfully until morning, when a knock at the door woke her with a splitting headache. Getting out of bed to open the door, she passed a mirror and saw that her entire face was abnormally red.

Lu Mannan stood outside, full of energy. "Morning."

"Morning." Shuangxu’s legs felt weak.

"Are you going scuba diving with Ah Yu later? He said you’ve won awards in swimming and are great at scuba diving too." Lu Mannan asked.

Shuangxu shook her head, her head throbbing heavily.

Lu Mannan noticed her complexion was off and reached out to touch her forehead. "Wow, your forehead is burning. How did you get such a high fever? Wait here, I’ll go get a doctor for you."

The doctor came to take her temperature, left some fever-reducing medicine, and Lu Mannan stood by her bed. "You definitely can’t go like this."

"I won’t go. You guys have fun."

Her eyes were too heavy to keep open. After a while, she heard the sound of the door closing—Lu Mannan had left.

The fever made her groggy, her body continuously sweating, every bone and nerve aching terribly. She couldn’t sleep peacefully, her eyebrows tightly furrowed, curling up under the blanket.

In her hazy state, she felt a gentle hand brush aside the damp strands of hair from her temples and lightly caress her cheek.

She tried hard to open her eyes, but the fever made her mind unclear, unable to distinguish reality from dreams.

"Brother..."

Shen Yu sat by the bed, his fingertip touching her feverish eyelids, his voice low. "Sleep, Xiao Jiu."

Shuangxu closed her eyes again at the reassuring sound and fell into a deep sleep.

The fever reducer took effect, and when she opened her eyes again, she was more coherent.

The bedside was empty, and the suite was so quiet it seemed no one had ever been there.

She remembered that Shen Yu was supposed to accompany Lu Mannan to go scuba diving today. Lu Mannan was trying it for the first time and had been looking forward to it before they came.

They must have already left.

---

chapters.title: Still Got to Hand It to Our Lord He
chapters.content:
She slept until almost noon, then took her own temperature. The fever had subsided a bit, but her body was extremely weak, with no energy at all.

There were many messages on WeChat. Shu Yang expressed her envy and jealousy, asking her to take some photos to satisfy her craving.

Shuangxu painted her a pie in the sky: [I’ll take you when you’re better]

She got up to drink a glass of water, then walked to the window to take a photo for Shu Yang. She saw a crowd gathered on the deck below.

Shen Yu and Zheng Zuye were facing each other in a standoff.

She froze, not even changing her shoes, and immediately ran out.

The incident where Zheng Zuye had almost bullied Shuangxu last night had been leaked by a crew member, and it eventually reached Shen Yu’s ears.

When he found Zheng Zuye, he was still drinking, with his arm around some unknown young model brought onto the ship, laughing vulgarly.

Shen Yu coldly said, "If you don’t want to be implicated, get lost."

The model immediately got up and ran away.

"What’s with the fierce attitude?" Zheng Zuye said. "You’re not here to settle the score with me, are you? I was just playing with your sister. I didn’t do anything to her. Isn’t she fine?"

"Xiao Jiu is not for you to play with." Shen Yu’s eyes were as cold as ice. "I warned you last time. If you have designs on her again, don’t blame me for being impolite."

Zheng Zuye calmly finished the drink in his glass and stood up to face him.

"Aren’t women just for playing with? If I don’t play with her, someone else will. It was fine when she wasn’t of age, but now that she is, and you’re still so protective, do you want to keep her for yourself?"

Shen Yu was a refined and elegant gentleman, while Zheng Zuye was the typical type who bullied the weak and feared the strong, hence his unbridled arrogance.

When Shen Yu’s fist landed on his face, his smirk didn’t even have time to fade before he was knocked to the ground.

The surrounding area immediately erupted in gasps and shouts. Lu Mannan was so scared she covered her mouth.

When Shuangxu ran down, Shen Yu had grabbed Zheng Zuye by the collar and slammed him against the railing of the deck.

The onlookers were all watching, some even recording with their phones.

She was about to go over when Lu Mannan grabbed her. "You’d better not go over there."

Seeing that Zheng Zuye’s nose was bleeding from the punch, Yue Zifeng and Zuo Zhong finally stepped in to stop them. "That’s enough. If you hit him any more, it won’t be easy to explain to Old Master Zheng."

Old Master Zheng was overly protective of his grandson, which was why Zheng Zuye had been raised to be so arrogant, lording it over others in Yan City. Since nothing serious had happened, beating his grandson like this might even make the old man seek revenge for him.

Zheng Zuye clutched the railing and got up, wiping under his nose. With half his face covered in blood, he looked even more arrogant. "Hit me! Why did you stop? If you’ve got the guts, kill me. Let’s see if my grandfather won’t be the first to slaughter your sister."

Shen Yu silently stared at him. Even Shuangxu had never seen him look so grim.

"Damn it." Yue Zifeng was so angry he could barely contain himself, but there was nothing anyone could do.

At this moment, a lazy figure swayed past Shuangxu and Lu Mannan.

"Cousin?" Lu Mannan called out.

He Tingzhou, probably having just woken up, had slightly messy black hair and an expression of annoyance at being disturbed from sleep. He didn’t even acknowledge Lu Mannan’s greeting.

He walked lazily toward the deck, and the onlookers automatically made way for him.

Shen Yu and Zheng Zuye were still in a standoff. Zheng Zuye was full of bluster. "What can you do to me?"

He Tingzhou sauntered over, lifted one foot, and kicked him off the railing.

"Holy shit!"

The ship instantly erupted in gasps and screams as a crowd rushed to the railing to look down.

Zheng Zuye plunged from the dozens of meters high deck into the sea with a splash. The dark sea and white waves swallowed him, and it took a long time before he resurfaced, furiously roaring in the water, "He Tingzhou, fuck your mother!!!"

He Tingzhou’s voice was lazily indifferent. "I don’t have a mother. Fuck your own."

...

After saying that, under the stunned and horrified gazes of everyone, he stuffed his hands in his pockets, turned around, and walked back from the deck.

As he passed Shuangxu, her mouth was slightly open in shock.

"Close it." He Tingzhou said, "You’ll drool in a minute."

When Shen Yu came over, his expression had already returned to normal. He placed his palm on her forehead. "Fever’s down?"

Shuangxu nodded. "Much better now."

Shen Yu didn’t bring up last night’s events. He only soothed her by rubbing her head. "Are you hungry? I’ll have the kitchen make you something to eat."

After arranging that, he walked over to He Tingzhou and placed his hand on his shoulder, giving it two heavy pats. "Thanks."

He wasn’t thanking him for the kick just now, but for saving Shuangxu last night.

"No need for thanks." He Tingzhou’s gaze swept over Shuangxu. "Your sister is my sister."

To Shuangxu’s ears, this sounded extremely hypocritical.

When had he ever treated her like a sister to look after?

Yue Zifeng returned from the deck, grinning widely. "Still got to hand it to our Lord He! That bastard has hated you for so many years for a reason—only you can deal with him."

Zheng Zuye hated him? Shuangxu couldn’t help but glance at He Tingzhou.

"Not finishing him off was truly a dereliction of my duty, burdening society." He Tingzhou’s flippant tone made it hard to tell if he was joking. "I’ll go apologize to the Queen Mother later."

"I let him float in the sea for a while. When he could barely move, I threw him a swim ring." Yue Zifeng said, "Venting is venting, but if we really killed him, the Zheng family would come after us for his life. I’ll have someone send a speedboat to pick him up and have the Zheng family come get him."

It wasn’t even lunchtime yet, but the chef had specially prepared fish soup noodles for Shuangxu—oh, not just for her, but for two people.

Lu Mannan also came in and sat across the table, ordering a bowl of noodles for herself.

The milky broth was rich and fragrant, and the freshness of the sea fish was something farmed fish couldn’t compare to. Shuangxu originally didn’t have much of an appetite, but unconsciously ate half a bowl.

Lu Mannan had barely touched her noodles.

Shuangxu put down her chopsticks and was about to leave the dining room when Lu Mannan said, as if to herself, "Your brother really dotes on you. When Le Yan upset you yesterday, your brother had her sent away in the middle of the night. And today, when you got a fever, he canceled the scuba diving trip."

Song Leyan had been sent away? No wonder she hadn’t seen her today.

They hadn’t gone scuba diving, so had she imagined seeing Shen Yu this morning?

Shuangxu looked at Lu Mannan, who lifted her head and said, "It was the first time I’ve seen your brother fight."

"He’s inherently a perfect gentleman, always composed and measured. I thought it would be very hard to provoke him."

"But I have to admit, he looked incredibly cool when he lost his temper and beat someone up."

Shuangxu understood what she meant.

Lu Mannan had always been jealous of her, and now with Shen Yu repeatedly standing up for her, she was probably feeling uncomfortable.

"My brother is very protective of the people around him, and he’s the same with you. If he stood by and did nothing when I was bullied, you wouldn’t like him either."

Lu Mannan rested her cheek on her hand. "That’s true."

"You two will have many more opportunities in the future. He’ll accompany you to do many things you want to do." Shuangxu consoled her.

Shen Yu was too good. Her luck probably wasn’t enough to have him for ten years; in the future, he would belong to someone else.

"You must be very happy to have a brother. I’m so envious of you." Lu Mannan said, "I’m an only child, with no brothers, sisters, or younger siblings."

Shuangxu envied her for having parents who doted on her.

"You do have a brother, don’t you?" she said. "Your cousin also cares about you."

"My cousin? He cares about me?" Lu Mannan suddenly let out two strange laughs, "Ha! Ha!" She straightened up, her emotions agitated. "When I was in elementary school, I once lost a game of hair-pulling and ran to him crying, wanting him to back me up. Do you know what he said?"

"What did he say?"

"He found me annoying and said, ‘Why don’t you shave your head? Then you’d be invincible.’"

Lu Mannan slammed both hands on the table, her resentment evident. "Have you ever seen a brother treat his sister like that?"

Shuangxu kept a straight face, held back for a moment, but couldn’t help it: "...Pfft."

chapters.title: So Hard to Please
chapters.content:
In the living room, Yue Zifeng was still nagging He Tingzhou: "I mean, when you saw that idiot bullying your sister, why didn’t you rush to help? You called two crew members—do you think their mouths can be trusted? Now the whole ship knows, and my sister has such thin skin. How embarrassing for her."

"You and your brain." Zuo Zhong scolded him, "Don’t you know how much Zheng Zuye hates Tingzhou? He’d snatch anything even remotely connected to Tingzhou. Maybe his interest in your sister would’ve faded in a few days, but if he saw Tingzhou protecting her, he’d fixate on her immediately—drugging or kidnapping her to get what he wants."

"Well, that’s true." Yue Zifeng smirked, "Zheng Zuye’s only true love in this life is our Lord He."

He Tingzhou lazily glanced at him: "If you want to go be with him, just say so. I’ll give you a kick to send you both off into the sunset together."

"You’re just not his type. What can you do?" Yue Zifeng swung his leg, schadenfreude dripping from his voice. "Stay away from my sister in the future. Otherwise, that beast will pester her again."

He Tingzhou neither agreed nor disagreed, his expression indifferent. He took a playing card from somewhere and flipped it between his fingers.

The yacht docked that evening. The clouds were dyed a gradient of pink and orange by the sunset, while the sea remained a deep, endless blue.

Lu Mannan got into Shen Yu’s car. Shen Yu closed the passenger door and turned to look at her.

Before he could speak, Shuangxu tactfully said, "You should take Miss Lu. I’ll go with Zifeng and the others."

Shen Yu reminded her, "Go home and rest. If your fever doesn’t break, remember to take your medicine."

Shuangxu nodded, watching their car drive away.

He Tingzhou’s Koenigsegg was parked by the roadside, with Yue Zifeng’s car behind it.

Shuangxu walked straight toward Yue Zifeng’s car. As she passed the Koenigsegg, the window rolled down, and He Tingzhou spoke: "Get in. I’ll take you."

Shuangxu hesitated but didn’t stop. She politely declined, "No need to trouble you, Tingzhou. We’re not going the same way."

She lived in East Third Ring, and he lived in Yansi—it was quite far.

With that, she continued walking toward Yue Zifeng’s car.

Hadn’t they made up last night? Why was he still so cold?

He Tingzhou rested his arm on the car window, his index finger pressing against his temple. Through the rearview mirror, he watched her get into Yue Zifeng’s car. Slowly, he pulled his gaze back and started the engine.

So hard to please.

After returning to Yancheng, Shuangxu didn’t see He Tingzhou for a while.

Apart from Shen Yu and Yue Zifeng’s circle, she and He Tingzhou didn’t have many overlaps to begin with.

She did run into him once by chance while dining out with Fu Yun. Coincidentally, He Tingzhou was at the same restaurant.

Shuangxu didn’t recognize the people with him, but they all treated him with great admiration. He, however, looked utterly bored. His gaze swept across the restaurant and briefly paused on her.

She noticed the woman next to him—the same qipao beauty she’d seen at the club before.

In a tight dress, her figure was graceful as she rested her chin in her hand, smiling and chatting with the others at the table. Under the table, her toes were secretly hooking He Tingzhou’s leg.

Shuangxu averted her eyes, refusing to look again.

As they left the restaurant, they happened to meet at the entrance.

"Tingzhou!" Fu Yun stopped and greeted him with a smile.

He Tingzhou responded lazily, his gaze sliding over Shuangxu, who stood on the other side of Fu Yun.

Shuangxu only politely called him "Tingzhou" once at the beginning, then turned her head to look at the road, waiting. Once Fu Yun finished talking, she left with her.

The engagement between the Shen and Lu families was the talk of Yancheng’s elite circles. The news had leaked, and every media outlet was writing about it nonstop. Reporters camped outside Shen’s villa and Shen Yu’s private residence every day.

A paparazzi’s telephoto lens caught a glimpse through a window—a young, beautiful woman with her arms around a man’s waist, lightly standing on her toes.

The man’s tall figure was half-hidden behind a sheer curtain. Though his face wasn’t visible, the outline of his jaw was enough to spark imagination.

The photo was published in major media outlets the next day and spread everywhere.

Xiao Liao, ever the gossip enthusiast, scrolled through the news excitedly: "Wow, this photo has such a great vibe! They look so perfect together!"

Shu Yang, lying on the edge of the bed and vomiting her guts out, fished an apple core from the trash can and threw it at her: "Shut up."

The nurse quickly cleaned up the mess, and Shuangxu washed a towel to wipe Shu Yang’s face.

"Seriously! Miss Shuang, look!" Xiao Liao held her phone up to Shuangxu’s face. "Doesn’t your brother look so handsome in this? And Miss Lu is so beautiful!"

Forced to look, Shuangxu nodded stiffly: "Mm, it really is a good shot."

Shu Yang pointed at Xiao Liao, wanting to curse but unable to find the right words.

Seeing her half-dead state, Shuangxu actually laughed: "It’s fine. Consider it exposure therapy."

Desensitization was a slow and long process. She realized she wasn’t as heartbroken as she had been at first.

Breaking free from her dependence on and attachment to Shen Yu was like flaying her own skin—agonizing, yet strangely easy.

Because she had no choice.

Lately, she only saw Shen Yu during weekends when she went back to the Shen family for meals. He’d ask a few questions about Xue’s condition, she’d answer them one by one, and that was the extent of their interaction.

"What’s exposure therapy?" Xiao Liao asked innocently, leaning in. "What are you allergic to?"

Shuangxu answered seriously: "I’m a little allergic to you."

Xiao Liao: "..."

Lu Mannan’s grandmother was elderly and in poor health, so she didn’t return to Yancheng with them. Instead, she stayed in Lincheng, where the climate was more suitable for her.

After the engagement was set, Shen Yu accompanied Lu Mannan to Lincheng to meet the elders.

Yue Zifeng’s sister was turning eight, and the Yue family, having a daughter late in life, doted on her endlessly. They had booked a hotel banquet hall to celebrate her birthday.

The birthday party had a children’s theme. To cater to the kids’ preferences, the entire banquet hall was decorated like a Disney castle.

Yue’s sister was dressed as her favorite character, Judy Hopps, while Yue Zifeng was forced to wear a fox headband and tail, becoming the butt of everyone’s jokes.

"Such a childhood ruiner." A few of his friends complained while snapping photos with their phones.

Yue Zifeng grabbed them by the collars: "Her best friend insists on playing Snow White, and we’re short on dwarves. Go, go, the costumes are all ready for you."

Zuo Zhong tried to resist: "Are you sure we’ll look like dwarves next to her and not giants?"

When they came out in their dwarf costumes, Shuangxu, sitting nearby, laughed so hard she nearly choked.

They were still one dwarf short. Zuo Zhong, struggling with a misbuttoned shirt, asked: "Isn’t Tingzhou here?"

"Ask him to be a dwarf? You’re dreaming! He wouldn’t even play the prince."

Shuangxu sipped her juice, thinking that He Tingzhou didn’t really have the demeanor of a prince anyway.

He was more like a dragon.

A malicious one.

Little Yue, dressed in her Judy costume, was adorable with her bunny ears bobbing. When she spotted Shuangxu, she ran over and grabbed her: "We found Elsa!"

Instantly, several little girls in colorful costumes swarmed her, pulling at her hands to drag her up.

"I’m not—" Shuangxu started, but a little girl came up to her, blinking with starry eyes: "Sister, you’re so pretty! Can you be Elsa, please?"

Well… fine.

Who could resist such eyes and praise?

The party planners had gone all out. There were children’s and adult-sized costumes, and the changing room was equipped with professional makeup artists and hairstylists.

Shuangxu couldn’t escape either. She was pulled away to change into Elsa’s blue dress.

The hairstylist had intended to give her a wig but, after a few adjustments, gave up: "Forget it. Your hair is so beautiful; we don’t need this cheap wig."

Instead, they braided her hair in the same style, letting it fall over her left shoulder.

Shuangxu stepped out of the changing room and back into the banquet hall. The hem of her dress was a bit long, so she held it up as she walked.

As she moved forward, a pair of dress shoes entered her line of sight. She quickly stopped, stepping back as she looked up.

He Tingzhou was looking down at her, his gaze slowly traveling from her head to her toes, then back up again.

Finally, it settled on her face, and he slowly, deliberately, raised one eyebrow.

---

chapters.title: Did You Eat Something Bad?
chapters.content:
That single raised eyebrow conveyed more meaning than any words. Shuangxu felt an inexplicable sense of shame.

She sidestepped around him and quickly returned to the banquet hall.

A little while later, as she was playing games with a few children, she heard a few exclamations of "What the hell?" behind her.

She turned and saw He Tingzhou, then froze.

He had changed into a white prince outfit. His legs were absurdly long, and the fitted waist accentuated his lean, taut waistline, leading up to broad, straight shoulders.

As soon as he walked in, the little girls shrieked excitedly and rushed toward him.

Little Yue immediately abandoned her beloved Judy role, declaring with authority: "I want you to be my prince."

He Tingzhou, perfectly at ease, sat down on the sofa: "In your dreams."

The forced-to-kneel dwarves on the floor looked at him resentfully: "Do little girls these days have double standards or what?"

Yue Zifeng was also displeased: "This is rich. We begged him for ages, and he refused. Now he goes and changes on his own."

The birthday party had invited Little Yue’s friends, classmates, and children from other prominent families. The entire venue was as lively as an amusement park.

The children’s attention shifted quickly. When the cake was rolled out, their focus instantly moved elsewhere.

Shuangxu finally got some peace. She walked to the sofa area and sat down far from He Tingzhou.

She had a glass of champagne and some cake. When her gaze swept past He Tingzhou, she accidentally met his eyes.

He was propping up his chin, his posture relaxed, as if he had been watching her for a while.

"What are you looking at?" she asked.

He Tingzhou’s lips curved slightly, his voice carrying a smile and unhidden frivolity: "Looking at the princess."

Shuangxu felt like he was mocking her: "There are princesses all over the place. It’s not just me."

"Is that so?" He Tingzhou’s tone was utterly insincere, his gaze still lingering on her with interest.

Shuangxu didn’t want to talk to him. On the boat, she had clearly realized her place and decided to keep her distance from him.

She lowered her head and ate her cake. He Tingzhou added, "You look cute."

...

She nearly choked on her cake.

For the rest of the party, she ignored He Tingzhou completely.

As the party was nearing its end, a waiter in a white uniform and tie passed by, taking a glass of champagne from a tray and handing it to Shuangxu.

She thanked him and took it, drinking half before returning to the changing room to get back into her own clothes.

The makeup artists had already left. The space was small and felt cramped. As she changed, she felt a tightness in her chest.

She thought she’d go out for some air after changing, but the feeling only grew worse.

Her heartbeat was accelerating, her breathing rapid. She felt a dizzying lightheadedness, as if her feet were floating.

Was she drunk? But she’d only had two glasses of champagne—it shouldn’t be this bad.

The discomfort didn’t ease even after she left the changing room.

A hotel staff member passed by and asked, "Miss, are you alright?"

Shuangxu didn’t know what was wrong with her, but she knew one thing: going home immediately was the best option.

"Please take me out."

"Follow me. The exit is this way."

Her dizziness grew worse. She followed the staff member for a while until they reached an elevator. The staff member pressed the button.

Suddenly, Shuangxu looked up at her.

The staff member turned back, offering a friendly smile.

In that instant, alarm bells rang in Shuangxu’s mind.

She suddenly remembered coming here with Shen Yu a long time ago. This elevator led upstairs.

Realizing this, she sensed something was wrong. Without thinking, she turned and ran in the opposite direction.

"Miss Song!"

The staff member was clearly faster than Shuangxu, whose steps were unsteady. She quickly caught up and grabbed Shuangxu’s arm.

"You’re not feeling well. Let me take you upstairs to rest."

Shuangxu struggled but couldn’t muster any strength.

"Do you know what you’re doing?" she gritted out. "Who sent you?"

The staff member didn’t answer, forcefully dragging her toward the elevator.

Zheng Zuye? It had to be him.

But he hadn’t shown up today, had he?

If he had, she would’ve been on guard, kept her distance, stayed as far away as possible.

Zheng Zuye probably knew that, which was why he hadn’t appeared at all.

In a banquet hall full of people, with children’s laughter everywhere, with people she knew and trusted, a waiter carrying a tray and serving drinks was too ordinary, too natural. How could she have been on guard?

Now the party was over, and the guests had left. She didn’t know if Yue Zifeng and the others had already gone.

No one would notice her missing at this point.

The floor was covered with a burgundy sound-absorbing carpet, and the soft footsteps were nearly inaudible.

But in her despair, Shuangxu still heard them.

He Tingzhou had changed back into his own clothes—white shirt, black pants, crisp and neat.

The moment she saw him, she violently wrenched free and threw herself at him with all her strength: "Tingzhou..."

She remembered his coldness on the yacht that night, but right now, she had no one else to turn to.

It was just her bad luck that she kept running into him.

He Tingzhou raised a hand and caught her.

His sudden appearance startled the staff member, who, upon seeing him, didn’t dare to keep pulling Shuangxu and quickly lowered her head before walking away.

Shuangxu could barely stand. Her hands clung to He Tingzhou’s arm like a lifeline.

Her accelerated heartbeat was so loud it felt like it would burst from her throat. Her body was limp, as if boneless, and she leaned against him, her breath scorching.

He Tingzhou saw that something was wrong with her. He lifted her chin and examined her flushed face.

"Did you eat something bad?"

Shuangxu nodded: "Near the end, someone gave me a glass of wine. I think there was something in it."

He Tingzhou frowned slightly and picked her up.

His embrace was broad and warm, giving Shuangxu a small sense of safety after her close call.

He Tingzhou took her to a penthouse suite. By the time Shuangxu was placed on the bed, the effects of the drug were already taking hold.

Her entire body was burning, and her mind was being consumed by the heat in her blood.

Being in a hotel room alone with a grown man in this state was dangerous. She struggled to stay awake.

She wanted to find her phone, but her bag was gone—it had been pulled off during the struggle. Her phone was inside.

She sat up: "Tingzhou, can you help me call my brother?"

Even in danger, her first instinct was still to seek Shen Yu.

He Tingzhou sat down on the sofa across from the bed, lit a cigarette, and said casually, "Your brother probably can’t help you with this."

"Then can you take me to the hospital?"

Smoke curled around He Tingzhou’s eyes, making it impossible for Shuangxu to see his expression. All she could hear was his indifferent voice: "The hospital can’t help you either."

chapters.title: How Do You Want Me to Help You?
chapters.content:
It was true—if she was seen in this state and taken to the hospital, the whole social circle would know by tomorrow.

So what if she was the victim? She would be the only one humiliated and mocked.

Shen Yu was currently discussing marriage with Lu Mannan; this kind of scandal might make the Lu family have reservations.

And then there was the Song family. If she brought shame upon them again, who knew if they would just put her on a plane and send her away for good.

So what could she do?

Shuangxu knelt blankly by the bed, the skin on her neck already flushed crimson.

He Tingzhou held his cigarette, his arm resting on the armrest, watching her with detached ease, calm and languid.

Shuangxu knew what her current situation meant.

If it were Zheng Zuye in front of her, she would grab a fruit knife and stab him to death first.

But with He Tingzhou... if it really came down to it... it seemed... maybe... it wasn't... impossible...

Her mind was torn, swaying back and forth.

Compared to being taken to the hospital in a grand spectacle, causing a chain reaction, sleeping with He Tingzhou seemed a little simpler.

A playboy like him, who had been through countless women, flirting casually without a care—he probably didn’t have any principles about chastity.

She had already been with a toad before.

After a fierce internal struggle, she clenched the bedsheet with her fingers and looked at the man sitting composedly on the sofa.

"Brother Tingzhou, can you... help me?"

She didn’t know what she looked like at that moment—her eyes slightly red, her clear almond-shaped eyes brimming with a shimmering glow. The innocent purity that made one hesitate to defile, mixed with chaotic desire, intertwined as she extended this invitation to the man. It was downright criminal.

He Tingzhou propped his forehead with his fingers, the warm orange light in the room casting shadows over his brows, hiding his eyes in the depths.

"How do you want me to help you?"

How else could he help?

What a wolf in sheep’s clothing, playing innocent.

"Can you... sleep with me?"

Her directness took him by surprise. He Tingzhou’s eyebrow twitched slightly as he took a drag of his cigarette, saying nothing.

"It’s fine. If you don’t want to, I can find someone else."

She was actually enduring immense pain—her fingers and toes were tensed up, afraid she might lose control and reveal her embarrassing state in front of He Tingzhou.

He would definitely mock her.

He Tingzhou lifted an eyelid. "Who do you plan to find?"

In Shuangxu’s circle of friends, there really wasn’t anyone she could "use" at a time like this.

Yan City was full of entertainment clubs; hiring an escort wasn’t difficult.

But in her current state, she couldn’t go find one herself. Shu Yang was at the hospital, Shen Yu had gone to Long City, and there weren’t many people she could trust.

"I can... ask Brother Zifeng for help."

The moment she said that, He Tingzhou let out a cold laugh. "Then remember to have him wash his neck clean, so your brother can chop it off when he gets back."

He misunderstood.

Yue Zifeng was different from him.

To Shuangxu, Yue Zifeng was like a close older brother, falling into a genderless category—he wasn’t even on her list of options.

But they often hung out, so he must know where to quickly find a good escort.

The problem was, asking Yue Zifeng to help her hire an escort would be incredibly awkward no matter how she phrased it.

If He Tingzhou was willing, she didn’t want to waste time looking elsewhere.

"Are you worried about my brother?" she said. "I won’t tell him. This is an accident. Just... just consider it as doing me a favor. If you feel like you’re losing out, I can pay you."

He Tingzhou had more than enough money. She was just grasping at straws—after all, he wouldn’t be happy helping her for free.

"Sure." He Tingzhou was easy to talk to. "But I’m expensive."

Shuangxu thought about it—she could probably afford one night. "How much?"

The man who had built Yun Dun Group into an industry leader had a business mind she couldn’t compare to.

"How much do you have in your card?"

Shuangxu had already invested all her savings into Feixue; she didn’t have much left. She answered honestly, "A million."

He Tingzhou took advantage of her current confusion and rising desire, driving up the price. "Then I want a million."

Shuangxu was stunned for two seconds. "A million?"

Was his thing made of diamond?

He Tingzhou lazily replied, "I told you, I’m expensive."

Her breathing was rapid, urged on by the effects of the drug. She felt like ants were gnawing at her body, her heart beating fast and wildly.

She understood—this million was just an excuse to refuse.

This kind of request was already embarrassing to say out loud; being rejected would be even more humiliating. She was already suffering, and she knew she shouldn’t have expected anything from He Tingzhou.

"Forget it."

There was a choked sob in her voice, but the words were too short to notice.

She stumbled off the bed, wanting to go to the bathroom to take a cold shower, but her legs were weak and her head was spinning. She hadn’t taken two steps before she fell.

He Tingzhou happened to be sitting there, making it look like a poorly acted attempt to throw herself into his arms.

He Tingzhou didn’t move, only shifting the hand holding the cigarette away as he let her fall onto his lap.

She was light, soft, and burning with heat.

Shuangxu’s hand pressed against his chest, feeling the firm contours of his muscles beneath her palm.

He Tingzhou glanced at her hand. "What are you doing? Planning to force yourself on me?"

Shuangxu hadn’t intended to, but the moment she touched him, her body instinctively wanted to press closer.

The torment spreading from her bones and blood made her, upon touching He Tingzhou, like a starving dog seeing a big steamed bun.

For some reason, she recalled the day the qipao beauty had hooked his leg under the table. She hadn’t seen him so chaste then.

Her mind was muddled, and she accidentally blurted out her thoughts: "You’re not worth a million. Others sleep with you for free, and you even buy them bags, cars, and houses."

As soon as she said it, she realized her slip. No matter how flirtatious he was, who he slept with was his freedom.

She tried to get off He Tingzhou, but he held her down.

He Tingzhou stubbed out his cigarette in the ashtray and lowered his head to question her: "Tell me. Who slept with me for free? Who did I buy bags, cars, and houses for?"

"That’s your business, none of mine."

Shuangxu pushed him away and tried to leave, but one of her feet had already touched the ground when He Tingzhou hooked his arm around her waist and dragged her back.

This time, her entire body was pulled into his embrace, their bodies pressed tightly together.

She felt something, and her mind went blank. Her blood boiled, and her heart pounded uncontrollably.

She stared at him with a flushed, stunned face. "You... you..."

"What?"

Shuangxu pressed against his chest to move back, her gaze instinctively flicking down to his black trousers.

When she looked up again, she met He Tingzhou’s eyes. The laziness and leisure were gone, replaced by a dark, abyssal depth.

His voice was low and casual: "Just what you wanted, isn’t it?"

"I didn’t." Her voice was barely a whisper.

"You didn’t?" He Tingzhou said. "Then who just offered a million to sleep with me?"

Shuangxu’s ears were about to burn. "I didn’t offer a million. You did it yourself."

She didn’t deny wanting to sleep with him, but she was quibbling over the price.

He Tingzhou let out a low laugh, lowering his head closer to hers. "Then how about I give you a discount?"

His deep-set eyes were sharp, but his smile was bewitching.

Shuangxu, like a scholar tempted by a fox spirit, asked, "How much of a discount?"

He Tingzhou lifted her legs and placed her on the bed. He knelt on the bed with one knee, his body looming over hers. His low, magnetic voice carried a hint of husky gravel as he tempted her: "Call me 'big brother,' and I’ll do it for free."

Was he deliberately using that address to humiliate her? He knew how she felt about Shen Yu.

"I don’t need your help anymore."

She tried to turn over and escape, but He Tingzhou pinned her knee down, pressing her into the bed.

Suddenly, he exuded a completely different aggressiveness, like a ferocious predator, full of dangerous vibes. At that moment, she was like a small animal with its throat pinned down by him.

The difference in their sizes was like a cage, completely trapping her.

She noticed the sharp outline of his Adam’s apple, the way it moved—inexplicably sexy.

She was incredibly nervous, her breathing rapid and heavy.

He Tingzhou’s gaze was deep. "Changed your mind again?"

Shuangxu glared at him with red-rimmed eyes. "I don’t need you to humiliate me."

"Who’s humiliating whom? You wanted to hire me, then said I wasn’t worth the money." He Tingzhou said, "Little princess, you’re really hard to please."

Just then, knock knock—there were two knocks at the door.

The dark, deep color in He Tingzhou’s eyes silently dissipated. He straightened up, pulled the blanket over her, and walked out of the suite to open the door.

Who would come knocking at this hour?

Shuangxu was still confused when she heard a man’s voice.

"I came as soon as I got your call. Is she alright?"

He Tingzhou’s voice was calm, showing no trace of the earlier turmoil. "She’s fine. Full of energy. If you hadn’t come, I’d have had to sell myself."

"..."

chapters.title: Who Comes First Between Me and Shen Yu?
chapters.content:
The private doctor rushed into the bedroom with a medical kit, took out an injectable, and administered it to Shuangxu.

"I'm not sure what the drug they used contains, so I can't completely neutralize it. This will only alleviate the symptoms, and it should take effect in about fifteen minutes. You might still feel a bit unwell, but you'll be fine by tomorrow."

The doctor packed up the medical kit, carefully avoiding eye contact with the woman on the bed the entire time.

He Tianzhou had already returned to the opposite sofa. He smoked with a casual, almost absent-minded demeanor.

"Know what to say and what not to say. Use your own judgment."

The doctor already felt as if a knife was pressed against his aorta with that leisurely remark.

"Mr. He, rest assured. Not a single word about tonight will leave my lips."

He Tianzhou neither agreed nor disagreed. He left in a hurry, closing the door as quietly as possible.

Shuangxu's long hair spread across the white bedsheet like soft, smooth black silk.

Her gaze was still slightly dazed, and the flush on her skin had not yet faded. She lay quietly on the bed for a moment before looking at the man on the sofa.

He Tianzhou had been watching her the whole time.

When their eyes met, he bit his cigarette, and the corner of his lips twitched slightly, revealing an ambiguous smile.

"What are you looking at?"

Shuangxu recalled how she had just taken the initiative to proposition him, even offering to pay to "solicit" him. A wave of shame and anger surged through her like a tide.

"You called a doctor. Why didn't you tell me?"

He Tianzhou lazily replied, "You didn't ask."

That was true. She had been the one to take the initiative, and he had just gone along with it, teasing her and watching her make a fool of herself.

He had saved her and even called a doctor for her. She had no grounds to blame him; she should be grateful instead.

"So what?" He Tianzhou lightly flicked his cigarette. "Disappointed you didn't get to sleep with me?"

Shuangxu pressed her lips together and turned her face away. "No. Thank you for your help. You can leave now. I'll pay you back for the room tomorrow."

After saying that, she buried herself under the covers.

This was so embarrassing. She never wanted to see He Tianzhou again in her life.

In the same hotel, in a luxurious executive suite.

Zheng Zuye had already prepared himself. After taking a shower, he wrapped a towel around his waist and lounged on the sofa with his legs crossed, waiting leisurely.

He had experienced all types of beauties. Women were all the same; after a few times, they became boring.
