But Song Shuangxu was different. He had lusted after her, failed to get her, and even been whipped with a ruler by the old man in front of Shen Yu.

He had almost forgotten about it, but then he saw Song Shuangxu again at the port last time. From a distance, he caught a glimpse of her figure climbing the gangway.

The once-green girl had blossomed, even more charming than before.

Shen Yu really had an eye for beauty. If he had known she would turn out like this, he should have made his move earlier and had his mother adopt Song Shuangxu, so Shen Yu wouldn't be in the way.

Zheng Zuye had never gone to such lengths for any woman. Shen Yu wasn't in Yan City these days, and Yue Zifeng was busy throwing a birthday party for his sister. It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

After getting her drunk, he could trick her into coming up. Even if Song Shuangxu refused, the drug would make her obedient eventually.

He waited and waited. The party downstairs had ended half an hour ago, but the person he sent still hadn't brought Song Shuangxu over.

Impatient, he was about to call and urge them when the doorbell finally rang.

Zheng Zuye immediately went to open the door. The female staff member he had arranged stood alone outside.

"Where is she?"

"Someone took Miss Song away on the road."

Zheng Zuye's face instantly darkened. "Who took her?"

The female staff member shrank back, lowering her head. "Young Master Yue."

The duck that was almost in his mouth had flown away. Zheng Zuye was furious and kicked the wall. "Fuck Yue Zifeng! Ruining my good time!"

Yue Zifeng carried his drunk sister, who had fallen asleep in the car, back home. He placed her on the bed as carefully as if handling a landmine, afraid of waking her up.

As soon as he set her down, his nose itched. He quickly covered his mouth and only let out the sneeze after closing the bedroom door behind him. "Ah—choo! Who's thinking of me?"

His phone rang. Zuo Zhong invited him out for a drink. "He Tianzhou is here too. Are you coming?"

"It's so late. Still drinking?"

"You have the nerve to say that. We've been squatting for two hours; our legs are numb!"

Yue Zifeng immediately gave in. "Alright, alright. I'm coming. Tonight's on me."

When Yue Zifeng arrived at Blue Night Club, the group was already in a private room, drinking and chatting. Someone had called a few female PRs in tight mini skirts to keep them company.

He Tianzhou, as usual, occupied a sofa by himself, his feet propped up on the coffee table, leaning back lazily. His wrist rested casually on the armrest, a glass of wine in his hand, untouched for a long time.

The dim, ambiguous lighting of the bar illuminated his bored expression. A pure-looking girl secretly observed him for a while before mustering the courage to sit next to him.

"Zhou Ye, what are you thinking about?"

He Tianzhou didn't even look at her, his tone indifferent and cold. "Not about you. What's it to you?"

Yue Zifeng came in and plopped down next to Zuo Zhong, laughing and chatting with them.

After drinking for a while, he turned his head and met He Tianzhou's gaze.

"What the hell are you looking at me for?" he asked, puzzled.

He Tianzhou looked him up and down with a thoughtful gaze, then hummed ambiguously. "Suddenly realized you have some looks too."

"You just noticed?" Yue Zifeng flicked his hair flirtatiously. "Even if I don't say nationwide, in Yan City, aside from you and Shen Yu, my stunning good looks should at least rank third."

The group jeered at him. Zuo Zhong spat, "Stunning good looks? You're just a stunning big face. What did they do wrong to be compared with you?"

"You're just jealous." Yue Zifeng patted his shoulder. "I'll rank you as Yan City's fourth most handsome."

He Tianzhou seemed genuinely interested in this ranking and suddenly asked, "Between me and Shen Yu, who comes first?"

His question made everyone look over.

"Oh, so you do care about this."

"Getting competitive, huh?"

"You two are hard to compare. It depends on who you ask. Those who like your type would definitely rank you first. But if someone prefers refined and elegant types, then Shen Yu would beat you by ten streets and a bend." Yue Zifeng explained earnestly. "Why are you looking at me? I'm telling the truth."

He Tianzhou's thin lips curled slightly in a mocking smile, then he leaned back lazily. "Good. I only deal with facts."

---

Shuangxu woke up the next morning feeling normal, just a bit weak.

The suite was so quiet you could hear a pin drop. Her bag and phone, which she had dropped the night before, were placed on the opposite sofa.

Shuangxu replied to the pending messages on WeChat. After putting her phone down, she picked it up again, found He Tianzhou's WeChat, clicked on his profile, and deleted him.

After a night's sleep, her emotions had stabilized. She just didn't want to see He Tianzhou again or hear his name.

"Next Wednesday, we have a meeting at Yun Dun. We'll get to see President He again!"

As soon as she arrived at the company, Xiao Liao chattered in her ear. "Boss, you're so unfair. President He is so handsome, and you didn't even tell me."

"Do you have his WeChat? Do you usually meet him? Can you take me with you next time?"

She couldn't avoid him. He Tianzhou was now a major client of Feixue, and she had personally gone to great lengths to secure this collaboration.

Shuangxu felt flustered and took out her noise-canceling headphones, covering both ears.

Fortunately, Feixue's small hydrogen-powered drone project wasn't significant enough to warrant the personal attention of the busy President He of Yun Dun Group.

On the day Feixue went to Yun Dun for their presentation, the one who met with them was the balding Director Fan.

Director Fan was somewhat arrogant. Throughout the meeting, he kept urging them to be brief, again and again.

He frequently checked his watch and, after listening to a rough overview, interrupted dismissively. "Alright, that's about it for today. Come back next Monday."

As they left the meeting room, Xiao Liao grumbled, "He didn't even listen properly, yet he wants us to come every week. What's so great about being the client?"

Old Fang, a long-time employee who had been with Feixue since its founding, was a few years older than them. He said, "The client is indeed great. You are in the client's house now. Watch your words and actions."

Shuangxu didn't say anything. As they walked down the hallway, they saw He Tianzhou from a distance at the other end.

He looked slightly different in the office compared to in private. His suit was sharp and neat, making him appear even more imposing.

His personal assistant and several executives stood beside him. The assistant noticed Shuangxu first and whispered something to He Tianzhou. Their conversation paused, and He Tianzhou turned to look at her.

Xiao Liao, who had been indignant just moments ago, changed her expression instantly. "Wow, that face is truly remarkable!"

...What about her principles?

Shuangxu knew she should at least greet him politely. Apart from being Shen Yu's friend and the young master of the He family, he was also Feixue's major client. She couldn't afford to offend him.

But as soon as she met He Tianzhou's sharp gaze, the scene from that night flashed in her mind like an unskippable pop-up ad, and she couldn't close it.

It was the most embarrassing moment of her life that she desperately wanted to erase.

Noticing her cheeks heating up, she quickly turned her head away.

---

chapters.title: A Refined Scoundrel
chapters.content:
Shuangxu wanted to pretend she hadn't seen him and walk away.

But she couldn't ignore the fact that everyone else had eyes. Old Fang, the seasoned flatterer, immediately went over to fawn over He Tianzhou.

"President He, thank you so much for your appreciation of Feixue. If it weren't for your keen eye and timely help, we might not have survived until now. You are Feixue's greatest benefactor. Everyone at Feixue holds you in the highest regard."

"Do they?" He Tianzhou implied, "It seems someone doesn't."

"How could that be?" Old Fang said, "Our President Song sheds tears of gratitude every time she mentions you."

...Don't lay it on too thick.

Old Fang gave her a meaningful look. Shuangxu knew He Tianzhou was referring to her, so she had to respond. "I am deeply grateful for President He's kindness."

She kept her eyes downcast, not daring to look at He Tianzhou's face, and instead fixed her gaze on the third button of his shirt. He Tianzhou said, "Should I take off the button and give it to you? Then you two can have a private chat."

Shuangxu endured the embarrassment and made an excuse. "Sorry, I have a stiff neck today."

He Tianzhou, with his hands in his pockets, smirked. "You turned your head just fine a moment ago."

...

"President He is a busy man. Every word from his mouth is worth millions. Let's not waste his precious time. Let's go." Shuangxu spoke respectfully but distantly, then turned around and left with a straight face.

Not only were He Tianzhou's executives behind him shocked, but even the people from Feixue thought she was being outrageously disrespectful.

"Boss Song, have you lost your mind? You dare to talk back to President He?!"

"But you don't understand!" Xiao Liao blindly defended her. "Boss Song is very familiar with President He. You only heard her sarcasm, but you didn't see President He's indulgence!"

Shuangxu glanced at her. "How many degrees is your myopia?"

Xiao Liao proudly replied, "680."

Shuangxu patted her head with a look of pity.

Old Fang earnestly advised, "Boss Song, I know you're familiar with President He, but you still need to be tactful in your speech. You're a refined and wealthy beauty; it's normal that you don't know how to flatter. Next time, leave the ass-kissing to me."

Shuangxu knew everyone was doing this for Feixue. She sighed inwardly. "Alright, I'll hold back next time."

Surely, she wouldn't be so unlucky as to run into the busy President He every time.

On Monday, they returned to Yun Dun. Director Fan kept them waiting in the meeting room for fifteen minutes before finally showing up.

During the meeting, he openly checked his phone. Shuangxu, sitting to his right, glanced at an angle.

He wasn't doing anything important, just messaging someone.

Xiao Liao scribbled on her notepad and, after a while, turned it toward Shuangxu for her appreciation.

She had drawn a pig's head in a suit, complete with a receding hairline.

Shuangxu pressed her lips tightly together, struggling not to laugh. "Be serious."

Midway through the meeting, the frosted glass door suddenly opened from the outside. Assistant Xu Qing pushed the door open and stepped aside.

He Tianzhou walked in.

Tall and long-legged, his imposing presence disrupted the team member who was explaining the PPT. The entire meeting room fell silent instantly, and everyone's gaze converged on him.

Director Fan hastily put his phone away. His portly figure sprang up from his seat, instantly transforming from a demanding client director into an obsequious old eunuch at the emperor's side.

"President He, why have you come in person? Has your meeting ended?"

He Tianzhou ignored him and walked straight in.

He looked different today.

Most of the time, He Tianzhou gave off a lazy and casual vibe, but today his suit was impeccably neat, and his tie was perfectly knotted. The tailored fit showcased his excellent proportions, and the dark color suited him well.

He wore a pair of silver-rimmed glasses on his nose. His usually slightly messy black hair was combed back into a slicked-back style today, with the ends naturally tousled, appearing casual yet meticulously styled.

Director Fan respectfully invited him to the main seat. He Tianzhou sat down, crossing his right leg over his left knee, his high nose and deep eyes exuding an unapproachable nobility.

Shuangxu's gaze lingered on him for no more than a second before his sharp black eyes caught her looking.

"President Song, is your neck better?"

Shuangxu averted her eyes. "Let's continue."

With He Tianzhou present, everyone became noticeably more tense. The team member explaining the PPT stammered and made frequent mistakes.

"Relax." He Tianzhou said, "I'm not a python. I don't eat people."

You're no better than a python.

Because of his words, Shuangxu subconsciously glanced at him.

Behind him was a floor-to-ceiling glass wall. The clear light streaming in through the glass, refracted by his lenses, gave him a different texture than she remembered.

It was the first time she had seen He Tianzhou wearing glasses.

Such a scholarly accessory didn't seem to match his demeanor, but for some reason, it looked harmonious.

Perhaps because the refined glasses neutralized the sharpness in his bone structure, reducing the oppressive feeling he usually gave off.

Shuangxu was about to look away when He Tianzhou suddenly turned to her without warning.

Caught off guard, their eyes met.

The usual laziness in his gaze was refracted by the lenses, making him appear hypocritically virtuous.

Not refined—more like a refined scoundrel.

"What are you looking at?" he said. "Is there a PPT on my face?"

...

Until the meeting ended, Shuangxu kept her eyes glued to the PPT, not daring to look at him again.

After listening to the meeting content, He Tianzhou picked up the document on the table and flipped through it. He asked a direct question. "When can the finished product be ready?"

Old Fang spoke up. "The first prototype has already been made. However, due to the very low volumetric energy density of hydrogen, the liquid hydrogen tank takes up a lot of space. We haven't found an effective solution to this problem yet..."

He Tianzhou didn't even lift his head. "I dislike repeating myself. If you don't understand, find a translator."

Old Fang faltered.

Shuangxu gave a projected timeline. "Three months."

"Too slow." He Tianzhou pressed firmly. "One month."

Shuangxu replied directly. "It can't be done."

He Tianzhou lightly lifted his eyelids, shifting his gaze from the document to her face with an ambiguous expression. "Quite bold, this subcontractor."

Several employees beside her frantically signaled to her.

This is the client boss, Boss Song! Control yourself.

She couldn't.

When she didn't see He Tianzhou, she was a normal, emotionally stable person.

But once she saw him, she was forced to recall that night—his deliberate teasing and her own disgraceful behavior. The embarrassment was unbearable.

She endured it and said, "I'm just being realistic. If President He likes big talk, I can draw it up. I can give you a 'finished product' next week. But you'll find it comes with a huge liquid hydrogen tank. Does President He want that?"

He Tianzhou drawled, "If I say I don't want it, will President Song throw a tantrum at me again?"

Instantly, several scorching gazes fell on Shuangxu. After a few seconds of shock, Xiao Liao excitedly grabbed the edge of the table.

That remark was too ambiguous. Shuangxu's ears burned.

Director Fan's narrow eyes darted back and forth between her and He Tianzhou like a searchlight.

"President He, please don't joke." Shuangxu forced herself to remain calm. "Before the energy storage problem is effectively solved, we don't want to hand over a half-finished product just to deceive you. Feixue hopes that what we ultimately deliver to you is an excellent product that meets market standards."

Everyone in Yun Dun Group knew that Mr. He was a man who never gave face.

He said one, and it was final. Decisive and uncompromising, there was no room for negotiation.

Director Fan feared him not only because he was the boss with life-and-death power but also because of He Tianzhou himself.

"Then two months." He Tianzhou said, as if possessed.

Shuangxu breathed a sigh of relief.

He Tianzhou leaned back in his chair, looking at her. Behind the lenses, his black eyes were lazy, but his tone was all business. "Please send the detailed technical documents to my WeChat, President Song."

Director Fan opened his mouth, wanting to ask, Don't you never use WeChat for work?

But the old fox, who had survived in the workplace for many years, understood perfectly well the first rule of workplace survival: don't ask what you shouldn't.

As soon as they left the meeting room and entered the elevator, Shuangxu was immediately surrounded by several intense gazes.

"Boss Song, are you and President He that close?"

Shuangxu kept a straight face. "We just know each other."

"But President He seems... different with you..."

Shuangxu said, "Have you all forgotten how hard it was to secure the collaboration with Yun Dun?"

Alright. Everyone's burning gossip souls were extinguished.

Back at the company, Shuangxu had no choice but to re-add He Tianzhou on WeChat.

The only silver lining was that He Tianzhou wouldn't message her, so he wouldn't find out that she had once had the audacity to delete him.

She sent him the documents he requested. He didn't reply.

chapters.title: Who Hit You?
chapters.content:
Grandpa Song’s surgery for a blocked blood vessel was the last thing Shuangxu found out about.

She only learned of it during a meal at the Shen family home, overhearing the conversation between Fu Yun and Shen Changyuan.

"You didn’t know?" Fu Yun was surprised.

Shuangxu remained calm. "No one told me."

"How could Cui Ning not even inform you about something this big?" Fu Yun hurriedly ordered someone to prepare nutritional supplements. "He’s still at the hospital. You should go see him right now."

"I don’t want to." Shuangxu lowered her head, indifferently eating her fish. "It’s not like seeing him will make him better."

"He’s your own grandfather. His heart surgery—if you, as his granddaughter, don’t even visit him once, people will point fingers at your back and call you unfilial." Fu Yun was only saying this for her own good.

Let them call her unfilial, then. Shuangxu let the words go in one ear and out the other.

"You child." Fu Yun sighed. "Do you want people to say we raised you poorly?"

Only then did Shuangxu put down her chopsticks and stand up in compromise.

Aunt Wang, seeing her out, nervously chattered, "When you see your grandfather, behave yourself. Be sweet with your words, say something nice."

Shuangxu had no expectations. "What’s the use of being sweet? Even if I talk my way into heaven, he still won’t like me."

Aunt Wang stood at the door, watching her get into the car, silently sighing. "Such a good girl... why doesn’t he appreciate her?"

It had been over a month since she returned to the country, and Shuangxu still hadn’t seen her grandfather.

Grandpa Song had never treated her like a granddaughter, so she owed him nothing. The bond between them was weaker than that of strangers. At least strangers didn’t despise her.

This visit was purely for appearances.

The entire hospital floor had been cleared out. When Shuangxu arrived, she happened to run into Song Leyan.

As soon as Song Leyan saw her, she crossed her arms and said arrogantly, "Who told you to come?"

Shuangxu couldn’t be bothered with her and walked past her toward the inner ward.

"Last time, Shen Yu kicked me off the boat, and now you dare to show your face in front of me?" Song Leyan turned her head and shouted for someone. "Zhang Ma, kick her out!"

Zhang Ma hesitated nearby, not daring to move. "Miss, this isn’t right..."

"I say it’s right, so it’s right." Song Leyan was domineering. "Are you going to do it or not? If not, I’ll kick you out too."

Shuangxu’s position in the Song family was too awkward—neither a host nor a guest—so the servants’ attitudes toward her were always delicate.

But no matter what, Zhang Ma didn’t dare to actually drive her out.

Just as Zhang Ma was caught in a dilemma, Cui Ning’s voice rang out: "Leyan, don’t cause trouble."

"I didn’t cause trouble. She’s the one who bullied me first." Song Leyan saw Cui Ning’s displeasure and humphed, shutting her mouth.

Cui Ning’s attitude toward Shuangxu remained lukewarm. "Go in."

Shuangxu carried the nutritional supplements into the ward. Grandpa Song was leaning against the head of the bed, being fed by a nurse.

She acted obediently. "Grandpa, are you feeling better?"

Grandpa Song looked at her with the same stern and critical gaze as when she was a child. "So you do remember I’m your grandfather. I’ve been in the hospital for half a month. Even subordinates from over a decade ago come to visit every day. Have you visited even once?"

I don’t need you to promote me, Shuangxu thought.

"I didn’t know about this."

Decades of political career made Grandpa Song’s words carry the oppressive weight of a superior. "If you didn’t know, it’s not someone else’s fault. You’ve been back in the country for so long and haven’t even been home once."

Shuangxu had been trying to keep up the pretense of obedience, but now she couldn’t be bothered.

She knew it was best not to argue—it was meaningless—but she still did. "It’s not my fault either. I don’t have the ability to see the future."

Song Leyan added fuel to the fire. "Grandpa, she runs to the Shen family every day to fawn over them. Where do we even factor in?"

Shuangxu shot her a cold glance. Song Leyan felt like she was about to slap her again.

Shuangxu spoke calmly, her words carrying a hint of indirect rebuke. "If you had raised me, I would’ve fawned over you too."

Grandpa Song caught the implication and coldly scoffed. "You’ve learned to be sharp-tongued. Leyan said you hit her last time?"

Shuangxu didn’t deny it. "I did."

Without warning, Grandpa Song raised his hand and slapped her across the face.

The nurse holding the bowl froze in shock. Shuangxu’s face was knocked to the side, and a red mark quickly rose on her fair skin.

Grandpa Song had held a high position all his life, and when his voice dropped, it carried a sharp, commanding presence. "Hitting Leyan in public—whose face were you slapping? Your own heart is crooked, causing so much trouble. Your father sent you away to reflect, to learn to behave, and what have you learned? The Shen family spoils you, doesn’t discipline you properly, and that’s because your behavior abroad brings shame to our Song family!"

Song Leyan gloated nearby. "I told you, I’d return that slap!"

Shuangxu’s entire left face burned with pain. All the slaps she had ever received in her life came from her so-called family.

She didn’t cry. She couldn’t even feel wronged—only annoyed.

"It wasn’t me who shamed the Song family; it was Song Leyan. If you care so much about the Song family’s reputation, sew her mouth shut."

Grandpa Song’s face darkened, about to explode, when Cui Ning pushed open the door. "Dad, Old Zheng is here to see you."

Grandpa Song’s expression immediately switched to a smile as he greeted the elderly Mr. Zheng, who entered with a cane. "Old Zheng, why are you here?"

Old Mr. Zheng was already in his eighties, leaning on a dragon-headed cane, his graying hair topped with a black flat cap. His eyes were sharp and bright.

Though he had long retired from the front lines, his influence in political circles remained strong. Everyone addressed him respectfully as Old Zheng.

"I heard you had heart surgery. Naturally, I had to come see you."

"It was just a minor surgery." Grandpa Song was amiable. "Zuye is here too."

Zheng Zuye had been staring at Shuangxu since he entered, his gaze as venomous as a snake’s, making her uncomfortable.

She stood to the side, unnoticed, waiting until the two elders had finished their greetings. Then she found an opportunity to slip out unnoticed.

Zheng Zuye followed her like a persistent ghost. "That night, did you sleep with Yue Zifeng?"

"So it was you."

"Who else could it be?" Zheng Zuye was unashamed, even cursing Yue Zifeng for stealing his prey. "I went through all that trouble setting up the trap, and in the end, he got the benefit."

Yue Zifeng? What did he have to do with this?

Zheng Zuye didn’t dare to touch her with the Song family’s servants nearby. He blocked her path and lowered his voice. "Song Shuangxu, stop pretending to be innocent in front of me. Either play with me, or I’ll tell your brother that you slept with his good brother. Doesn’t he want to kill me? I’d love to see if he’d kill his good brother first."

Shuangxu was disgusted by him. "Do you think my brother will spare you for drugging me?"

"I dare you to tell him." Zheng Zuye was fearless, leaning in to whisper menacingly, "If I mess with you, the worst I get is a beating. But if this blows up, your grandfather, who cares so much about face, will make you marry me to save the Song family’s reputation."

"I just want to play with you. Getting married would be too much trouble."

Shuangxu clenched her teeth.

She knew Zheng Zuye was telling the truth.

If this got out, the Song family would go to any lengths to preserve their reputation. The best way would be to turn this scandal into a joyous occasion.

That night had nothing to do with Yue Zifeng. She couldn’t let him take the blame and be forced to marry her. He’d be wronged to death.

He Tianzhou? Forget it. Not only had nothing happened between them, but even if it had, He Tianzhou wouldn’t take responsibility for her.

In reality, nothing had happened that night. So in the end, either Old Zheng would let it slide and suppress the matter, or she’d have to marry Zheng Zuye to give an explanation.

Either way, it was a dead end for her.

A hand grabbed her wrist, pulling her behind someone. She looked up to see Shen Yu’s back—just like so many moments from her childhood.

"Get lost." Shen Yu said coldly. "Unless you want me to beat you up in front of your grandfather."

"Just a few words. Look at you, so nervous." Zheng Zuye acted shameless, but before leaving, he gave Shuangxu a meaningful look. "Think it over. I’ll wait for you."

Only after Zheng Zuye entered the ward did Shen Yu turn back to her. "What did he tell you to think about?"

Shuangxu’s mind was in chaos. "Just the same old things."

A shadow of gloom passed through Shen Yu’s eyes, but his tone remained gentle. "Ignore him."

Shuangxu lowered her head, lost in thought.

"Did you hear me?" Shen Yu asked.

She nodded. "I know."

Shen Yu’s gaze fell on her swollen left cheek, his expression slightly darkened.

Only then did Shuangxu remember the slap. She had been so bothered by Zheng Zuye that she’d forgotten the pain.

She instinctively tried to turn her face away, but Shen Yu’s fingers lifted her chin, turning her face back.

"Who hit you?"

She hadn’t felt wronged before, but now, looking into his eyes, her nose suddenly stung.

"My grandfather."

---

chapters.title: Dog Thief
chapters.content:
Shen Yu remained silent for a long time. After a while, he moved his hand up, pressing his warm palm against her injured cheek.

"Does it hurt?"

Shuangxu couldn’t hold back anymore. She almost burst into tears.

During the ten years she was raised by Shen Yu, she had never suffered the slightest grievance.

Back then, she wasn’t Song Shuangxu—she was just Shen Yu’s little sister, Xiao Jiu.

She had been obedient and lovable. Shen Changyuan and Fu Yun had both adored her. Yue Zifeng and his friends had doted on her. No one would have dared to hit her, and even if someone had wanted to, they would’ve thought twice.

But as soon as Song Mianzhi returned to the country, she became Song’s daughter again, and it was as if she had instantly turned into something despicable.

Sometimes, Shuangxu selfishly wished they had never come back.

"Brother..." She suddenly grabbed Shen Yu’s sleeve.

She wanted to tell him about Zheng Zuye drugging her, to hide behind him as she used to, knowing he would solve any problem for her, no matter how big.

"Is Xiao Jiu alright?" Lu Mannan’s voice rang out just then.

The unfinished words in her throat suddenly choked up.

Lu Mannan walked over, and Shuangxu let go of Shen Yu’s sleeve.

"I came with your brother to visit your grandfather. Thank goodness we arrived in time. Did Zheng Zuye bully you?" Lu Mannan asked.

"No." Shuangxu buried all her emotions.

"Your grandfather was too harsh. Your face is all swollen. Let me take you to get it treated." Lu Mannan looked pained.

"It’s fine. I’ll just ice it when I get back." Shuangxu said, "You two should go in."

Her tone was too calm, as if nothing had happened. If not for the shocking bruise on her face, no one would have guessed she had been slapped so hard.

After saying this, she walked into the elevator, turning to press the button without looking back at Shen Yu.

Night was falling. The hospital entrance was bustling with people, all with somewhere to go or someone waiting for them.

As she stepped outside, Shuangxu finally felt the burning pain on her face. It hurt so much she wanted to cry.

But no one would pick her up and gently wipe away her tears when she cried anymore.

At that moment, she didn’t want to go home. The Song residence, the Shen residence, or even the empty house on Songming Road—none of them felt like home.

A heavy weight pressed on her chest, suffocating her. She sat down on a bench at the bus stop, watching the endless stream of cars passing by.

Strangers walking past stared at her face. She couldn’t see them, but she imagined she must look a mess.

But she didn’t care.

Night fell silently. The girls waiting for the bus beside her suddenly stirred.

"Wow, such a handsome dog!"

"Hello, hello, what’s your name?"

"Hey, it’s ignoring us."

Shuangxu slightly turned her head and saw a robust and majestic Doberman weaving through the crowd at the bus stop, walking slowly toward her.

She didn’t own a dog, and to her, all dogs of the same breed looked identical—Dobermans were all sleek black with a bit of tan.

But this one was particularly cold and imposing, with an aura like a domineering CEO... It looked familiar.

She couldn’t tell if it was He Tianzhou’s dog, but the Doberman had already approached her, stretching its head toward her.

She instinctively scooted far to the side, even preparing to stand up and leave.

The Doberman dropped what it had been holding in its mouth onto the bench.

An ice pack.

Shuangxu blinked for a few seconds. "For me?"

The Doberman sat down but turned its head away, as if offended by her rejection.

"Sorry." Shuangxu apologized. "I’m a little afraid of dogs. It’s not personal."

The Doberman seemed to understand. It turned back and nudged the ice pack toward her with its snout.

Shuangxu picked up the ice pack and pressed it to her face, looking around.

She saw neither He Tianzhou’s car nor any suspicious figures.

The burning sensation on her left cheek gradually numbed under the cold, but it didn’t stop hurting—it just changed the way it hurt.

As she iced her face, the Doberman sat beside her like a cold, aloof bodyguard.

But it was too eye-catching. A beautiful woman with a swollen face and a majestic large dog drew even more stares from passersby.

Shuangxu stood up, and the dog stood with her.

Leaving it behind seemed ungrateful. She hesitated for a moment. "Where’s your owner?"

The Doberman didn’t move, as if it didn’t understand her.

Shuangxu sighed and took out her phone, dialing He Tianzhou’s number.

After three rings, he picked up, his voice casual. "President Song, to what do I owe the pleasure?"

His question left Shuangxu confused. Hadn’t he sent the dog with the ice pack?

Maybe she had the wrong dog. Or maybe the dog was a spirit?

"I ran into a Doberman. I don’t know if it’s yours."

He Tianzhou drawled, "Ask it."

Shuangxu looked down, meeting the dog’s gaze.

...

"Have you lost your dog or not? Don’t you know?" Shuangxu frowned. "If it’s not yours, I won’t bother."

"It is lost. I’ve been looking for the dog thief." He Tianzhou immediately pinned the blame on her. "So it’s you."

"Where are you?" Shuangxu asked.

There was a two-second pause on the other end. She heard He Tianzhou say, "Turn around."

Shuangxu held the phone to her ear, turning around in confusion. Across the wide road and the rushing traffic, she saw a Koenigsegg parked by the side.

The driver’s window was half down, revealing He Tianzhou’s absurdly handsome face.

So he had been this close all along.

Shen Yu and Lu Mannan entered the ward. Grandpa Song, seeing them, was cordial. "Ah Yu and Mannan are here."

Lu Mannan studied his approachable demeanor, unable to imagine that he was the one who had slapped Shuangxu’s face like that.

"Grandpa Song, are you feeling better?"

Grandpa Song smiled at the same question. "I’ve been recovering well these past few days. Thank you for your concern."

Among the younger generation in Yan City, Shen Yu was one of the most outstanding. Grandpa Song had great appreciation for this junior.

Originally, Shen Changyuan had planned for Shen Yu to enter politics. With his abilities and the Shen family’s support, he could have easily reached the vice-ministerial level by now. Unfortunately, he had no interest in political maneuvering.

The Song and Shen families were close, and Grandpa Song had once considered a marriage alliance. However, the one he had wanted to marry to Shen Yu wasn’t Shuangxu—it was Song Leyan. But five years ago, Shuangxu’s scandal had nearly dragged both families’ reputations down, making it inappropriate to bring up the subject again.

Now that the Shen family was discussing marriage with the Lu family, the matter had to be dropped.

This was also one of the reasons for his many grievances against Shuangxu.

Lu Mannan was usually good at acting cute to win the favor of elders, but perhaps because she had seen Shuangxu’s injury, she merely smiled and didn’t approach him.

Shen Yu was always polite in his dealings with others. After inquiring about the old man’s health and exchanging pleasantries, he said to Lu Mannan as they prepared to leave, "You go back first. I have a few words to say to Old Song."

Lu Mannan seemed to guess what he wanted to talk about. After closing the door behind her, she didn’t go far.

Inside the ward, Shen Yu casually brought up, "I heard Xiao Jiu made a mistake and angered you."

The air in the ward seemed to still at his words.

Shuangxu was indeed a Song, but in reality, she had grown up under Shen Yu’s care. By bringing this up, he was likely trying to stand up for her.

"Did she come to you to complain?"

"Not exactly. I ran into her on my way here. Her face was badly swollen." Shen Yu said, "I’ve been away for a while. Did she cause trouble? Why were you so angry with her?"

Cui Ning chimed in, "It’s nothing serious. She and Leyan had a quarrel, and in public, she actually laid hands on Leyan. Grandpa was just angry that she had no sense of propriety. No matter how much they argue at home, they shouldn’t let others laugh at them in public."

Shen Yu’s lips curved into a faint smile. "I thought it was something serious. Xiao Jiu has always been obedient. She’s just too soft-hearted and always gets bullied, so I taught her to be a little more assertive. If someone bullies her, she should fight back. It’s not her fault."

Grandpa Song was displeased. "I know you’re biased toward her, but she’s my granddaughter. If she does something wrong, I can’t discipline her?"

The smile on Shen Yu’s face had already faded to almost nothing.

"You can discipline her, of course. But she was raised by me. If she really did something wrong, I’m responsible. Next time, if anything happens, I’ll deal with her. You have a heart condition—don’t get so worked up."

chapters.title: Applying Medicine
chapters.content:
He Tingzhou was driving a Kurinam today, parked directly across from the bus stop. Shuangxu had never seen this car before, no wonder she hadn't noticed it earlier.

She didn't know when he had arrived.

After hanging up the phone, the motionless dog sitting on the ground stood up and walked toward the sidewalk.

After a few steps, it turned to look at her.

Shuangxu had no intention of going to He Tingzhou. She said to the dog, "You go yourself. I'm going home."

Du Bin turned back to her, signaling her to follow.

"I'm not going," Shuangxu said.

The dog, just like its owner, was domineering. It directly bit the hem of her pants with its mouth and tugged her in that direction.

"..."

It was surprisingly strong. Shuangxu really didn't want to make a scene in public by struggling with a dog.

Mainly, this dog was too fierce; she was indeed a little afraid.

She was forcibly escorted like a prisoner, step by step, from the sidewalk across the street to He Tingzhou's car.

He Tingzhou had already gotten out of the car, arms crossed, leaning against the car door, watching her being herded over by the dog.

The evening light was thin, like a layer of deep blue filter, making the whole world seem a bit blurred.

He Tingzhou had high, prominent cheekbones and sharp, narrow eyes. The lines of his face, with their rises and falls, created a strikingly handsome appearance.

Dressed in all white with black pants, he stood out excessively on the dimming street.

Shuangxu stopped about a meter away from him: "The dog is returned to you."

He Tingzhou straightened up and walked toward her. Shuangxu instinctively took a step back. Since she didn't have his long legs, He Tingzhou caught her arm and suddenly pulled her into his embrace.

Shuangxu hadn't expected his sudden action. When she collided with him, that cold, pine-like scent instantly stirred her memory.

At that moment of unstable heartbeat, she heard a motorcycle speed past behind her.

He Tingzhou loosened his grip on her arm and looked down at her: "Why is your face red?"

Shuangxu kept her composure: "If you get hit, your face would be red too."

He Tingzhou's gaze slowly traveled across her left cheek.

It was terribly swollen. The subcutaneous capillaries had probably burst. Her delicate skin was one reason, but the person who hit her had shown no mercy.

Shuangxu pushed his hand away. He Tingzhou asked, "Was the cake good?"

"What?" After asking, she understood from the dark look in his eyes.

She pressed her lips together. Even after being slapped, she had to endure this sarcasm. Annoyed, she said, "Why don't you try it yourself?"

Her sharp words didn't anger He Tingzhou at all. He gave a slight smirk: "Too bad, no chance. The person who dares to slap my face hasn't been born yet."

Shuangxu fell silent.

His arrogant tone, though infuriating, was the truth.

Who would dare to slap the face of this young master?

He Tingzhou took a tube of ointment from a bag with a pharmacy logo, unscrewed the cap, and dipped his fingertip into the ointment before bringing it near her face.

Shuangxu instinctively flinched. He Tingzhou directly gripped her chin, holding her face in place.

"It's not poisonous. Don't move. It's for the swelling."

"I can do it myself," Shuangxu tried to resist.

He Tingzhou said with a hint of mockery, "You've been sitting there on display for half a day. Didn't see you doing it yourself."

What did he mean by "on display"?

As he spoke, his fingers had already touched her cheek. The slight coolness had an immediate soothing effect.

Shuangxu gave up resisting. She turned her face slightly, her gaze falling on the roadside greenery.

Even without looking, she could still feel that strong, overwhelming presence of his gaze locked on her face. He Tingzhou lowered his head, his focus on applying the medicine making her cheeks heat up uncontrollably.

Shuangxu pressed her back against the car door, trying to put as much distance between them as possible.

"They want to look. What can I do? I can't exactly gouge out their eyes."

Her features were bright and delicate. If she were a bit more seductive, she would be dazzling.

But she carried a natural purity, with soft, rounded eyes that were lively and gentle, easily inspiring a protective instinct.

Too close, the tiny vellum hairs on her face were faintly visible in the dim light, and her eyelashes trembled slightly from tension.

He Tingzhou held her chin with his thumb and index finger. As his thumb moved against her cheek, her head obediently followed his lead.

He spread the ointment, looking down as he said, "Why not? Didn't bring a spoon?"

Shuangxu was speechless for a moment. She turned her eyes to look at him: "You gouge out someone's eyes with a spoon?"

He Tingzhou raised an eyebrow: "Then what would you use?"

His eyes were unusual, with a cold, sharp edge like a sword, yet the upward curve at the outer corners was charming and alluring. The combination of these two traits was contradictory and dangerous.

Shuangxu turned her eyes away: "I've never gouged out eyes before. How would I know?"

After applying the medicine, He Tingzhou let her go and threw the ointment back into the car.

Shuangxu secretly sighed in relief.

Feeling inexplicably uncomfortable, she was about to leave when He Tingzhou leisurely wiped his fingers clean, then took a cake box from the car and handed it to her.

Shuangxu looked at the cake, confused: "What's this for?"

He Tingzhou hooked his finger through the white silk ribbon on the cake box, his thin lips lazily tugging: "You've had the appetizer. Don't you want the main course?"

...

This man.

Shuangxu knew good from bad. After a moment of silence, she still took the cake.

She sat on a roadside chair and slowly ate the cake while He Tingzhou leaned against the Kurinam's door.

He had plucked a leaf from somewhere and was idly pinching it between his fingers.

The dog squatted beside him, both of them watching Shuangxu eat the cake.

The tiramisu was surprisingly good. As she ate, Shuangxu felt the weight of their stares.

She turned her head. Du Bin's usually cool eyes were fixed intently on the cake in her hand, licking his lips.

Shuangxu asked He Tingzhou: "Can he eat it?"

He Tingzhou glanced at the dog, bluntly: "It's poisoned. The dog will die if he eats it."

Du Bin dejectedly flopped to the ground.

After finishing the cake, it was completely dark.

Her face didn't seem to hurt as much, and her mood had returned to calm.

He Tingzhou drove her home. By the time they reached 9 Songming Road, the night was deep.

Shuangxu got out of the car at the entrance, stood there for a moment, and still said to He Tingzhou: "Thank you."

Her tone was slightly tense. One favor for another; today's medicine and cake couldn't offset his terrible behavior that day.

He Tingzhou curled his lips, leaning back against the seat, casually: "Don't thank me yet. Remember my noble image in your heart right now. Think about it before you curse me next time."

Had she cursed him? That didn't count.

"I haven't cursed you," Shuangxu said. "Every time, you tease me first. I'm just resisting after being oppressed."

He Tingzhou's dark eyes lazily glanced over: "So, do I need to apologize to you?"

Shuangxu replied firmly: "You don't need to apologize either. Next time, before you bully me, think about it first."

After saying that, she turned and went inside. When she reached the downstairs, she saw Shen Yu's car parked there.

Shen Yu stood by the car, a cigarette burning between the fingers of his hand hanging by his side. His gaze was fixed on the distance, the shadow of the phoenix tree falling on him. Lost in thought, he didn't notice Shuangxu approaching.

"Brother, why are you here?"

Shen Yu came back to his senses, saw her, and extinguished the cigarette.

"Where have you been?"

"Met a friend." Shuangxu said.

Shen Yu looked at her left cheek. The swelling had subsided a bit. "Did you take care of the injury on your face?"

Shuangxu nodded: "Applied medicine."

After May began, the temperature rose quickly. The night wind no longer felt cold but instead carried a subtle, lingering coolness that one would only notice after a while.

Shen Yu asked her: "When you were at the hospital, what did you want to tell me?"

The impulse to depend on him like a child who hadn't grown up had already cooled down. Shuangxu shook her head: "Nothing."

She couldn't always stay under Shen Yu's protection, enjoying his shelter. That right had been taken away from her five years ago.

Shen Yu seemed to be in a low mood today. He quietly looked at her for a while, then raised his hand to rub her hair.

His eyes were well hidden in the night. He said gently: "Go upstairs. Rest early."

---

chapters.title: Proposal
chapters.content:
It took several days for the swelling on Shuangxu's face to completely subside.

She wore a mask to work, and her colleagues tactfully refrained from asking about it.

In the tea room, everyone was discussing the news about a group of people being arrested for drug use at a nightclub.

This incident had caused such a stir because it involved several wealthy and well-connected young heirs.

Shuangxu had been busy searching for new composite materials for hydrogen storage and wasn't interested in such matters. She let the conversation go in one ear and out the other.

Shu Yang had slipped out of the hospital and took Shuangxu to a nearby Japanese restaurant for tonkatsu lunch. Xiao Liao tagged along to freeload.

During the meal, Shu Yang brought it up: "I heard one of them has a big background, last name Zheng. Do you know him?"

Shuangxu was taken aback: "Zheng Zuye?"

"I don't know his full name. The news didn't mention it, only 'Zheng someone.' I heard the little nurses at the hospital gossiping. They said his grandfather is very powerful." Shu Yang lowered her voice, "The kind who stands on the city gate during a military parade."

That must be Zheng Zuye then.

Shuangxu wasn't sure if Zheng Zuye was really involved with that stuff. Those rich kids might act wild usually, but the older generation still considered drugs taboo.

The Zheng family certainly had the ability to ensure his safety, but after this incident, they would probably keep a close watch on him for a while.

That would give Shuangxu some peace.

She wondered if this had anything to do with Shen Yu?

As Shuangxu pondered, Shu Yang's chopsticks stealthily reached toward her plate.

"Focus on eating, don't steal my tonkatsu," Shuangxu precisely blocked her chopsticks with her own. "You shouldn't eat fried food."

Shu Yang sighed and honestly put it down, eating her salmon salad instead.

"There's an Aquarius meteor shower this weekend," Xiao Liao, who had been playing on his phone, suddenly announced. "The best viewing spot is Dongyu Mountain. Want to go?"

"What's so great about a meteor shower?" Shu Yang, lacking romantic cells, said, "It's just some rocks falling from the sky, burning up in the atmosphere before they even hit the ground."

"You can make a wish," Xiao Liao turned to Shuangxu for resonance. "Right, little boss?"

Unfortunately, his expectations were misplaced. Shuangxu said, "I've never made a wish on a meteor shower."

Xiao Liao was baffled: "You've never made a wish? Do rich people like you have such smooth and satisfying lives that you don't need to wish for anything? I'm starting to resent the rich!"

Shuangxu laughed: "I used to have wishes. I made them to my brother. They came true relatively quickly."

"Then what about now?" Xiao Liao asked.

"Now?" Shuangxu took a sip of the clear sake in her glass. This bottle was dry, with a slightly strong bitter aftertaste.

"Now I have no wishes."

Xiao Liao opened his mouth to ask more, but Shu Yang stuffed the tonkatsu into his mouth: "The tonkatsu is so good. Do you still have time to talk? If you don't eat it, I will."

Everyone knew that Shuangxu had started a company with her friends. Yue Zifeng and the others were aware of this.

Her small business, in the eyes of these wealthy young masters, was like children playing house.

That day, after Shuangxu finished a meeting, the big-eyed receptionist knocked on the glass door of the conference room and came in: "President Song, someone is looking for you. He's quite handsome and says he's your brother."

Shen Yu?

Shuangxu immediately stood up from her seat: "Where is he?"

"In your office."

Shuangxu returned to her office. As she opened the door, the man inspecting her office turned around.

"Hey, done with your work, President Song."

Shuangxu wore a white, fitted blouse with a black printed half-skirt and a string of Australian white pearls around her neck.

She was already like a bright pearl, and this outfit made her look even more gentle and delicate.

Seeing that it was Yue Zifeng, she couldn't say she was disappointed, but a hint of expectation faded.

"Brother Zifeng," she asked, "why are you here?"

"Passing by, so I came up to see you." Yue Zifeng sat on her desk. "I ordered afternoon tea for you. Am I good to you, little sister?"

Shuangxu's portion was placed on the coffee table: coffee, qingtuan, and some exquisite Chinese pastries.

She sat down to eat and asked Yue Zifeng: "Did you come to see me for something?"

"So smart. You can tell?"

"No one visits without a reason." Shuangxu ate an almond cookie, blinking her eyes. "When have you ever come to see me?"

"What kind of talk is that? Do we need to see each other every day to prove our friendship?" Yue Zifeng walked over and sat next to her, picking a preserved plum from the plate to eat.

"Your brother and Manman's engagement banquet is set for the end of next month. Aunt Fu and Aunt He had someone pick the date."

Shuangxu slowly chewed the almond cookie, remaining silent.

"Although it was arranged by the family, Manman wants your brother to propose to her." Yue Zifeng said, "She's just a kid, same age as you. You must understand; she just wants a bit of romance."

"What does this have to do with me?" The almond cookie was a bit dry. Shuangxu swallowed it and put down the half-eaten piece.

"We don't have any experience with proposals. We brainstormed for half a day and couldn't come up with anything interesting. Manman doesn't like the usual clichés, so we're asking you for ideas."

Shuangxu said: "I've never proposed to anyone either."

"You're a girl. You and Manman get along well. You must know what she wants."

Although he wasn't Shen Yu, Shuangxu was still a little happy to see him.

But that little happiness also faded slowly after knowing his purpose.

"Did my brother ask you to come to me, or did she ask you to come to me?"

This question left Yue Zifeng a bit confused: "They didn't ask me. I was just passing by, came to your company to see you, and asked you about it by the way. This is your brother's big life event. I thought you'd want to be involved."

This reminded Shuangxu that, as his sister, she should actively bless and contribute ideas.

But she had never been proposed to, nor had she proposed to anyone. Asking her to bless and contribute ideas was really difficult.

After a moment of silence, Shuangxu said: "What she wants is just the sense of ceremony in your brother's proposal, not the method. I heard there's a meteor shower this weekend. Dongyu Mountain is the best viewing spot. You can try that."

The word "meteor shower" itself carried a romantic quality. The grand spectacle of nature became a grand blessing. Who wouldn't be moved by that?

The timing was also perfect. Yue Zifeng had an epiphany: "You're brilliant, little sister!"

The brilliant one wasn't her.

After Yue Zifeng left, she called Xiao Liao in and had him take away the remaining pastries to eat.

Afternoon tea was provided to everyone in the company. Everyone was praising how handsome and kind the little boss's brother was. Shuangxu's portion was clearly more abundant than theirs.

Xiao Liao, deeply moved, stuffed the persimmon custard cake into his mouth: "You're giving all this to me? Little boss, you're too good to me!"

Shuangxu patted his head: "You deserve it."

Shuangxu had only provided inspiration. As for the specific planning of the proposal, she wasn't involved.

Yue Zifeng and the others arranged the weekend trip to Dongyu Mountain and posted it in the WeChat group.

This group had been created a long time ago, with Yue Zifeng as the admin. Shuangxu was one of the first batch of "elders" in the group, right after Shen Yu's profile picture.

Over the years, this small group had only included their close, trusted brothers, totaling more than a dozen people. They hadn't added new members in years.

Not to mention ordinary drinking buddies, even their girlfriends weren't qualified to join.

Lu Mannan was an exception.

To maintain the element of surprise, Yue Zifeng's Dongyu Mountain trip was labeled as "weekend camping," but everyone knew this trip was for Shen Yu's proposal.

Such a big event, everyone expressed that they must attend. Even Zuo Zhong, who was supposed to go abroad for business, had canceled his ticket and postponed his work.

In the entire group, only Shuangxu and another perpetually inactive young master hadn't replied.

Yue Zifeng tagged them both individually.

[@9.9 @H You two remember to clear your schedules for the weekend, don't forget]

When Shuangxu saw it, besides this message, there was also a private message from Lu Mannan.

It's Manman not slowly: [Xiaojiu, are you coming?]

chapters.title: You're Not Going to Crash the Proposal, Are You?
chapters.content:
Shuangxu had just gotten off work and returned home.

She didn’t reply to Yue Zifeng but instead responded to Lu Mannan: [I’m optional that day.]

Lu Mannan said: [I want you there to witness it, but I’m also afraid something unexpected might happen if you come.]

They understood each other implicitly, so they could be frank without beating around the bush. Directness was best.

Shuangxu said: [Then I won’t go.]

Shen Yu’s major life event—she didn’t want to miss it. Even though she knew that happiness would be built on her own sorrow, she still wanted to be there to bless him.

But at the same time, she didn’t want to ruin this equally important moment for Lu Mannan. If Lu Mannan wanted her to stay away, she wouldn’t go.

Lu Mannan said: [You’re not going to crash the proposal, are you?]

Shuangxu, expressionless: [You’re just proposing, not getting married. What would I crash?]

Lu Mannan: [Take that back! Take it back! You ruined my surprise!]

Shuangxu: [...]

Shuangxu hadn’t eaten dinner yet. She never learned to cook and had no interest in it. She ordered takeout on her phone and, while waiting, sat on the floor by the window, gazing at the night view.

The large flat at 9 Songming Road was spacious and vast. Living alone, there was a pin-drop silence that felt eerily quiet.

Outside the floor-to-ceiling windows were the dazzling lights of Yancheng, a city of over twenty million people. Every time she looked out at the night view through the folding windows, Shuangxu felt her own insignificance.

The takeout arrived, and she went to get it, arranging it on the dining table.

Perhaps out of some vengeful impulse—though she wasn’t sure who she wanted to take revenge on—she ordered a lot: crispy fried chicken drenched in cheese pull, and a large pizza.

It was a feast, but eating alone was joyless.

She thought for a moment, then took a photo and sent it to Shu Yang and Xiao Liao.

Shu Yang, who ate bland hospital meals every day and felt like she was becoming a celestial being, sent a voice message that lasted a full sixty seconds.

At the end, she said, “I’m blocking you now. Unblock you after you finish eating.”

Xiao Liao was more direct: [Wait for me! I’m taking a taxi over right now!]

Shuangxu’s mood improved: [Come. You can sleep in the fish tank tonight.]

Half an hour later, Xiao Liao rushed over, even bringing half a dozen beers on the way.

“Wow, such a beautiful night view! So this is how rich people’s Yancheng looks—totally different from ours!” Xiao Liao pressed against the glass. “Living in a place like this, do you have no worries at all?”

“Yes, I do,” Shuangxu said. “Rich people get constipated too.”

“True!” Xiao Liao instantly felt mentally balanced.

Shuangxu simply laid out a mat by the window, and the two sat on the floor, admiring the night view while eating fried chicken and drinking beer.

“Little boss, have you found your turtle yet?”

Shuangxu shook her head. “Probably not. It’s been missing for a long time.”

Turtles were hardy, but they weren’t immortal. It had been so long with no sign—maybe it had starved to death in some corner.

“Then just get another one,” Xiao Liao said lightly. “If you find the old one later, you’ll have two.”

“I’m not getting another,” Shuangxu said. “Where would you sleep?”

Xiao Liao lunged at her: “You’re cursing me!”

Shuangxu laughed so hard she collapsed.

With Xiao Liao around, her mood lightened considerably.

That night, Shuangxu didn’t actually make her sleep in the fish tank. Instead, she took her to the guest room.

The guest room had never been used. Xiao Liao rolled around on the bed like a dog marking its territory, then peacefully folded her hands over her stomach.

“Don’t wake me up tomorrow. I’m sleeping here for three days and three nights.”

Shuangxu returned to her own bedroom. Before sleep, she checked her phone and saw a message from Lu Mannan.

[I still hope you come. Sincerely. Ah Yu definitely wants you there too.]

On Saturday afternoon, Shuangxu changed into a lightweight hiking jacket, put on her backpack, and went downstairs—only to find Shen Yu and Yue Zifeng already waiting for her.

This was the most complete gathering yet. Lu Mannan had brought a few of her own friends. Several cars lined up, each filled with people.

Lu Mannan, sitting in the passenger seat of Shen Yu’s car, called out to her: “Xiao Jiu, Ah Yu’s friends are in our car. You take my cousin’s car first.”

The rear window rolled down, revealing a strikingly handsome man and woman inside.

The man was Shen Yu’s friend, the president of Hengtai Bank—Shuangxu had met him before when she was with Shen Yu. His newlywed wife was the eldest daughter of the Bai family in Yancheng.

“Shen An ge, Qing Mei jie,” she greeted politely before heading to the car behind.

He Tingzhou was driving the Kurin. Seeing him still made her uncomfortable, so she bypassed the passenger seat entirely.

She climbed into the back, fastened her seatbelt, and when she looked up, she unexpectedly met He Tingzhou’s gaze in the rearview mirror.

He wore a black stand-up collar jacket, making his features appear even sharper and more defined.

He Tingzhou had a piece of candy in his mouth and watched her indifferently through the mirror.

“Do I look like your family’s chauffeur?”

Shuangxu said, “I’m not feeling well today. I want to sit in the back.”

“What’s wrong?” He Tingzhou asked.

Shuangxu: “Everything’s wrong.”

He Tingzhou curled his lip. “If you’re that uncomfortable, should I find a sedan chair to carry you up the mountain later?”

Shuangxu averted her gaze first, refusing to engage further.

What relieved her was that, after a while, Yue Zifeng—who had gone to buy water—returned and took the passenger seat.

“Let’s go, let’s go.”

Yue Zifeng chattered nonstop the entire way, while Shuangxu remained quietly in the back.

As the chief commander of this proposal operation, he assigned Shuangxu a glorious and arduous task.

“Little sister, today you don’t have to do anything. Just be responsible for handing your brother the ring at the critical moment. Listen for my signal, got it?”

Shuangxu hummed in response.

Yue Zifeng turned to look at her. “Why so unenthusiastic?”

Shuangxu raised her voice: “Got it!”

He Tingzhou suddenly laughed.

Shuangxu didn’t understand what he was laughing at and continued looking out the window.

He Tingzhou drove with one hand on the wheel, his left arm resting on the window frame. He crushed the hard candy in his mouth—the crisp yet muffled sound carried a hint of orange flavor.

“Where’d you get the candy?” Yue Zifeng rummaged through the glove compartment but found nothing.

He Tingzhou jerked his chin backward. “Ask the little princess.”

Shuangxu glanced at him in confusion. She didn’t have any candy.

Yue Zifeng actually reached out to her. “Princess, give me one.”

“...I finished them.” Shuangxu said.

The caravan drove east for over an hour before reaching the Dongyu Mountain camping base.

---

chapters.title: The Second Lead Still Has Scenes
chapters.content:
The camping base was located on Dongyu Mountain. When they arrived by car, Shen Yu and the others had already gotten there first.

Lu Mannan was originally standing next to Shen Yu. He Tingzhou parked the car, and as the three of them got out, Shen Yu walked over.

He first examined Shuangxu’s face. “Is your injury better?”

“It healed a few days ago.” Shuangxu said.

Shen Yu said, “Rest for a while, eat something. We’ll set off in an hour.”

Shuangxu nodded and noticed Lu Mannan and her friends all looking in their direction.

Lu Mannan’s friends were the same group of sisters from before. Because of the unpleasantness on the yacht last time, she was afraid Shen Yu would be displeased, so this time she hadn’t invited Song Leyan.

Shuangxu spotted the twin sisters.

Shen Yu had booked the entire place in advance. Today, the whole mountain would be free of outsiders.

Those who had arrived early had already set up camp stoves, and all kinds of picnic cooking utensils, ingredients, and drinks were ready.

He Tingzhou set up a folding chair on the anti-corrosion platform, crossed his right leg over his left, and sat on it like an old man.

Yue Zifeng had specially brought two professional DSLR cameras and a DV camcorder to record the day’s ceremony.

He handed the DV to He Tingzhou. “You film later. I’ve adjusted all the settings. Go scout the location, find a good angle, and shoot some empty scenery shots. I’ll get someone to edit a big production later.”

He Tingzhou didn’t respond. He lifted his eyelids, giving Yue Zifeng a noble look that said, Are you ordering me?

“This is your own cousin,” Yue Zifeng said, shoving the DV into his hands. “Remember, when the sister hands over the ring, give it a big close-up.”

He Tingzhou lazily took the DV. “The second lead still has scenes.”

Shuangxu, who was nearby drinking water, paused: “...”

“What second lead? I want you to film the ring close-up!” Yue Zifeng felt he had entrusted the wrong person. This young master’s dictionary clearly lacked the phrase “follow orders.” What if he didn’t even turn the camera on?

He Tingzhou fiddled with the DV, panning the lens over the campsite where everyone was resting.

Yue Zifeng walked over to discuss the operation plan with Zuo Zhong and the others. Lu Mannan and her group of friends were busy grilling meat and making milk tea. Shen Yu stood with Zhou Shengan, while Bai Qingmei Mei, having picked a wild grass from somewhere, wove it into a ring and slipped it onto Zhou Shengan’s finger.

The lens panned to a certain direction. Today, Shuangxu had tied her hair into a bun, a round, plump mass perched on her head.

She held her phone, taking photos of the distant mountains. The loose strands of hair on either side were blown by the wind, and from her hairline to the tip of her nose was a smooth, unbroken line. Her bare face was light and translucent, like a pearl perfectly nurtured within a shell.

After the meat was grilled, everyone gathered at the table to eat.

Shuangxu sat next to Yue Zifeng. Lu Mannan handed her the dish she had just served. “Xiao Jiu, this one’s for you.”

Shen Yu, who had just walked over, said, “She doesn’t eat bean sprouts.”

Lu Mannan froze.

Shuangxu still reached out to take it. “It’s fine.”

Lu Mannan pulled it back, smiling as if nothing had happened. “Don’t force yourself. I’ll get you another plate.”

Bai Qingmei Mei and Zhou Shengan, who arrived last, sat next to Shuangxu. They had only exchanged a quick glance in the car earlier, so now they finally had time to talk.

Shuangxu wasn’t very close with Bai Qingmei Mei, but Bai Qingmei Mei was very friendly to her. “The last time I saw you, you were competing in a swimming race. It’s been so long—you’ve grown up.”

Shuangxu smiled. “I wasn’t back yet when you got married. Congratulations on your marriage.”

She usually seemed cold, but when she smiled, the faint creases under her eyes made her look sweet.

Bai Qingmei Mei was only a few years older than her, yet she treated Shuangxu like a child, pinching her cheek with a smile.

“Swimming race?” Zhou Shengan asked.

“Yes, the Youth Swimming Championship. She won first place, isn’t that amazing?” Bai Qingmei Mei chatted excitedly. “She left the second-place finisher far behind. After the race, a group of reporters surrounded her for interviews, and the director kept cutting to her face. Too bad all those shots were edited out in the replay.”

“That day, we all went to watch the race. Court Zhou was there too.”

Shuangxu’s expression showed clear surprise as she looked at He Tingzhou diagonally across from her.

He Tingzhou was there that day? She didn’t remember.

She had participated in the race, and Shen Changyuan and Fu Yun were overjoyed, buying dozens of tickets. Close friends and relatives each got one. It was natural that He Tingzhou received an invitation.

He himself clearly didn’t care much about such trivial matters. He didn’t even spare her a glance, his indifferent tone: “Is that so? No memory of it.”

After finishing the meal and resting for a while, the group prepared to start climbing the mountain.

From there to the mountain summit observation deck was still a distance away—it would take two hours to climb.

It offered just the right amount of hiking enjoyment, making the proposal ceremony under the meteor shower feel like a hard-won joy. At the same time, it wasn’t so strenuous that everyone would be exhausted, their makeup ruined, affecting the beauty of the important moment.

Before setting off, Shen Yu reminded Shuangxu: “It’ll get cold at night. Bring a hat.”

Shuangxu had often gone hiking and camping with him before. Shen Yu was a very considerate older brother. She had never worried about anything—he had always taken care of everything.

Fortunately, she had prepared fairly well before coming, packing a cold-weather hat in her backpack.

The climbing team formed a single file. She originally followed behind Shen Yu and Lu Mannan.

Lu Mannan, probably not used to exercise, soon started complaining about being tired. Shen Yu took her already light bag, then turned back and reached out to Shuangxu.

Shuangxu shook her head. “No need, brother. I’m not tired.”

As they continued climbing, the twin sisters called out, “Mannan, let us take a photo for you!” They squeezed past Shuangxu to get in front of her.

Shuangxu stepped aside to let them pass. After the group of sisters went ahead, she saw He Tingzhou strolling slowly behind, filming the scenery with the DV.

It was evening, and they were chasing the sun as it hid behind the mountains. They walked and stopped, the views endlessly beautiful.

After climbing higher, the temperature indeed dropped. Especially when passing through mountain streams, the humidity in the air increased, and the flowing water brought a chill. Even with a jacket, it felt a bit cold.

Shuangxu took out her hat and put it on, following the people in front as they stepped on stones to cross the stream.

The last step had a bit of a height gap. Yue Zifeng turned back to help her: “Come on, slow down.”

Shuangxu took his hand and stepped up onto the stone.

He Tingzhou walked behind her, his gaze slowly sliding over their joined hands.

After she got up, Yue Zifeng let go of her hand. Someone called him from ahead, and he went over.

Shuangxu was about to continue forward when He Tingzhou called from behind: “Little yellow hat, give me a hand.”

Shuangxu turned to look at him, then at the others ahead, realizing he was calling her.

Fine. Her hat was indeed yellow.

This height was a bit challenging for a girl, but the men in front had all climbed up on their own. None of them asked for help. At 1.88 meters tall, he was plenty capable.

But Shuangxu wasn’t that petty. She grumbled but extended her hand: “This rock isn’t even as long as your leg.”

He Tingzhou took her fair, slender fingers. They were soft, with a slight coolness.

Shuangxu tried to pull him up with all her strength, only to realize how naive she was.

She almost got pulled down by He Tingzhou, stumbling forward a step. She was one step away from falling with him.

At that moment, her expression must have been filled with terror. Fortunately, at the last second, He Tingzhou’s other leg stepped up, and he steadied himself on the ground.

Shuangxu immediately let go of his hand and turned away to walk forward.

During a rest stop, the sky had already darkened. He Tingzhou stood at the edge of the cliff with Yue Zifeng and the others, smoking.

Shuangxu didn’t go over to Shen Yu’s side. She sat alone on a stone in the corner, listening to everyone chat and joke around.

A few girls who were dressed too lightly huddled together, shivering. “Why is it so cold up here?”

“Didn’t I tell you to dress warmer?” Yue Zifeng sounded like a mother scolding disobedient children. He tsked. “There’s a waterfall up ahead. It’ll get even colder.”

That said, he still took off his jacket and gave it to them with gentlemanly grace.

Zuo Zhong also gave up his jacket, but one girl was still hugging herself and shivering, casting a hopeful look toward the nearby men.

He Tingzhou’s bone structure was truly superior. From the side, the lines of his brows and nose rose and fell with perfect rhythm, like the undulating peaks of distant mountains.

Yue Zifeng said, “He-ye, take off your jacket and give it to her.”

chapters.title: Xiao Jiu, Don’t Be Afraid
chapters.content:
The girl’s face flushed slightly, her expression tinged with anticipation.

He Tingzhou held a cigarette between his lips, his dark eyes slanting over. "Which one do you want me to take off?"

"Like I’d ask you to take off your pants." Yue Zifeng said, "If I told you to take it off, would you?"

He Tingzhou narrowed his eyes slightly, a mischievous smirk tugging at his lips, his tone light and teasing. "If you want to, go ahead. Do it yourself."

Yue Zifeng: "Damn it!"

Shuangxu couldn’t help but laugh.

He Tingzhou heard it and glanced at her sideways.

Shuangxu immediately stifled her laughter.

The lazy, indifferent look in He Tingzhou’s eyes slowly faded. He took the cigarette from his mouth, stood at the edge of the cliff, and looked at her as he said, "Song Shuangxu."

"Don’t move."

Shuangxu froze. She had never seen such an expression on He Tingzhou’s face before.

He was either cold or, like just now, casually indifferent. This deeply focused and serious gaze was unusual.

On the other side, Zhou Shengan pulled his wife behind him and said, "Where’s Shen Yu?"

Shuangxu realized something was wrong. Following their gaze, she turned her head very, very slowly and saw a bright green snake peeking out from a branch about a meter behind her.

"Holy shit!" Yue Zifeng jumped in shock. It was getting dark, and he couldn’t see clearly. "Is that an emerald green snake or a bamboo pit viper?"

Zuo Zhong’s voice was grave. "Bamboo pit viper. Look at the shape of its head—triangular means it’s a bamboo pit viper."

"This snake is venomous, little sister, you must not move!"

He didn’t need to say it—Shuangxu was already terrified.

She had been afraid of all kinds of snakes, insects, and rodents since she was a child, especially snakes. She couldn’t even look at a picture of one without breaking out in goosebumps, let alone a live one staring at her from such a close distance.

She didn’t know how to tell the difference between a bamboo pit viper and an emerald green snake, but the bright green color on the snake’s body was especially horrifying.

Its triangular head was even more chilling, and when it stared at Shuangxu, it sent shivers down her spine.

She didn’t dare to look, yet didn’t dare to look away. Every hair on her body stood on end. She clenched her palms tightly, but her fingers still trembled uncontrollably.

Her entire body was tense to the extreme. She was terrified, but she didn’t dare to move recklessly, afraid of provoking the snake’s attack.

Please, could it just go away?

Yue Zifeng and Zuo Zhong were frantically pacing. "Is there a stick? Find a stick!"

Bai Qingmei, with her richer outdoor experience, said, "It’s too close. Unless you hit it in one strike, it might get startled and attack Shuangxu. Plus, the branch is too soft—it’s not easy to hit."

"So what do we do?"

He Tingzhou had already extinguished his cigarette. He looked extremely calm, and his tone when speaking to Shuangxu was ordinary.

"Do you have a trekking pole?"

Shuangxu’s face had turned pale, her voice tight with a tremor. "Yes."

"Hold it." He Tingzhou said, "If it attacks you, fight it off."

Shuangxu wanted to cry but couldn’t. Fight it off? As if.

But He Tingzhou’s composed tone, even in the face of such danger, calmed her terrified heart just a little. She quietly reached for the trekking pole beside her and gripped it tightly.

He Tingzhou said, "Now, slowly stand up. Come over here."

Shuangxu moved extremely slowly, lifting her bottom off the rock at a turtle’s pace.

Her movements were extremely light and careful, shifting inch by inch.

Everyone fell silent, not daring to make a sound. No one dared to step forward.

"What’s going on?" Shen Yu, who was some distance away, noticed the abnormality. When he saw the branch behind Shuangxu, his expression suddenly darkened.

Lu Mannan was so scared she immediately grabbed his arm.

"Ahhh~~~! There’s a snake!" The girls behind them screamed.

Forget the snake—Yue Zifeng was startled by their screams.

Shen Yu, who was usually the epitome of gentlemanly grace toward women, rarely wore such a cold expression. He said in a deep voice, "Shut up!"

The snake was still stimulated by the sharp, sudden screams. Its body, which had been still on the branch, suddenly moved.

Shuangxu’s heart leapt into her throat.

He Tingzhou had somehow already moved to her side at some point. He grabbed her wrist and pulled hard.

At the same time, the snake lunged. Shuangxu was so scared her soul nearly left her body. In that critical moment, He Tingzhou’s right hand swiftly and precisely pinched the snake’s neck.

Shuangxu’s body hair stood on end.

He Tingzhou let go of her and walked to the edge of the cliff, throwing the snake down.

Before Shuangxu, who was still frozen in place, could react, she was pulled into Shen Yu’s arms.

Shen Yu’s voice still carried lingering tension as he held her and soothed, "It’s over. Xiao Jiu, don’t be afraid."

Shuangxu’s terrified nerves slowly relaxed. She turned her head toward He Tingzhou.

Yue Zifeng was pouring mineral water over his hands, washing them while expressing his admiration with all his heart. "Boss, you’re my idol! You even dare to grab a venomous snake with your bare hands—what the hell are you not brave enough to do?"

He Tingzhou washed his hands leisurely under the water, his brow furrowed in extreme disgust.

His tone was still as casual as ever, and with a straight face, he replied, "Watching horror movies."

The young master’s germaphobia kicked in. He scrubbed for three minutes, used up two bottles of water, then wiped his hands twice with disinfectant wipes before reluctantly drying them.

Shen Yu took Shuangxu to rest. Before sitting down, she looked behind her with lingering fear. There were no trees or bushes, so she finally felt at ease.

She took out a bottle of mineral water from her bag to drink, but Shen Yu swapped it with a thermos.

"Drink something warm."

To her surprise, the thermos contained pear and ginger tea. The rising steam, in the cold mountain air and after the shock, felt especially comforting.

"Did Auntie make this?"

Her face was still a little pale from the scare. Shen Yu gently patted her head. "Drink."

After several hours, the ginger tea had cooled to a drinkable temperature. The warmth spread through her as she drank, and she slowly sipped from the thermos, her body warming up.

She didn’t notice that, not far away, the twins were looking at her with disdain.

Because of the unexpected snake encounter, they rested a little longer. Once Shuangxu had recovered from the shock, they continued upward.

Zuozhong looked up at the sky. "Do you think it might rain soon?"

"Impossible." Yue Zifeng was absolute. "I checked the weather forecast. We came all this way to see the meteor shower, not to watch it rain."

---

chapters.title: Xiao Jiu Isn’t That Kind of Person
chapters.content:
Because of the earlier incident, Shen Yu paid extra attention to Shuangxu on the way up the mountain.

To Yue Zifeng and the others, this was the most natural thing in the world. It was only right for a brother to take care of his sister. If his own little troublemaker had been there today, he’d probably collapse after two steps and demand to be carried up the mountain.

The twins, however, looked like they couldn’t stand it. They complained to Lu Mannan, "Manman, look at her—she’s monopolizing Shen Yu."

Lu Mannan said, "He’s Xiao Jiu’s brother. It’s only natural for him to take care of her."

"He’s not even her real brother." The older twin, the one who had gotten slapped for talking too much last time, said, "I already told you—their relationship isn’t pure. And she even admitted she likes Shen Yu. Her best friend told us herself."

"Didn’t you see him hugging her right in front of you? Isn’t that slapping you in the face?"

Lu Mannan said, "Xiao Jiu was scared by the snake. A Yu was just comforting her."

"It’s just a snake. Why make such a big deal out of it? Look at her now—she’s successfully made Shen Yu feel sorry for her."

"If you ask me, you shouldn’t have let her come today. It’s such an important day—aren’t you afraid she’ll ruin it?"

"Alright, stop. Xiao Jiu isn’t that kind of person."

Lu Mannan couldn’t deny that she did feel a little down.

Shen Yu had been very attentive to her this whole time, but she could tell that it was more out of gentlemanly courtesy. The way he cared for Shuangxu was different—natural, like breathing.

She knew she should understand, but after all, she was just a young girl in her early twenties. She still felt a little jealous.

"She’s just pretending to be innocent in front of Shen Yu. She’s actually really scheming. Manman, you’re just too soft. You can’t beat someone like her, a master of schemes."

Shuangxu had recovered and looked back.

Even though He Tingzhou was always mean to her and often teased her, that was one thing. The thousands of years of Chinese civilization and its accumulated language were not enough to express how she felt when she saw He Tingzhou grab that venomous snake.

He Tingzhou walked at the very end of the group, with many people between them.

She only glanced at him once, but He Tingzhou noticed. He suddenly looked up and met her gaze.

Across the long line of people and their chatter, his eyes lingered on her face, locking eyes with her.

A few seconds later, Shuangxu was the first to look away.

The night sky was vast, and the wind on the mountaintop was invigorating, carrying the scent of the forest, though it was even colder.

After reaching the observation deck, Director Yue began organizing everyone to set up camp. He even had Shuangxu, who bore a great responsibility, rehearse a few times at the observation deck.

If he weren’t afraid of ruining the surprise, with his meticulous and perfectionist spirit, he would probably have dragged Shen Yu and Lu Mannan up to rehearse in person.

The process was actually very simple. After all, Shuangxu was just a tool—she didn’t even have a single line.
