Yue Zifeng handed her the ring box. "You hold onto this. This is the most important thing today. Don’t lose it."

Shuangxu put the ring box into her backpack. "Got it, Director Yue."

After confirming the process, they were about to return to the campsite when Lu Mannan’s friends arrived with colored lights and other decorations to set up the venue.

The twins called out to her, "Shuangxu, come help us. We rested for too long earlier, and now we’re running out of time. We’re afraid we won’t finish."

Shuangxu turned to look at them.

The twin sisters were senior members of Song Leyan’s fan club. Normally, they followed Song Leyan’s every word. Shuangxu had just returned when she had an unpleasant encounter with them at Shen Yu’s birthday party.

Besides the two of them, there were two other girls Shuangxu didn’t recognize. They were Lu Mannan’s friends from her time in Lincheng.

It was a legitimate request, so Shuangxu didn’t refuse. She stayed to help.

Yue Zifeng checked his watch. "Then you all stay busy. I’ll go back first and come find you later."

They had balloons, colored lights, electronic candles, and even rose petals that had been carried all the way up the mountain.

Their task was to wrap the colored lights around the railings, scatter rose petals on the steps, and leave the balloon inflating to Shuangxu.

Everyone had their own duties. The other two girls quickly finished with the rose petals. "Miss Song, we’ll go back and help Manman with her makeup."

Shuangxu responded. She was almost done with the balloons when she suddenly heard someone exclaim, "Oh no!"

The twins were leaning over the railing. "Whose bag is that? I didn’t see it and accidentally kicked it down."

Shuangxu’s bag had originally been placed on the right side of the steps. She turned her head and saw that her bag was no longer there.

She immediately walked to the railing and looked down. Her backpack had fallen into the bushes below.

"My bag wasn’t there. How could you have kicked it?"

The older twin looked wronged. "I didn’t do it on purpose. I was wrapping the lights here and didn’t see it. You didn’t place it properly—you can’t blame me."

The younger twin said, "Maybe when they were placing the candles earlier, they thought it was in the way and moved it."

This pair of twins—the older one was sharp-tongued, while the younger one seemed honest and simple, but in reality, they were cut from the same cloth.

Shuangxu frowned. "You’re causing trouble in the wrong place and time. Do you even have a brain?"

"We didn’t do it on purpose. What do we gain from knocking your bag down?"

Shuangxu coldly replied, "That’s why I said you don’t have a brain."

She didn’t want to waste time arguing with them. She turned and started walking down from the observation deck.

That bag contained the ring. If she couldn’t find it, tonight’s proposal would be ruined.

The twins didn’t follow. Shuangxu didn’t expect their help in the first place, nor did she pay them any more mind.

Her phone was in the bag, so she couldn’t call anyone. She had to go herself.

Her sense of direction was average at best. The sky was getting darker, and the flashlight’s range was limited. The unfamiliar mountain path felt like a maze.

She groped her way down, occasionally looking up to judge the direction based on the observation deck’s position. But the mountain path was winding. What looked like a short distance from above took forever to cover.

She finally picked up her bag from the grass. The first thing she did was open the zipper to check. Thankfully, the ring was still there.

The twins walked back to the campsite together. With only the two of them, they dropped the act.

"Will this work?"

"Relax. That forest is like a maze. Even I get lost sometimes after coming here so many times. She definitely won’t be back anytime soon. Does she really think she can show up on a day like today? She must have bad intentions."

"Won’t they go look for her?"

"The meteor shower is about to start, and Shen Yu’s going to propose. Who has time to worry about her? They’ll only notice she’s missing after the proposal. Let her stay there for now."

The younger twin was a little worried. "What if she comes back and tells Shen Yu?"

"We didn’t do it on purpose. How were we supposed to know she’d get lost? If she can’t find her way back, it’s her own fault for having a bad sense of direction."

The two chuckled as they walked back. From a distance, they saw He Tingzhou with his DV camera. They quickly fell silent, lowered their heads, and hurried past.

chapters.title: Why Is She Called Xiao Jiu
chapters.content:
Shuangxu retraced her steps, and suddenly, a drop of water landed on her shoulder.

Rain?

She quickened her pace, but the sudden downpour arrived with fierce intensity, turning into a torrential rain in an instant, the heavy raindrops pounding down on her.

The sky darkened further, and the pouring rain made the mountain path even harder to recognize. The road became muddy and slippery.

She took out her phone to call someone, only to unfortunately find there was no signal.

With the rain, everyone would probably stay at the campsite and not go to the observation deck.

This place was still some distance from the campsite. Walking through the mountains in a storm was too dangerous and terrifying. Shuangxu didn’t want to take the risk, so when she came across a cave along the way, she took shelter inside to wait out the rain.

She roughly remembered the way; once the rain stopped, she could go back.

But Shen Yu and the others might worry if they found her missing. Just in case, she hung her yellow cold-weather cap on a tree branch outside the cave.

The cave was dry, just a little dark. She turned on her flashlight, found a clean spot, and sat down to rest.

There was a shallow stream inside, and the faint sound of flowing water suddenly reminded her of that snake. Nervously, she swept the area with her flashlight.

Thankfully, the surroundings were empty. Nothing was there.

But she couldn’t relax for long before she started to feel cold.

The mountain was already chilly, and with the heavy rain, the perpetually damp and cold cave sent a bone-deep chill through her.

Shuangxu was freezing. She stubbornly turned her phone off and on again, but there was still no service. She gave up in resignation.

What kind of weather forecast had Yue Zifeng been looking at? It was completely wrong.

With rain this heavy, forget about a proposal—even a meteor shower would be impossible to see.

Maybe the storm came quickly and would leave just as fast. If they were lucky, they might still catch the original plan and not let everyone’s hard work and effort go to waste.

The rain poured for a while, and the downpour showed no sign of stopping. As Shuangxu listened to the rain, amid the storm’s roar, she suddenly heard footsteps.

Footsteps in the rainy night—like the beginning of a horror movie. Her nerves instinctively went on alert, and she picked up a rock from beside her for defense.

A tall shadow approached the cave entrance through the storm. In the flashlight’s beam, He Tingzhou’s excessively handsome face appeared.

The unexpected encounter left Shuangxu stunned for several seconds before she finally put the rock down.

Shuangxu had been wearing a hat when she arrived and had taken shelter in time, so she was only slightly damp. He Tingzhou, however, was in much worse shape.

His hair was nearly soaked through, his black tactical jacket was drenched, and his face was wet with rain.

He Tingzhou lowered his head and entered the cave, probably having rushed to escape the rain, as he was still slightly out of breath.

He stood there, staring at Shuangxu for a moment. Once his breathing steadied, he mockingly curled his lips. “You’re quite the clever monkey, knowing to take shelter.”

As if she were an idiot who wouldn’t think to get out of the rain.

Shuangxu guessed he was just bitter because he’d gotten drenched while she hadn’t.

“Aren’t you here to escape the rain too?” she said softly.

He Tingzhou flicked the rain off his clothes, pushed his hair back, and sat down two steps away from her, leaning against the cave wall.

His entire face was damp, the wet hair making his features even more striking—thick brows, deep-set eyes, sharp and overwhelmingly handsome.

The DV camera was casually tossed to the ground, already soaked through. She didn’t know if it was broken.

It was so late, and he was still filming. Sure enough, only a close cousin like his beloved younger cousin could make him this devoted.

They were both in the same boat. Even though this person was someone she avoided at all costs, having someone familiar with her in this moment of distress still lessened her fear a great deal.

He Tingzhou didn’t speak, leaning there to rest. Neither did she.

The two of them ignored each other, like two strangers who just happened to take shelter in the same cave. Only the clear stream trickled softly between them.

The storm continued, and the cold seeped into her bones. Shuangxu gradually turned pale from the chill, curling up.

A rustling sound came from beside her—He Tingzhou was taking off his jacket.

Shuangxu’s first thought was that he meant to give it to her, but she quickly dismissed the idea.

At the cliffside, when Yue Zifeng had asked him to be a gentleman, he had acted as if it were none of his business.

No gentlemanly manners, so where would he even find any to display?

Besides, the cave was freezing. He must be cold too.

He Tingzhou draped the jacket over himself and tilted his head toward her. “Come over here.”

Shuangxu’s mind, inopportune as ever, recalled the time he had held her tightly in his arms, the heat she had felt from him.

In the dimness, her cheeks warmed slightly. Without thinking, she refused, “No need.”

He Tingzhou’s dark eyes gazed at her indifferently. “Between you freezing to death and me freezing to death, there’s a compromise option where we both stay alive. Come here.”

His tone brooked no argument, and Shuangxu’s fingertips were already numb from the cold. If this continued, by the time the rain stopped tomorrow and Shen Yu found her, she might be a frozen popsicle.

After a long hesitation, she slowly inched toward He Tingzhou, carefully lifting a side of his jacket and tucking herself underneath.

He Tingzhou glanced at her but didn’t respond.

His tactical jacket was waterproof, warm and dry inside, carrying his signature cool and composed scent.

The moment she got close, every cell in Shuangxu’s body seemed to catch a cold—then suddenly spike with fever.

It reminded her of how she had once been far too intimate with him.

She shared the jacket with He Tingzhou to keep warm, but she also tried to keep her body from getting too close to his. These two conflicting goals left her body stiff.

The flashlight illuminated the cave wall in front of them. He Tingzhou closed his eyes, and Shuangxu thought he was going to sleep, so she prepared to turn off the flashlight.

Just as she picked it up, He Tingzhou spoke: “Don’t turn it off. I’m afraid of the dark.”

In everyone’s eyes, He Tingzhou was a man without any fears.

He was reckless and free, even daring to catch poisonous snakes with his bare hands. Yet he was afraid of the dark?

Shuangxu found it strange. She turned the flashlight back on and shifted the light toward him.

“Why is your nickname Xiao Jiu?” He Tingzhou suddenly asked.

Actually, only Shen Yu called her that. Lu Mannan had picked it up from him.

Shuangxu said, “I was born on September 9th. Shuangxu means September.”

He Tingzhou offered a unique perspective: “September 9th, huh. Shouldn’t you be called Chongyang then?”

Shuangxu was momentarily speechless before retorting, “Then why aren’t you called He Jianjun if you were born on August 1st?”

He Tingzhou laughed, and since they were so close, Shuangxu could even feel the slight vibration of his Adam’s apple.

He opened his lazily drooping eyelids and glanced at her. “How do you know my dad didn’t consider it?”

Shuangxu looked at him in bewilderment. She had just been speaking casually. He Jianjun and He Tingzhou had completely different vibes—an entire modern Chinese history apart.

“My dad was a soldier. I was born on August 1st, and he thought it was fate. He wanted me to join the military from a young age.” He Tingzhou paused for a few seconds. “My name was given to me by my mom.”

This was the first time Shuangxu had heard him mention his mother.

She turned to look at He Tingzhou, who was also looking at her.

The flashlight cast his profile onto the stone wall—high nose bridge, long lashes casting deep shadows.

Shuangxu’s heart inexplicably sped up. She turned away and said, “My name was also given to me by my mom.”

After that, they fell silent again.

He Tingzhou’s body was very warm. In the cold, damp cave, he was like a heat source, perfect for keeping warm.

Gradually, Shuangxu’s body warmed up, and the cold was no longer unbearable. Leaning against the wall, she fell asleep.

She woke up to an overly heavy weight on her shoulder. Opening her eyes, she found that He Tingzhou’s head had somehow slid onto her left shoulder.

Shuangxu immediately tensed up. As she reached out to push his head up, she felt an unusual heat.

She paused, pressing her palm to his forehead.

He had a fever.

---

chapters.title: Imprinting
chapters.content:
“Tingzhou ge?” She tried calling him.

No response.

“He Tingzhou?”

He must have passed out from the fever; she couldn’t wake him. Shuangxu hesitated for a moment before deciding not to push him away.

He Tingzhou was much taller than her, and this awkward leaning position was very uncomfortable for him.

For the sake of that bamboo green snake, she carefully straightened her back, trying to make him more comfortable.

She didn’t know how long He Tingzhou had been in the rain. His skin was scorching hot, and his breath was burning.

His hot, heavy breath fell on her neck, quickly turning her fair skin red.

A slight shiver spread from that spot, creeping through her limbs like vines. Now she didn’t feel cold at all—she was about to combust.

Her body was stiff as a poker, her fingertips tightly gripping her pants, her toes digging into the ground.

He Tingzhou’s weight was too much for Shuangxu’s small frame. Her left shoulder ached terribly, but he slept deeply, unaware.

This was the middle of nowhere, with rain pouring down. There were no doctors or medicine. It was a real problem. She didn’t know when the rain would stop, and letting his fever continue wasn’t an option.

He was the only child of Commander He. What if his brain got fried from the fever?

He was already bad enough—his combat skills were off the charts. If he became stupid on top of that, he’d truly be a menace.

Shuangxu’s gaze swept the surroundings and landed on the stream.

After a moment, she cupped He Tingzhou’s head and chin with her palm, carefully lifting his heavy head.

The sharp angles of his jaw pressed against her hand. Her fingers accidentally brushed his scorching lips, and she jerked away as if electrocuted.

She placed He Tingzhou against the cave wall and carefully slipped out from under his jacket. Turning her back to him, she unzipped her outer layer and quietly took off the inner vest.

When she finished putting her clothes back on and turned around, she found that He Tingzhou had opened his eyes at some point.

One of his legs was slightly bent, his wrist resting on his knee, leaning against the wall. His dark, deep eyes silently watched her.

“When did you wake up?” she asked.

“When you were taking off the second layer.” He Tingzhou’s voice was lazy, probably because of the fever. The slightly hoarse, warm, and gravelly tone brushed against Shuangxu’s ears, making her cheeks burn instantly.

She bit her lip.

This man—how could he not have the decency to look away? He just stared openly.

If it weren’t for the fact that he was sick, she’d really want to hit him.

Of course, she couldn’t win in a fight against him.

For a moment, she didn’t want to deal with him at all. She glared at him angrily, sulking for a few seconds before turning and walking to the stream. She soaked her vest and wrung it out.

With a tight expression, she knelt beside He Tingzhou and placed the damp vest on his forehead to cool him down.

Fortunately, the cave was dark, and the flashlight’s light was weak. Shuangxu could still keep her composure.

“You have a high fever,” she explained. “I don’t know when the rain will stop, so this will have to do for now.”

The cotton fabric, washed in the mountain stream, carried a coolness infused with faint traces of her light fragrance.

It was hard to describe exactly—like a gentle woody rose with the lightness of white tea, somewhere between pure and warm, making one want to bury their face and inhale deeply.

He Tingzhou’s Adam’s apple bobbed as he swallowed. In the dim yellow light of the flashlight, he tilted his head back and closed his eyes.

Unable to see his eyes, Shuangxu felt much more at ease.

After a while, once the vest was warmed by his body heat, she took it off and re-wet it.

Even though it was summer, the mountain stream was still very cold. Her hands ached from the chill after being in the water too long.

She repeated the process several times to cool him down, then sat beside him, exhausted and nodding off.

Suddenly, she noticed movement beside her. She looked over drowsily and saw that He Tingzhou’s face was unusually pale.

His forehead was covered in sweat, his brows tightly knit, and weak groans escaped his throat. His entire body, even in sleep, seemed to be in a state of high tension and unease.

Like a trapped beast struggling, the usually uninhibited man now showed a contradictory vulnerability.

Shuangxu immediately sobered up. At first, she thought it was the fever and reached out to check his temperature.

The moment her hand touched his skin, He Tingzhou reflexively grabbed her wrist with surprising force.

Shuangxu’s wrist almost snapped. She cried out in pain, and He Tingzhou opened his eyes.

His dark eyes were as sharp as blades, deep and thick as undissolved ink.

He was still breathing slightly heavily. Seeing Shuangxu’s face pale from pain, the grip on her wrist slowly loosened after a few seconds.

“Sorry.” His voice was hoarse and rough. His fingertips soothingly rubbed her wrist a couple of times.

Shuangxu pulled her hand back. The initial shock and near-tears from pain were replaced by surprise at his apology.

He Tingzhou actually apologized.

It was as rare as a dog meowing.

“I had a nightmare,” He Tingzhou explained.

Shuangxu rubbed her wrist. “A person like you still has nightmares?”

“I’m not a god. Of course I have nightmares.”

Shuangxu said, “You’re definitely not a god. You’re more like a rakshasa.”

He Tingzhou glanced at her, his body now relaxed, his arm resting on his knee as he leaned back. “Am I that scary?”

“Don’t you know how bad your reputation is? They say you almost killed someone.”

Whether the rumors were true or not, no one cared. Gossips just loved spreading sensational stories.

Shuangxu paused, then said, “In a way, we’re in the same boat.”

Both of them had a ruined reputation in others’ eyes.

He Tingzhou, however, lazily said, “My bad reputation is because they love meddling and stirring up trouble. Yours is well-deserved.”

Shuangxu: “…”

“What crime did I commit?” Shuangxu found herself surprisingly calm. Hearing him say that, she didn’t feel angry.

“My mom abandoned me, my dad didn’t want me, and others treated me like trash. Only my brother picked me up and brought me home, loving me like a treasure. Is it strange that I love him?”

“That’s not love. That’s imprinting.” He Tingzhou’s casual gaze fell on her, his voice mocking. “Little princess, you don’t even understand what love between a man and a woman is.”

Shuangxu felt a little unhappy, but she couldn’t quite say why. She just felt that He Tingzhou was denying her feelings for Shen Yu.

“You wouldn’t understand.” She said, “You have no male virtue.”

He Tingzhou scoffed lightly. “How am I lacking in male virtue? When you wanted to sleep with me, wasn’t I the one who kept my chastity and refused?”

“…”

Shuangxu didn’t want to engage with him. She turned her face away, refusing to speak further.

Her mind kept turning over the phrase “imprinting,” and before she knew it, she had fallen asleep.

She didn’t know how long she slept, but in her drowsy state, she seemed to hear commotion—someone was calling her name.

Yue Zifeng ran to the cave and looked inside, freezing in place.

The two people who had been missing all night were leaning against the wall, depending on each other for survival. Shuangxu was using He Tingzhou’s leg as a pillow. The young master, who had never been known for tenderness toward women, was surprisingly and patiently serving as a human cushion.

He Tingzhou was awake. Seeing him, he reacted with extreme calm. “They’re here.”

“My goodness, we finally found you.” Yue Zifeng’s voice was hoarse. He stuck his head out of the cave and shouted toward the outside, “They’re here! In here!”

Shuangxu was woken by the noise. She blinked awake, disoriented, and found that the cave was much brighter now.

It was morning, and the rain outside seemed to have stopped.

When she opened her eyes and saw He Tingzhou’s face above her, she was confused for a moment, not realizing what was happening.

He Tingzhou lowered his gaze, looking at her. “Comfortable?”

Realizing she was lying on his lap, she quickly sat up.

Strange—she had clearly fallen asleep sitting up last night.

A series of footsteps approached the cave. Shen Yu strode in, his tense and solemn expression easing only slightly when he saw her.

chapters.title: Whose Little Vest Is It?
chapters.content:
Yue Zifeng finally managed to relax after a night of mental strain. "Your brother was worried sick. We searched for you two all night. It was pouring rain last night, and in these remote mountains, we were terrified something might happen to you."

The twins had not expected the sudden downpour, and everyone was stranded at the camp. Shen Yu noticed Shuangxu was missing from the observation deck where she had stayed to set up the venue.

He went to pick her up with an umbrella but couldn’t find her.

Then, he realized He Tingzhou was also missing.

And that’s when things escalated.

No one slept that night. They searched through the mountains in the rain, from the camp to the observation deck—a distance that shouldn’t have been too far—yet they searched all night, nearly turning the entire mountain upside down.

"I passed this cave at least three times. Damn it, I should’ve come in to check!" Yue Zifeng pounded his chest in frustration.

Shuangxu asked curiously, "I left my hat outside. Didn’t you see it?"

"No, maybe the wind blew it away," Yue Zifeng said. "Weren’t you at the observation deck? Why didn’t you run back when it started raining? Why hide here?"

Shuangxu opened her mouth to answer, but the twins behind the crowd spoke first: "Ah, it’s our fault. While I was setting up the fairy lights, I accidentally knocked over Shuangxu’s bag. It fell down. I said it was too dark, and the bag wasn’t important, so we could wait until morning to look for it. But she insisted on going down to find it."

"Right. We were going to go with her, but she walked too fast and we got separated. We thought it wasn’t far, so we went back to meet up with you first."

"In hindsight, we should’ve gone with her no matter what."

The twins were quick to seize the initiative, portraying themselves as sincere and painting Shuangxu as stubborn and unyielding. Now, even if she claimed they had deliberately kicked her bag down, it would seem like she was making unreasonable accusations.

Shuangxu silently watched their coordinated performance.

Before she could speak, Yue Zifeng couldn’t hold back and cursed, "You dropped her bag? She had the ring in it! And you wanted to wait until morning? By then, the wedding proposal would’ve been ruined. Were you planning to put the ring on Lu Mannan’s finger yourselves?"

The twins’ expressions changed instantly. Lu Mannan, hearing this, also glanced at them.

The two panicked: "We didn’t know…"

Yue Zifeng was already displeased that they had left their sister alone outside last night, and now, knowing they had almost lost the ring, he was even more annoyed.

"Useless! You can’t do anything right!"

After all, they were friends Lu Mannan had brought. Scolding them was also slapping Lu Mannan in the face. Zuo Zhong quickly stepped in to mediate: "They didn’t do it on purpose. Besides, the rain last night was terrible. The proposal couldn’t have happened anyway. You should’ve checked the weather forecast more carefully."

Yue Zifeng was left speechless.

Shen Yu crouched in front of Shuangxu. After a night of running around in the rain, he looked visibly exhausted.

"Are you hurt?"

Lu Mannan, who had also searched all night, looked worried: "Are you okay? You scared me to death."

Shuangxu shook her head. "I’m fine, but Tingzhou is running a fever."

Yue Zifeng reached out to touch Tingzhou’s forehead, but Tingzhou swatted his hand away. "Did you wash your hands?"

"Holy shit, you’re burning up! Quick, back to base. Call a doctor!"

Shen Yu helped Shuangxu to her feet. "Let’s go."

The romantic proposal plan was a complete failure, and now a precious young master was sick.

Zuo Zhong and the other young men went back to the camp to pack up, while the rest took Shuangxu and He Tingzhou back to the mid-mountain base first.

The mood on the way down was far from the joy and relaxation of the ascent. Everyone was exhausted from the sleepless night and rested as soon as they returned.

Shuangxu went to take a shower first. As she changed out of her dirty clothes, she remembered her vest.

She had been in such a rush after waking up that she forgot about it. It was probably left in the cave.

The doctor they had called had arrived and was giving He Tingzhou an IV. He was resting in bed, while outside, everyone was busy—some boiling water, some cooking, all eager to serve.

Someone brought a bowl of handmade noodles, but He Tingzhou had no appetite and left it on the table without a glance.

Yue Zifeng came in, saw he wasn’t eating, sat down, and started slurping the noodles. "I’ve been searching for you all night. I’m starving."

"When I came back yesterday, weren’t you loitering outside the camp? When did you go to the observation deck?"

He Tingzhou, weaker than usual due to his illness, was too lazy to even open his eyes. "It rained. I got lost."

"You got lost, but you still walked in the opposite direction? What kind of sense of direction is that?"

As he spoke, he looked up and noticed a white vest hanging on the clothes rack.

"Cough!" Yue Zifeng almost choked on his noodles. Pointing at the vest, he asked, "Whose little vest is this?"

He Tingzhou lifted his eyelids and glanced at it, answering as if it were the most natural thing in the world: "Mine."

"Bullshit! How could you fit into something this small?"

"It shrank."

"Do you think I’m stupid? This style is clearly a woman’s. Where did you get it? In just these two days, and you disappeared for a night—when did you hook up with one of the women on our team? Who is it?"

He Tingzhou, annoyed by his nagging, ignored him. "If you’re so bored, go up the mountain and play with bamboo leaf green snakes."

Yue Zifeng finished his noodles and was about to leave with the bowl when He Tingzhou spoke again.

Lying in bed, his lazy gaze swept over the DV on the table. Casually, he said, "It got rained on yesterday. Check if it’s broken."

When Shuangxu came out after her shower, Zuo Zhong and the others had already returned to the base.

Shen Yu was sitting in a chair with his legs crossed, gently calling her over: "Come eat something."

The portable stove on the table was cooking a Korean-style hot pot, small flames bubbling. Lu Mannan carried over some washed fruit. "Xiao Jiu, come quick. I made this especially for you."

Shuangxu thanked her. Lu Mannan sat next to her, resting her chin in her hand and smiling at Shen Yu. "Am I not a good fiancée?"

At that moment, Yue Zifeng came out of the opposite room with a strange expression, tilting his head to signal Shen Yu, who stood up and walked over.

The two stood together as Yue Zifeng showed him something on the DV.

Lu Mannan muttered, "What are those two up to?"

Shuangxu, eating a shrimp slide, looked up. Shen Yu turned his head at that moment.

His gaze was as calm as water, like the stream in the cave, carrying a bone-chilling coldness.

That glance wasn’t directed at her—it was at Lu Mannan.

"What the hell is this?" Yue Zifeng cursed. "Should I call them over now?"

"Not yet." Shen Yu’s expression was unreadable. Calmly, he said, "Let Xiao Jiu finish eating."

---

chapters.title: Mannan Had Long Disliked Her
chapters.content:
By the time Shuangxu finished eating, Yue Zifeng had someone call the twins over.

Almost everyone had gathered, and though they didn’t know what was happening, they could tell from Yue Zifeng’s expression that something was wrong.

He usually had a smile on his face, so his sudden seriousness was a clear sign of trouble.

The twins, still uneasy from the previous night’s events, tried to act nonchalant when called over: "Uh, we have plans tonight. If you guys want to keep playing, we’ll head out first."

"What’s the rush?" Yue Zifeng said. "Our business isn’t finished. Where do you two think you’re going?"

"What business?"

"What business? Don’t you two have a clue?" Yue Zifeng’s tone wasn’t friendly. "I’ll ask you—how did the sister’s bag fall?"

The twins’ expressions visibly tensed. They instinctively glanced at Shen Yu first.

He held a cigarette between his fingers, the red ember flickering, his cold gaze unsettling.

Shuangxu sat beside him, calm and composed, giving nothing away.

"It was an accident," the twins insisted. "Miss Song, we know you’re upset about being lost in the cave all night, but we already apologized yesterday. Why are you still holding a grudge?"

"We really didn’t mean it. We just wanted to give Mannan a special ceremony. We were too excited and didn’t pay attention."

Shuangxu said, "Whether you did it on purpose or not, we all know the truth."

"You just don’t like us, do you? Last time, you slapped me for no reason, and I didn’t even hold it against you. You can’t just falsely accuse us out of nowhere."

Shen Yu looked at Shuangxu. "Last time?"

Explaining the slap would mean revealing the reason—and at that time, the twins had been spewing filth about Shen Yu.

Everyone present was a friend of Shen Yu and Lu Mannan. Shuangxu didn’t want to say it, and she couldn’t.

She furrowed her brows and remained silent.

The twins, seeing her hesitation, gained confidence. "That’s right. You have your brother to back you up. Your family has power and influence. Does that mean we deserve to be bullied by you?"

The younger twin tugged at her sister’s sleeve, forcing a meek tone. "Forget it."

Look—now the blame was on her again.

First, she had slapped them for no reason, and now she was falsely accusing them. Her image as a tyrannical bully was complete.

If Shen Yu backed her up now, it would confirm the accusation of abusing power.

These twins were experts at this kind of manipulation, their skills honed in real-life drama.

Bai Qingmei, who had been half-asleep, perked up. From somewhere, she produced a handful of sunflower seeds, cracking them open as she watched, even sharing some with Zhou Shengan beside her. Zhou Shengan peeled the shells and handed the kernels back to her.

Seeing Shuangxu temporarily suppressed, Bai Qingmei’s inner director took over. "Shuangxu, it’s your turn to turn the tide. Go!"

Shuangxu: "..."

Go where?

As she lifted her gaze, she saw He Tingzhou coming down the hallway from the opposite direction.

He wore a black hoodie, his broad shoulders accentuated. Still a little weak from his illness, he pushed his mobile IV stand, the half-empty bag of fluid hanging from it, the tube connected to the back of his hand.

Someone immediately stood up to help. "Lord Zhou, why are you out?"

"Watching the show." He Tingzhou sat down leisurely, leaning back. "How far along are we?"

...

Even a fever couldn’t stop him from watching the drama.

Shuangxu didn’t want to waste her breath. She looked at Yue Zifeng. "Brother Zifeng, can you stop beating around the bush?"

She didn’t know what had happened, but Yue Zifeng must have had a reason for calling them over.

"Hah, you wouldn’t believe it." Yue Zifeng gave a cold laugh, inserting the DV’s memory card into a computer. After a few operations, he turned the screen toward the twins. "Take a look for yourselves."

He Tingzhou: "Huh? Isn’t this the video I took?"

Yue Zifeng said, "I was checking the DV earlier and accidentally opened it. Found something incredible."

He Tingzhou’s filming skills were… questionable. The video was shot very casually, with no real framing or technique.

The mountain was dark at night, and the footage showed distant, blurred mountains stretching into the horizon under the night sky.

The background was quiet, with only the rustling of footsteps on grass and branches. Soon, voices appeared—two women speaking.

"That forest is like a maze. Even after coming here so many times, I still get lost sometimes. She won’t be back anytime soon..."

"The meteor shower will start soon, and Shen Yu is going to propose. Who has time to worry about her? We’ll notice she’s missing after the proposal. Let her stay there..."

"If she can’t find her way back, it’s her own fault for having a bad sense of direction..."

The twins’ identical faces twisted in shock. They saw the unchecked panic in each other’s eyes.

They never expected their private conversation to have been recorded by He Tingzhou!

Shuangxu was surprised too.

He Tingzhou raised an eyebrow slightly. "Oh."

The group of older brothers, who had watched Shuangxu grow up, couldn’t sit still after hearing this.

"Are you out of your minds? How could you do something like this? Messing with Shuangxu right under Shen Yu’s nose—do you have a death wish?"

"I’m impressed. You talk so convincingly. I actually thought you two were innocent!"

"With mouths like that, you could’ve been great lawyers. You could turn innocence into a death sentence."

"You two are insane!" Lu Mannan looked disbelief. "If something had happened to Xiao Jiu, could you have taken responsibility?"

As she finished, she noticed Yue Zifeng’s strange expression as he pointed at the video, which wasn’t over yet.

The two women continued chatting, their voices clearer now.

"Mannan has long disliked her. She’s just too polite to say it. This is the perfect chance to get back at her."

"Serves her right for always clinging to Shen Yu. She’s such a nuisance."

The room fell silent. The people who had been furious moments ago were now speechless.

After all, they were friends Lu Mannan had brought. Turns out, it was all her idea.

The fiancée disliked her little sister-in-law-to-be so much that she deliberately left her in the mountains at night...

The looks on their faces said it all. Lu Mannan froze for a few seconds, instinctively defending herself. "Don’t look at me like that. I didn’t tell them to do it."

No one spoke.

One was a sister they had raised, the other was a soon-to-be fiancée. They couldn’t take sides—only Shen Yu could decide.

Moreover, her cousin He Tingzhou was sitting right there. Who dared say a word against her?

Yue Zifeng was also at a loss. His impression of Lu Mannan had always been that of a bright and lovely girl—she didn’t have, or at least didn’t seem to have, such a malicious heart.

Lu Mannan looked at Shen Yu. "Do you believe me?"

He slowly took a drag of his cigarette, saying nothing.

The twins, realizing they were doomed, feared Shen Yu’s retribution and tried to cling to Lu Mannan as their lifeline. "Mannan, you can’t abandon us! We were helping you get revenge!"

Lu Mannan was left speechless.

The heavy silence was suffocating.

He Tingzhou showed no reaction. He didn’t speak up for his cousin, nor did he show any intention of upholding justice as an elder brother.

He lazily propped up his chin, looking completely indifferent.

But his mere presence was the strongest support for Lu Mannan.

Shuangxu understood this. She thought he had come out deliberately to back Lu Mannan.

Regardless of whether Lu Mannan was truly behind it, they had to consider the Lu family’s face, the He family’s face.

In the stifling silence, Shuangxu spoke up: "This has nothing to do with Miss Lu."

"She knew the ring was with me. If I had gotten lost and couldn’t return, who would deliver the ring to her? She was looking forward to the proposal. She wouldn’t do something so stupid."

Yue Zifeng glanced at her and nodded in agreement. "Right. I told Mannan that."

The atmosphere finally eased.

"I knew Mannan wasn’t that kind of person."

Shen Yu said nothing, stubbing out his cigarette. "Let’s go."

The group packed their things, loaded the luggage into the cars, and prepared to head back to the city.

Lu Mannan walked up to Shen Yu. "I really didn’t know about last night. I didn’t know they..."

Shen Yu never once expressed his stance on the matter. He neither said he didn’t believe her nor that he did. His calm tone made him seem particularly indifferent.

"Control your friends. There won’t be a next time."

Lu Mannan could tell from his attitude that he didn’t care whether she knew or not. What mattered to him was that someone had bullied his sister right under his nose.

She couldn’t help but feel wronged.

She didn’t get into Shen Yu’s car, instead turning away in a huff and getting into the one behind.

When Shuangxu came out, Shen Yu was talking to Yue Zifeng. Seeing her, he said, "Go back with Tingzhou."

Shuangxu wanted to ask why, but Shen Yu ruffled her hair—a gesture of comfort, but also a signal not to ask further.

chapters.title: Temporary Nanny
chapters.content:
The twins were put into an SUV, exchanging glances secretly. Shen Yu didn’t say anything, and the matter was settled so easily?

The convoy drove down the mountain. The car in front continued toward the city, while the SUV turned right at the fork in the road, leaving the convoy behind.

The twins realized something was wrong and panicked: "What are you trying to do? Where are you taking us?"

The car passed through a winding mountain road, going deeper into the mountains. Gradually, the road became narrower and rougher, eventually turning into a bumpy dirt path.

This mountain was even more primitive than Dongyu Mountain, untouched by development. The dense forest blocked out the sunlight, and there were no camping sites—hardly even any flat ground. Apart from a few extreme backpackers seeking a challenge, few people ever came here.

The SUV stopped in a completely unfamiliar forest. Yue Zifeng tossed the twins and their luggage out of the car, clapping his hands.

"You’ve never been to this mountain before, right? Neither have I. Time to test your sense of direction."

The twins instantly understood his intention: "You can’t just leave us here!"

"This place is unfamiliar to all of us. Who knows if there are snakes or wolves or other wild animals? It’s dangerous in the deep mountains and old forests. How can two girls spend the night here?"

Shen Yu, still in his hiking gear, remained refined and elegant, but his voice was ice-cold: "Xiao Jiu can spend the night in the mountains. Why can’t you?"

The two were on the verge of tears, pleading: "It was all because of Manman’s instructions! We really don’t dare do it again. Please, we swear we’ll be respectful to Miss Song from now on and never talk nonsense again!"

Shen Yu remained unmoved: "Last time, why did she hit you? What did you say in front of her?"

Their eyes flickered, too guilty to answer.

Shen Yu said: "Do I need to pry your mouths open?"

Seeing Yue Zifeng actually pick up a stick, the two girls, terrified, quickly blurted out: "We just… said a few idle words…"

Then, trembling, they repeated what they had said before, softening the worst parts.

The wind rustled through the treetops, sending a chill down their spines. Shen Yu’s face, shadowed by the dense forest, was as cold as Shuangxu.

Yue Zifeng was furious: "They’re not blood siblings, but it’s no different! Don’t look at them with your filthy, perverted eyes to insult them! Damn it, I should’ve torn your mouths off!"

"The road into the mountains will be blocked for three days. No one will come here. After three days, you can try to see if you can make it back to Yancheng."

Shen Yu had no more time to waste on them and turned to get back in the car.

This place was nearly 70 kilometers from the city. The mountain roads were rugged, and there was no one to call for help. The two girls cried as they pounded on the car door: "We have no food or water! If you leave us here, we’ll really die!"

"Three days won’t kill you!" Yue Zifeng snapped. "There’s plenty of water in these mountains. Drink if you’re thirsty. If you’re hungry, go look in the bamboo forest. Maybe you’ll find bamboo vipers. String them up and roast them. After all, you two are more venomous than they are. Eating them might just cure you with poison."

With that, he rolled up the window and drove off.

The car bumped its way down the mountain. Yue Zifeng cursed under his breath: "It’s all because of that idiot Song Leyan spreading rumors! Who knows how the Song family raised their child, turning her into such a moron. If she were my sister, I’d slap her to death!"

Shen Yu remained silent the whole time. Yue Zifeng noticed him rubbing his temples and finally shut up.

He Tingzhou, who was sick, leaned back in the rear seat with his eyes closed to rest. Zuo Zhong was driving.

Shuangxu lowered her head, playing on her phone. After a while, she heard He Tingzhou’s hoarse voice beside her: "Do you have any water?"

"Yeah, yeah, yeah." Zuo Zhong, driving with one hand, reached back to hand him a bottle of purified water.

He Tingzhou didn’t take it: "I want it hot."

"Forgot you had a fever." Zuo Zhong wasn’t at the age where he carried a thermos everywhere, and He Tingzhou wasn’t usually the type to drink hot water either. They hadn’t prepared one when they got in the car.

"Then endure it a little longer. We’ll be there in less than an hour."

He Tingzhou didn’t respond. Shuangxu felt a gaze on her and turned to meet his eyes for a few seconds.

Silently, she handed him the thermos from her bag. Shen Yu had filled it for her.

The young master still refused, justified: "It’s too hot."

So difficult to please. Shuangxu had no choice but to pour the hot water into the lid, blew on it a few times, and when it felt about right, handed it to him.

Only then did He Tingzhou lift his delicate hand, take it, and sip lightly. It was probably still a bit hot, as he frowned, but he didn’t complain further and drank slowly.

After finishing the cup, he handed the lid back to Shuangxu: "I’m hungry."

Zuo Zhong said: "I have energy bars here. Want one?"

He Tingzhou: "Too dry."

"Bread?"

"Not fresh."

"Banana, apple, orange?"

"Don’t want any."

Zuo Zhong sighed: "Then what do you want to eat, my lord?"

That gaze fell on Shuangxu again. Staring.

She was helpless: "I don’t have any food."

He Tingzhou, condescending: "Then peel me an orange."

...

Shuangxu had no choice but to take the orange and peel it for him.

She had always been the one taken care of by Shen Yu, but now she had become his temporary nanny, forced to wait on him patiently for half an hour.

When they reached the toll booth, Lu Mannan came over from another car, knocked on the window, and got into the front passenger seat.

"Where did Shen Yu take them?"

"Relax." Zuo Zhong said in his usual easygoing tone, "No killing, no dumping bodies. It’s a society ruled by law."

It was obvious Shen Yu would teach them a lesson. Lu Mannan fell silent for a moment: "Should I have been in that car too?"

Zuo Zhong saw she was in a bad mood and comforted her: "What are you thinking? It has nothing to do with you. There are so many of us here. How could we let those two frame you?"

"You didn’t tell me that Zifeng was going to give you the ring." Lu Mannan said to Shuangxu, "I didn’t know the ring was with you."

Zuo Zhong, who was driving, looked at her in surprise: "Then earlier, when you and Zifeng were talking..."

He stopped mid-sentence, realizing they were helping her cover up.

Shuangxu kept a straight face: "I’m giving you a way out. Why say so much?"

"Why do you believe me?" Lu Mannan asked like a stubborn little girl, "Even your brother doesn’t believe me."

"I didn’t say I believe you. I’m just giving your cousin face."

Shuangxu finished, and He Tingzhou lifted an eyelid, glancing at her.

She didn’t notice and continued: "Otherwise, you’d have no way out, my brother would be caught in the middle, and Brother Tingzhou would be in a difficult position too. Making such an ugly scene is bad for everyone."

"Why would I be in a difficult position?" He Tingzhou asked.

"You’re her cousin. If things escalate, you’d have to protect her."

"I don’t need to protect her." He Tingzhou’s voice was cold and ruthless, with no trace of sibling affection. "I’m weak and fragile, incapable of even tying up a chicken. How could I protect such a big blind woman?"

...

You can’t tie up a chicken, but you can tie up a venomous snake.

Lu Mannan puffed out her cheeks in a silent sulk, knowing he was right.

"Fine, it’s my fault for making friends with the wrong people. I should take responsibility." She turned to Shuangxu, "But I really didn’t tell them to bully you. Do you believe me?"

Shuangxu studied her for a moment. Lu Mannan’s eyes were sincere and open.

From the few times she had interacted with Lu Mannan, she could tell what kind of person she was. Well-protected by her family, she was naive and carefree, worldly-wise but not cunning.

She did harbor some jealousy toward Shuangxu, but she had always been direct about it.

Shuangxu said: "I never doubted you."

Lu Mannan immediately pouted, looking like she was about to cry.

"Don’t cry." Shuangxu added, "It’s not that I trust your character. I just think you’re not that stupid."

What good would it do her to stay out all night? Shen Yu would definitely worry, or notice she was missing that very night. Even if it didn’t rain, he would disrupt the proposal ceremony to look for her.

For Lu Mannan, the gains wouldn’t outweigh the losses.

Compared to such underhanded tricks, Lu Mannan would probably prefer to witness their happiness with her own eyes.

"Same thing. Anyway, you believe me." Lu Mannan knew what mattered.

When the car reached Songming Road, Shuangxu got out. Lu Mannan followed, hugging her.

Her much-anticipated proposal had fallen through, and she had almost been wronged. Although Shen Yu hadn’t blamed her, his attitude had hurt her deeply.

At a time when she was being suspected, the person she loved most hadn’t stood by her side to support her. The only one who believed her was Shuangxu.

She sniffled, her voice choking: "Xiao Jiu, thank you."

---

chapters.title: Brother, I Wish You Happiness
chapters.content:
A few days after returning from Dongyu Mountain, Shuangxu went back to the Shen family for dinner in the evening. Fu Yun was trying to persuade Shen Yu.

"You don’t know what Mannan is like? She would never do such a thing. You’ve wronged her. She must feel aggrieved. Even Shuangxu believes her. Why don’t you?"

"If her friends offend Xiao Jiu, she shares the responsibility. If that counts as wronging her, then fine, I wronged her."

Shen Yu was replying to emails on his phone, not even looking up. "When Xiao Jiu was little and I took her out, if she knocked over someone’s vase, I’d still have to apologize and compensate."

As long as it wasn’t a major principle issue, Shen Changyuan never contradicted Fu Yun. But this time, he said: "On this matter, I agree with A Yu. The kind of friends you keep reflects your character. Look at A Yu and Shuangxu—they never associate with shady people."

Fu Yun said: "Mannan has lived in Lincheng since she was a child. She doesn’t have many friends in Yancheng, which is why she got close to them. Her friends may not be great, but she has a good heart."

Shen Changyuan: "Then this is a good opportunity for her to see their true colors. She should consider whether to continue associating with them. She often spends time with Leyan and her crowd—none of them are easy to deal with."

Fu Yun sighed. "Mannan is still a girl. Can’t you just apologize and coax her a little?"

Shen Yu noticed Shuangxu at the doorway first and put down his phone: "You’re back."

Shuangxu walked in, holding a box of cakes: "Auntie, I made some osmanthus cakes for you."

She had specially bought the ingredients, spending an entire afternoon busy at work. She mixed glutinous rice flour and rice flour with water, sifted it, and layered it into the mold, covering it with fine gauze before steaming for half an hour.

The steamed rice cakes were soft, sweet, and fragrant. She cut them into small squares and sprinkled dried osmanthus flowers on top, making them look very pretty.

"I didn’t add sugar. I prepared a jar of osmanthus honey. Try some."

Fu Yun’s smile was forced: "I can’t eat. Your brother hurt Mannan’s feelings because of you. They’ve been in a cold war for days."

Shuangxu put down the osmanthus cake she had picked up.

"Are you blaming me, Auntie?"

"It’s not that. Your aunt just worries too much. Young people are bound to have disagreements." Shen Changyuan reached out to take it. "Let me try."

He took a bite of the osmanthus cake and praised it generously: "It’s really good. Shuangxu’s cooking is better than any bakery’s."

The topic shifted. Shuangxu went to the pond to see if Gui Gui had returned, but there was no sign of him.

When she came back, the three of them were no longer in the living room.

Dinner was already prepared. She went upstairs to call Fu Yun and Shen Changyuan to eat.

As she walked to the master bedroom door, she raised her hand to knock but heard voices inside.

Fu Yun’s voice was heavy: "Before A Yu marries Mannan, it’s best not to let Shuangxu meet him. I’m not blaming her, but this whole thing started because of her. If she hadn’t gone, Mannan wouldn’t have had a falling out with A Yu. A Yu is too protective of her, which makes Mannan feel wronged. Who could bear that?"

Shen Changyuan disapproved: "Is it necessary to guard against the child like that? Shuangxu was raised by A Yu. If someone bullies her, who should protect her if not him? If he gets married and ignores his own sister, then he wouldn’t be A Yu."

Fu Yun’s voice rose: "If he keeps protecting her like this, his marriage to Mannan might be ruined by Shuangxu!"

"Shuangxu hasn’t done anything. How can you assume the worst of her? This time, it was clearly Mannan’s fault first. You’re making too much of this!"

"Making too much of it?" Fu Yun’s emotions were agitated. "Am I wrong to say she has feelings for A Yu?"

Shen Changyuan: "That was all Leyan’s rumor. Don’t listen to their nonsense."

"I’ve seen her diary!"

With Fu Yun’s words, Shuangxu felt as if someone had punched her heart hard.

There was no sound, but it hurt so much it numbed her.

Shen Changyuan fell silent in shock.

Fu Yun continued, her voice lowering into sobs: "Hasn’t she caused A Yu enough trouble? He raised her, and yet she harbors such thoughts, making people point at his back and call him a pedophile, a pervert."

Fu Yun’s voice dropped further as she wept: "Don’t I care about her? She’s a child I watched grow up. Do you think I want to force her away, send her to such a distant place? Who am I doing this for?!"

Shuangxu didn’t know how she made it downstairs. She only snapped out of it when she heard Wang Shi’s voice.

Wang Shi smiled as soon as she saw her, proudly showing her the medicinal soup simmering in the pot.

"Madam called you a few days ago. When she heard you had menstrual cramps, she specially learned how to make this Si Wu Tang. It’s made with dang gui, chuan xiong, white peony, and prepared rehmannia. It’s great for nourishing and replenishing blood. Madam also told me to give some to your cousin when it’s done. She needs blood tonic the most with her condition."

Perhaps it was the steam from the medicinal soup warming her, but Shuangxu’s eyes felt hot.

"Thank her for me." she said.

"Why not tell her yourself? Why have me relay the message?" Wang Shi smiled.

"I have some urgent work at the company. I need to go work overtime."

Wang Shi looked surprised: "Dinner is about to be served. You’re leaving now?"

"I’m not hungry. Please tell Auntie for me."

Shuangxu left under her puzzled gaze.

As she stepped out, she saw Shen Yu sitting on a chair in the outdoor pavilion.

The sky had already darkened. A wisp of smoke curled from his fingers, and his silhouette in the cool summer night breeze looked a little lonely.

Shuangxu stood at a distance for a moment before walking toward him.

"Brother."

Shen Yu’s thoughts returned, stubbing out his cigarette. He turned his head, his voice as gentle as ever: "What’s wrong?"

The night breeze was cool, gently brushing against Shuangxu’s long hair like a tender hand.

She said: "It really wasn’t Miss Lu’s fault. She was really looking forward to your proposal that night. The rain ruined the surprise she wanted, and then she spent the whole night searching for me with you. She must have felt terrible too."

Shen Yu asked: "Did Mom send you to persuade me?"

Shuangxu shook her head.

"Miss Lu is a good person. Cheerful, enthusiastic, and straightforward." Shuangxu had envied her, been jealous of her, but never disliked her.

"She really likes you."

The orange-yellow light from the courtyard lamp fell into Shen Yu’s eyes. He was silent for a while before asking her: "Why are you telling me this?"

Shuangxu smiled slightly: "Brother, I wish you both happiness."

chapters.title: Be Good. I’ll Reward You When We Get Back
chapters.content:
Shuangxu didn’t let the driver take her. After leaving the Shen family home, she walked along the clean, straight asphalt road for a while.

Passing the Song family’s house, she saw the grand villa from a distance.

The brightly lit house stood tall in the night. She had lived there for a while as a child, but it hadn’t left her with any good memories.

As she passed by the garden, she paused briefly, looking through the fence at the corner where she used to squat.

Now, it was empty—only carefully tended flowers and plants remained.

She had never seen the house from this angle before. Had Shen Yu seen her from here back then?

A child squatting silently in the same spot every day must have seemed strange.

The house was lively inside. She had heard that Grandpa had been discharged from the hospital, but she hadn’t gone to visit.

A servant hurried past the garden, noticing her standing by the fence. The servant looked surprised. "Miss Shuangxu? Why are you standing there?"

"I was just passing by." Shuangxu replied before turning to leave.

The servant said, "Aren’t you coming in? Director Si is back today, and the old master is home too."

Shuangxu didn’t stop walking. "Then I won’t disturb their reunion."

She went to the hospital to see Shu Yang. Just as she reached the door of the ward, she heard Shu Yang’s solemn voice inside: "We must never let Shuangxu find out about this, understand?"

Xiao Liao answered solemnly, "Don’t worry, I won’t breathe a word of it."

Shuangxu pushed the door open with a sudden force.

Inside, the two of them sat cross-legged on the hospital bed, facing each other. A large pot of bright red crayfish sat on the small mobile dining table between them, their hands covered in disposable gloves.

The door swung open, and the two of them, mouths greasy from sucking on crayfish, turned their heads simultaneously, frozen in place.

The quiet, serene air of the ward was filled with the tantalizing spicy aroma of the crayfish.

"..."

Shuangxu spoke, her face expressionless: "My timing isn’t great, is it?"

Shu Yang immediately pointed at Xiao Liao with a crayfish head in hand. "It’s all her fault for tempting me. I just made the same mistake anyone in the world would. What was her intention in bringing crayfish to the hospital?"

Xiao Liao almost jumped up. "You were the one who said you were depressed from eating hospital food and asked me to bring something exciting!"

"You think I was serious when I said that? You should have stopped me from going astray."

"Who was it that threatened to fire me?"

The two accomplices, who had been in cahoots, instantly turned on each other to shift blame.

Shuangxu closed the door and walked past them as they bickered. The two instinctively covered the pot of crayfish at the same time.

"It’s already bought. Throwing it away would be a waste of food."

"If she doesn’t eat it, I can. I can finish three pots by myself."

Shuangxu pulled over a chair and sat down. "Any extra gloves?"

Xiao Liao immediately handed her a pair. Shu Yang asked cautiously, suspiciously, and carefully, "You’re really letting me eat?"

"It’s not my body that’s injured." Shuangxu elegantly put on the gloves. "Chen Peiran’s trial hasn’t started yet, but it’s fine. If you can’t hold out until then, I can burn the verdict for you."

"..." Shu Yang reluctantly took off her gloves. "I’m not eating! I have to outlive him."

The crayfish became Shuangxu’s meal. Shu Yang then took out two bottles of beer she had stashed in the cabinet and opened them for the two of them.

Shuangxu glanced over. Shu Yang said with deep sorrow, "Only these two bottles! You two are getting off easy."

Shuangxu had left without eating dinner, and now she was truly hungry. Xiao Liao had ordered the spicy flavor, which Shuangxu couldn’t handle well, but she still buried her head in eating, her taste buds stimulated by the painful yet exhilarating spice.

Shu Yang leaned against the headboard, gnawing on a cucumber. After a while, she suddenly asked, "Feeling down?"

Xiao Liao lifted her greasy face. "I’m feeling great!"

"Eat your food, idiot." Shu Yang looked at Shuangxu, but Shuangxu didn’t even lift her head.

After a while, Shuangxu answered a different question: "I’ve researched several liquid hydrogen system suppliers. There’s a company in Longcheng called Huifeng Technology that specializes in small and medium-sized liquid hydrogen tanks and refueling systems. Their representative is very interested in cooperating and has invited me to attend next week’s Hydrogen Energy Development Summit in Longcheng."

"Go for it, little workaholic." Shu Yang said. "How did I have such good vision to dig you up?"

Shuangxu smiled slightly, peeling a crayfish shell. "Cherish me, or you’ll regret it when you lose me."

Shuangxu’s flight to Longcheng was on Wednesday afternoon.

She brought along the company’s top technical expert, while Xiao Liao was left in Yancheng as Shu Yang’s personal food inspector.

The weather in Longcheng was perfect—clear skies. When the plane landed at the airport, as she disembarked, she saw a private jet landing at the same time through the glass of the jet bridge.

The cabin door opened, and a tall, sharp figure descended the stairs, dressed in black from head to toe, with strikingly long legs. A pair of sunglasses hung on his face, and his steps down the stairs were lazily slow.

She was too far away to see clearly, but she felt that the man’s demeanor somewhat resembled He Tingzhou.

Shuangxu first took the expert to the hotel to settle in. The company’s travel budget wasn’t high, so she paid out of her own pocket for two executive suites.

While checking in at the front desk, the expert, carrying his own backpack, said embarrassedly, "President Song, I can’t let you spend extra money on me."

"What’s there to be embarrassed about? You’re Feixue’s treasure. Your value is far more than just one executive suite."

The expert’s face turned slightly red. Shuangxu smiled. "Let’s go."

As they entered the elevator, a hotel bellhop in uniform pushed a luggage cart inside, on which sat a black case.

The bellhop smiled and greeted her. Shuangxu nodded politely before looking away.

Their rooms were on the 7th floor. After they got off, the bellhop continued up to the top floor to deliver the luggage to the penthouse suite.

The meeting with Huifeng was scheduled for the next two days. Shuangxu put her luggage in the room, changed clothes, and decided to go out and explore in the evening.

Out of courtesy, she invited the expert, but he was too socially anxious and preferred to stay alone in the hotel. Shuangxu didn’t force him and left by herself.

As soon as she got in the car, the driver asked, "Beautiful, here for tourism?"

Shuangxu was curious. "How can you tell? Don’t I look like a local?"

"Our eyes are trained for this. The moment you stepped out, I could tell you were a tourist. Locals look at their own city like they’re looking at an old wife at home—they’ve seen it all, no freshness left."

The analogy was crude but oddly fitting.

Even so, when Shuangxu asked about fun places, the driver chatted enthusiastically, introducing many famous local attractions and specialties along the way.

Compared to Yancheng’s heavy historical atmosphere, Longcheng was younger, more fashionable, and more relaxed.

She ate at a local specialty restaurant, wandered the streets aimlessly, and returned to the hotel around 9 PM.

Xiao Liao sent her a video, pointing at Shu Yang on the hospital bed. "Little boss, I’m reporting in my real name—she’s trying to secretly order takeout again."

Shu Yang also pointed back at her. "You just wait."

"You can threaten me all you want. The little boss said that right now, she’s the one in charge at the company. You can’t fire me. I’m an imperial envoy on a mission!"

As Shuangxu entered the elevator, she was looking down at her phone. She smiled and sent Xiao Liao a voice message: "Be good. I’ll reward you when we get back."

She had been abroad for a few years, and her personality had become more reserved and calm. But a few years earlier, when she had been carefree and followed Shen Yu, she had been very cheerful.

Her short, almond-shaped eyes were sweet when she smiled, and her voice was soft, as if every word she spoke carried a little wave.

Only after sending the message did she notice someone else in the elevator. She lifted her gaze from the black trousers, meeting He Tingzhou’s downward glance.

He Tingzhou had his hands in his pockets, his dark eyes sweeping over the phone in her hand. From the inverted screen, he could vaguely make out the chat profile picture—it was a photo of a man’s abs.

The contact was saved as "Xiao Liao."

---

chapters.title: Ever-Changing Tastes
chapters.content:
Shuangxu was a little surprised. She recalled the figure she had seen from afar at the airport. She hadn’t expected it to really be him.

"Brother Tingzhou, what a coincidence."

"Not a coincidence." He Tingzhou kept his hands in his pockets, his gaze subtly shifting away from her phone. "I’m also attending the summit you’re here for."

Using an abs photo as a profile picture—what kind of decent person does that?

Superficial. Vulgar. Ill-intentioned.

"Oh." Shuangxu turned to stand slightly in front of him to his left.

The elevator ascended. Seeing that he had no intention of speaking, she didn’t initiate conversation either, standing quietly beside him.

After a few seconds of silence, He Tingzhou’s indifferent voice casually asked, "Did you come alone?"

"There’s also a subordinate." Shuangxu replied.

He Tingzhou said nothing more.

When the elevator reached the 7th floor, Shuangxu lifted her foot to step out. He asked leisurely, "Does your subordinate live here too?"

"Yes."

After Shuangxu answered, she heard He Tingzhou let out a very soft, mocking laugh.

She detected the sarcasm in his tone but didn’t understand the reason. "Is there a problem?"

This floor was for executive suites. At Yun Dun Group, only directors and above had this travel standard. Feixue, a company so poor it could barely make ends meet, certainly wouldn’t book executive suites for ordinary employees.

So, most likely, they were sharing.

He Tingzhou leaned against the elevator wall. The overhead light cast a warm tone, but his gaze was coldly dismissive. "I wish I had a boss as ‘generous’ as you."

"You are the boss. You could be more generous to your subordinates." Shuangxu restrained her temper as she said this, then turned and walked out.

Back in her room, as she showered, she inexplicably thought of He Tingzhou’s expression again.

She couldn’t describe it, but she felt that her previously good mood had suddenly become stifling.

She didn’t understand why He Tingzhou was always so sarcastic toward her.

He had helped her, saved her, but every time she thought their relationship had grown a little closer, she was jolted awake, reminded not to read too much into it.

Forget it.

He Tingzhou was never someone she could consider a friend.

The next morning, the contact at Huifeng Technology remained silent. As the agreed time approached, Shuangxu took the initiative to call them, but the line was busy.

For the next hour, she couldn’t reach anyone at Huifeng.

This kind of unannounced no-show was what Shuangxu disliked most. She frowned, already sensing something was wrong.

Feixue had experienced similar situations before—plenty of them. The expert worried, "Do they not want to cooperate anymore?"

Shuangxu stopped waiting and hailed a car. "Let’s go to their company."

The two arrived at the industrial park where Huifeng Technology was located and asked for the customer director in charge, Director Zhang.

The secretary said, "Director Zhang is currently meeting with a client. Please wait a moment."

They waited nearly another hour.

Shuangxu checked her watch, then got up to find the secretary. "Is Director Zhang done with his client?"

"I’m sorry, Director Zhang had an urgent matter and has already left."

Shuangxu didn’t speak, just stared at her silently.

The secretary’s face turned awkward under her gaze. She stammered, "I told him, but he said it was urgent and left in a hurry."

This wasn’t something a mere secretary could decide. Shuangxu knew it was useless to make things difficult for her.

"Then please tell Director Zhang that basic integrity matters in business. If they don’t want to cooperate or have any concerns, they should have made it clear before we came, rather than leaving us waiting like this, playing games."

Shuangxu added, "Since you’ve ‘invited’ us to make this trip, I’ll send you the bill for the flights and hotel later. Please reimburse us."

After leaving Huifeng, the expert was disheartened. "Why do we always run into this kind of thing? Another wasted trip."

They stood by the roadside waiting for a car. Shuangxu looked at the distant blue sky and towering buildings, still calm.

"People always have to take some detours. It’s not a complete waste. The Hydrogen Energy Development Summit is tomorrow. We might as well go and see—maybe we’ll gain something else."

"But you’re not even mad." The expert said. "If it were President Shu, she would’ve exploded by now."

"Because getting mad doesn’t help." Shuangxu smiled. "Actually, it’s best if you can vent your anger. Suppressed anger turns into knots, growing somewhere in your body. President Shu is much more carefree than I am."

When they returned to the hotel, by coincidence, they ran into He Tingzhou at the entrance.

A stretched Rolls-Royce was parked in front of the hotel. He Tingzhou wore a charcoal-gray suit, rare for him to have every button fastened, his tie perfectly straight.

His chief assistant, Xu Zhen, had already opened the car door, and he was about to get in.

Shuangxu was caught between politely greeting him and politely pretending not to see him when she stumbled slightly on the carpet.

The expert immediately steadied her arm. "Hey, be careful!"

"It’s fine."

Shuangxu straightened up. Not far away, He Tingzhou had already noticed them.

He stood by the car, the custom black paint highlighting his sharp features. His cold, narrow dark eyes casually swept over Shuangxu.

Then, following her arm, his gaze shifted to the man beside her.

The man’s shirt was tasteless, its hem tucked into jeans. He carried a student-style black backpack and wore black-rimmed glasses, his head a mop of natural curls.

Apart from his skin being somewhat pale from lack of sunlight and his features being somewhat refined, he was otherwise unremarkable—throw him into any university, and you’d find twenty more just like him in a second.

Seeing He Tingzhou staring at the man for several seconds, Xu Zhen also glanced over.

Then, he explained to He Tingzhou who the man was.

The expert who had accompanied Shuangxu on this trip was a genius who had entered Yancheng University at the age of thirteen. His surname was Cheng, and his first name was a rare character, Yi. Everyone at Feixue simply called him "Big God."

He was Feixue’s treasure, and his only flaw was his social anxiety.

When Chen Peiran had split from Shu Yang, the first person he tried to take with him was Big God. It was said that Chen had called him over a dozen times and sent dozens of 60-second voice messages, harassing Big God so much that he had to block Chen at 3 AM.

He Tingzhou didn’t speak, his eyes fixed on the approaching pair.

Shuangxu was about to greet him when He Tingzhou’s critical gaze shifted back to her. With ambiguous meaning, he said, "Your taste is truly ever-changing."

chapters.title: I'll Pick You Up Tonight
chapters.content:
"What?" Shuangxu didn't understand.

He Tingzhou: "Nothing, just complimenting you."

Shuangxu didn't believe him; he never said nice things about others.

She wanted to introduce the two of them, but when she turned around, the "god" was eight zhang away, his face clearly saying, "Don't call me, don't call me, don't call me."

Shuangxu knew he dreaded social interactions the most. He even avoided company dinners if he could. Normally, unless necessary, the company never required him to participate in such events. This time, since the business trip involved technical issues, he was brought along.

Seeing how resistant he was, she gave up the idea.

"He is our company's technical director, but he has social anxiety, so I won't introduce you."

He Tingzhou mocked, "Your company's temple is small but has many gods. Is everyone a director?"

Shuangxu was a bit unhappy: "There's no way everyone is a director. There's only one technical director. He is the core figure of our company. The flight control system you were interested in before was programmed by him."

Still defending him.

He Tingzhou's cold eyes scanned the otaku up and down. Thin and pale, he couldn't even do twenty push-ups without gasping. Where would he get abs?

"Director Song is still so easy to fool. Isn't she quite sharp in front of me, using all her IQ to deal with me?"

Shuangxu was completely confused, unable to understand what he was talking about: "Others aren't like you, always bullying me."

He Tingzhou, with his hand on the car door, asked her, "How have I bullied you?"

The way he pronounced those two words was lazy, adding a hint of ambiguity. Xu Zhen, beside them, professionally lowered his head, mindful of his own business.

Shuangxu wisely chose to end the conversation: "I'm going back first."

Before He Tingzhou could react, she quickly walked up the stairs. The waiting "god" hurried to catch up, and the two entered the hotel side by side.

The next day's Hydrogen Energy Development Summit was held at the convention center.

This summit gathered top companies and experts in the hydrogen energy industry. Shuangxu took it very seriously and arrived early with the "god."

In such an industrial setting, women—especially beautiful ones—were rare. As soon as Shuangxu, dressed in professional attire, walked in, she attracted many gazes.

A man came over to chat, and upon learning that their company also supplied liquid hydrogen, Shuangxu started talking to him.

But the man's interest was clearly not in Feixue.

When she asked about their company's lightweight low-temperature liquid hydrogen storage tanks, he asked her, "How old are you this year? You don't look like you've graduated yet. Which school do you attend?"

When she asked about storage and transportation issues, he asked her, "Miss Song, you're so beautiful. How come you're still single?"

It was like talking to a cow.

Under his burning gaze, she lost interest and patience in the conversation: "If I were ugly, would being single make sense?"

"Ah, that's not what I meant." The man took out his phone. "Your company needs low-temperature liquid hydrogen supply, right? Add me on WeChat. Let's find a chance to talk properly..."

"No, I don't like working with unprofessional people."

After turning away, Shuangxu saw Director Zhang from Huifeng Technology, with a few people from Chenxing around him.

Seeing how happily they were chatting, she instantly understood why she had been stood up yesterday.

After losing to Feixue in the cooperation with Yun Dun Group, Chenxing unexpectedly snatched the supplier here.

The people from Chenxing saw her and smirked: "Director Song, I heard you went to Huifeng yesterday and got stood up. What a coincidence, Director Zhang was discussing cooperation with us yesterday. He was too busy to see you."

Shuangxu calmly replied, "There is more than one liquid hydrogen supplier. If Huifeng doesn't work out, I'll just switch to another. If you like chasing after Feixue, go ahead. Let's see how long you can keep it up."

Director Zhang looked a bit embarrassed and didn't dare to look at her directly. After the Chenxing people left, he privately apologized to her.

"Sorry, Director Song. I didn't mean to stand you up. I really didn't have time yesterday..."

Shuangxu interrupted him: "Before officially signing the contract, you have the right to choose. I completely understand. But there's no need for such hypocritical words. You must eat, drink, and use the bathroom every day. No matter how busy you are, you have time to send a message."

"To be honest, I did have the intention to cooperate with you. Otherwise, I wouldn't have invited you all the way here. But they contacted me and offered to introduce me to Director Fan from Yun Dun Group. You also know that Yun Dun Group's layout in the hydrogen energy industry chain is unmatched by other companies. In addition to the drone sector, they also have liquid hydrogen heavy truck projects and medium to large liquid hydrogen aircraft projects. If we can establish a long-term cooperative relationship, it will greatly benefit our company's development."

After listening, Shuangxu found it a bit funny.

"If you hadn't stood me up yesterday, you would have known what a big detour you took. Feixue's client is Yun Dun Group."

"And Chenxing...?"

"They are fooling you." Shuangxu said, "You fall for it faster than a monkey."

Director Zhang was completely stunned, still in a daze, when Xu Zhen, dressed in a suit, walked up to Shuangxu and respectfully said, "Miss Song, President He invites you over."

Shuangxu turned around and saw He Tingzhou standing on the other side of the venue.

He was surrounded by people, wearing a dark gray three-piece suit, tailored to fit him perfectly. From his shoulders, chest to waist, and legs, the lines were elegant and smooth, without a single wrinkle.

His tie was tied in a precise Prince Albert knot, and the pocket square in his left chest pocket matched his shirt. From head to toe, he exuded an air of noble elegance that drew everyone's attention.

His tall and straight figure was too outstanding, as was his identity. The host of the summit, President Feng, and a group of relevant leaders and experts gathered around him.

Unlike Shen Yu, who valued etiquette and gentlemanly demeanor in his interactions, He Tingzhou never gave face to anyone.

The respect and flattery from those around him, he couldn't even be bothered to pretend. His arrogant gaze swept across half the venue and landed on her, crooking his finger at her.

Shuangxu was led over by Xu Zhen, and everyone's attention focused on her, filled with curiosity.

Shuangxu didn't really understand why He Tingzhou called her over. To introduce her? He wasn't that kind.

As she approached, He Tingzhou's bored expression finally faded. Amid the silent anticipation of the crowd, he introduced her: "My subcontractor."

Shuangxu: "..."

It was the first time she heard someone introduced like that.

Ordinary subcontractors didn't need him to specially introduce them. Everyone tacitly understood that this "subcontractor" was not ordinary, and their attitude toward Shuangxu was polite and friendly.

She responded politely, smiling as she stood beside He Tingzhou. Borrowing his light, many company representatives came forward to network. In no time, her hands were filled with business cards.

Among them were not a few liquid hydrogen suppliers more famous than Huifeng.

The president showed interest in Feixue's liquid hydrogen drones. The "god," despite his social anxiety, once he started talking about drones and flight control systems, entered a state of non-stop chatter. His speech was rapid and dense, constantly spouting professional terms that were too obscure for ordinary people, exuding an aura of a high-IQ nerd.

Such rare talent was hard for the businessmen not to appreciate, and they praised He Tingzhou for his keen eye in spotting it.

Shuangxu thought, what does that have to do with him?

"This is our company's technical director, Cheng Shi."

Cheng?

He Tingzhou raised an eyebrow slightly: "Then who is Liao?"

Shuangxu looked at him strangely: "My assistant. You've seen her. She went with my senior sister on the day of the signing."

He Tingzhou didn't remember.

But he remembered that there were two women that day.

After the meeting officially started, someone thoughtfully rearranged a seat for Shuangxu in the front row, right next to He Tingzhou.

She listened to the speeches very intently, occasionally lowering her head to take notes, with both arms resting on the table, as serious as a student in class.

Not until the meeting ended did Shuangxu pack up her things, preparing to leave with the "god."

He Tingzhou's indifferent gaze swept over the otaku director who had been following her like a tail the whole time, and said with feigned solemnity: "Leaving already? I have a few questions about your flight control system. Director Cheng, let's have dinner tonight and chat about it."

The "god" was taken aback and instinctively looked to Shuangxu for help.

Shuangxu immediately said, "Sorry, President He, but he has social anxiety and isn't used to face-to-face conversations. If you have any questions, I can compile the information and send it to you."

"That's unfortunate." He Tingzhou, at some point, had taken the pen she was writing with and was twirling it between his long, distinct knuckles. "I don't like reading text. I prefer face-to-face conversations."

Shuangxu pressed her lips together, thinking for a moment: "Can I talk to you about it?"

He Tingzhou looked at her for a few seconds, then slowly put the pen cap back on and handed it to her: "Sure. I'll pick you up tonight."

---
